features: Retro Keyboard Mouse Set: Use 2.4GHz Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo to enjoy a comfortable and efficient typing experience, featuring 104 vintage typewriter rounded keys for a smooth and responsive press and click

Aesthetic Keyboard: This colorful keyboard features a unique design with a mix of colors and macaron-inspired elements, creating a vibrant addition to your workspace. The clash of hues adds energy and creativity to your keystrokes, while the macaron-inspired palette brings a touch of sweetness and joy to your work experience. This girly keyboard is a visually stunning accessory that brightens up your workspace with its colorful and lively design

User-friendly features: The wireless mouse offers 3 DPI settings (800-1200-1600), and the ergonomic keyboard's optimized tilt angle reduces hand fatigue, with buttons that fit the fingers for a comfortable typing experience.

Auto Sleep Keyboard & Mouse: Wireless keyboards and clicky mice have an auto-sleep mode, once you stop using the wireless keyboard set for a while, they will work at a lower current for energy saving. They can go on for months without the hassle of replacing batteries
2.4G Wireless Plug and Play: Enjoy wireless connectivity at a range of 30 feet by plugging in a USB receiver without any software. Simply connect your portable keyboard and mouse

Wide Compatibility Office Supplies: Compatible with Windows 7 / 8 / 10 operating systems and Mac OS, the keyboard and mouse combo includes a full-size keyboard and a high-sensitivity mouse. They work perfectly with your PC, laptop, smart TV, desktop, or notebook computer, etc.
Free Clean Tool: The high-density soft brush is ideal for cleaning dust from all kinds of keyboards and crevices.
24-Hour Service: The cute keyboard set comes with a one-year free replacement service encounter any problems, please consult our 24-hour service

features: Tri-Mode Wireless for Mac/WIN: The S102 PRO gaming keyboard features mac/win compatibility (FN+A/S) and three connection modes, for dominating a late-night match on PC via 2.4Ghz wireless (FN+3), easy switching between 2 paired devices via BT (FN+1/2) or worry-free plug-and-play with the USB A-to-C cable right out of the box. NOTE: The S102 PRO keyboard is a membrane keyboard (not a mechanical keyboard). It does not support hot-swapping, and the switches cannot be replaced.

Intuitive Control with Volume Knob, Display & Shortcut: Mid-game and needing a vibe change? Attending online meeting and needing to turn up volume? Simply dial up the volume with the rotary knob or use FN shortcut to cycle through RGB settings, without ever alt-tabbing or breaking your focus. The TFT screen, also an intuitive helper, let you monitor the essentials such as keyboard connection status or battery percentage in a glance.

Silent Keyboard in Full Size Layout: With a dedicated number pad and full set of function keys, the S102 PRO offers the familiar spacious layout with dedicated number pad and all function keys, making office tasks and document work a breeze. With silicone structure, this membrane keyboard offers a whisper-quiet typing experience, perfect for late-night study in shared dorm or professional work in open-concept office.

Creamy Keyboard with Adjustable Height: With a 2cm mid-height front designed to keep your hand in a natural, neutral position for all-day coding or gaming marathon, the S102 PRO ergonomic keyboard features the sculpted, tiered Cherry profile that mirrors the natural curve of finger movement for strain-free comfort. The adjustable kickstands, offering 3 typing angles, allows you to find the perfect incline for your specific desk height or setup.

RGB Backlit Gaming Keyboard: With stunning dynamic RGB backlight, the S102 PRO gaming keyboard provides the perfect "vibe" for midnight gaming sessions. The smooth transitions and rhythmic RGB effects of S102 PRO, adjustable in brightness and colors, turns a simple desk into a professional battle station, while the gaming mode (FN+W) turns the ASDW keys into arrow keys for convenient left-hand control.

aPlusContent.title: Product description Tri-mode Connection  Large 2000mAh Battery  100% Full Size Layout  Backlight & Indicator Light  Dual-Function Knob
aPlusContent.rawText:
Product description
Previous page
Next page
1 Membrane Keyboard 2 Comfy Typing 3 Quiet & Creamy 
←Tri-Mode Connection - Battery - PC/MAC Compatible - Size & Weight→ 
Tri-mode Connection 
USB-C Wired/2.4Ghz Wireless/BT1/BT2 

The S102 PRO gaming keyboard supports Mac/Win (FN+A/S) and 3 connection modes: 2.4Ghz wireless (FN+3) for late-night PC gaming, BT (FN+1/2) for seamless switching between 2 paired devices, and USB A-to-C for instant out-of-the-box plug-and-play. 
Tips: If WIN Key stopped working, use FN+WIN to en/disable it. If WIN/Alt swapped places, use the WIN/Mac switch besides USB port to swap OS Mode.
The video showcases the product in use.The video guides you through product setup.The video compares multiple products.The video shows the product being unpacked.
Aula S102 PRO Membrane Gaming Keyboard
Large 2000mAh Battery 
Rechargeable battery with 150H playtime 

The S102 PRO rechargeable keyboard features a 2000mAh high-capacity battery with low power consumption and extended endurance, delivering up to 150 hours of use (backlight off) and 25 hours (backlight on) on a single charge. 
Tips: This keyboard charges when plugged in – always use a computer USB port for charging; direct power adapter use may damage the battery. 
100% Full Size Layout 
105 Keys + Screen + Knob 

The S102 PRO full-size keyboard comes with an integrated numeric keypad, intuitive display and dual-function rotary knobs. The numeric keypad boosts efficiency for financial tasks, the display clearly shows battery level, charging status and keyboard connection mode, and the dual knobs offer easy control of volume, multimedia playback and backlight settings. 
Experience Whisper-Quiet Typing with Silent Membrane Keyboard 

Enjoy a peaceful typing experience with the S102 PRO silent membrane keyboard. Perfect for shared workspaces or late-night productivity sessions, this feature ensures your keystrokes won't disturb those around you. Combine comfort and consideration in one sleek design. 
←Dynamic Lights - Dual Function Knob→ 
Backlight & Indicator Light 
Dynamic RGB Backlight 

Upgrade to the S102 PRO Creamy Keyboard and effortlessly boost your office productivity. It boasts a rich selection of pre-set dynamic RGB lighting effects, from gentle breathing modes to eye-catching flowing gradients—each carefully calibrated. Brightness can be freely adjusted via the top knob or key combinations. 
Turn On/Off Backlit: FN+Backspace. 
Toggle Backlight Effect: FN+Enter. Backlight Color: FN+\|
Backlight Brightness/Speed: FN+↑↓←→
Dual-Function Knob 
Multimedia Control & Backlight Adjustment 

S102 PRO full-size keyboard with a built-in screen and control knob comes with an integrated numeric keypad, greatly boosting office efficiency. The dual-function volume knob supports volume adjustment, mute control, and backlight switching, while the screen displays key information in real time, including battery level and keyboard connection status. 
Knob Function: Volume & Backlight Control (Knob to Swap)
Does it have programmable keys? 
The S102 PRO keyboard is not equipped with dedicated software, so custom key functions, macro settings, and personalized backlight customization are not supported. 
Is this keyboard noisy while typing? 
The S102 PRO membrane keyboard offers an ultra-quiet, comfortable typing experience, perfect for offices and shared working spaces. 
Does the backlight remain on continuously? 
No. In wireless mode, the backlight will automatically turn off after 6 minutes of inactivity, and the keyboard will enter power-saving mode (light sleep after 6 minutes, deep sleep after 30 minutes). Press any key to wake the keyboard. 
How is the battery level displayed? 
The battery level is shown in 10% increments. Please note that the displayed percentage is not fully accurate, with a typical deviation of around 10%. 
How to wake up the keyboard from sleep mode? 
Please press any key twice in succession to wake the keyboard.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Finally got it to work and now I love it.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I wanted a plug and play keyboard to replace my beloved apple bluetooth keyboard. This did not come with a wire for USB c to USB c, and there wasn't a quick start guide in the teeny little instruction booklet that was kind of a mess to read.  I almost returned this bc I couldn't get it to work despite it being almost fully charged.  I couldn't get the keyboard to respond in any way.  It was maddening.  It turned out I needed to have it switched on ---which it was, then I had to press the function key and A for apple.  That was it, it worked perfectly after that.I did notice if I had too many windows open on my little iPad that the response time lagged with this keyboard and I never noticed that with my apple keyboard.  But after closing the window it worked fine.I would rate this a 4 star experience if I were to include the frustration of getting this keyboard connected.  Having only used Apple products for the last few decades, I wasn't use to the confusing setup and it was mostly due to the instructions...thank goodness for AI, that helped immensely.  However, everything about the keyboard, including the price was excellent.  We'll see how long the battery lasts, and how it will need to be replaced.  One note is not to overcharge the battery, and not to charge too often.  So with the battery display, this will be helpful.  I'm going to assume it's similar to charging an EV car, never drop below 20% and never charge over 80%.It's a great size to balance on my lap while sitting on my lounge chair and working on my iPad.  It's easy to switch from iPad to my Mac by switching the Bluetooth connection, it comes with 2. The keyboard is silent...I was looking for a creamy keyboard...but a silent keyboard is actually what I needed --I never heard of a silent keyboard prior.  Every one I've had has clacked.  I just didn't know silent existed.  Listening to someone pound away on a keyboard is actually annoying.  So if you are in an office environment that may not be ideal, unless you want everyone to hear you working hard 😊

As for the price, it was reasonable for the color options because I've seen some keyboards that were over $199 in basic black.I'm usually a Logitech customer, and my last Logitech keyboard lasted six years, so I was hesitant to try a different brand. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a very good full keyboard, with inverted T arrow navigation keys, numeric keypad, home/end/pgup/pgdown/delete/insert grouping, and 12 function keys. It's also backlit with a good variety of lighting modes. So far I'm really happy with it. Could it be better? Sure; it lacks a wrist rest, ergonomic layout like a Microsoft Natural, and doesn't have dedicated media control keys (although this last point isn't a big deal for me since this keyboard is for use with a computer that won't be used for multimedia).However, keyboards are a very personal thing and a big deal these days, so here are some more details to help you understand this keyboard's features.Weight: It's not as heavy as the dedicated gaming mechanical keyboards that seem popular now with gamers and programmers. But it's not flimsy either. Light enough to not be much hassle if you're going to be traveling with it.Key feel: This keyboard is not one of the loud clicky ones. It does feel more tactile than a typical membrane keyboard, and the keys have a nice travel when you press them, but the click sound is very soft. These are regular-style keys, not chicklet keys.Lighting: I wasn't too worried about have top RGB features, but sometimes if it's darker in the room I do like some backlighting. This keyboard is a nice compromise between keyboards that have only white backlight, and keyboards that have a full software control app that let you customize everything. There is no software with this keyboard, it has several modes all configured using the function keys. Here are the lighting modes:- Lighting off/on- Neon mode: multiple colors light up three static zones on the keyboard. There are a few combinations you can select. The colors stay the same in the zones and don't change.- Spectrum mode: 7 colors rotate and fill the entire keyboard continuously. So it'll be lit red, then fade into purple, then blue, then green, etc.- Static mode: You cycle through and pick the color you want of the 7 supported colors, and it will stay lit continuously with just that one color.There are brightness and breathing effects that you can configure for each of the modes.I only use static mode, but gamers might like the other ones. I saw more expensive boards that only did spectrum or only had one color.Key visibility: The keys are not painted so they're a little hard to read in poor lighting if you don't use the backlight. However, I did like that the symbol keys had the correct placement for lower/upper case characters. I have seen many expensive keyboards from Razer, Corsair, Alienware, etc., that often invert the upper/lower case labeling for symbol keys and number keys. If you're an experienced typist, you'll work around that, but it bugs me when I see it. I found out later that this is an intentional design decision so that the more commonly used lower case symbol is more visible when backlit (the lighting doesn't cover the entire key and ends up emphasizing whatever character is in the upper case position). But you won't have to worry about that with the ReDragon.Key layout: After looking at the huge variety of keyboards on Amazon, you'll notice that some smaller keyboards don't have the numeric keypad or the six-key navigation group. Or that some have that ANSI style keyboard with the bigger Enter key but then put the slash key somewhere else. Or some that have compressed distance between keys or even smaller keys to make it more compact.This keyboard has an ISO keyboard layout with 104 full-sized keys. The key spacing is about a quarter-inch, which is similar to other full-size keyboards I've used.For the price, I think this is a great peripheral. Longevity would be my only concern, and I'll update this review later if I run across any issues.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Bought 2 of these keyboards.  Both stopped working 5-6 weeks after purchase.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: When I purchased the first Redragon K509 keyboard, I also purchased a Redragon S107 keyboard and mouse combo at the same time.  The keyboard in that S107 combo looks identical to this K509 keyboard.  It even has the exact same instructions, looks identical, and behaves exactly the same.  This K509 keyboard appeared to be a good value.  I felt the quality was good for the price.  The LED's were not fixed colors (which is good), and the LED's could be set in many colors, in "breathing mode" and constant brightness.  However, when set to constant brightness, the lights dim a significant amount.  I could live with that.I would give this K509 model a fairly high rating, but after 6 weeks, the first keyboard stopped working.  Windows would no longer recognize the device.  I tried plugging it into different USB ports, but that made no difference.  I tried using the keyboard on 2 other PC's, and they had the same trouble recognizing the device.  I figured I just had bad luck, and ordered a second, exact same keyboard.  After 5 weeks, this second keyboard started having the exact same trouble.  Windows would no longer recognize the device.  It couldn't even tell it was a keyboard.  Again, I tried this keyboard different USB ports and on two other PC's.  It would not work no matter which port or PC I plugged it into.  Other devices, including other keyboards, work on each of the USB ports I tried on the 3 different PC's.  I also have a Redragon S107 Keyboard that is part of the Redragon S107 Keyboard/Mouse combo.  That keyboard still works great, and looks and behaves identical to the K509, except for the label underneath the keyboard.  The S107 keyboard (not this KB) works just fine on all 3 PC's, and I still use it without trouble, to this day. I have contacted the manufacturer and attempted to get support for this product, multiple times, and they said that it was a problem with the USB port, and to plug into another port.  I had tried this, as well as trying the keyboard on multiple USB ports on two other PC's.  The manufacturer would not admit that the problem was with the keyboard.  I was given instructions how to remove the unrecognized device in the Windows "Device Manager", and let windows recognize the device again.  This had no effect.  After the problems began, each time I plug in the keyboard, it would light up for a few seconds, the PC would make the typical "USB device attached" sound, then the light would turn off. Two or three seconds later, it would light up, PC makes the sound again, and lights turn off.  It would repeat this for various number of times, before the keyboard would eventually have the lights stay ON, and look as if it was working, but none of the keys would respond.  When I check Windows 10 "Device Manager", I would see the keyboard listed as "Unknown USB Device (Device Descriptor Request Failed)"  The Device Status read as, "Windows has stopped this device because it has reported problems. (Code 43) A request for the USB device descriptor failed."  I like this keyboard.  I would purchase another, but I worry that there may be a design or manufacturing flaw, causing an increased chance of the device failing to be recognized by the PC.  I have only tried two of these keyboard, so I cannot be sure.  But 0 out of 2 is not a record that would inspire the confidence for me to recommend this keyboard to anyone.I get this exact same behavior and error on all 3 PC's... an HP desktop, a Dell/Alienware desktop, and a Microsoft Surface Pro 4 Tablet PC.  My Redragon S107 Keyboard and mouse combo continues to work just fine.  I have an older USB keyboard being used instead of the two Redragon K509 keyboards.  Neither K509 keyboard was damaged, dropped, or misused in any way.  They get plugged in, and remain in a fixed position from that point forward.  No food or drink is consumed near them, because they are located around other sensitive equipment.I should have attempted a product return on Amazon, but it was already outside the window of time I could return or exchange the product.  That is on me.  However, the manufacturer still would not admit that the keyboard was defective in any way, in spite of the obvious evidence to the contrary.

The keyboard in the box was wrapped in bubble wrap which was hella thoughtful. For a $50 keyboard, there's alot of work put into it and I totally appreciate that especially for those who are just starting out using mechanical keyboards, this is a great starter.The keyboard itself is hella solid. It was alot heavier than I thought it would be but i Love that because that means the keyboard won't move easily. It's a thick base, and is amazing for the price. It's very comfortable to use too. It was also a bit bigger than I thought it would be but I think I just got used to my Ducky One 2 Mini too long lol.Theres even little adjusters on the back of the board to raise it if flat doesnt work for somebody (like me). I bought this keyboard for one of those reasons. Also, the box came with a instruction mini booklet which is nice because nowadays with budget buys, you dont get those kinds of things that explain how the product works. Also, it came with a red dragon sticker which i was completely stoked about. It also came with a keycap remover, I already have one but an extra one will be handy.Theres 9 backlight options and they're all sick. super easy to change too. I'm just a steady RGB kinda gal so I didn't really care about the options too much but if you do, the options are great. cool part I love about this keyboard too is the arrow keys. My Ducky One 2 Mini doesn't have that and I don't really care but for developing, those can come in handy, so i'm stoked. Red switches are relatively quiet, it's not super loud but it's got a nice click to it.I'll update for long term use at some point, but I dont think i'll be disappointed.Overall, do I recommend this? Yeah. 100%. For the price, its a hella good deal. Great budget buy, great starter mechanical keyboard, and wicked solid itself.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Top Quality & Aesthetic DesignTop Quality & Aesthetic Design
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If you are interested in transitioning from an old school to mechanical keyboard, want something with an absolutely sick looking design, is simple to use, and doesn't have insanely loud key press noises, this is definitely a top option! I have had this unboxed for barely 30 minutes and am already in love with it. It was super easy to plug-n-play and use the built in functions immediately.I have used old style, full-length keyboards for decades and was extremely hesitant to try out a mechanical keyboard, especially because of the noise I had heard from seeing video reviews and how unsure I was if I could deal with the loss of full buttonology. One major reason I looked into one of this type/size was that I realized one of the main reasons I have issues with soreness and pain in my left shoulder, neck, and upper arm is due to how I would position my left hand and tilt the keyboard in order to use the traditional movement keys WASX on a full sized keyboard for gaming. With this one, my arm is now in a natural resting position at 90 degrees against my side, negating the angular stress on all those muscle groups, and when I want to do some typing while gaming, I don't have to stretch across the board to my left as much with my right hand to get to home keys.Additionally, one big assumption killer was that, even though the size is cut down by a ton from a full-sized keyboard, the muscle memory transition to the slightly more compacted keys took hardly any time at all when typing with home keys. I type about 100 WPM, so I assumed I'd have a super difficult time with this aspect of the transition, but the spacing of keys doesn't have a huge difference of feel. The other big plus is that the noise level isn't huge on key press when gaming, and is not bothersome when typing; it's not that high pitched clickity clack you might get from many other types, rather a dull, thud-like sound.Now add in the amazing painted design (especially if you like Japanese wood block print/art), and the colored light functions, which mind you are accessible by using the keyboard and the built in mini screen aka not requiring you to download software, as well as the pre-programmed FN + <key> functions that replace the buttons you lost from a full sized keyboard, and this thing is just a dream.HIGHLY RECOMMEND to one and all, especially old folks like me that are afraid to make that leap into transitioning to a mechanical style board.P.S.: If you're looking for actual dimensions of the keyboard itself, which are not on this Amazon page nor on the company's item page, they are approximately as follows: 12.75"x5.75"x1.375"-0.875" (the last number is the height, without the height extenders being used, at the top of the keyboard vs. at the bottom. it slopes upward towards the back)

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I really liked the color and the frogs, and wanted to try a 75%. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great quality - Not the best instructions
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have only had this keyboard for a few days, but I will say that it is of very nice quality and works well with my Lenovo Yoga Laptop. The feel and size are great, the keyboard is a bit on the heavier side, which I don't mind. and it seamlessly connects while also super cute!The only reason I did not give the keyboard 5 stars is that the setup instructions were a bit vague and did not include how to download the software needed to set up and customize (I was able to figure it out, and the colors work great, and I can upload GIFs to the screen). I had to visit the brand's website to download and install the software (steps not included in the manual). I think if you have a general understanding of how to set up these types of keyboards and download software, it's fine, but adding these steps would make everything much more streamlined.Besides that, everything else works great so far, and I really like using the keyboard!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Love this keyboard! It’s compact (75%) and has a creamy sound when typing. It’s more of a dull and thumpy sound if that helps! features: Fast Trigger Gaming Keyboard: AULA WIN68 HE magnetic gaming keyboard offers an industry-leading 8,000Hz polling rate and 8x faster response time than traditional mechanical keyboard. Combined with ultra-low latency (0.3ms), it ensures your commands take effect instantly, giving you an edge in the game. The fast trigger keyboard is perfect for gamers and coders, greatly enhancing the gaming experience and work efficiency.

Hall Effect Keyboard with Magnetic Switch: Equipped with advanced hall effect magnetic switches, the WIN68 HE black gaming keyboard offers adjustable actuation point(0.02mm-3.44mm), and each key can be personalized to the smallest unit of 0.1 mm, providing an ultra-precise keying experience. In addition, press/reset sensitivity can be individually set via software to match the keystroke habits of different people in different types of games

Customizable Web Driver: The mechanical gaming keyboard is equipped with a professional web driver that allows users to customize RT/SOCD/DKS/MT/TGL functions, key mapping, macro editing, RGB lighting and other settings on windows systems without downloading(This driver does not support MAC, only compatible with Windows system). It provides one-stop management of the keyboard, allowing users to truly experience customization and personalization. Web driver connection: bit.ly/m/AULA

16.8 Million RGB Backlit keyboard: The light up keyboard features 16.8 million colors of RGB lighting effects with south-facing LEDs for a better visual experience. 14 preset lighting effects add a great ambience to your games. Lighting effects and brightness can be easily adjusted via driver or FN and key combinations. The backlight can be turned off if not needed

60% Compact Wired Keyboard: Designed for professional gamers, the 60% gaming keyboard saves up to 40% of desktop space while retaining the arrow keys and basic function keys. FN and key combinations unlock all keyboard commands. The 68-key wired gaming keyboard with detachable USB cable provides gamers with a more stable connection and greatly enhances the gaming experience. The small size and lightweight design make it easier to carry and perfect for business trip

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Budget HE keyboard that gives you all you need...
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: AULA WIN68 HE is my first ever HE keyboard, after years of being in the world of mechanical keyboards and exclusively favoring the brown switch (tactile) I always watched many videos and people praising HE keyboards and the edge they give to you in gaming primarily. We all know of the famed Wooting 60 HE which started this trend in gaming world both the price and being only 60% give's it only a small and competitive market for a few individuals that can afford it or need it for professional e-Sports. As primarily a single-player gamer I was blow away with how much HE switches changes your experience of playing and gives you for the first time ever something that gamepads had over keyboards, and that is you don't need to push the key all the way for it work, both only a slight push fulfils the given command that you want (MMOs and racing games benefit from this the most). The web software is one of the best features of this keyboard and it allows you to customize every single key however you want it, every key supports rapid trigger as well as customizing the dead zone as well as primarily the sensitivity of the keys. The standard version that I have allows you to customize the sensitivity from 0.8mm to larger if you prefer (default being 1.70mm, while mechanical boards clock at 2.1mm). Keyboard is hot swappable and you can change your magnetic switches really easily. Brightness and RGB is also good with no complaints in that department (you can customize it in the web software). The build quality is also good and think that board was upgraded to PBT switches since when typing on them the feel sandy and rough, sound quality is quite since magnetic switches are linear switches (both better in every way), and the keyboard is wired only which I prefer since I am using it on my personal PC and have no need to use it elsewhere. HE keyboards are definitely the future and every professional or enthusiast e-Sport gamer simply must have this keyboard because it gives them and edge in every way that mechanical keyboard simply cannot give at the moment! I recommended this board for anybody who is on the fence over coming to the HE world.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Love the Colors - Matched My Home Office Perfectly!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've only had this keyboard for a few days, but so far I'm very happy with it. One of the main reasons I chose it was the color scheme, light blue, navy blue, and white, which matches my home office perfectly. The RGB lighting is a nice bonus, and I especially love that I was able to set it to blue to complement my workspace.The keyboard connected without any issues and has been very responsive while typing. The keys were a little clickier than I prefer out of the box. While they weren't excessively loud, I wanted a softer typing experience, so I switched out the switches. Now the keyboard is much quieter (soft touch), which is exactly what I was looking for.Another thing I noticed right away is the weight. This keyboard feels solid and substantial, and it stays in place on my desk while typing. I got the unit with 108 keys because I type often and needed a full-size keyboard. As for the price, it was reasonable for the color options because I've seen some keyboards that were over $199 in basic black.I'm usually a Logitech customer, and my last Logitech keyboard lasted six years, so I was hesitant to try a different brand. However, this keyboard had the colors I wanted and seemed to come from a reputable company. So far, it has exceeded my expectations. If it holds up as well as my Logitech did, I'll be extremely pleased.Based on my experience so far, I would definitely recommend it.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a very good full keyboard, with inverted T arrow navigation keys, numeric keypad, home/end/pgup/pgdown/delete/insert grouping, and 12 function keys. It's also backlit with a good variety of lighting modes. So far I'm really happy with it. Could it be better? Sure; it lacks a wrist rest, ergonomic layout like a Microsoft Natural, and doesn't have dedicated media control keys (although this last point isn't a big deal for me since this keyboard is for use with a computer that won't be used for multimedia).However, keyboards are a very personal thing and a big deal these days, so here are some more details to help you understand this keyboard's features.Weight: It's not as heavy as the dedicated gaming mechanical keyboards that seem popular now with gamers and programmers. But it's not flimsy either. Light enough to not be much hassle if you're going to be traveling with it.Key feel: This keyboard is not one of the loud clicky ones. It does feel more tactile than a typical membrane keyboard, and the keys have a nice travel when you press them, but the click sound is very soft. These are regular-style keys, not chicklet keys.Lighting: I wasn't too worried about have top RGB features, but sometimes if it's darker in the room I do like some backlighting. This keyboard is a nice compromise between keyboards that have only white backlight, and keyboards that have a full software control app that let you customize everything. There is no software with this keyboard, it has several modes all configured using the function keys. Here are the lighting modes:- Lighting off/on- Neon mode: multiple colors light up three static zones on the keyboard. There are a few combinations you can select. The colors stay the same in the zones and don't change.- Spectrum mode: 7 colors rotate and fill the entire keyboard continuously. So it'll be lit red, then fade into purple, then blue, then green, etc.- Static mode: You cycle through and pick the color you want of the 7 supported colors, and it will stay lit continuously with just that one color.There are brightness and breathing effects that you can configure for each of the modes.I only use static mode, but gamers might like the other ones. I saw more expensive boards that only did spectrum or only had one color.Key visibility: The keys are not painted so they're a little hard to read in poor lighting if you don't use the backlight. However, I did like that the symbol keys had the correct placement for lower/upper case characters. I have seen many expensive keyboards from Razer, Corsair, Alienware, etc., that often invert the upper/lower case labeling for symbol keys and number keys. If you're an experienced typist, you'll work around that, but it bugs me when I see it. I found out later that this is an intentional design decision so that the more commonly used lower case symbol is more visible when backlit (the lighting doesn't cover the entire key and ends up emphasizing whatever character is in the upper case position). But you won't have to worry about that with the ReDragon.Key layout: After looking at the huge variety of keyboards on Amazon, you'll notice that some smaller keyboards don't have the numeric keypad or the six-key navigation group. Or that some have that ANSI style keyboard with the bigger Enter key but then put the slash key somewhere else. Or some that have compressed distance between keys or even smaller keys to make it more compact.This keyboard has an ISO keyboard layout with 104 full-sized keys. The key spacing is about a quarter-inch, which is similar to other full-size keyboards I've used.For the price, I think this is a great peripheral. Longevity would be my only concern, and I'll update this review later if I run across any issues.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Bought 2 of these keyboards.  Both stopped working 5-6 weeks after purchase.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: When I purchased the first Redragon K509 keyboard, I also purchased a Redragon S107 keyboard and mouse combo at the same time.  The keyboard in that S107 combo looks identical to this K509 keyboard.  It even has the exact same instructions, looks identical, and behaves exactly the same.  This K509 keyboard appeared to be a good value.  I felt the quality was good for the price.  The LED's were not fixed colors (which is good), and the LED's could be set in many colors, in "breathing mode" and constant brightness.  However, when set to constant brightness, the lights dim a significant amount.  I could live with that.I would give this K509 model a fairly high rating, but after 6 weeks, the first keyboard stopped working.  Windows would no longer recognize the device.  I tried plugging it into different USB ports, but that made no difference.  I tried using the keyboard on 2 other PC's, and they had the same trouble recognizing the device.  I figured I just had bad luck, and ordered a second, exact same keyboard.  After 5 weeks, this second keyboard started having the exact same trouble.  Windows would no longer recognize the device.  It couldn't even tell it was a keyboard.  Again, I tried this keyboard different USB ports and on two other PC's.  It would not work no matter which port or PC I plugged it into.  Other devices, including other keyboards, work on each of the USB ports I tried on the 3 different PC's.  I also have a Redragon S107 Keyboard that is part of the Redragon S107 Keyboard/Mouse combo.  That keyboard still works great, and looks and behaves identical to the K509, except for the label underneath the keyboard.  The S107 keyboard (not this KB) works just fine on all 3 PC's, and I still use it without trouble, to this day. I have contacted the manufacturer and attempted to get support for this product, multiple times, and they said that it was a problem with the USB port, and to plug into another port.  I had tried this, as well as trying the keyboard on multiple USB ports on two other PC's.  The manufacturer would not admit that the problem was with the keyboard.  I was given instructions how to remove the unrecognized device in the Windows "Device Manager", and let windows recognize the device again.  This had no effect.  After the problems began, each time I plug in the keyboard, it would light up for a few seconds, the PC would make the typical "USB device attached" sound, then the light would turn off. Two or three seconds later, it would light up, PC makes the sound again, and lights turn off.  It would repeat this for various number of times, before the keyboard would eventually have the lights stay ON, and look as if it was working, but none of the keys would respond.  When I check Windows 10 "Device Manager", I would see the keyboard listed as "Unknown USB Device (Device Descriptor Request Failed)"  The Device Status read as, "Windows has stopped this device because it has reported problems. (Code 43) A request for the USB device descriptor failed."  I like this keyboard.  I would purchase another, but I worry that there may be a design or manufacturing flaw, causing an increased chance of the device failing to be recognized by the PC.  I have only tried two of these keyboard, so I cannot be sure.  But 0 out of 2 is not a record that would inspire the confidence for me to recommend this keyboard to anyone.I get this exact same behavior and error on all 3 PC's... an HP desktop, a Dell/Alienware desktop, and a Microsoft Surface Pro 4 Tablet PC.  My Redragon S107 Keyboard and mouse combo continues to work just fine.  I have an older USB keyboard being used instead of the two Redragon K509 keyboards.  Neither K509 keyboard was damaged, dropped, or misused in any way.  They get plugged in, and remain in a fixed position from that point forward.  No food or drink is consumed near them, because they are located around other sensitive equipment.I should have attempted a product return on Amazon, but it was already outside the window of time I could return or exchange the product.  That is on me.  However, the manufacturer still would not admit that the keyboard was defective in any way, in spite of the obvious evidence to the contrary.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Bigger than I thought, but real amazing qualityBigger than I thought, but real amazing quality
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I bought this keyboard for work to use in the office. I already have a Ducky One 2 Mini at home for gaming and wanted something similar but on a budget for working as I am a developer and prefer typing on a mechanical keyboard than anything else.I read the reviews and didn't doubt the quality. Receiving it, it also didn't fail me on that.I received it today, ordered it last night so it came quick.I ordered the red switches, which I think will take some time to get used to as I'm used to Cherry MX Browns but thats not a problem. When I received the keyboard, the packaging was solid. It reminded me of when I bought my Ducky One 2 Mini, the box is high quality and it's amazing for the price. The one thing I noticed was how heavy the box was, which said to me that this keyboard would be solid. The box was also sealed which I appreciated. The keyboard in the box was wrapped in bubble wrap which was hella thoughtful. For a $50 keyboard, there's alot of work put into it and I totally appreciate that especially for those who are just starting out using mechanical keyboards, this is a great starter.The keyboard itself is hella solid. It was alot heavier than I thought it would be but i Love that because that means the keyboard won't move easily. It's a thick base, and is amazing for the price. It's very comfortable to use too. It was also a bit bigger than I thought it would be but I think I just got used to my Ducky One 2 Mini too long lol.Theres even little adjusters on the back of the board to raise it if flat doesnt work for somebody (like me). I bought this keyboard for one of those reasons. Also, the box came with a instruction mini booklet which is nice because nowadays with budget buys, you dont get those kinds of things that explain how the product works. Also, it came with a red dragon sticker which i was completely stoked about. It also came with a keycap remover, I already have one but an extra one will be handy.Theres 9 backlight options and they're all sick. super easy to change too. I'm just a steady RGB kinda gal so I didn't really care about the options too much but if you do, the options are great. cool part I love about this keyboard too is the arrow keys. My Ducky One 2 Mini doesn't have that and I don't really care but for developing, those can come in handy, so i'm stoked. Red switches are relatively quiet, it's not super loud but it's got a nice click to it.I'll update for long term use at some point, but I dont think i'll be disappointed.Overall, do I recommend this? productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great keyboard, definitely happy with the purchase - great price too.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Easily the best keyboard I've ever bought, and I've bought some high-tier brands in the past for over a hundred dollars.It comes with a keyswitch tool, extra switches, and does not feel cheap in quality.It also sounds nice when typing. It's that kind-of "muted clack" sound. Hard to describe such things but that's my best shot at it.The size is standard array and my fingers feel good on it.I was able to switch out my keycaps for WASD (I prefer circular key caps for those) and the caps do not clash with the other caps what-so-ever.The wireless bluetooth and plugged in modes both work well; I was able to use it wirelessly for about 3 days of near-constant use before having to plug it in.Honestly, I just left it plugged in since then so not sure how well the battery is on a recharge.The lights are appealing, the keys look nice; the color scheme is kinda abstract but I'm not mad about it.Overall, great keyboard, and it's held up for a couple months now with no degradation.Thanks Redragon. Appreciate a good product.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Bought both keyboards so I could compareBought both keyboards so I could compare
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: (TLDR): The “LED” one (less expensive) works/sounds just as fine, the only real difference is the “QWERTY” one has brighter and more vibrant backlighting.If you just care about functionality/affordability, get the cheaper one. If you care more about aesthetics, spend a lil more!- - - - -I have two fellow gamer friends who desperately needed new keyboards, and since I already bought them keycaps, I decided to look for affordable mechanical keyboards for them. Amazon recommended these, reviews seemed promising, but I had another issue.. what’s the difference?? Why is one $10-15 more?? Nothing really explains the difference here and Google couldn’t help me with wtf LED vs QWERTY was (I thought they both were?? 🤨 Idk still learning about keyboards, bear with me here) A few reviews said one was brighter than the other, but other than that, I was unsure why one cost more.One friend only cared about functionality as they work from home, but the other friend very much cares about aesthetics and has a nice gamer setup. So figured, I’ll just get both!So here’s a breakdown of all the notable but pretty settle differences:RBG LED (White Logo)On Box: Sindri Red DragonPrice: Cheapest Option (great for what you pay for, best affordable option)Sound: Red Switches, not “silent” imo but not too loud either (I think this one sounded SLIGHTLY clackier, but friends couldn’t tell difference, maybe I just watch a lot of keyboard videos to notice lol)Base: Black “Metallic” appearance (bottom keyboard in light pic) Felt slightly lighter, not all that noticeable thoughLighting: Not nearly AS vibrant, but still bright enough (top keyboard in dark pic) When you first plug in, the light is stagnant.Functionality: No lag so far, smooth typing, perfect for casual gamers or work useRGB QWERTY (Red Logo)On Box: Rudra Red DragonPrice: Slightly Pricier (still great for what you pay for tbh)Sound: Red Switches, same, not “silent” imo but not too loud eitherBase: Black Plastic appearance (top keyboard in light pic) Felt slightly heavier.Lighting: Much more vibrant (bottom keyboard in dark pic, pic doesn’t do justice, it was significantly brighter) When you first plugin, the light is flowing.Functionality: No lag so far, smooth typing, perfect for gamers and work use- - - - -My review is already long af, but I’ll have my friends update me on overall usage overtime. The “aesthetics” friend plays way more games on their PC, so I’ll be able to tell heavy gamer use for the QWERTY one. While the “functional” friend will be using it for work, as they work from home, so I’ll tell more daily use for the LED one. 👍 I’ll ask more about the settings as well as time goes on, for now, they’re just happy with their new keyboards!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Decent for a deal, but could be more durable.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I wouldn't buy this keyboard for more than thirty dollars, but it goes on sale enough that I believe it's worth buying for the twenty or so dollars the bring the price down to. I've had this keyboard for over a year, and it's worked flawlessly for most of that time. There's not much to say about it, functionally. It's a standard full-sized mechanical keyboard. It's not quiet, but I like how clicky it is, personally.Now, for the reason I don't recommend you buy this for full price. About nine or ten months into owning this item, the keys started to behave finicky. The 'R' key no longer lights up and the 'A' key has a problem with double inputs. I'll give the keyboard this, I use it a lot. I'm a writer and a gamer, so I've really put it through its paces. I'm also not as anal about maintenance as I probably should be. If you regularly dust and clean under the keycaps, it would probably last you a good deal longer.If your like me, someone who puts your keyboard through heavy use, I would go with something more durable. If you only intend to game with it, it should be fine for about a year, which for twenty dollars is a fine deal.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is one of the best keyboards I’ve bought on Amazon. It has a great build layout, the keys feel comfortable and responsive, and typing on it is smooth, quiet, and creamy. It was easy to set up and works perfectly right out of the box. It comes with a charger that is  the new charger of many devices including Apple, = very compatible.  The design is sleek and modern, and it offers excellent value for the price. I highly recommend this keyboard to anyone looking for a reliable, quality option.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 7, 2026Reviewed in the United States on July 7, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Keyboard is amazing, has all of my needs met. It's a full keyboard with NUM pad, has a backlight that can be adjusted either by color, by pattern, or by brightness, AND connects to multiple devices simulataneously. The keyboard is *NOT* quiet. But it's a "thocky" sounding keyboard. The taps are thick, muffled, and soft. I do wish the booklet that came with it had better instructions. I couldn't find in it how to switch the backlight pattern and had to ask Alexa on the product listing after it arrived. But the booklet does show how to program the buttons, install the software, and switch between connection modes. I'm definitely a fan for the price. Other keyboards with these features can be up to $70+ so this is basically a steal and such a great product for the value.I'd get more but because it connects to multiple devices, I only need one!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 10, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This keyboard is beautiful, it’s very easy to use, and sounds so creamy! Some of the videos including one I tried to make myself, make the sound appear a bit more “clicky” than it really is. The keys actually do have a very full bodied and creamy sound. It’s easy to type with for work or gaming really. The RGB lights are easy to navigate even if you don’t have the driver. And it’s build allows for easy typing and less tension in your hand. It has a pretty solid build, and for what you pay I’d say it’s more than worth the price!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I absolutely love this keyboard! The color is so cute, and I really like the soft, clicky sound when typing. The keys feel comfortable, and typing on it is honestly so satisfying. I just love using it!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 11, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This keyboard is pretty amazing. It's very easy to set up and use. I use it for both office-type work and online gaming. It is not a quiet keyboard, typing makes some sound, which I personally prefer.I love the extra controls like the dial for volume. The LED lighting has a lot of customization, even including adding a custom color, if you install the " AULA S99 三模RGB版 " software, but there are also shortcut keys to just quickly flip through the preset modes/colors.It has multiple options for connection(BT/GHz/USB), and they all work smoothly & without error that I've encountered. I like that there is the option to keep it on consistently if it's plugged in(USB), but I wish there was the option to do that while running on its charge too(BT/GHz). If it isn't plugged in, it will go to sleep with inactivity, but that's really my only complaint.I have not noticed any type of lag or input errors when using it. If anything, it's a little extra sensitive and, when first using it, I was typing some double letters by accident, so it is very responsive. I found it to be perfect even for fast-paced online competitive gaming, which says a lot for a small and affordable company/product. For the price, it's a no-brainer.AULA, PLEASE MAKE A MOUSE TO GO WITH THIS THAT HAS CUSTOMIZEABLE LEDS AND A COUPLE BUTTONS ON IT PRETTY PLEASEEEEEE. <3
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on May 15, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Epic price and amazing keyboard. Yes the going to sleep can be a bit annoying but the battery last forever because of that feature. Love the color and feel. Super happy with this keyboard.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 10, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This keyboard is adorable, has great soft (not super quiet, but soft feeling) key presses, its responsive, and it has great connectivity options. Its a happy medium between a full size keyboard versus a compact layout, and it's so easy and smooth to type on.That said, the RGB backlighting does not work for me. I've followed the instructions sent with the keyboard, followed the troubleshooting instructions from AULA and from Amazon, used AULA's software for this keyboard, tried factory resetting, and googled for help videos or anything I could find. Reached out to AULA's support, and they were unwilling to assist and just directed me to Amazon. All I could find on Amazon was the seller's support information. At this point I'm just accepting that it's a defect and something must be wrong within the keyboard, and I'm not savvy enough to diagnose their hardware issues nor do I have the time or will to demand a refund or replacement.The keyboard works great without RGB, but it was a big feature for me when purchasing this as it was mostly an aesthetic purchase. Yeah, I could have picked other options, but I chose this because of the price and I wish I hadn't. So, knocked two stars off for me.TL;DR - it's just a keyboard that you can use on multiple devices. If you just want simple for a good price, this is for you, cause it's a solid option. Don't expect support from the seller or be surprised when the extra functions don't work.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on April 16, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Cute, has a few quirks but good keyboardCute, has a few quirks but good keyboard
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I love this keyboard. It’s surprisingly sturdy. The keycaps and comfortable and they make a bit of a blend between creamy and clacky but they’re still quiet enough for a shared office space.I wish I had more options for the color of the backlight without installing the software as I use this keyboard with a work computer that I cannot install that on, so my choices are basically a terrifying red or rainbow.The Bluetooth connection to my computer is *fast*.The USB C connection only works if the cord is USB-C to USB-C, but the cord provided is USB-A to USB-C so that’s annoying.It also doesn’t seem to hold its charge and I don’t know why. I always have it plugged in to power so it’s fine, but I get a lot of “battery 0%” notifications and if I do unplug it it stops working immediately. I may test if charging is for some reason a USB-C to USB-C requirement as well.My keyboard in the picture is up on a keyboard riser so it isn’t actually that tall or angled. I do recommend a riser if you want a better angle for typing.

features: 【Optimized 75% Compact Layout&Innovative Gasket Structure】The F75 redefines space efficiency with its 75% compact layout. This design integrates all the essential keys in a smaller footprint, making it perfect for streamlined desks and mobile setups without sacrificing functionality. Experience the pinnacle of comfort with the gasket structure. This advanced design ensures a flexible yet firm typing experience, reducing fatigue during prolonged use while maintaining a consistent and responsive key feel.

【Acoustic Mastery with Five-Layer Padding】The F75 boasts a five-layer sound and shock-absorbing internal design, including two layers of Poron foam, IXPE switch pad, PET sound enhancement pad and a bottom silicone pad. This sophisticated construction significantly reduces typing noise and resonance, delivering a tranquil and focused typing environment.

【Precision-Engineered 1.2mm PCB&Pre-Lubricated Mechanical Switches】At the heart of the F75 is a meticulously crafted 1.2mm single-key slotted PCB. This precision engineering ensures that each keystroke is registered with accuracy and stability, providing a satisfying and reliable typing experience. The FF75 also features factory-lubricated mechanical switches that offer a seamless and smooth actuation. This pre-lubrication process ensures a fluid, consistent keystroke right from the start.

【Three-Way Connectivity for Every Scenario&4000mAh Battery】Offering BT, 2.4GHz wireless, and wired USB connectivity, the F75 adapts to your specific needs. Whether it's for a clutter-free wireless setup or a stable wired connection, this keyboard is ready for any situation. Equipped with a large 4000mAh battery, the F75 delivers extended usage times. This generous battery capacity ensures that your keyboard is always ready for long work sessions or intense gaming marathons.

【Multimedia Control Knob&Full-Key Hot-Swap Functionality】Effortlessly fine-tune your media settings using the integrated multimedia control knob, adding a layer of convenience that ensures swift adjustments without disrupting your workflow. Dive into a realm of customization with the full-key hot-swappable sockets of the F75. This feature facilitates seamless switch replacements, accommodating your desired typing feel, whether it's for gaming, typing, or creative endeavors.

【Finely-Calibrated Stabilizers&Cherry Profile Double-shot PBT Keycaps】Discover refined keystrokes with our precision-tuned stabilizers, offering stability and a hushed typing experience. Say goodbye to key wobble as your keystrokes gain enhanced accuracy. The F75 takes durability to the next level with its Cherry-profile double-shot PBT keycaps, ensuring a perfect blend of robustness and stylish design. These keycaps stand resilient against wear, maintaining a sleek appearance that defies the test of time.

【Ultra-Responsive Low-Latency&Vibrant 16.8M RGB Illumination】Engage in the dynamic glow of the F75's RGB backlight, presenting a rich spectrum of 16.8 million colors for a personalized typing environment. Tailor lighting patterns to suit your preferences, creating a desktop atmosphere that adapts to your mood. With its ultra-responsive, low-latency connection, the F75 ensures each keystroke is not only vividly illuminated but also delivered with swift and unwavering precision, whether you're gaming or typing away.

Can the charging light be turned off? 
Yes, press "FN+L_Shfit" to switch the charge indicator until the LED is off. 
How do you make the the knob adjust volume? 
The knob has two functions, If you find that rotating the knob cannot adjust the volume. Long press the "knob" until the LEDs of the "Win" and "Caps Lock" keys flash 3 times, indicating a successful mode switch. Then you can adjust the volume 
Can you re-program the keys for Mac users? 
This keyboard is Mac and Windows compatible, but the driver only supports Windows, so Mac users will not be able to re-program the keys. 
Why doesn't the "WIN" key work? 
The "FN+WIN" combination can lock or unlock the "WIN" key. When the "WIN" key is locked, it will light up in white. In the locked state, the "WIN" key will be disabled.

items.name: Can the charging light be turned off?
items.text: Yes, press "FN+L_Shfit" to switch the charge indicator until the LED is off.

items.name: How do you make the the knob adjust volume?
items.text: The knob has two functions, If you find that rotating the knob cannot adjust the volume. Long press the "knob" until the LEDs of the "Win" and "Caps Lock" keys flash 3 times, indicating a successful mode switch. Then you can adjust the volume

items.name: Can you re-program the keys for Mac users?
items.text: This keyboard is Mac and Windows compatible, but the driver only supports Windows, so Mac users will not be able to re-program the keys.

items.name: Why doesn't the "WIN" key work?
items.text: The "FN+WIN" combination can lock or unlock the "WIN" key. When the "WIN" key is locked, it will light up in white. In the locked state, the "WIN" key will be disabled.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A year later, still my daily driver, sounds as good as it types
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: A year in and this is still my daily driver. The gasket mount and five-layer dampening actually deliver, every keystroke has a deep, satisfying sound without being loud or hollow. It's the kind of thing that's hard to go back from once you're used to it.Build quality has held up well over a year of daily use. Hot-swappable switches mean I've been able to experiment without worrying about damaging anything, and the 75% layout hits the right balance between compact and functional, I've never missed having a full number pad.The knob is genuinely useful, not just a gimmick, quick volume control without digging through settings. Battery life on wireless has stayed solid too, don't find myself charging constantly.A year later, still my go-to keyboard, no regrets. If you want something that sounds as good as it types, this is worth it.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I picked up this keyboard because my previous keyboard broke suddenly, and I needed one for the next day. This was the best option for overnight delivery, so I placed the order and didn't really expect much. I'm really into mechanical keyboards and I have high standards for them, so when I tell you I was really pleased with what I heard and felt when this arrived, I'm not joking around! I've been using this for about a week now and I've got to say it exceeded my expectations.Pros:- Price! Mechanical keyboards can get really expensive, but if you're looking for a cheap entry into the hobby this seems like a decent option- Hot-swappable. I enjoy the switches but it's nice to know I have the option to change if I'm feeling it- Gasket mounted. The sound and feel of this keyboard are levels above what I would expect from a keyboard of this price- PBT keycaps. I'm going to swap mine most likely but it comes with decent keycaps- nice linear switches. I got the LEOBOG Reaper Switch option, tbd on how long these last but out of the box they feel really nice and combined with the mounting make a really nice sound when typing. I've been asked a few times in the office about the keyboard already!Cons:- Plastic. Hey, for this price I wouldn't expect anything else- Latency. I miiiiight be imagining things and I haven't tested yet but I do get the sense that it's a bit slower than my previous boards. I've seen a few reviews that suggest the same so definitely keep this in mind if it's important for you.Things to consider:- Software. I haven't and I don't plan on getting the software for this keyboard. I also wouldn't suggest it unless you're dead-set on setting up some custom configuration that isn't available with the hotkeys (I don't even know what the software supports). From the sound of it, other reviewers seem to have a lot of issues with it so I wouldn't even bother. That being said I just set it to have a solid white backlight and I'm happy with that.- Longevity. I've only had this a week, I'm keeping my hopes up that it lasts but you never know. I'll update this review if anything happens in the coming weeks or months.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Price to performance KING, Plug and play no bloatware, better than keyboards 3 times the price
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was very surprised with how well this keyboard preforms, it's almost silent and for a membrane I find the responsiveness to be very satisfying, I only bought this because the price was un beatable and I was coming from a 180 dollar razer keyboard and let me tell you I fully switched to the steel series , it feels better to use while gaming in my opinion and totally changed my view on spending 100s on a gaming keyboard , I also love how it is basically plug and play , no software is needed , I find the colors to be clean and aesthetically pleasing on the eyes , also the individual keys are luminated perfectly unlike my razer keyboard , it's also light weight and even so it doesn't move under constant pressure , I actually prefer the rubberized hand rest to my leather razer one, all in all you can't beat the price to performance here , like most reviews on here with this keyboard this thing rocks, I also don't review many items but this keyboard deserves it .

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I hated having to return this because this keyboard looks great and felt *so good* to use. The keys were buttery smooth and had a nice texture to their surface. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Don't want a loud keyboard? You want this....
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have been using the same Logitech wireless keyboard for somewhere around 12 years. My 8 month old has decided that it is very fun to play with that one. So I was in the market for a much needed upgrade and replacement.PROS: The keys have good travel and are, more importantly, not crazy loud. They do have an soft click to them that is satisfying for use typing or playing games but without the click is dampened to the point that, if you wish to type quietly, this is possible by just not pressing so hard. When you are putting alittle more force into the typing, say something intense is happening in your game, they are audible and clear.The keys and wrist rest are made of a very finely textured soft touch plastic, while the body is made of harder plastic. This offers stiffer construction so the board does not flex at all under normal use, while being easy on the hands to use for extended periods of time.RGB is bright and adjustable via the SteelSeries GG application which will sync the lighting to all SteelSeries devices if you so wish to. I use a Rival 3 mouse which has an illuminated scroll wheel RGB. Colors between the two match perfectly.The media controls are very handy. By default the wheel rolls to change volume and clicks in to mute while the button acts as play/pause.Key brightness can be controlled by pressing the SteelSeries key (located to the left of the right CTRL key and then pressing F11 or F12 for down and up respectively. There are 10 levels of brightness.CONS: It does not have a wireless which is ok but is something to note.The play/pause media button is illuminated and does not change from white.To be expected at this price point the RGB is sectioned equally off to 10 vertical zones.When the backlight is not on they keys are very hard to see.Overall this keyboard checks all the boxes for an all around winner. Soft on the hands. Quality construction. Enough RGB to please everyone but the most extreme RGB heads. Media controls are quick and easy to get to.I will be sending one of these to my buddy who is in need of an upgrade also.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Almost perfect -1 star for for forced account requirement
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: UPDATE: 1/10/24 - Long term comment here - I love this keyboard, buying one for my wife now... It has been working flawlessly for over 1 year now without a single hiccup and gaming every night!! Originally purchased Nov '22 - I highly recommend this product!**************************************************I am not easily impressed and i am not one who would normally spend $50 on a keyboard... This is my first product from Steel SeriesLet me just get this 1 Major Negative out of the way first. This prevented a 5-star review that i nearly never give <sigh>1. The default light pattern is RGB and you have little control out of the box, at best you can control the speed at which the color changed across the zones. Quick google search said you need to install the OEM software to get more control over the colors. Hmm, i wasn't pleased about that but so be it, a lot of OEMs do it and its just more crap running on your pc to slow it down..2. Software installed was 270MB, pretty darn big TBH, It installed tons of irrelevant stuff for products i do not own.. This could certainly have been done better.3. YOU MUST CREATE AN ACCOUNT with Steel Series to change anything about your product!!!! WHY??? Just another account username and password to track just so i can set a static color???**On the bright side, the control software Does Not need to run to keep your color settings, i do suspect if you use the other feature the software provides then you may have to have the software running in the background.OK, that is the ONLY gripe i have so far, Tempted to give a 3- star but that would be me placing too much weight on something that really annoys me and not fair to this product.So, What is good about this item? Taking the software issue out of the equation, it would be a 5 star product for sure. The only thing that would make it better is a lower price.I had just a few simple requirements for my keyboard and this fits perfectly.- Quiet - I hate the clackity clack typing sound especially when gaming- Backlit - I hate RGB and rolling RGB on a keyboard, i find it distracting. I like a nice soft glow to illuminate the keys so i can see the letters in the dark. I used to use blue or purple but have settled on red these past few years.- Compact, but full keyboard layout (108 keys?) - I hate big @$$ keyboards with tons of buttons, switches and misc. macro keys. Yes they have their purpose and are useful to some people, guess I'm getting old an traditional.- Durability - Who doesn't want that???Side note, Ergonomics IMHO is a personal preference but i kind of feel like the buttons are too high against the base but the keypresses are solid and actuation defined like when pulling the trigger on a quality firearm, you barely feel the slack being taken up and the you get a crisp break of the trigger.Very light keys with positive stroke, it's just good, end of story.All boxes checked with this keyboard - Durability TBD but it feels pretty solid so far. Backlight can be very dim or resemble the surface of the sun (not quite but it is bright). I know they call it "Steel Series" but this thing as some weight to it, it's not heavy but it is clearly not just a block of super thin/cheap plastic..I have not thoroughly explored the software capability but a brief romp around the menu's looks to be extremely inclusive and a similar type ecosystem to Corsair's iCue ecosystem which allows the software to interface and control all aspects of the OEM's product line. I found a lack of details or explanations for some of the features but not to terrible, most options are pretty straight forward.I believe in HONEST reviews and this has been my honest review that i almost didn't do but morally i have to give credit to Steel Series on a good product, they earned that much especially since this is the first product of theirs i have ever purchased.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: As a Keyboard snob and a very hard keyboard user, I really like this keyboard and this company overall.  It has a nice break for each key and while the typing is not whisper quiet, it is much less than a cherry red mechanical.  I can touch type easily and quickly as everything is where it should be.  I also have a older Apex 5 keyboard with the Cherry Brown keys I believe - great keyboard as well, but noisy.  I think this Apex 3 is superior in feel and typeability.  I have never used the wrist rest before on any keyboards due to my very large hands, but this time I gave it a go, and it really improved the overall feel through my wrists.  I am now a believer in the hard smooth angled wrist restsOne thing I really like about this keyboard is that you can get the white LEDs pretty bright so that I can program without overhead lighting and never not see the keys - it is bright enough and it looks legit while being bright.  I am too old for the RGB effects, just give me bright white keys!On my Apex 5, I wore the keys to a high shine and it still hasn't missed a beat.  Steel series knows how to put out a extremely useable, high quality product every time.  I have had virtually all the big names keyboards and they all have their charms, but for reliability and quality, none has surpassed this manufacturer in my experience, although some have equaled it.From a dollars and cents standpoint - this is a excellent value!

features: 【TFT Screen: The Interactive Interface】AK820 Pro mechanical keyboard comes equipped with a TFT Screen, serving as your interactive interface for real-time updates and customization. The high-definition display allows for customizable visuals, battery status, date & time display, connectivity & OS display, and backlight effects. With this TFT Screen feature breakdown, it’s easily to understand the full range of its capabilities.

【A Popular 75% Compact Design】Designed for both enthusiasts and professionals alike, the Ajazz AK820 Pro offers a combination of innovation and craftsmanship that's hard to beat. This 75% compact mechanical keyboard maximize your desk space and enjoy a sleek look with this 75% layout. It's also perfectly portable, allowing for seamless typing experiences, delivering a superior typing experience without compromising on features or functionality, wherever you are.

【Wireless & Wired Connectivity】The Ajazz AK820 Pro supports connection via BT or 2.4GHz for wireless connectivity, or with the included Type-C USB cable. With BT 5.1, the keyboard responses faster and save more power than the former BT versions. The keyboard is also easily switched among the three modes for efficient multitasking and speedy performance. Included 4000mAh battery ensures a long and steady use, without worries of short out.

【Gasket-mounted & Flex-cut PC Plate and PCB】Experience a typing feel like never before with our gasket-mounted design coupled with a Flex-cut PC plate and PCB. The gasket mounting method isolates the plate and PCB from the case, significantly reducing vibration and noise. In the meanwhile, the Flex-cut design in both the PC plate and PCB allows for a slightly flexy, yet stable typing experience. Every keypress is both cushioned and precise.

【South-facing LEDs with 1.6M RGB】Illuminate your setup with the Ajazz AK820 Pro's vibrant LED backlighting, featuring South-facing LEDs that offer superior shine-through capabilities. With a staggering 1.6 million color combinations, you can customize your RGB lighting profiles to suit your mood, occasion, or overall aesthetic.

【Mac/Win Compatibility】What's more, the keyboard is fully compatible with both Mac and Windows operating systems, ensuring that you can enjoy the full range of its features irrespective of your computing preferences. With the customizable TFT screen, you can easily switch between Win and Mac modes, enhancing your overall usability and productivity.

1.6 Million RGB Backlight 
How to Toggle the RGB Backlit 

The Ajazz AK820 Pro Wireless Gaming Keyboard is equipped with customizable RGB backlighting. Not only can you switch existing lighting effects with shortcut keys. It also allows the user to personalize the keyboard via the driver., and create a captivating gaming atmosphere. The vibrant lighting effects can be easily adjusted to match your preferences and add an extra touch of style to your gaming station. 
Tips: FN+X = Turn on/off backlight, FN+\| = Toggle the backlight effect 
2-in-1 Multifunction Knob 
Multimedia + Backlight Settings 

Equipped with a TFT smart display and knob, this keyboard allows you to conveniently access and control various functions. The smart display provides information such as battery status, connectivity mode, and more, while the knob enables quick adjustments to volume levels or lighting effects. 
Tips: FN+Knob = Enter the setting page, the knob controls the left and right direction, press the knob to confirm 
Pre-lubricated Linear Switches 
Ajazz Gift Switch + Ajazz Flying Fish Switch 

Featuring a unique gasket-mounted construction, this keyboard ensures optimal typing comfort and reduced noise levels. The 5-pin mechanical switches offer a satisfying tactile feel and quick response, making every keystroke smooth and precise. You can choose between the Ajazz Gift Switch or the Ajazz Flying Fish Switch, both of which provide excellent durability and a distinct typing experience. 
Tips: The keyboard supports 3/5-pin mechanical switches. Users can change it according to their needs

Is this keyboard hot swap with 5 pins? 
The switches used in this keyboard are 3-pin. But the keyboard's hot swap socket supports 5-pin mechanical switches. 
Is there any way I am able to customize the RGB settings without using a Windows computer? 
You can use the keyboard screen to operate the mode change of RGB lights. If you need to use macro editing software, you need to use Windows system. 
Can you remap the keys? 
Yes, the driver allows you to map keys, record macros, set keyboard backlighting and load GIF images for the screen.
