productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Pleasantly surprising quality for the price, get the Gift switch version! Great Sound and Value!Pleasantly surprising quality for the price, get the Gift switch version! Great Sound and Value!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Honestly I'm quite pleasantly surprised with the board. Definitely get the Gift Switch version and not the Flying Fish version, at least if your preference is a slightly better feel than barely touching the key to make it immediately bottom out. The Gift switch isn't too much heavier to initially press down, but it has a stronger resistance to being pressed all the way down, and the initial difference at least for me personally is definitely my preference. If you want a super light switch though, the Flying Fish version may be for you, I just found I kept accidentally pressing keys I didn't mean to, but have a much more enjoyable experience on the Gift switch version!The overall typing experience and feel is really solid, one of the best sounding keyboards and over all feel I've ever personally typed on. This is especially considering my previous keyboard that wasn't integrated into my device I owned was I believe a corsair k70 or something similar from 5 or more years ago that was probably worse build quality and definitely lacked any sort of upgradability without needing to de-solder every switch, among other things that are just way too much hassle and when the idea of modding keyboards was way relatively novel.This board, is definitely unapologetically plastic, but for being all plastic, there really is not all that much give. It has pretty much every modern feature you'd be looking for:- Solid quality keycaps and material (at least in terms of sound and feel, how they hold up after a lot of use will need further use)- A gasket mount which makes the overall typing experience feel a little softer.- A really nice typing sound and feel, probably aided by some extra layers of foam and or other things in the board that's way more technical know-how than I can describe, point is, without modding at all, sound and feel are really nice!- South facing LEDs for less risk of clearance issues modding in the future, particularly certain keycap profiles (OEM, XDA just a few examples).- Hotswappable switches! If a key switch were to wear out and or you wanted to change the switches out for ones that feel different to type on, you can do so without needing to solder the switches, it's simply much more beginner friendly.- A Knob for easy access volume control!- A Software that admittable is kind of, not fantastic (and kind of difficult to actually find, I just recommend the v1.0 on epomaker's site) but allows you to change the lighting modes and stuff a little bit easier than following through the manuals fn + (various key presses) for different effects, as well as I believe change some keybinds on the keys. If you are having issues getting it to allow you to change things on the keyboard, note that it has to be specifically plugged in via usb and not a wireless connection with the included dongle or bluetooth.- A Screen on the keyboard that can display gifs though I haven't specifically set that up myself since it's just not that important to me. A genuinely let down on the screen is that you can adjust it to be your computer's date and time via the software, but it is not at all really customizable beyond just the gif option. It's stuck using the 24hr clock instead of am/pm, and at least I don't believe you can change it. If learn otherwise I'll update this review!- USB C to A, Bluetooth, and 2.4g Dongle connectivity that at least testing specifically via 2.4g dongle, has no real world latency difference in terms of feel wireless vs wired!- RGB! The colors are pretty solid, a fair bit of decent customization options, but nothing really to write home about, definitely less customization compared to a Razer or Corsair keyboard, but enough that in general for most people, probably won't really matter especially if you stick it to one solid color. A couple downsides to the RGB is that if you have caps lock or windows lock, or are charging, there's a bright LED that definitely kind of bleeds into the other LEDs around them which can lessen the overall look, especially since I don't believe you can change those LEDs specifically.For what it is, it's a very solid board that I can definitely see myself potentially doing a little bit of light modding with over time as I get a little more into the custom keyboard hobby. Given my experience with it, it's feels like a very nice starting point to learn what I like in terms of feel and to be able to change and adapt it easily over time! It's definitely not perfect, but it's quite a huge value even over a board that's probably $20 cheaper, this is definitely worth it for the over all value proposition, unless you're gonna start looking at more around $100 boards.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Possibly the best keyboard I will ever own
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I can’t even put into words how much I love this keyboard. The keys feel like good quality material and respond quickly. If you are looking for a full customizable keyboard, then I recommend buying this A.S.A.P.. It has 19 different lighting modes and tons of colors. There’s even an app that you can use to customize it all. You even import your own GIF! The keyboard also comes with tools to take off the keycaps and switches if you want to put on different ones. The sound of the keys is my favorite part. They’re just the right volume and have a creamy sound to them. There is also a mode for Bluetooth if you want to use it without a cord in the way and it has a great battery life. The keyboard is heavier than I thought, but I kind of like that about it. It even has kickstands at the bottom to elevate the keyboard up; which is great for people that are pretty tall. Lastly, the price. I bought this while it was on sale, so it was around $55; which I felt at first was expensive, but the $55 was 100% worth it. Especially since the quality and customization is just top tier. If your okay with dropping a good amount of money for a keyboard and are looking for the best quality, I highly recommend.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: This keyboard is amazing, requires a little set up time.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: CONS-I would like to start off with the bad news first and say that I ordered this keyboard as a new product but when it arrived, it came in an old keyboard box. The keyboard itself appeared to be in relative new condition though, so maybe just recycled and reused an old box, (Not a huge issue and actually good for environment). When I plugged in the keyboard, the screen was by default in Chinese and though it was not a huge issue trying to change it from Chinese to English. The software for the keyboard was the same way and defaulted to Chinese as the main language. Not a big deal, once again just a simple switch. The instruction manual also defaults to Chinese first (not a big deal, just flip to the end of the book for English). But I will say that for international buyers maybe they should have changed to English as default for the keyboard. The software needs to be cleaned up and updated, as well as the website; (it looks like one of those scam websites and malware/virus software).PROS-This keyboard is actually very good. I having been using mechanical keyboards for over 10 years (Red Switches & Blue switches) and I though I'm not an expert in custom keyboards and all the different switches. This keyboard is definitely a very good one. I really like the type of sound it makes when I'm typing on it; similar to popping bubble wrap maybe? With to the red switches on this keyboard, if I wanted to be more silent about the sound I can still type without depressing the keys all the way down. This keyboard also comes with a screen on it and generally around this price point there aren't many keyboards that come with a screen. The screen is customizable with the keyboard software, though I will agree with many others that it did take some research and the software UI is not the best. It still works and looks pretty cool.

And supports 10 cool music rhythm lighting effects with driver. Lighting brightness and speed can be adjusted by the knob or the FN and key combination. N key rollover, and supports WIN key lock to prevent accidental touches in intense games

Multi-function Control Knob: This AULA 75% wireless gaming keyboard is equipped with functional knob to switch gaming mode or office mode. In gaming mode, you can rotate the knob to adjust the brightness of the lights, and click the knob to switch the lighting effects easily; in office mode, rotate the knob to adjust the volume, and click the knob to play or pause. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: AULA F75 Review Glacial Blue Reaper SwitchesAULA F75 Review Glacial Blue Reaper Switches
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been using the AULA F75 keyboard as my main keyboard, and it has been a great upgrade from my previous one, especially considering the price. I mainly use it wired, but I also tested the Bluetooth connection and it worked perfectly fine with no issues. The overall connectivity has been excellent, and I haven’t had any problems using it with my games.The RGB lighting looks really nice and adds a lot to the keyboard’s overall appearance. I do wish there were more RGB customization options and selections available, but the included effects are still enjoyable and look great.The Reaper switches feel and sound amazing. In person, the keys have a really creamy sound profile, while in videos they seem to come across as a bit more thocky. The typing experience feels smooth, satisfying, and enjoyable.The multifunction knob is one of my favorite features. I mainly use it for controlling volume, and having quick access without needing keyboard shortcuts is extremely convenient. It’s a small addition, but it makes everyday use much easier.For gaming, this keyboard has been great for me. Everyone has different preferences when it comes to switches and keyboard feel, but personally, I really enjoy using it while gaming. The responsiveness, comfort, and connectivity have all been solid.Overall, the AULA F75 is an excellent upgrade at its price point. I’m very happy with it so far, and I’m definitely interested in trying out other versions of this keyboard in the future. For now, this has been a fantastic choice, and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a quality mechanical keyboard without spending a lot.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This keyboard has a great feel right out of the box. The pre-lubed switches provide a smooth, satisfying keypress, and the sound is pleasant without being excessively loud.The 75% layout is a great balance between compact size and functionality. It keeps the important navigation and arrow keys while taking up considerably less desk space than a full-size keyboard. The wireless connectivity is also convenient and makes for a cleaner setup.The hot-swappable design is a major plus for anyone who enjoys customizing their keyboard. Being able to change switches without soldering gives you plenty of options to personalize the typing experience later.The keys feel responsive and consistent, whether I'm typing or gaming. The overall construction also feels solid, especially for the price.Overall, this is an excellent mechanical keyboard with a smooth typing experience, useful wireless functionality, and plenty of customization potential.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is the first mechanical keyboard that i got and i absolutely love it. It definitely makes the typing experience more relaxing - the keys have the perfect creamy think to it. If you type really fast it sounds like pebbles in the creek ^.^I did some research before getting a keyboard since i wanted something of a good quality but was prepared to drop $100+ on it. Very pleased with the quality of t his one - it feels very sturdy, the keys have just enough resistance to effortless typing.With the knob you can switch different color modes and adjust the brightness or control volume.It also allows pairing with 3 devices (and switch with a brass of a button, well, 2 buttons but u get it) via Bluetooth and it’s very convenient since i can use it with my computer, iPad and steam deck.I use Mac book and the translation from cmd , option and, control buttons are a bit confusing since the keyboard is for windows, but once you get used to it it’s ok.All my friends without mechanical keyboards now want one and all my friends with one approved the buy =DDOh, and I obviously replaced the keycaps - now the light mode really looks magical.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is the best sounding keyboard I have ever laid my hands upon. The sound of the keys are so satisfying, and they make typing such a fun experience. I also love the colors, and the multiple RGB light mods. There was some discussion on the risk of downloading the software since some said that it had malware, but I ran the download file through a scanner and there was no problem. I haven't had many chances to test the bluetooth connectivity, but so far, the keyboard connects smoothly and quickly to my devices. One reason why I bought this keyboard was its size, and I was not dissapointed! It is the PERFECT size, not too small and not too big. I'd give this four and a half stars if I could, because I only have some minor issues. The battery indicator light keeps flashing, and I tried to figure out how to make it stop but I don't think that's possible. To most people, this wouldn't be an issue, but personally, I found this really annoying. I ended up taping over the indicator because it was really bothersome. Another thing is that when you put the keyboard in office mode, you can't control the lights with the knob anymore. The only way you can change it is by simulatenously pressing on fn + \ but it can be hard to change it that way since you have to time it, so that the keyboard actually registers that you're clicking both keys at the same time. It's a little annoying but I suppose I could just only use the knob for that.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great quality and value, like the design and feel. Good company
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this on a big sale, like half off cyber day or something, and it’s been a really great value. I’ve been missing mechanical keyboards for decades lol and as soon as I had a lot of typing to do, I was like oh now’s my excuse hehe.  This one didn’t disappoint, even tho i wasn’t even sure what kind exactly I ought to get, since it’s been so long since I’ve used any!  Did a little research, got the red switches, cos I don’t want it TOO loud or clacky, I type very fast, don’t need to press down hard all the way with each stroke, so this one sounded right.  Well it’s great! I type much more accurately again, now that I’m using a proper keyboard and not those bs flat macbook integrated key pads lol.  This is a dream by comparison.  I like that it lights up and I can change the style or turn that off.  And it comes with extra switches and keys too! So this should last me forever. I got a mouse from the same company that goes with it well too. I like the colors too, and I’m VERY particular about subtleties in color combinations as an artist haha. It’s got a nice retro, kinda gamey look, which as a millennial I’m a sucker for. Tho I don’t actually game so I can’t comment on that for this, at least not since the 90s when I was playing Super Nintendo with my brothers!I had a bit of issue with the mouse I received, and the company reached out right away to refund or replace! So service seems to match the quality of product. I’ll def look to them next time I need any other devices in this category.  I did also get a wrist rest to go with it, i think that is extra needed for these kinds of keyboards, since they’re raised a bit more than those flat membrane style ones. Don’t want to get chronic wrist or finger joint issues, that can also cause or worsen arthritis (my uncle just had surgery for exactly this) so I def recommend getting ones for mouse and keyboard that feel right for you. So nice when you finally get a great quality product again, for once! (I waited like almost a year before I wrote this, just to be sure. Nothing more unhelpful than premature reviews lol).

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It's a new love, but a strong love.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I will start by saying that I've used Red Dragon stuff before. Years and years ago I had one of their membrane keyboards and one of their gaming mice. They performed flawlessly in all the time I owned them but I eventually changed color scheme and wanted to branch out so I tried a different brand keyboard and a Corsair mouse. I don't recall the other brand keyboard, but it had an aluminum body and was fairly nice. Over the years though I was constantly swapping switches out and then the LEDs started to die off, and it just reached the end of its life cycle really.I came back to Red Dragon because I wanted a nice mechanical keyboard but I think the boards that cost $100+ are, frankly, silly. I did debate between this keyboard and some of the other "off brand" boards but this one had great reviews and I love love love the kind of old school style to it.I am so glad I went with this keyboard. The design is freaking gorgeous. It's like a retromod done to an old IBM keyboard. The lights are certainly pretty, but I'm a basic fella so I already switched them over to solid white. They look great, and the light shines through the keycaps perfectly. There is also a sleek little light bar on the side of the board that I didn't notice in the pictures but looks super classy. Speaking of keycaps, THEY GIVE YOU AN ENTIRE SET! So if you don't like the color scheme that it comes with (as pictured) you can feel free to swap them out. They also give you some new switches for when these ones start dying off, I believe they give 8 of them, along with the tool to swap the switch and the keycap.On to the switches... Ohhhhhhhhh, boy they are GOOD. I cannot speak to longevity yet, and I will update when the first switch dies and I have to replace it, but initial impressions are so good it is unreal what this board costs. The feel is excellent, but the sound is where it's really at. A nice, somewhat loud but muted thunk with each press.The board itself is all plastic, but don't let that dissuade you, because it feels like a very high quality plastic. I think this board actually weighs more than the board it is replacing with the aluminum body, and they're both the same style board. The legs are double adjustable and move into place with a loud click.Honestly so far, I am absolutely blown away by this board. I hope it lasts a long, long time because I do not want to get rid of it any time soon.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on May 31, 2024

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My old wireless keyboard died so I figured it was time to get a new one and I decided to go with a wired one this time. The reviews seemed good on this keyboard and the price wasn't outlandish so I figured I'd give it a shot.The first thing that sticks out is the weight. It's sturdy and feels very well built, not like a cheap Chinese knock-off. The plastic all feels quality and the keys are smooth pressing motion. It's going to take me a bit of getting used to using a mechanical keyboard again after using a membrane keyboard for so many years, but I do like the clicking sound.Next you will notice this company does not cheap out on customer satisfaction. I bought this keyboard expecting only a keyboard. Instead I found a complete second set of keys, extra pieces to replace the mechanical part underneath the key, and a key puller tool as well. Completely unexpected but something that will automatically endear this companies customers to them.Lastly, the keyboard functionality itself. It is RGB and if you like having an RGB setup then you'll love the look of the white keyboard with the colors underneath. There is a button native on the keyboard itself that lets you change the RGB preset as well. I haven't fully counted but there seems to be around 10 presets with everything from colors slowly moving across the keyboard to zig-zagging back and forth, and if you don't like RGB there's an option to turn it off as well. The last nice bit is that in the very top right above the num-lock button row there are 4 additional keys: Mute on/off, a calculator button that pulls up your calculator app, a screenlock button that works the same was as pushing win+L, and a homescreen button that will minimize all of your windows and take you back to your desktop.The keyboard is nice and spacious and feels great to use so far. Especially for the price, this is the keyboard to get imo.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: For much too long I had been using the cheap flat keyboards that came with my last two (yes, 2) PCs. After almost a year of frustration with the latest HP keyboard, which lacked certain keys I used frequently and had keys I never used, not to mention the microscopic function keys, I started shopping. What I really wanted was a good solid keyboard like I had with my first three desktop computers. This one delivers and then some. It never occurred to me to get a keyboard that also puts on a light show!Several similar keyboards popped up in my browsing, but the look of this one stood out to me. Maybe it was the terracotta space bar. So I ordered it. I couldn't be happier! The keys have a nice solid feel to them and they bounce back without sticking. They're not quite as close together as the cheap-o keyboards had them so I'm making fewer typos.In addition to the classic 104 key configuration, there are an extra four keys that can do whatever you want. It took me a couple weeks to find the software to make them do that, though. The microscopic manual was no help in this regard. It mostly dealt with lighting effects, if you can read it at all. I needed a magnifying glass in addition to my reading glasses. Anyway, I poked through the Redragon website and waded through a few pages of models to find software for mine and I was in business. (I had previously done a search for this model number's software and it came up with no results.) That was the only challenge I had with this product. Once the software was installed I had my custom keys set just the way I wanted them in a few minutes.Speaking of keys, this keyboard has two complete sets. I'm torn as it whether this is useful or wasteful. I guess two things can be true at the same time. You can make all of them white (except the space bar) or all of them black (including the spacebar) or any combination thereof. A tool is provided to pop them out as needed. Just one caveat here. The second set of keys do not have the secondary function icons printed on them as the first set has. That might be a problem for some folks.Of course, I love the colorful backlighting! I prefer the two steady-state modes, one a rainbow effect and the other has random colors for each key. Or you can choose one of several colors for a uniform look. To change the color pattern press the FN key followed by INS to toggle amongst the different motion effects. Or you can press FN>DEL and change the color of the effect you're currently on. Press FN and either the up or down arrow keys to adjust the brightness. Similarly, FN with the left or right arrow keys controls the speed of the motion effects. I wish the slowest speed was a lot slower to keep the motion from confusing my eyeballs while I type. If you don't want the keys to be backlit, you can always turn them off completely by pressing FN>Spacebar, or turn them back on again the same way. The white keys are just as easy to read with the lights on or off. The black keys are less clear when dark, but still readable.Fun, functional, and solid construction make this the best keyboard I've ever had.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Really Loving this Keyboard -  Gemini Eclipse Option
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First I want to say that I got the Gemini Eclipse Option. So this is for that specific out of the box keyboard I got. Sometimes there are reviews that are different options all in one spot. I will also say that I got this on sale at 32 dollars, so I am reviewing it at the mindset of that price. With all that being said I really like this keyboard. I use it wired for home gaming pc, and plan to have my office set up around the monitor set up and be able to easily swap between main pc, and work laptop. So far, so good I would say and extremely happy.I did not download the software for the keyboard, and I realllllllllyyyyyy like that I can just plug it in, and have it usable as a keyboard without having to download all the bloated software that other companies have you download. It doesn't even try to prompt you or anything, I love it.The keyboard feels amazing. It has very solid typing, and its quite. It does not have that switch mechanical feel, but you it looks like you can change those out if you want to switch it up. The keys are slightly slimer, but as someone with slightly bigger hands, it still feels fine to type with and not congested, but I think that is also something you can swap out too if you wanted something different, its just this out of the box keyboard.I like that they utilized the space in the top right for the additional media keys and moved the traditional caps lock , and other locks, panel to the middle of the keyboard. It's easier to see, and it gives more function to the keyboard itself. There are also still the traditional function combos, but I am a simpleton/lazy, and like only having to push 1 button for certain things I use a lot.I haven't tried the Bluetooth or 2.4 dongle too much yet, so I can't give proper feedback on how they work, but will update.This thing a little weight to it, which makes me feel like it's more durable, strong, and not cheaply made. If I had something to cover they keys, I could see this being a good portable keyboard, but I don't plan on using this portably.What really got me get on here and write a review though was what it came with, again, I am speaking specifically to Gemini Eclipse Option. It came with the cord for the keyboard(usb-c to usb), A key removing device, a cool well made set of stickers(when I say well made I mean like old school thicker almost vinyly feel and thickness), and my biggest surprise, because I didn't the full title, a whole set of other keys! Pleasant surprise right. The second color set that I received, didn't have the option to pick(okay with me), are blue keys in the middle and white keys on the outside. Its basically the inverse color of this pattern, but replacing the pink, or w.e. the color is, the spacebar and ESC key, with the regular blue. I thought that was a pretty cool thing to do to allow you to start customizing off the start, and would help people, or kids, into learning how to customize keyboards out of the box. I did get this keyboard on sale at $32 which was around the price point of similar keyboards, which I went back to check, didn't come with a second set of keys.Overall, super happy with the keyboard, I have it survives the test of time, and doesn't fall victim to my inability to not spill my drink. Thank you for the great product!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent for the priceExcellent for the price
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I picked this up for fifty dollars, and at that price it's a fantastic value. If you're looking for a backup board or just a board to build and tinker with, this is a great option. And the spare set of keycaps is a good bonus--no idea why the product page didn't even mention them, since it's actually a pretty big deal. If you're looking for an entry board to get into moddable mechanical keyboards, though, you'll want to be aware of the issues with this particular board before picking it up.The switches I used:Main - Chosfox Arctic Fox (light blue base, white stem).Space/Enter - Kailh Box Crystal PinkMisc - Kailh Box Crystal JadeKeys I really don't want to press accidentally - Kailh Box Crystal NavyI also swapped the keycaps to some dye-sublimated PBT caps I bought elsewhere. Just to be clear, the pictures of the assembled board are NOT showing the spare keycaps. The spares were blue and white, and I took a separate picture of those.Things I like:- Price, obviously.- Hot swappable and has 5-pin sockets.- 108 key- Came with a whole extra set of keycaps. At this price, and especially for a 108 board, that's basically unheard of.Things I don't like:- Stock switches break easily (see Other Thoughts below for detail)- No software for Linux and no VIA/QMK support as far as I could find.- The cable that comes with it has a very large USB A connector, which looks bad and takes up a lot of space. I just used a better A-to-C cable that came with another Redragon keyboard.- The manual is minimalist (whatever, cheap board), but it has a placeholder Prop65 warning, which is, uh... not great. See picture. Not sure if this is just part of a document template that should have been removed because there are no applicable substances, or if there ARE applicable substances and they just didn't report them properly.Other thoughts:1. LEDs are north-facing. This works fine for double-shot keys with the legend on top, but if the legend is on the side facing you the light doesn't really come through. For boards with a bezel/recessed plate I prefer south-facing LEDs for this reason.2. There is no foam in the interior of the board. It's just a PCB in a plastic housing, with a thick foam overlay separating the PCB from the bezel/mounting plate. If you're looking for "thock" you'll definitely need to mod this. I'm a monstrous philistine who loves clicky switches, so this was actually better for me. I take the foam out of my keyboards if they have it.3. Pulling the stock switches might break them. I had to really pull and wiggle, and it bent the top housing of the switches and broke the retention pins on the bottom housing. I swap switches all the time in my other boards and I've never had this kind of problem before. The new switches I put in have polycarbonate bases and I can pull them out just fine. The box included a lot of extra switches, so I'm guessing this is a known problem. If you're looking for your first customizable mechanical keyboard maybe spend a little more for something else. Or at least have replacement switches in-hand before you pull the stock ones.4. The +4 keys in the top right are: Mute, Calculator, Lock, and Desktop. The first two are standard XF86 codes, but Lock sends left_meta+l and Desktop sends left_meta+d. I wanted these to be volume down/up, but as far as I'm aware there is no built-in way to modify what these keys send (there is software for Windows, but I don't use Windows). Luckily I didn't have any shortcuts that used d or l, so I was able to just add those as bindings in my Hyprland config and use them how I wanted to, but if you're not on Windows and already have left_meta+d or left_meta+l bound you may not be able to use those keys without plugging it into a Windows system or doing USB passthrough to a Windows VM to run the configuration tool.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great feel. Great sound. Not so great durability (so far)
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I like it. Lets get that out of the way first. It has a great mechanical feel to it without being loudly obnoxious. A light clicking as expected makes this a fun keyboard to type on. It looks cool with the various colors on the keyboard (it actually ships with a whole keyboard replacement of keys). The RGB colors are pretty cool too, but still figuring out how to control them. I will get there! Overall a great feel and fun to use.Now the not-so-good. I am still having trouble getting a good feel for my wrists after switching from the Logitech MX (still an AWESOME keyboard). This keyboard has a higher profile so it probably needs some more adjusting. It is only connected via USB-C so no wireless. I am ok with that and the provided cable is more than long enough to get you connected. I bumped a key (the PRTSC) while adjusting the keyboard. It popped off. It was broken. Way too easily. I was able to pop off (hot swap) the broken piece but the key itself seemed ok. The problem is the pin that holds the key broke and is stuck inside the key, making the key pretty much worthless. So a couple days in and an unusable key (thank goodness for the replacement part).Overall I like it, but it could be a bit more solid. I have a Logitech MX mechanical at home that I love. But the price is about $110 more for that keyboard.

1. Where is the USB receiver, and do the keyboard and mouse need separate ones? 
Both devices share one single USB receiver to save your computer ports. It is located inside the battery compartment on the bottom of the mouse. 
If you cannot find it or have any setup issues, please call our staff immediately. 
2. Are batteries included in the package, and what are the specific battery requirements? 
Batteries are not included. The keyboard requires 2 AAA batteries, and the mouse requires 1 AA battery. 
The package includes: 1 keyboard, 1 mouse, 1 USB receiver, 1 Type-C adapter, 1 wrist rest, and 1 instruction manual. 
3. Does this typewriter-style keyboard and mouse set work with MacBooks? 
This set works best with Windows. While standard typing works great on a Mac using the included adapter, the top shortcut keys (F1-F12) do not fully work with Mac systems. 
If you need any assistance with connection, our support is always here. 
4. Is this typewriter keyboard very loud when typing? 
It makes a standard, comfortable typing sound and does not have the loud, sharp clicking of a mechanical keyboard. While it is not completely silent, the sound level is normal and great for a regular office space. 
5. What should I do if the keyboard or mouse stops responding after a break? 
To save battery, both devices go into a sleep mode after 30 minutes of no use. Simply double-click any key or mouse button to wake them up instantly.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It Works Great, Soft Keys Sound, Quiet Mouse, and Very Easy to Type On!!!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It was just delivered today and it was very easy to add the batteries to the keyboard and the mouse.  Connection to our MAC desktop computer was also easy.  I am using it right now to type this review.  The baby pink color is beautiful and the keys are very easy to type on.  The mouse works great, too. The keys don't stick in any way and I can really get some speed on them, haha!  :-)  The mouse buttons are very quiet and so are the keyboard keys and spacebar.  This is very, very nice.  The little stick-on charms are cute, too, consisting of a carrot, a flower, a sleepy little blue star, a fried egg, and a pink smiley face with a green bow.  The only thing I noticed that isn't working, unless I'm mistaken, is that when I press the "Num Lock" button, the #1 on the top right section of the keyboard does NOT light up as the manual states.  The manual states that it will light up "green" when the "Num Lock" button is activated.  So far, no light at all, but I can live with that as long as everything else works fine.  This is a very nice and very soft sounding keyboard.  It's worth the price!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this keyboard for the looks and back lighting, I misread the description and thought this was both plug-in and bluetooth connectible, but its not, its plug in only, not a big deal just that it does need to occupy a USB-C/A port on your laptop if that's what you're planning to use it with.I also felt like I was a little bit mislead because the item name states that its for Windows/MAC/PC, but then in the item description/details it says its not compatible with Mac/iOS? lol not sure what that means. I received the item nicely packaged, plugged the drive into my 2024 M3 Macbook Air and both the keyboard and mouse was instantly connected. I was able to figure out how to configure the keyboard settings as a Mac keyboard, simple function + W keys did the trick, so far the keyboard and mouse has had zero connectivity issues, both are very responsive despite going to sleep after a couple of minutes, the lighting colors and brightness are adjustable on the keyboard, overall super cute. Have not used it long enough to test the battery life, but since its rechargeable, I'm assuming it should be fairly convenient even if it doesnt last too long.The only down side is, it doesn't have buttons on the keyboard to control the volume, it does have buttons for the brightness of both the screen and keyboard. The mouse has buttons on the bottom to change lighting/DPI, cannot adjust light brightness on the mouse. Keyboard and mouse itself are both pretty lightweight, easy to carry around if needed. Decent purchase so far for the price.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Reliable, Comfortable, and Great Value Wireless Keyboard
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Logitech K250 Bluetooth Keyboard has been an excellent addition to my workspace. Setup was quick and effortless, and it connected to both my Windows PC and Mac without any issues. The Bluetooth connection has been stable and responsive, making it easy to switch between tasks without worrying about lag or dropped connections.One of the things I appreciate most is the compact design. Despite having a full numpad, the keyboard doesn’t take up excessive desk space, making it a great option for home offices, workstations, and smaller setups. The keys are comfortable to type on and provide a pleasant typing experience, whether I’m working on documents, spreadsheets, or everyday browsing.The build quality is impressive for the price. It feels sturdy without being heavy, and I like that it’s made with recycled plastic. The spill-resistant design provides additional peace of mind, especially in a busy workspace where coffee or water is often nearby.The included numpad is a huge benefit for anyone who regularly works with numbers, budgets, or spreadsheets. Combined with the long-lasting wireless convenience, it makes daily productivity much more efficient.Considering the quality, comfort, Bluetooth connectivity, and Logitech’s reputation for reliability, this keyboard offers excellent value for the money. It’s a practical, well-designed keyboard that delivers exactly what most users need.Overall, I highly recommend the Logitech K250 to anyone looking for a dependable wireless keyboard that’s comfortable, compact, and affordable.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 5, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this keyboard after my last bluetooth one crapped out. I wasn't looking for anything fancy, and it's not. But it is comfortable, and I like the way the keys feel. Honestly, I even like the way it looks.The only downside is that one of the control buttons near the shift button will erase an entire sentence or two if it is accidently touched. That's annoying, but not enough for me to give it a four star.It's fairly quiet. I actually like the way it sounds.I use it every day, sometimes for a couple of hours. The batteries are going strong.I am glad I didn't go for a more expensive option. It doesn everything I want it to.It's compatible with my tablet and connects right away. I don't even have to reconnect it every time. I just start tapping the keys and it is ready to go fairly quickly.Over all, this is a great value for your money. I highly reccommend it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great keyboard. Small as it can be, while having full-size keys. Pleasure to type on.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This keyboard feels great in use. It's almost silent, and the keys feel cushioned and "luxurious" as you type. That probably sounds stupid, but compared to the flat keys on my laptop, this is a welcome change.The keyboard membrane on my 5-year-old laptop (Asus TUF Gaming F17) is going out, and the keys 7, Y, H, N, and M (right down the middle) are no longer reliable, and very frustrating sometimes. I bought this keyboard to sit on top of, and take the place of, the built-in keyboard and it works perfectly for that.I can get the replacement part for my laptop that contains the lower housing frame and new keyboard, but then I would have to transfer all the guts and the monitor to the new lower housing. I could probably do it with minimal cussing and have it actually work when I was done, but for $24 I decided to go this route, a Bluetooth keyboard in place of the built-in one. I don't ever move or carry the laptop, it just sits on the table in my shop, so this will work fine.Very satisfied with the quality, and as I said, it's a pleasure to type on, compared to the flat, no-travel keys on the built-in keyboard. One more Logitech product that I'm satisfied with. Logitech and Anker (the latter having nothing to do with this item). Two names in electronic accessories that haven't let me down. Yet. Let's hope they never do.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 31, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am writing this review from my iPad simply because my laptop is currently connected to this awful keyboard, rendering it frustratingly useless.It does connect easily but that’s the only positive.  Over and over again, this keyboard misses typed letters which results in large blanks.  The biggest and most headache-inducing issue is that it will randomly repeat a letter 10-30x in a row for no reason.  I spend more time hitting the backspace button than just about anything else.The function keys are also all over the map;  they sometimes work but most of the time the action taken is not correct or it is the action of the key next to it.I’ve tried everything, including slowing down the speed of the keyboard as was recommended on comment boards.  Nothing works.  Instead, the letters are just repeating very, very, very slowly and the constant backspacing is taking forever.Unfortunately the return window has passed, so this thing is going to gather dust in my office closet while I find a better keyboard that will do its job.Strongly recommend staying away from this.  Logitech used to be a great brand that I could trust so I’m terribly disappointed.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on March 4, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Feels cheap, but hard to complain at this priceFeels cheap, but hard to complain at this price
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This keyboard definitely looks and feels very budget, and the plastic construction makes that obvious right away. The whole board has a strong plastic feel, and if you twist it even a little bit, you can hear the frame making plastic creaking noises. It doesn’t exactly feel sturdy or premium.The key feel is also pretty mediocre. The keys feel a bit mushy and not very satisfying to type on. If you’re used to better keyboards or mechanical ones, the typing experience here will probably feel pretty underwhelming.That said, I can’t be too harsh on it. This is a very cheap keyboard, and for the price it does the basic job. It connects easily over Bluetooth with no lag, and it even comes with the AAA batteries included. So it’s still a decent value for a simple everyday keyboard. Four stars feels fair for what it is.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Super quiet, especially when I'm never going to use it.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'm trying the keyboard out for the first time on this review. The feels is dead as dead can be. I read that the keyboard was quiet in reviews, which it is to the credit of the reviewers I did read, but omitted from those reviews was a genuine lack of responsiveness. Typically keyboards have a break over point/force in the key throw that serves as tactile feedback to the person typing, and generally improves speed and the experience. This keyboard is a serious departure, and I can't imagine anyone who types a lot would be happy with this board. I don't type much, but bought this board because it was close on specs to another logitech keyboard I used for many years, the K360. After many years of service that board started glitching. The great thing about that board was its small footprint despite having a full number pad. Being an engineer, I use the number pad and really miss it was it isn't present. This board just about the same specs on paper, but it feels completely different. Other things where it falls short relative to the K360, no on/off slider and the arrow keys are jacked. The K360 is by no means a gaming keyboard, but this thing is on ludes. If you like mushy keys, have at it. I'm going to give it a shot. I'm old, but not stupid, or made of money, could warm up to it. As a back up I can imagine a scenario where i need it and batteries are dead. Its cheap, I'm cheap, what else is there to say. The K360 was cheap, felt great to type on and only needed batteries a small handful of times during it's service. Would love to just buy a new one of those.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Keep ample supply of batteries nearby
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: his keyboard does exactly what I needed it to do—stay quiet. No loud clack-clack echoing through calls, even on sensitive audio. It’s a solid choice if you’re working around microphones or just prefer a softer typing sound.Connectivity was easy, and it’s been reliable so far. The keys feel comfortable once you get into a rhythm.That said, the spacing is just slightly different from my previous keyboard—barely a millimeter or so—but it’s enough to throw you off at first. There’s definitely a short adjustment period before your fingers recalibrate. Also, it doesn't blow through batteries super fast, but I promise you'll want some spares handy because Murphy's Law dictates that you will be in the middle of something important when they go out!Overall, a dependable, low-noise keyboard that works well once you get used to the feel.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great, unique, and very bright keyboard
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was a little hesitant to purchase this keyboard after reading the reviews, especially considering the frequent mention of typing difficulty with the keys on the keyboard. I mean it looked great, but the whole purpose of a keyboard is typing on it and if it poses problems in that area, it could be a real deal-breaker.I went ahead and ordered it anyway because it just looked so cool. After receiving it, I plugged it in and, with a little trepidation, began typing on it. I found that getting accustomed to the keys was a very minor concern. In fact, I would not even consider it an issue at all. I think it caused me to hit another key in addition to the one I was typing once or twice; however, I’m not a great at keyboarding, so it could very well have been me. On the best keyboards, I use the backspace key quite frequently. At the same time, I have had training in using a keyboard and can type without the hunt and peck method. It helps that this keyboard also has a little raised line on the F and J keys so you can get the correct hand placement without looking. I think the thing that throws people off is not the size of the keys as much as the feel. Because they are circular, with a raised edge around the outside of the key, they feel different underneath your fingers, so it takes a little getting used to in that respect. It’s a bit of a distraction at first.It has a generous six feet of cord, which is usually ample for most setups. The cord also has a hook and loop strip which keeps the cord together when not in use. The cord is not braided, but it should hold up under regular use.The video for this keyboard was taken under very bright lighting and the RGB colors show very well. I purchased this for my work office, where I have bright lighting, so this was a big plus. Upon plugging in a second time, it remembered my RGB settings I had on it before it was unplugged.I read a lot of reviews that mention the audible click for the Cherry red mechanical keys. While certainly different than a non-mechanical keyboard, when I began typing on this keyboard, I really did not notice the sound until I was writing the review, and what had been said by other reviewers called my attention to it. The switches I have on my keyboard for my home computer are mechanical Cherry brown, and I did not notice a lot of difference in the loudness of the sound. In fact, for an office environment, even with others around, I don’t think it would be that much of an issue, unless of course a co-worker has misophonia, then any keyboard would probably be difficult for them to tolerate.Overall, I really like this keyboard. It is very bright and has a lot of onboard color options. There are a lot of RGB keyboards that can be had for cheaper, but as the saying goes, you get what you pay for, and in this instance, I am happy with what I had paid for. Not having disappointments is worth something in itself.ADDENDUMAfter further typing with this keyboard, I decided to amend my review. I still really like it, but there is a little getting used to the keyboard before one is comfortable with it.Since the space of the keys took up more space than the keyboard I replaced, on the vertical plane anyway, I figured that the size of the keys could not be the problem. If anything, they were spaced further apart than a regular keyboard. So, I began to think of other factors that might affect the feel of this keyboard.First, I tried folding a couple of pieces of paper and raising the wrist rest by about 1/8 of an inch. This seemed to help, but it still wasn't where I wanted to be. I finally got somewhere very close to perfect when I folded the attached wrist rest under the keyboard, took my 3/4-inch-high traditional wrist rest, set it about ½” inch to an inch from the keyboard, and put the feet on the top of the keyboard down so the top is elevated. That pretty much did the trick, though there will probably be a little tweaking I'll do along the way. It still takes a little getting used to; however, the change in hand positioning has made so much difference.After some experimentation, I believe that the awkward feel of the keyboard was not due to the size of the keys as some reviewers had said. In fact, as I mentioned, the keys took up more space on the keyboard than the keyboard I was using. If anything, the keys were spaced a little too far apart. I think this is because they are round and do not fit together like square keys.But, after doing some trying of different things, I think what I found was a way to successfully type with much less adjustment of style or a learning curve. For me, it has much more to do with my hand position in relation to the keyboard than the keyboard itself.Furthermore, I think the provided wrist rest is too low and too close to the keyboard for optimal functioning.So, for me, I think the best answer was to use a traditional wrist rest and have the back legs of the keyboard extended. That seemed to provide a more natural position for my hands in typing. With a little help from AutoCorrect, and the occasional gratuitous use of the backspace key, I was flying across the keyboard in no time.If you purchase this keyboard, which I would recommend, I encourage you to try some experimentation yourself and find what works best for you.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A solid deal on a solid keyboard with some limitations on the bells and whistles.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Strictly as a keyboard, five stars.  The sound and feel of each keyboard click is very satisfying, and the keys are responsive to the slightest press, but not so responsive that you can't rest your fingers on them.  It has the standard 108-key layout, plus four dedicated keys for volume up, down, and mute and calculator.  Additionally, the FN key and the top row of F keys are shortcuts for common features and functions.It gets a one-star ding, however, for the extended functionality.The lack of management software found in other keyboards of this type is the root of the problem.  The Fn+F-Key combos are un-modifiable (and unlabeled).  The method for changing the key colors is actually pretty easy, but there is a limited range of colors.  There's no ORANGE.That being said, however, the cost is about half of what I've paid for keyboards with that software, so... I'm happy with it.Also, while I did not at first like it, I now ADORE the fact that the num, scroll, and capslock keys are their own indicators, turning white when active.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: So Nice to Type on This!!So Nice to Type on This!!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I absolutely ADORE this KEYBOARD!!! 1st of all, I am not a gamer. I wanted a backlit keyboard so I could use my computer in low lighting 1st thing in the morning with my coffee and after the dinner dishes have been put away in the evening. I had been typing on an HP SmartCard CCID keyboard, which does have mechanical switches so I wasn't to worried about having to adjust to the sound or feel. Let me tell you, this Royal Kludge keyboard beats typing on my old kb by LIGHT years!! The keys have just the right amount of sensitivity, much easier to press to actuation than the old kb. I love the clickyness of this kb too. It has more of an almost "dual" click to it, much better sounding than the old kb. The round keys did not take getting used to as some of the other reviews on here claimed. For me, they are EASIER to type on, and spaced just enough so that they don't interfere with each other. I feel I can type faster on this, I guess because they are easier to press, really don't know. The lighting is really beautiful. I love all the different effects and brightness levels available. There were several reasons I chose this particular kb when I made the decision to treat myself to a backlit board. 1st, it had to be mechanical. 2nd, it had to have individually lit, dimmable multi-color keys. 3rd, it had to have a wrist rest. I know, you can buy your own stand alone wrist rest, but I felt like for the money these backlit boards with all the features I mentioned cost, it ought to have a WR. 4th, it had to be beautiful and fun. And finally, it had to come in at less than $75. This ticked all the boxes, but I was not prepared for what a joy it is to use this keyboard! I LOVE the steampunk vibe and retro look combined with the gorgeous lighting. I LOVE the ease of typing. I LOVE the sound!! The cord has a little velcro piece attached to gather any slack in, which was an added little bonus to me so I don't have to worry about my dog getting into the slack. The ONLY thing that could be improved on IMO is the wrist rest could have been padded. I'm all about comfort and ergonomics so I will most likely purchase a gel rest to use instead of the included plastic one. I will probably just remove the existing one altogether rather than keep it folded beneath. I will say that the kb is quite awkward to use with the wrist rest tucked beneath it, both sitting flat or with the legs extended for incline. Speaking of the legs, there are two different settings of incline which I found to be quite nice. I currently have mine on the steepest incline setting and it gives me great visualization of all the keys even though I don't need to see them, just for certain characters I don't use often. All in all, I am so pleased with my purchase. If you're still on the fence, just GET IT! You can always return it if it's not for you. :)Edit: I did purchase a pretty turquoise mf/gel wrist rest, came with a separate little one for the mouse. But instead of removing the attached plastic wr, I just place it in front of it. I don't tuck the attached wr under, but keep it extended and my padded rest butts up to it. I have long fingers so this setup works really will for me. Will add a pic.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Ok, firstly, I rarely write reviews. I had this in one of my lists for 2 years and it went on sale on Black Friday for $50 and decided to get it. I read all the negative reviews also and purchased it anyway (I'll follow up on those later).Let me start by saving I have never had a luxury keyboard or anything like that. I typically worked with stock or easily affordable keyboards and mice. So if you're like me, this review will  be most helpful to you. I cannot critique this from a high-end perspective because I am a plebian lolI love this keyboard. The response and tactile elements are very satisfying. The LEDs are beautiful and not distracting. There are a bunch of different color settings to equip (Fn + Del, Page up, Page down, Home, etc). To me everything about this keyboard is a win.There is a little learning curve as there is transitioning to any keyboard of a different size, however, there is a little more of a learning curve going from square keys to rounded keys (this took me 2-3 hours). From the moment I took this keyboard out of the box I knew it was going to be great.The keys are straight up ASMR and the push back on the keys is fantastic for the tactile sensation. Let be clear that this keyboard does make audible clicks and may be louder than what you're used to working on (for me I was working off of a laptop keyboard). I love that though and that's where the ASMR comes in.Also, I think different sides of the keyboard have different button click feels to me; which I love. This is the best keyboard I have ever owned and I am very much loving it for the price.Some of the one star reviews say there is fading on the keys after use and the silver key rings fall off. There is a 5 star reviewer (I believe) that put the Amazon link for replacement keys. A full set is under $20. For this keyboard, I have no problem buying the keys and doing that in the future if need be. To me that's absolutely worth it.Another reviewer said that the Volume +, Volume -, Mute, and Calc keys didn't correspond to the functions on the key itself, this has not been my experience. I am unsure what happened with their item but this is not something I've experienced. I also find the dedicated Calc Key fantastic because I will be using this keyboard for work and sometimes I do need to use the Calculator.A few one star reviews said the keys ghost or activate commands unprompted, this has not been my experience.I think one reviewer said there is no light for cap lock or the other locks. I can confirm that there is indeed a light but you don't see as well because everything is lit up, but there is definitely an extra light that comes on when cap lock and num lock is on. If this is very important to you, you can change to a less bright setting where that will stand out more (easy way to see it without doing this is looking at the key rim directly in-front of that key, or the key toward the right; it will reflect back a little off the rim).I can't speak toward longevity unfortunately, but from the way it feels and responds now and the quality of it's build, it doesn't feel like it's going to break on me, but, that remains to be seen in time. I did get the extra warranty with this just in case. Actually, particularly because of the 1 star reviews. I think 2 or 3 years was $8.It's a wonderful keyboard from my perspective and I would gladly buy it again. Hope this review was helpful to you!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I do not need a fancy keyboard with countless useless features.  I just want a good, durable keyboard that feels good to use, sounds nice, and will reliably work for years.  I have found that Logitech has been delivering on those expectation for year and continues to do so with this keyboard.My only gripe is that it is not compatible with their Unifying Recievers.  Bummer.  That means that I have to use an available USB port to connect this keyboard to my machine, rather than using the reciever I already have for my mouse.  I could have bought this in a kit with a mouse, but I like the mouse I have but the keyboard that it comes with is not so good.  I am having to mix and match.  That is on me.  It would be nice if Logitech stopped trying to outthink consumers and just made keyboards and mice all work with the same unifying receivers, but whatever.I wanted a simple keyboard.  This one is simple.  It is a step up from their K270 which is an office workhorse.  The biggest difference with this one is the palm rest.  If you are a lazy bum like me, you don't hold your wrists above the desk to type like you should have been taught in typing class.  No, your wrists are collapsed and resting on the desk, giving you carpal tunnel syndrome, sore palms, and arthritis.  With a palm rest, your wrists are slightly elevated, making the physical punishment of office work just a little bit less severe.Like all Logitech products, they have done a good job making a durable, reliable keyboard.  There is a good tactile feel.  The haptics have not been ignored, but they are not perfect.  Just fine at this price point.  The sound of the keyboard is ok.  Not a nice snappy click, but more of a hollow, plastic, tap.  Its fine.  It gets the job done, but in a quite office, it is far from silent and can sound a bit like a squirrel trying to get out of a lunchbox.Even though it might not seem like it, I am really happy with this keyboard.  I had to replace my K270 when my assistant dumped coffee into it.  I chose this one because it was basically the same but with the palm rest.  I like the palm rest.  Even though it is just hard plastic, it feels nice. It has a nice texture, no sharp edges, and it transitions nicely between the keyboard and the desk.  My typing speed is up from normal too.I recommend this keyboard if all you are looking for is a basic, but good keyboard.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been using the Redragon K719 Wireless Gasket Gaming Keyboard for a few months now, and I’ve been extremely happy with it. Right out of the box, the keyboard looked amazing, and the Jade Cloud color gives it a clean, premium appearance. The keys feel smooth to type on, and the sound is fantastic without needing any modifications.One of my favorite features is the TFT display. Setting a custom GIF was quick and easy using the software, and it adds a fun, personalized touch to my setup. The knob is also very convenient for adjusting volume and other functions, making the keyboard even more enjoyable to use every day.Overall, this keyboard offers incredible value for the price. The build quality is excellent, the typing experience is satisfying, and it looks fantastic on any desk. If you’re looking for a mechanical keyboard with great sound, useful features, and a premium feel right out of the box, I highly recommend the Redragon K719.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 18, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I originally bought this keyboard because of the listing photos. After placing my order, I noticed some reviews showing presumably older versions with opaque, Century Gothic-style keycaps that didn’t let the RGB shine through, which was disappointing. Thankfully, I believe Redragon has updated it, because mine came exactly as pictured with shine-through keycaps, and the lighting looks great.The software took a little digging to find since it seems to have been updated. The first version I found didn’t even have an English option, but I eventually located the correct one without too much trouble. The software itself is a bit clunky and definitely has some grammatical errors and misspellings, but it gets the job done.As for the keyboard itself, I absolutely love it. There are tons of RGB effects and personalized color customization options, as well as a few preset save slots. My favorite is the reactive lighting, but there are plenty of other effects to choose from. The multifunction knob works well with both turning and pressing, and the little GIF display is adorable. Setting up a custom GIF was surprisingly easy.Keys sound and feel fantastic.Overall, this keyboard exceeded my expectations. If you’re worried about receiving the older opaque keycaps shown in some reviews, it looks like Redragon may have updated them. For the price, I’m really happy with this purchase. I love it!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 18, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I love this keyboard! The keys sound nice and thocky, closer to a wooden sound than a metallic sound. The main reason I got this keyboard was due to the tri-mode connectivity! I work from home, and have my work laptop and my personal computer on the same desk. I was getting tired of switching from one keyboard to the other, and decided to look into a keyboard that could switch modes from USB to Wireless on two devices. This keyboard does just that, while sounding great, feeling amazing, and looking beautiful! Redragon always has the best keyboards at the mid tier price range, and I have been a loyal Redragon keyboard user for close to 8 years! The only thing that got me to upgrade from this keyboard was a Wooting 80HE, but I can't quantify how much I miss my tri-mode connectivity.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 20, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Way better than I expected, great entrance to mechanical keyboards.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I wanted to build my own keyboard, but wanted a small form with a number pad. the cheapest barebones kit that met that criteria was over $80, so I figured I'd give this a shot. I have never had/used a mechanical keyboard and didn't want to put a ton of money into it right away. I also didn't want a super loud click, I think those ones sound really annoying. I was very pleasantly surprised by the feel, quality, weight, and sound of this. I actually am able  to type faster on this than my old membrane keyboard. The RGB is way better than I was expecting, it's bright, has tons of modes, and the battery is surprisingly long with it on.Connectivity hasn't been an issue either, I have the usb dongle in my computer, and the bluetooth linked to my phone so I can quickly switch between them if I have a long text to send.My brother is a mechanical keyboard snob, and he was very surprised by how quality this felt and typed. The switches are smooth and quiet enough that I don't feel a need to change them, but I like that I have that option for so little cost.I think my only criticism is that I wish the keyboard was a little wider so that the 0 key in the numpad could be a full size. I still hit the right arrow button a lot when I'm using the numpad quickly. Overall it's not too big of a deal though.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 27, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Love this keyboard and the company!Love this keyboard and the company!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have had this keyboard for a couple of months now and I gotta say that it is so gorgeous! I get compliments on it all the time at work and I love bragging about it! The keyboard is made well, it is able to handle my incessant pounding and the sound is light enough to not bother my coworkers. The keys have a milky quality to them, so if you like a noisy keyboard this isn’t for you, but the layout and the larger than average lettering has made my typing speed so much better. I don’t often use it off the usb wire, but what I have seen indicates that it has a good amount of battery life. One of the keys came damaged and while the company was not able to get me a replacement, they did give me some credit back on the keyboard. Considering similar keyboards are in the $100+ range, this one is a good option for those wanting to either dip their toes into mechanical keyboards or budget-conscious folks.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Like most Redragon keyboards, a great product
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've got a few other keyboards of theirs, and absolutely love them.  I had tried the one that's like a typewriter with the rounded keys yesterday, but it just didn't type as well as their other ones and I had to return it to get this instead.This is much like a bluetooth version of the one on my Alienware gaming desktop, and it feels great.  Love the clicky keys, great key travel, very responsive.  LED options work well although I just leave it at the default wave one it does since I don't care what the patterns are, just that I can see the right keys at night as I work in the dark.Hopefully the battery will last as expected.  This was purchased to replace a junk Satechi SM3 keyboard that seemed OK at first and just got worse as time passed.  Had it now about 5 months and can't stand it anymore and the battery life is awful.  But since I've had no issues with quality on the other Redragon keyboards, I'm not expecting issues with this one.Unlike the other one I tried, this one has the power switch on the side, which I FAR prefer to how they normally put it on the bottom.  Not sure I have any real use for the LCD display but it's there.  I do appreciate the quick knob for volume though. But I'm disappointed that the pressing of the knob is how you engage the options for the LCD panel rather than muting the sound.Solidly built, has some heft to it, and does not feel even remotely cheap.The numeric keypad is the thing that lost the star though.  Crammed in as it is, missing the other keys, this has a tiny little key for the number zero, which is going to cause my touch typing all SORTS of issues over time...

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Sounds great, looks great, and overall very nice
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Keyboard was super easy to set up! Keys also sound amazing and I love the unique font and graphics that are on the keys. Being able to have a keyboard that looks custom for such a good price is awesome for someone like me who is new to PC gaming but loves aesthetics. The smaller screen is also super nice with showing the time and making it easy to adjust the RGB of the keyboard itself. I will note that I can't figure out how to change the date on the keyboard screen and it's set to one day ahead of the current date, but that's not a major issue and probably something I am just not figuring out yet. The volume control knob also works great and is a nice added convenience. Very happy with my purchase and will recommend this keyboard to others!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on May 5, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have owned several red dragon mechanical keyboards over the years, I love them for their high quality and low price, but this is by FAR my favorite keyboard so far. The keys are mint switches which I've never tried but I'll never not use again, they feel and sound absolutely amazing. When you're typing away you don't get that loud, audio spiking click like a red or blue switch, you get a solid low thud. It sounds like raindrops hitting a wood roof, you could easily sleep through it. The tactile sensation doesn't even suffer like having a membrane keyboard, it provides a nice balanced resistance force that thuds right when it bottoms out, something that's hard to describe the feel of. I cannot stand a numpad-less keyboard so the inclusion of this full sized numpad while keeping the overall size relatively small is phenomenal. The volume knob has a nice tactile feel as well. The little LCD screen is awesome, and surprisingly crisp at a low resolution thanks to its small size. A lot of keyboards have had monochrome screens in them but this one is full color and you can upload your own gifs to the app, which you'll need to download in order to customize the keys, RGB, and screen. I wish it had SignalRGB or openRGB support but unfortunately it does not. The frame is plastic, usually red dragon makes nice cheap metal frame keyboards, but it doesn't flex when you're typing on it so it's a pass for me. It can flex a little bit you need to be deliberately trying. This also makes it a little on the lighter side so it's easier to accidentally move.Note:-You might need to download the red dragon k719 software and update the firmware with it in order for the windows key (and some others) to work
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 21, 2025

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Teclado completo y original con pantalla integrada
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: He estado utilizando el teclado Redragon K719 PRO y me ha parecido un teclado muy completo tanto para gaming como para uso diario, el formato de 95 teclas tiene un buen equilibrio entre tamaño compacto y funcionalidad.La pantalla que tiene es uno de los detalles más interesantes, permite visualizar información útil y añade un toque diferente al teclado frente a modelos más tradicionales.La perilla de control facilita ajustar funciones rápidamente, como volumen u otros parámetros según la configuración, es un añadido práctico que mejora la experiencia de uso.El sistema de amortiguación de ruido ayuda a que la escritura resulte más suave y silenciosa, algo que se nota especialmente en sesiones largas frente al ordenador.Es un teclado bien construido, funcional y con extras poco habituales como la pantalla integrada.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This has got to be the best value keyboard out there. Everything I wanted in a keyboard, this has at about 1/2 or even 1/4 of the cost of most other keyboards. Buying this for so cheap I expected it to be made out of cheap plastic and be light and flexible, but this couldn't be further from the truth. It is even sturdier than the $200 corsair keyboard that I had previously. The keys are quiet which is a big reason I wanted a new keyboard and I admit they are ever so slightly mushy so those looking for a clicky keyboard, this is not the board for you. When I was buying this I expected it to be janky, however, everything works as advertised! There is no noticeable latency, connection is easy, and all functions work! I don't plan on installing the software to change the RGB as their are many patterns and colors to choose from that fit my needs built into the keyboard. Overall, I would recommend this keyboard to anyone and everyone unless you are looking for a loud and clicky keyboard!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The K673 is the keyboard I would recommend to anyone who wants to dip their toe into the mechanical keyboard waters.I've bought roughly 10-12 mechanical keyboards through Amazon and other outlets (e.g. Drop.com) over the past 10 years -- all of them reviewed as great values for their price point at the time they were released. AULA WIN60 HE Hall Effect Keyboard-The Perfect Blend of Precision and Durability 
What is the Hall Effect? 
The Hall Effect is a physical phenomenon that allows our keyboard, like the AULA WIN60 HE, to detect whether a key has been pressed by sensing changes in the position of a tiny magnet beneath each key, rather than relying on traditional mechanical contact. This means every keystroke can be recognized with exceptional precision, while also avoiding the wear and tear issues common to traditional switches over time. 
Why Choose the AULA WIN60 HE Hall Effect Keyboard? 
Unmatched Precision: With Hall Effect technology, the AULA WIN60 HE offers unparalleled accuracy, ensuring that every keystroke is registered correctly. It's perfect for gaming or tasks requiring rapid responses and fine control.
Extended Lifespan: Thanks to its innovative design without physical contact points, the AULA WIN60 HE is virtually immune to wear from use, ensuring long-term stability and reliability.
Adjustable Actuation Force: Customize the force required to activate a key according to your preferences. Whether you prefer a light touch or a firmer press, this feature caters to different user needs, making the AULA WIN60 HE highly versatile.

What is the Hall Effect? 
The Hall Effect is a physical phenomenon that allows our keyboard, like the AULA WIN60 HE, to detect whether a key has been pressed by sensing changes in the position of a tiny magnet beneath each key, rather than relying on traditional mechanical contact. This means every keystroke can be recognized with exceptional precision, while also avoiding the wear and tear issues common to traditional switches over time. 
Why Choose the AULA WIN60 HE Hall Effect Keyboard? 
Unmatched Precision: With Hall Effect technology, the AULA WIN60 HE offers unparalleled accuracy, ensuring that every keystroke is registered correctly. It's perfect for gaming or tasks requiring rapid responses and fine control.
