productPageReviews.reviewTitle: For the price? Hell yeahFor the price? Hell yeah
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was looking for a new keyboard since my old one was white and only had one color RGB, and I wanted to have a black set up with something that can have different RGB colors. I first came across this keyboard on TikTok and many compared it to the Wooting. I’m not a techy person but I saw many people talking about the good specs and how it has different functions such as customizable RGB or customizable actuation options (I think that’s how you spell it).When it came today, I was really excited as I was watching some TikToks on the keyboard (always do that when I get new stuff), and was really thrilled.It came packaged well, came with everything, and connectivity was really easy. I think it is heavier than my previous keyboard, which I personally think is good. It sounds much better and thockier than my previous one, which I was so happy about. I’m a much more “thocky” person so this keyboard made me so happy.Connecting the keyboard to the software was really easy. I don’t want to download anything so I just used the web version, and it works perfectly fine. The customization is great!Also, the actuation point or whatever it’s called is really customizable. For anyone that plays games where you have to have fast reaction time, I recommend putting it really low. For me personally, I only really play Roblox, so I keep it at around 0.75-1.Great keyboard for the price. 100% recommend!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 8, 2026Reviewed in the United States on August 8, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Insane value: great feel/performance, weak software
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this for my girlfriend and it honestly surprised me. The sound and feel were so good that it genuinely competed with (and in some ways felt better than) my custom Wooting build that cost a lot more. Performance-wise it does what you want from a hall-effect keyboard: responsive, consistent, and great for competitive gaming.The main downside is the online software. It works, but it is not polished and does not feel premium. That said, once you set your actuation/rapid trigger the way you like, you are not going to be in the software very often.Testing this keyboard also made me realize my Wooting needed an upgrade. I ended up buying Geon Raw HE 40g switches, which cost more than this entire keyboard, and they ended up feeling nearly the same in practice.I am looking forward to buying from them again in the future. This is coming from someone who cares about competitive, quality gear (Finalmouse Starlight-12 Last Legend, Logitech GPX 1/2/2C, Wooting 60HE, and Artisan pads like the Hayate Otsu, Hien, and Zero). If you are on a budget and want strong competitive gear with great sound and feel, this is an easy recommendation.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on February 1, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Absolutely love this keyboard! I bought the Aula WIN60 HE in white and it looks amazing on my desk. The 60% size saves so much space and the RGB lighting is beautiful without being too much. For the price ($42.99) the build quality is incredible. Keys feel super smooth and responsive thanks to the Hall Effect switches. Rapid Trigger makes a huge difference for gaming. 100% Amazon's Choice for a reason - highly recommended!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 31, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good purchase (but has some diy needed)
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Okay, I should start off by saying this is 100% purely based on my opinion/experiences with it, doing testing, gaming, and getting my settings just right, all immediately out of the box.One thing I immediately right off the bat did NOT like about the keyboard was the keycaps, they HAD to go, they felt very uncomfortable and cheap, and overall made the keyboard sound worse (I could just be making this up, but after switching keycaps there’s a noticeable difference in the feel and sound of it)The keyboard's stock keyswitches get the job done, (I think?) accurate actuation, amazing response time, honestly no complaints about them, they do what you need them to and sound decent (I heard that gateron keyswitches work with this keyboard and eventually I plan to test that, when I do I’ll update with whether or not it works, and if the keyboard plays nicely with them, may also include a sound test video :3)Overall, great feel on the keyboard itself, it’s decently hefty, but it helps to keep the keyboard in placeOne side note, during me switching the keycaps I was pressing down pretty firm on the keyboard, and it had a goood bit of flex in it, not sure if that’s a bad thing though?Oh yeah I don’t wanna forget the polling rate, it’s absolutely 8k polling and it makes my usb ports go nuts with my AMD system lol, still works great though even considering the fact it takes everything else out to use it fully sometimes (gonna test the intel pc soon for the usb bonkery, will update on that)Anyways I can definitely recommend this keyboard, but I suggest replacing the keycaps when you get it, so be sure to order them with it or have them at the ready to swap them out.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 29, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Honestly, this keyboard is really nice. When it comes down to the quality, it’s not bad at all, it has a sturdy frame and solid keys that give it a premium feel. The sound profile is pleasantly subtle; instead of the loud pen-clicking noise some mechanical keyboards have, it offers more of a light tap, kind of like tapping on a phone screen. It’s satisfying without being noisy.The color is nice and sleek, and the overall functionality is great. That said, if you’re someone who doesn’t like compact layouts, I wouldn’t recommend this, it’s a 60% keyboard so there’s no dedicated function row or numpad. But if you’re aiming for a clean, uncluttered desk setup and want to avoid big, bulky boards, this one’s definitely for you.The typing feel is excellent, and the value is pretty solid for what you're getting. One thing to note: the software for the keyboard isn’t a traditional downloadable program, instead it’s browser-based witch may be a downside for some, but it still works well.A standout feature is the ability to adjust key sensitivity. This essentially allows you to change how far you need to press a key for it to register, which is fantastic for competitive gamers and fast typists alike. It's responsive, customizable, and overall just a great experience.In short, if you want a compact, high-performing keyboard with great build quality and advanced features like adjustable actuation, the Alua Win60HE is a solid pick personally.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great Keyboard for the PriceGreat Keyboard for the Price
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Context: I've been looking at 65% and smaller keyboard for a while. I've had a Logitech Pro 10 Keyless for a couple years. It's a mechanical board and it's been great, but I wanted  something wireless and quieter in the office for when I need the silence. I looked for a couple days at various keyboards on here and went ahead and took a chance with an off-brand one. The Logitech board I have was over $100 and I just wasn't putting that sort of money down again.Pros:- PRICE; in a market over-saturated with keyboards that are overpriced, this was a welcomed change.- Size is great; still has arrow keys!- I've used Bluetooth since day one with no lag.- The keys are definitely quiet.- LEDs are easy to program without software.- The 3000mAh battery is legit. I have used it heavily for about a week since purchase starting with around 90% battery and it's down to 45%; very happy with this battery life.- Angle can be adjusted.- Can be used with Bluetooth, 2.4GHz USB adapter, or wired.- Included cable is great; nylon braid has no permanent kinks.Cons:- Like many of the quieter, knock-off keyboards, I sometimes brush a key lightly and it recognizes it as a stroke. This leads to errors in my typing. Not a huge deal as I'm a bit more careful, but definitely noticeable if you have fatter fingers.- The spacebar sounds different than all the other keys. It's pretty hollow sounding (like most space bars) but it seems to echo pretty loudly on this keyboard.Overall:5/5; While there are a couple cons in my opinion, this cheaper keyboard absolutely exceeded my expectations. My Logitech board is definitely higher quality overall (and still made in China) but for a quarter of the price, this is a great option! I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a smaller keyboard footprint!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great First Value Mech Keyboard For Macbook ProGreat First Value Mech Keyboard For Macbook Pro
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So far a great keyboard! Have had it for a week now and it works great for Macbook Pro. Granted this is my first mechanical keyboard but it has a great feel and nice click to the key actuations. Easy to change out the keys and customize the layout however due to sizing for a 63% keyboard not all custom keys will fit where they’re supposed to like conventional Shift-FN-ALT key on the right side of the layout. The lighting is very nice, bright and easy to change, though there is no custom software this works out better for mac where software compatibility is sometimes an issue. There are plenty of lighting options though it would be nice if there was an explanation in the box for all of the different settings. Battery life isn’t the best when using the brightest RGB settings but it still gives you a few days on a full charge. I’ve heard the longevity on this keyboard isn’t the best but that remains to be seen for me, so far it’s great. The only issue I had when pairing this keyboard was a  Mac OS pop up saying it did not recognize the keyboard however if you ignore this the keyboard works perfectly with all the keys corresponding to their designated functions correctly so far as I’ve seen. I’m not a gamer, i’m a photo retoucher/video editor and this serves me perfectly.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Lasted a month before dying- unable to get it to charge
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this keyboard a month ago after a friend of mine purchased the same exact one. I loved the design and how it functioned. The color options are also a plus! I have used it daily (for hours on end) and have not had any issues with it. I love the sound of the keys (red) and the spacing between keys isn't too small for me even though it is a more compact keyboard. Up until a few days ago, I had yet to charge it. However, It suddenly died on me yesterday and since then I have not been able to get it to charge. I've tried the cord it came with, different cords, tried both directly into a USB wall plug, and with a usb adapter box into a standard plug in. I noticed with my friends keyboard that when you plug it in, the space bar turns red for a bit indicating that it is charging. That does not happen to mine. I have reached out to the seller in hopes they have some tips or a replacement, as I really do like this keyboard. I'm hoping I just received a faulty one. I will update this post if I hear back from them.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on February 15, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It’s great, when it works!It’s great, when it works!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I needed a keyboard for a small office space I set up in my bedroom. When I saw the size of this, I figured it would be PERFECT, and it is to a point. The size makes it much easier to have full control over the keyboard, and it doesn’t take up unnecessary space. I love the light functions that the keyboard comes with, and switching it from Bluetooth to wired is super simple. My main complaint with this keyboard is that is seems to “die” over night. I find this really odd since I use it wired. Every morning when my system comes on, the keyboard starts to flash through it’s color spectrum then quickly shuts off.. almost like it’s not holding a charge. At this point none of the keys are functional, and it’s almost as if I have an unplugged keyboard. I’ve tried a ton of tricks to get this to stop happening, and the only thing that works is to unplug it and plug it back in. Although it may just be a dud keyboard that I ended up with & the majority of them may not do this, it easily becomes an inconvenience and is a bit of a disappointment.

features: 【Ergonomic Design, Enhanced Typing Experience】Improve your typing experience with our computer keyboard featuring an ergonomic 7-degree input angle and a scientifically designed stepped key layout. The integrated wrist rests maintain a natural hand position, reducing hand fatigue. Constructed with durable ABS plastic keycaps and a robust metal base, this keyboard offers superior tactile feedback and long-lasting durability.

Even in low light, easily identify keys for enhanced typing accuracy and efficiency. Choose from 15 RGB color modes to set the perfect ambiance for your typing adventure. 【Whisper Quiet Design】Experience near-silent operation with our whisper-quiet gaming switch, ideal for office environments and gaming setups. The classic volcano switch structure ensures durability and an impressive lifespan of 50 million keystrokes.

Control play, pause, and skip functions directly with the 12 multimedia keys for a seamless gaming experience. (Please note: Multimedia keys are not compatible with Mac)
【Lifetime Support】If you are not satisfied with our product or service, please feel free to contact us. Each TECKNET product comes with a lifetime support (registration required).

Why does the backlight turn off after 5 minutes? 
Because the gaming keyboard automatically enters sleep mode after five minutes to save power, you can press any key or Fn+PgDn to reawaken the backlight. 
Is this a mechanical keyboard? How loud is this keyboard? 
It's a membrane keyboard. This RGB keyboard is relatively quiet, enabling you to immerse yourself in the gaming atmosphere. 
Can I turn off the light on this keyboard? 
Yes, press the "FN+ PgDn" (Page Down) Key to turn on/ off the backlight. 
How to adjust the brightness and breathing speed? 
You can hold the "FN+↑ / ↓" to adjust the brightness and hold the "FN+← / →" to adjust the breathing speed. 
How do I adjust the 7 lighting modes? 
You can press the "FN+Insert / Home / PgUp / Delete / End" to select your favorite illumination mode.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Definitely a Budget Keyboard - But a Nice Budget Keyboard
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Overall, I'm fairly impressed with the TECKNET RGB Gaming Keyboard. It's a lot better than I thought it would be for a budget keyboard. It looks really good and the keys are pretty responsive, though you do have to press a bit more to get them to respond than I'm used to with my old, loud mechanical keyboard. It is pretty quiet, too, which is nice if you need to type with others in the house or late at night.Having said that, there's one thing that's really bugging me about this keyboard. All of the keys are great ... all of them except the spacebar. The spacebar uses two cheap springs, one on either side, to cause the spacebar to 'equally' spring up after a press. This key feels less solid than the other keys and the way this one was put together makes the spacebar the one noisy key on the entire board. It's not bad, but since the other keys are so quiet, the spacebar stands out and after a good bit of typing, I find it's annoying me. The spacebar should be as quiet as all the other keys and it's not. As nice as this budget board is, the spacebar makes me consider sending it back for a refund.Set up is super simple. I'm on a Windows PC and all I had to do was plug in the USB cable to my PC and I was ready to go. You can't get any simpler than that. But you also expect that from keyboards.Customizing the lighting is limited compared to more expensive keyboards where you can download software and control almost every aspect of the RGB lighting. However, the colors you're given and the control you do have via the keyboard is good. In my case, it's good enough.Overall, this is a nice keyboard that, in my opinion, looks better than the asking price, but is definitely a budget board.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Ein Ersatz für meine alte Tastatur mit Beleuchtung und Kabel von Speedlink musste her. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It's my favorite style of keyboardIt's my favorite style of keyboard
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Great keyboard with 99% in common with my all time favorite keyboard... the ASUS keyboard MODEL: AW211.The only reason I'm switching out my keyboard after 8-9 years is because of the amount of dirt that builds up over that time period. I am hoping the Amazon Basics brand MD-005 keyboard has the same longevity. Immediately you'll notice the keyboard layout is the same until you reach the only 3 lights on the top right, but I believe the cord is a foot longer on the Amazon model.With my ASUS motherboard and AMD chipset, this keyboard fails to be recognized (unlike my ASUS one) on startup. I simply have to unplug my MD-005 USB and plug it back in and no further issues until I turn my PC off again.I use this keyboard for internet browsing and some work, but mostly for gaming actually. The responsiveness and feel of these keyboards is unmatched, but the amazon one (for better or worse) has slightly stiffer keys in terms of how much effort they require to push down. On rare occasion, one time so far, a keystroke will be missed. This could very well be user error.All in all, even with the issue of needing to plug it back in every restart, this keyboard well worth it. It's nothing fancy, but it's exactly what I wanted.I removed a star as my hands get more tired of typing on this keyboard than my ASUS one and the inconvenience of needing to unplug and plug it back in on startup. I would however still recommend this keyboard despite these flaws. While I am gaming the stiff keys are not noticed.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Effective, cost effective, and easy to use.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Workhorse keyboard. It's wired so need to worry about battery, and the cord is pretty long too. The buttons are responsive, and make very little noise. Plug it in and it works, PnP functionality compatible fir windows. The keys are a bit small compared to larger mechanical keyboards but it definitely works well. The best part? I used one of these for 3-4 years gaming before encountering sticking keys. And getting a new one is so cheap it was pocket change compared to the pricy ones. My recommendation? If you need an external keyboard, or several, this is the way to go. Good backup keyboard too! For the casual gamer it has very little latency and it's quite ergonomic. It IS flat though, so if you prefer yours angled, you'll need your own stand or other accessories.All in all, it does exactly what it's designed to do, and it does it well. 10/10

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Now I have to say, I tend to have a love/hate relationship with keyboards, especially gaming keyboards.  The "good" ones to me tend to be very chunky, big keys, etc.  I keep thinking of an IBM Selectric typewriter, and if you don't know what that is then get off my lawn.Now my daily computer is a MacBook Pro. I use the Magic Keyboard when docked and, well, it's a low profile keyboard that I like very much.  Going from that to a pro-level mechanical gaming keyboard is really a shift.  So here, Razer seems to have solved my dilemma.  This is a low profile keyboard but it does have a positive response that is expected from a gaming keyboard.  But it also straddles a line between pure gaming and pure general use.  In that it works, and works well.  Think of this as a keyboard that isn't 100% focused on the gaming.Now then, about the functionality.  It does what it's supposed to do, though some things are little absent.  Media control buttons are just those...buttons.  No scroll wheels or dials.  Odd to me.  Layout is generally as expected, and I'm old school enough to really want the ten key there.  The clicking of the keys is a nice thing to me, as it does provide some positive feedback...the keyboard isn't as mushy as a purely membrane keyboard.  It's not quite as positive though as purely mechanical either.  Yes, I confirm the ad copy that this is a hybrid, which does require some compromise.So this all said, lighting is in ZONES and not individual keys.  This gets me a bit perturbed as I kind of like WASD to be set off from the rest of the keyboard.  The zones are mostly decent, in that I mean the two right hand zones follow the format of the keyboard, but after that I'm not seeing a rhyme/reason to the zone borders.  And yeah, you have to use Synapse/chroma for the functionality and colors.  That is, well, I'm not reviewing Synapse but I'll say I have a love/hate relationship with it.I like the wrist rest, and really recommend keeping it on there especially if you're using this as an everyday keyboard.  I like having it there for general use, but in gaming I tend to remove it and rotate the keyboard slightly clockwise to make it more accessible with my left hand.  It responds well enough for this amateur gamer.  It has great build quality for the application, inasmuch as it's not designed to take a serious pounding but it IS sturdy enough to work well for most anything under that.Responsiveness is similarly appropriate.  It's wired only, so take that into account...you'll need a USB port.So I like it.  A lot.  It's not a pro keyboard, but I'm not a pro.  Accounting for the compromises, I don't see anything there that seriously impedes the mission of the product.  Yeah, the zone lighting is a bit yuck, and the anti-ghosting...isn't there...but for shall we say motivated amateur use I like it a lot.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I spent over a year looking for the perfect keyboard. You'd think I would have gone straight to Razor, since I'm such a Razor fangirl (Naga mouse, headset, etc.), but I kept going with cheap keyboards. I was looking for a very specific type of keyboard: mechanical feel, low-profile keys, satisfying clicking sounds that aren't too loud, and preferably RGB. This checks ALL those boxes. Seriously, I'm kicking myself for not just getting it sooner (though by the time I decided to finally get it, it was on sale, so the timing worked out). I like that the wrist rest is magnetic - the magnets are actually pretty strong, too, which means I don't have it sliding around even during my furious typing sessions. The keys are soft to the touch, but have a really satisfying click. It's not silent, but it's definitely a lot quieter than other mechanical keyboards I've had. The backlighting colors are bright and pleasant; I like that it doesn't just switch between 3 or 4 colors, but rather fades into each shade, so you get the true rainbow experience, without any flashing between colors. I haven't had any issues with it at all, zero lag whatsoever. The price is honestly really good for something this solid and comfortable. I use it for gaming and for my WFH job, so I'm on it all day, and it's honestly the best keyboard I've ever had. Another Razor win!Oh - a quick side note, this doesn't really matter to me, but it might to some people: I noticed that in a couple of games, it gets weird flashing patterns and sticks to one or colors. In Fortnite, for example, it only lights up blue, and flashes at random intervals. That's the only game it's really been noticeable though, so if you don't play Fortnite or you don't care, then disregard this!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Amazing but moving backwards in features
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: As someone who has been here since v1 of this keyboard and loves this series I do have some minor issues with the v3 listed here.The Good- Absolutely love the bouncy feel of the mecha-membrane and Ive even built my own keyboard. There is just something so good about the typing actuation and how quiet it still is.- Full size can be really nice when I need a number pad and as a developer it just allows a lot of customization- Works on Mac and PC very well and the media controls are a nice touch- I used the previous versions and bought about 5 for others in my family with no issues- Low profile keys now are a great touch- One of the best typing experiences allowing a good hybrid from laptop keyboards to a semi-mechanical feel and quite quiet for the experience (though not silent). Id compare to a brown switch.The Bad- Marketing on this really irritates me because they sell and almost IDENTICAL looking version that is only a membrane for $30 less and it is nowhere near the typing experience.- V2 had a soft pad for the wrist rest and now its gone? Why move backwards?- The magnets feel less strong on the keyboard to wrist rest- I really wish they sold a 65% version of this keyboard for better portability- Treated as their "budget" keyboard so there is no snap-tap for gaming (would be nice)- Could complain about no hot-swappable keys but its ok for the technology- No Bluetooth or wireless connections.Ill end this all by saying this is still one of my favorite keyboards and quite unique but it seems they are moving backwards instead of forward. V2 had a bit more to offer minus the media control in comparison and lower profile keys. I just wish they made one of these that was a higher tier and treated with the same quality as their full mechanical boards and a bit smaller. Overall I still love the feel and quality on this keyboard and I cant argue with the pricing at all for the feel. Highly recommended buy but Im leaving a star off for the features that they removed and the easily fixable complaints I listed.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Beautiful, Comfortable, and Worth It — Just Keep It CleanBeautiful, Comfortable, and Worth It — Just Keep It Clean
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I absolutely love this keyboard! From the moment I started using it, the quality really stood out—it feels sturdy, well-made, and not cheap at all. The keys have a soft, satisfying feel with great response, and best of all, it’s quiet, which is perfect for working in shared or quiet spaces.The comfort and ergonomics are a huge plus. I can type for long periods without any strain, and everything feels very natural. The size is perfect too—not bulky, but still fully functional with all the keys I need.Speaking of functionality, it’s been reliable and super easy to use. I haven’t tried the Bluetooth connectivity since I always use the included USB receiver—and it works flawlessly for me every time.Now let’s talk about the pink color—because it’s beautiful, but it does need care. From what I read in other reviews, it can stain easily. The key is simple: clean it daily or every other day to keep it looking brand new (check out my video!).I’ve had mine since late December and it still looks like new thanks to this cleaning kit (it even includes a microfiber cloth):🧼 Cleaning Kit: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CPGPFW5QDirections: Using the cleaning solution included in this kit, lightly spray onto the microfiber cloth—avoid spraying directly onto the surface. Gently wipe in circular motions without applying heavy pressure. Finish by buffing dry with a clean, dry section of the microfiber cloth.Also, avoid using hand lotion or hand sanitizer before using the keyboard.If you’re willing to maintain it, this keyboard is 100% worth it. Stylish, comfortable, and functional—you’re welcome 😎

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Relieves my arm/wrist pain - highly recommend even if you don’t have pain yet
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Love it! This is my second Wave Keys purchase - the first one I bought for work. I have mild arm/wrist issues after years of daily keyboard work, and purchased after recent PT for these issues. I quickly adapted to this keyboard. It is not as aggressive ergo-wise as some other keyboards, so it is an easier adjustment. it works beautifully! Quiet typing (the previous version of this keyboard was larger and loud, very 90s design), so this update was welcome! The palm rest is comfortable -not squishy if you are used to that but cushioning is enough for me. Battery life is very good, literally 8-12 months or longer between replacement. I have used rechargeable batteries with no problem. Price is reasonable although you frequently can find discounts. Pair it with a trackball or other ergo mouse. Also I like the color - an understated pale rosy pink.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 4, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Skip the no-names. Go with a true ergonomic keyboard from a brand leader.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'm new-school old-school. My favorite keyboard of all time was the Microsoft Natural keyboard from the mid-90s. I pounded that thing into the ground over nearly 20 years and it never gave me a problem.Then it died and I was on the hunt for another ergonomic keyboard. My new go-to - though it doesn't have the tactile, mechanical feedback that seems to be the rage these days - is the Logitech K860. This review isn't about that keyboard, but it tells you a little about my preference. Ergonomic curve, ergonomic split, and ideal for a touch-typist who typically does about 80wpm when he's flying.When I needed a new keyboard for a remote office on the west coast, I immediately thought about the K860. But the problem with the K860 is size. It's wide, like battleship wide, like it takes up waaay more space than I had on the desktop in the temporary space out west. I wanted something ergonomic, with a little more tactile feedback, but that would be slightly smaller to fit the narrower space on the desk out west.Enter the Logitech Wave Keys. What a revelation. Solid typing experience, with more bounce than the K860, and with just enough ergonomic dip and wave to keep fatigue at a minimum. Plus, it fits a narrower desk nicer than the K860.Also, Bluetooth was a must. I can't stand the 2.4g dongles. they always get lost. You won't lose a keyboard, but you might lose that tiny little dongle. The Bluetooth on this keyboard was 100% reliable over two weeks of work at the remote site. I was typing non-stop for almost 10 days and never once flashed back and said, "Gee, I wish this was my K860."In short, a pleasurable workhorse that fit the bill and gave me just the right layout to be productive without constantly fat-fingering the wrong keys.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 10, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good Keyboard, But More Compact Than the Logitech K350 Wave Keyboard
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If you're replacing a Logitech K350 Wave keyboard like I was, here's the honest scoop after one week of daily work use.The Good:* Quiet, soft keys with a nice tactile feel — much gentler on the ears and fingers than standard keyboards.* Comfortable padded wrist rest that actually helps during long typing sessions.* Handy shortcut buttons for common apps.* Very lightweight and easy to move around.* Wireless connectivity works flawlessly so far.The Not-So-Good:It's noticeably more compact than the K350. The entire layout is smaller, which means keys are closer together. My muscle memory from the larger K350 caused frequent typos for the first several days. The arrow keys and number pad area feel especially cramped.This is a great modern ergonomic keyboard if you want something smaller and more portable than the old K350, or if you're coming from a standard full-size board. The wave shape still provides that comfortable hand position. Battery life is unknown after just a week, but Logitech's track record is excellent.I'm confident I'll adapt fully with more time — it's already growing on me. If size isn't a concern for you, this is an easy recommendation.But it is not the Logitech K350.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on May 26, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: If you have wrist pain, buy this
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If you work on a computer and type consistently buy this. I work at a computer and type a lot at my job, and my wrists were starting to feel it. I bought this along with the wave mouse and my wrists havent hurt since. It takes a little bit of getting used to for the shape of it, but if you confidently type on a normal computer (without looking at the keys constantly) you will pick it up quick. Its not too too different from a standard flat keyboard, but just enough different to require maybe a few days to get used to. The feel of typing on this is great. The keys are fairly quiet and the perfect amount of springy under your fingers. Ive had this for almost a year and havent needed to charge or change batteries. It comes with 1 dongle and can connect multiple pieces (I have the wave mouse and this keyboard on one). The wrist rest is comfortable and the material is resistant from getting gross (sometimes the cloth ones get gross with constant use). Overall best keyboard I own for work.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 4, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have been using this keyboard for work and personal use for 2 days and am loving it so far. It's perfect for my needs and here's why:1. It has all the functions I need and then some2. It's just the right size. I was using a separate keyboard for my personal pc than for my work laptop and the other keyboard is much larger, not leaving much room for my mousepad in the desk tray.3. It connects seamlessly to both, my laptop and desktop so I don't even have to use the other keyboard now! I wasn't looking for that but is a HUGE plus now that I have it setup. You can save 3 connected devices and switch between them using F1, F2, and F3. This was a huge help since I use the same monitor for both devices (I bought an hdmi splitter for that) but would have to use 2 different keyboard/mouse each time I switched. Now I only use 2 different mouses (mice?) which I'll probably upgrade as well.4. The keys have good response without being noisy. You can hear them, which I prefer, and feel the feedback, also preferred, but you don't have to press hard and don't get the loud click-clack of old school keyboards.5. It's comfortable to use, at least for me. The palm rest cushion is soft but seems like it will hold up for a long time. The major keys are reachable without lifting my palm and there was minimal adjustment from my much larger keyboard.6. Very easy setup (I use Windows...can't speak to Mac, Google OS, etc.). As soon as I turned on the keyboard, it paired with my laptop. I had to do absolutely nothing for setup (see note below).The ONLY very small con I have is that it doesn't tell you anywhere in the packaged instructions that you can pair multiple devices. I knew this from another reviewer. Even then, I had to search how to do it, because it's not obvious on the Logitech website. Once I figured it out, it was very easy to do (have your laptop/pc/whatever search for bluetooth devices and hold down the button F1/2/3 button that you want to assign to that device. The device will then discover the keyboard and you're good to go).Other Notes: I would recommend this keyboard to anyone. It's pricier than other keyboards I've bought but I didn't add a con for that because I believe it's definitely worth it. You can change how the function keys work using their application and even setup "smart actions" which will do a bunch of stuff like opening your favorite apps and a bunch of other stuff. All of this stuff is configurable too, although, I haven't tried to use it yet. I just needed a keyboard so I didn't have to use my laptop keyboard but got many features I didn't even know I needed! Get this keyboard!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on January 11, 2024

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Perfect but could be improved upon
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I like this keyboard is more ways than one! Not only does it connect via bluetooth, you can also connect via wireless dongle. Your choice. It's small and not overpowering for your desk. My previous Logitech Wave Keyboard was about 4 - 5 inches longer and about 2 inches taller. I actually like this smaller size. I also like that it uses batteries and doesn't require you to recharge it. So much better! Just change out batteries when you need to. The only thing I do wish is that the keys had wider, brighter markings. I'm in a dimly lit room and it can be a little more difficult to see the upper keys. I would also like to see them remove the mute key and replace it with a calculator key. That's the only key I miss from my previous keyboard.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 22, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Perfect ergonomic upgrade for long work days, very comfortable memory foamPerfect ergonomic upgrade for long work days, very comfortable memory foam
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this Logitech Wave Keys as a birthday gift for my dad to use at his accounting firm, and he absolutely loves it. Because he spends long days doing heavy data entry and typing up emails, I wanted to get him something that would help with wrist fatigue. The wave layout of the keys does a fantastic job of keeping your hands and forearms in a much more natural posture, and unlike some extreme ergonomic keyboards, the learning curve on this one is very minimal. The integrated memory foam palm rest is incredibly comfortable and provides excellent support. It also easily pairs with multiple devices, and the battery life is supposedly fantastic. If you spend a lot of time typing and want to upgrade your office setup, this is an excellent choice

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: A well-designed and well-built keyboard that offers full functionality in a compact form factor
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: A well-designed keyboard, well-sized and highly functional.  It feels well-designed and well-built. It was easy to connect to my PC and easy to manage via the Logi Options+ app, which I also use to manage a Logi mouse.  Part of the magic of why it's easier on your hands is the compact nature of key placement, i.e., it offers all the functions of a full-size keyboard but in a smaller form factor. My hands are large (i.e., I wear size large gloves), and I find the keyboard perfectly well laid out; I don't feel crowded, but this might be an issue if your hands are even larger.A couple of items that I will need to get used to are the placement of the delete key and the arrow keys.  I figure it'll take a couple of days, and I'll have the muscle memory, so no biggie.  The keys are quiet and firm, yet easy to push.The wrist rest is nice, and I think it will help address the numbness issues I encounter during long work sessions.  I'm using it on a sit-and-stand desk and will fine-tune the height to get things dialled in right, but in the meantime, it's working well.You can program a number of the function keys via the Logi Options+ app, something I've done with the mouse; this can be a huge time/keystroke saver for repetitive work.  You can also enable the top row to be either F-keys or media keys, which means you don't have to push the function key along with the F-key that you want to use.In case you're wondering, no, this keyboard is not backlit. More importantly, it has raised lines on the home keys, and as a touch typist, this is all I need. I don't look at the keyboard, and don't need it to be backlit.  To be honest, I would find it distracting and annoying.  Yes, the Caps Lock key has a tiny light on it.Between writing for my PhD and my day job, I easily type for 10+ hours a day, hence why I opted for the ergonomic layout. Other than the minor items mentioned above, which I can adapt to, I think this will be an excellent keyboard to work with.This is an excellent keyboard and well worth the price. I would highly recommend it for someone who can touch-type, doesn't care about backlit keys, and wants the enhanced functionality of programmable keys.***Update one week laterEverything above is still true, but I found the keyboard to be too small for my hands; there were too many awkward finger twists, etc., and it was interrupting my typing/workflow.  So, I returned it and got the larger Logi ERGO K860 For Business keyboard - love it!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: First impression: Good keyboard for typing, gaming, and small hands.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I only just received this item today, so I cannot yet speak to its longevity, but I am very happy with it so far. My previous keyboard was a permanently borrowed Corsair Strafe RGB Mechanical Gaming Keyboard. It worked well enough, but one of the arrow keys had stopped working, and one of the letter keys was hit or miss if it worked. On top of that, it was very heavy (I game/type with the keyboard in my lap) and the cord loved getting in the way. This keyboard, on the other hand, is much lighter. It has a heft to it that seems to be just about right. It doesn't dig into my legs, but it's not so light that it feels cheap. Typing is fast and easy (I can type over 100 wpm with few errors on a regular day, but I am backspacing much less with this keyboard, and I seem to be able to go a bit faster) The sound is not too loud, nor too quiet, and is quite satisfying. I have small hands (small isotoners are a bit too long for my fingers) and it doesn't feel uncomfortable to reach all the standard keys. And even though it makes it longer than would be fully comfortable for long gaming sessions, the number keypad was a must-have for me as an old-school typist and data entry person. I do wish the keys had a bit of light coming through for when it's dark, but it's not essential for me since I've been touch typing since high school in the late 80s/early 90s. So far there has been no lag using it wirelessly with the 2.4hz option. I appreciate that the lighting goes away after 3 minutes of no typing and I look forward to seeing how long the battery lasts since I spend long periods of time either just using the mouse to navigate around streaming services and often have the computer asleep on days when I take care of the grandkid. Overall I'm happy to have found this purple keyboard, and am pleased with the quality for $60.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I picked up the Logitech MK470 Slim Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo for my lab computer — an older AMD build running Windows 10 and Linux — and it’s been exactly what I needed. The low‑profile design makes it easy to keep in a drawer and pull out only when I’m working on that machine, which helps keep my main desk setup clean and uncluttered.Keyboard:The keys are quiet, low‑travel, and comfortable for quick tasks or light typing sessions. It’s not meant to replace a full mechanical keyboard, but for a lightweight, portable option, it feels great. The slim profile also makes it easy to slide away when I’m done.Mouse:The mouse is equally compact and responsive. It’s nothing fancy, but it tracks well and is perfect for occasional use. The shared USB receiver keeps things simple — plug it in and both devices connect instantly.Compatibility:So far I’ve only used it on Windows 10, and it’s been flawless. I haven’t needed it for Ubuntu yet, but Logitech’s combos usually work fine across Linux distros without extra setup.Overall:If you want a clean desk and a keyboard/mouse you can stash away until needed, this combo nails it. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent keyboard layout and great feel.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My first impressions of this keyboard are very good. The keyboard layout makes sense and all the keys are where you would expect them to be. The arrow keys are full size and easy to access. This is extremely important to me as I use the arrow keys frequently and half size keys that are crammed in between other keys on the keyboard are just to awkward to use effectively. This keyboard layout is perfect.I've been looking for a keyboard where the Fn + Arrow keys mimics the Home and End keys and was very pleased to see that this one does this. I very frequently move my cursor around documents and like to jump to the beginning or end of a line and using the Fn + Arrow keys makes this simple. It basically mimics the Fn key on my laptop where I developed my muscle memory to do this, so finding a keyboard that mimics this functionality is a huge plus for me.Also, my previous keyboard was wireless so it would eventually turn off the backlight to save power. This is very annoying and defeats the purpose of being able to see the keyboard when you need it to. Since this one is hard wired, the backlight stays on indefinitely. The dedicated backlight buttons enable me to easily change the intensity of the backlight to three different power levels and off.The keys click perfectly and are very comfortable for a touch typist. The printing on the keys is clear and both the letter and the border of the key are backlit to make it easy to see in the dark.There is a dedicated Fn Lock key that changes the top row of keys from F1-F12 to their alternate functions. Since I routinely use the F5 key to refresh my screen, I don't use the Fn Lock, but it's good to know that it exists.The only unanswered question is durability. But after using it for one day, I'm very pleased with it and give it high marks.My only wish list item that it's missing is that pressing the caps lock doesn't light an indicator on the key itself, but a cap locks light in the upper right hand corner of the keyboard. I like being able to look at the cap locks key and determine immediately whether it's on or not, so this is the only checkbox that it doesn't check, but overall, it offers great value for the money and I'm very satisfied with it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Didn't expect to like it, but I do.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I replaced a mechanical  RGB keyboard with this due to "click" sound reasons that annoyed my spouse.So, I just returned a great ROCCAT Vulcan 122 keyboard for this low profile RGB keyboard, and I thought I would be greatly disappointed from just owning a award-winning mechanical master piece to a budget version of a scissor switch keyboard. I have to say, after I have been playing with this for a bit I am happily surprised, the keys are somehow soft feeling yet with a tactile feel to them but without the "click" noises from a mechanical keyboard, I am very custom to these type keyboard, most people are these days since it is usually the standard issue with new computers, however, they usually don't have any type illumination to the keys so they are not great in low light settings. This keyboard has 7 colors to choose from, you can easily adjust the brightness and which color you want directly from 2 keys on the keyboard set between the right [Alt], [Ctrl] key which I accidentally hit a couple of times with my palm, for future versions maybe put those buttons either under the  [Delete], [End], [PgDn] button section of the keyboard to avoid accidental hits. Not a huge issue but a side-note.Other than that, there is not much to say, so far it performs like a keyboard should, it seems to respond well to every keystroke, soft but tactile feel to the keys, firm and steady with no "wiggly" keys.The illumination is "soft" and bright enough on the lowest settings to lit up every key and it has a backlit that doesn't take over the entire keyboard if that makes sense, some keyboard have such a bright backlit it overpowers the key-lights so they drown and with all that light you still cant see the letters of the key which some people need. I don't have the muscle memory in my fingers to remember the wheree the keys are so I need to see the keys when I type or play, not a problem with this board even on the brightest setting, But really, its good enough on the lowest setting. On my keyboard though, the FN row, Win Alt Ctrl and arrow buttons seem to have less illumination than the main keys of the keyboard, not at all a problem on the bright settings but its worth noting that on the low setting they are visible but much less so.As usual the space-bar, Shift buttons has a slightly louder noise level, I have seen people commenting on that on multiple Scissor keyboards, that usually comes from the added little steel pin, that most scissor keyboards have to make those "longer" or "wider" keys "uniform," meaning it gives them a more even press, without it you risk ending up with having to make sure to press the key in the dead center for it to register the keystroke, with it you can hit the key on the edges and it will still register, makes sense? but for that reason it gives a bit of a different noise, still very quiet, just adds that little "plastic hits steel" sound. This time, absolutely no noise complaints from my spouse.It comes with a 4' cord which is plenty long if you ask me, people want ultra long cords for some reason, I sit with the screen maybe 2' away from me at all times, I see no reason to have longer cords. The cord does feel a bit cheap to me, it works but my other keyboard had this thick braided and nice cord which felt solid and like it was made with quality, this cord is thinner, feels and looks cheap and you get the feeling that this is what will fail first with this keyboard.That said, for the money you are spending on this keyboard I have to say I am surprised so far, typing and using the keyboard it feels almost as good as the $160 mechanical I replaced with this board. Even though it doesn't have any Ghosting  or rollover features it responds ok in the game I play and typing, this review is all typed down with this keyboard.For $27 this keyboard is a solid choice if you can't afford a mechanical keyboard or if you like me have a spouse that gets annoyed with the "click" sounds from mechanical boards and you are looking for a quiet keyboard with some solid illumination.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Extrem Leise, beleuchtet, sehr angenehmer Tastenanschlag !!
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Dies ist nun schon meine zweite Tastatur von ARTECK., und eine andere würde ich mir auch nicht mehr kaufen.Gerade für mich als YouTuberin ist es wichtig, dass meine Technik funktioniert und mich nicht im Stich lässt. Dazu gehören auch meine PC-Keyboards, die ich an alle Rechner habe. Zwischen meiner ersten ARTECK und der Lieferung meiner zweiten, hatte ich einige Tage eine andere Tastatur - harter Anschlag, die Tasten viel zu hoch, Buchstaben bleiben hängen, durch viel zu hohe Tasten kommt man versehentlich auf unerwünschte Neben-Tasten. Aber nicht bei DIESER!ARTECK hat sehr niedrige Tasten, so wie man es vom Laptop oder einem Notebook kennt. Dadurch ist der Anschlag sanft und sehr angenehm. Da ich stundenlang Konzepte (Drehbücher) für meine YouTube-Videos schreibe, ist es mir sehr wichtig, dass die Tastatur LEISE ist - ARTECK ist kaum hörbar (man hört lediglich meine längeren Nägel - wenn man aber kurze Nägel hat, hört man sie - unter den Alltagsgeräuschen - überhaupt nicht.Das ARTECK-Keyboard für den PC kommt mit Tastenbeleuchtung. So kann man zwischen folgenden Farben wechseln: Rot, Grün, Blau, Gelb, Magenta, (Pink-Lila), Türkis und Weiss. Dazu ist lediglich der Druck auf einer einzigen Taste notwendig, und jeder kann die Farbe wählen, die für ihn am angenehmsten ist oder die ihm Spass macht. Wenn die Tastatur auf WEISS eingestellt ist, gleicht sie einer Apple-Tastatur, was ich persönlich als sehr chick und edel empfinde. Ausserdem macht es das Arbeiten in den Abendstunden sehr angenehm, da die Beleuchtung stark genug ist, um selbst im Dunkeln arbeiten zu können.Die Stärke der Beleuchtung lässt sich zusätzlich in 3 Modi "dimmen" - leichte Beleuchtung, mittlere und helle.Die Lieferung erfolgt sehr schnell, und der Kundendienst ist einfach grossartig! Freundliche und sehr zügige Kommunikation bei Fragen oder neue Bestellungen. Fragen hatte ich keine, da die Tastatur selbstredend ist. Einfach den Kabel in den USB-Stecker des Rechners stecken, Beleuchtung aktivieren (falls man das wünscht), und legt sofort los.Keine nervige Installations-Software, keine offenen Fragen.Das ARTECK-Keyboard hat keine "Füsschen", die man hinten ausklappen muss, damit man die Tastatur erhöht - wir alle kennen diese "Füsschen" die IMMER abbrechen. Dieses Keyboard ist so konzipiert, dass sie hinten erhöht ist, so dass man im hinteren Bereich eine leichte Erhöhung von 2 cm hat. Dadurch ist sie eine sehr gelungene Mischung aus flacher Laptop-Tastatur und Erhöhung einer externen Tastatur. Ich selbst nutze sie als externe Tastatur an meine Laptops um meine Rechner zu schonen. Gerade Laptops und Notebooks haben 2 Schwächen: Die USB-Anschlüsse und die Tastaturen, die den Rechner viel schneller kaputtgehen lassen.Mit einer Länge von 43 cm und einer Breite von 11,5 cm ist sie ideal für Viel-Schreiber. Die Haupttasten (Buchstaben) haben eine Grösse von 1,5 x 1,5 cm, so dass man immer jede Taste "erwischt" und man kommt nicht auf eine unerwünschte Neben-Taste.Der Nummerische Block muss jeden Tag neu "eingeschaltet" werden, da er sich nach dem Runterfahren des Rechners automatisch abschaltet. Das wäre die einzge Änderung, die ich mir wünschen würde. Aber da dies auch nur ein Knopfdruck ist, kann ich sehr gut damit leben. Vielleicht ändert es ARTECK in der kommenden Zeit - würde mich freuen!Was ich als ebenfalls sehr wichtig empfinde, ist die Abnutzung der Tasten. Mein erstes ARTECK-Keyboard habe ich vor ziemlich genau 1 Jahr bestellt, mittlerweile habe ich 2 Stück, da ich an 2 Laptops arbeiten muss. Selbst nach "Tippen ohne Gnade" ist die Beschriftung nicht abgenutzt. Noch heute sehen die Buchstaben wie neu aus. Das schätze ich an ARTECK, da die meisten Tastaturen-Beschriftungen sich schnell abnutzen.Alles in einem kann ich diese Tastatur wärmstens empfehlen - was ich auch schon bei meinen YouTubern getan habe. Immer wieder sind Menschen von ihren Tastaturen, und deren Lautstärke beim Tippen genervt. Da empfehle ich gerne meine - ich bekomme KEINE Werbe-Gelder von ARTECK - das ist ledilich meine Überzeugung, aus persönlicher Erfahrung! Auch mein YouTube-Team ist mittlerweile mit dem ARTECK-Keyboard bestückt - und siehe da....  das ganze Team "klappert" zufrieden auf ihren externen Tastaturen - ob beruflich oder zwischendurch privat. LEISE und zuverlässig, so dass keiner von uns den anderen stört, oder von Tasten-Geklapper des anderen genervt ist. Die einzigen Geräusche bei uns ist sanfte Musik im Hintergrund und das fröhliche Lachen meines Teams.Einmal hatte ich von einer Freundin Besuch, die sich wunderte, warum mein Team "nur auf ihren Bildschirmen gucken" - nein, sie ARBEITEN - nur eben lautlos...  :-)))KLARE KAUF-EMPFEHLUNG !!!!!!!

There's a problem with my keyboard and mouse that I can't solve, what should I do? 
Find the EDJO support team immediately, we will be 100% responsible for each of our products and customers. 
Is there only one USB receiver? Where can I find it? 
YES, the wireless keyboard and mouse share ONE USB receiver, it is stored on the back of the mouse next to the battery compartment. 
Are keys quiet and comfortable to type on? 
Yes. Soft membrane keys provide quiet and smooth typing. Enjoy quiet and comfortable typing all day. No need to worry about disturbing others. 
What functions do the shortcut keys on the wireless keyboard have? 
Differing from other keyboards, it is more inclined to help improve your work efficiency. The functions of the shortcut keys are as follows: 
Music, Volume-, Volume+, Mute, Previous Track, Next Track, Play/Pause, Stop, Home, Email, Computer, Search 
What does the package include? Does it come with batteries? 
Package include: wireless keyboard *1; wireless mouse * 1; USB receiver * 1; user manual *1. NOTE: batteries NOT included.

features: 96% Layout & 3.98" Smart Touch Screen: The AULA L99 wireless mechanical keyboard with a touchscreen turns an ordinary input device into a smart desktop command center. The screen displays time, battery level, system and connection status. It supports custom interfaces like animations, GIFs, frames(driver required), and integrates a calculator, touchpad and mini numpad to enhance work efficiency. Tap to switch settings intuitively, upgrading the traditional computer keyboard into a visual smart terminal. Wake on-Touch: Press any key to instantly wake up the screen when it’s off. (Note: Protective film included, torn off before use.)

Tri-mode & Large Capacity Battery: The AULA L99 gaming keyboard supports USB-C wired 2.4GHz wireless BT5.1 modes for flexible connection to PC, Mac, laptop, tablet, or phone. BT mode can connect up to 3 devices. Serving as a low-latency wireless gaming keyboard and efficient office wireless keyboard. Built-in 8000mAh high-capacity battery, the creamy keyboard with number pad fits long-time work and high-intensity gaming, freeing you from battery anxiety. (Note: Charge with the original cable. Do not use fast charging.)

Programmable Software: With the AULA L99 driver, all keys support macro programming, allowing you to record and edit complex commands to boost work efficiency and gain an edge in fast-paced keyboard gaming. Driver download: soaidriver.com. (Note: The driver only supports windows system in wired mode.)

Hot-Swappable & PBT Keycaps: As a hot swappable mechanical keyboard, it supports full-key 3/5-pin hot-swapping, allowing solderless DIY switch replacement to meet personalized needs. Pre-lubricated Caramel Latte switches provide a smooth feel and a creamy keyboard sound. AULA L99 is equipped with both durable, non-fading PBT keycaps for long-term use and transparent keycaps for a stylish, personalized look. (Note: Turn off the keyboard power when replacing the switches.)

Gasket Mount & 6 Layer Soundproof Filling: The mechanical gaming keyboard adopts an advanced structure with an extended integrated silicone pad and PCB single-key slotting, which better optimizes resilience and stability for a softer, more elastic typing feel. Six-layer sound-dampening filling fills the gaps between the PCB, positioning plate and switches, effectively eliminating cavity noise caused by switches striking the positioning plate, ensuring pure sound and a soft, smooth typing experience with every keystroke

RGB Backlight: The custom office keyboard features 16 million color RGB backlighting with multiple dynamic effects. Colors and effects can be switched through the screen, software, or shortcut keys, creating a stunning light up keyboard atmosphere that complements any desktop setup, delivering both style and functionality

How to fix a black screen? 
1. Press any key to check. 
2. Use FN+Backspace to toggle the screen. 
3. Press FN+Esc to restart the keyboard. 
4. If still not working, download firmware update from soaidriver.com (see video for details). 
How to download the software driver? Is it compatible with Mac? 
1.Download the software via : soaidriver.com 
2.This Aula L99 mechanical keyboard is compatible with Windows, Mac, iOS and Android systems, but the software only supports Windows and requires wired mode. 
How to customize image animations and personalize the screen? 
1.Download and install the Aula L99 driver in wired mode with windows system. 
2.Open the software, find the IPS Screen option, and click to upload an image or GIF. 
What should I note when charging the L99 keyboard? 
1.Use original cable & computer USB port only. 
2.Do not use phone fast chargers,or overvoltage adapters. 
How to adjust the backlight of Aula L99？ 
Adjust backlight color via on-screen colors or shortcut keys. 
FN+\I=switch 19 lighting effects;FN+Tab=switch lighting colors,FN+↑/↓=lighting brightness+/-;FN+←/→=lighting speed.

aPlusContent.rawText:
Product description
Make Typing More Comfortable 
The split design helps to position wrists and forearms in a natural, relaxed position. The keyboard has comfortable wrist rest so you can place your wrist on the cushioned palm to rest and enjoy the typing. The keyboard has built-in 4 foldable legs so you can adjust to your favorite typing angle. 
Easy Setup and Use 
Just simply insert the nano USB receiver into your computer like desktop or laptop, then the keyboard can be used instantly. No need driver. 
The USB cable is for charging only, please use the USB dongle stored at the back of the keyboard to connect the keyboard to the PC. 
The Keyboard will work up to 33 feet or 10 meters. It allow you to gain quick access to common functions, such as volume level, playback control, brightness, and more. It also provides arrow keys, number pad with ergonomic design. 
The keyboard is windows layout, some keys and function will be different on Mac. 
Comfortable, quiet typing 
The whisper-quiet, low-profile keys bring a whole new level of comfort to your fingertips. What's more, keep all your most-used functions and media controls closer than ever Windows-dedicated hot keys. Keyboard with scissors kick construction can be used more than 3 million times continuously. 
Rechargeable Battery 
Built-in industry-high rechargeable Li-polymer battery provides 6-month use on a single charge. (based on 2 hours non-stop use per day)

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great replacement for Microsoft split ergo keyboard.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am very pleased with this keyboard so far. I've used Microsoft ergonomic split keyboards for years, but since Microsoft stopped making them, I needed to find an alternative.This keyboard is reasonably priced, well-built, and has a nice typing sound. It's not completely silent, but it's not overly loud either, and I don't find it distracting at all.The split design does an excellent job of supporting a more natural hand and wrist position while typing. It allows me to place my hands comfortably at shoulder width, which helps reduce strain during long work sessions.One concern I have is key durability. On my previous Microsoft keyboards, the lettering on the keys eventually wore off, so it will be interesting to see how well these hold up over time.Based on my experience so far, I would highly recommend this ergonomic split keyboard to anyone looking for a comfortable and affordable alternative.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 6, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This keyboard is awesome! I took me a minute to get used to new writing patterns, going from a "regular" keyboard to an ergonomic one. But this is smooth and seems to work well and there isn't a lag with it, which is nice.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Comfortable design, clean setup with no wires!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is truly an excellent and comfortable keyboard. I was getting a lost of wrist pain and cramping from using standard flat keyboards so when I saw the split/angled design of this one, I figured I would try it out. The price was within budget, it was wireless and very responsive. I use it daily for gaming and work and I no longer have any wrist discomfort after the long work day and gaming sessions.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 5, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: So, so, not as great as a DELTON though
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The color is very sleek black, it's extremely responsive and easy to use, the size isn't too large and fits in spaces well, the connectivity is instant once plugging in the USB and turning the board on. While it's a really nice keyboard overall, it's not my favorite and I'm glad I've ordered a few others to try before I fully set on one. The keys are not quiet in my opinion, most of them sound more mechanical but the space button is LOUD and very clacky, which as a person who types most of the day it gets kind of annoying. The adjustability of the legs to put it in a more comfortable position is nice and it's definitely ergonomic with a SLIGHT curve in it, but the curve isn't large and the arrows being placed within the board to save space isn't my favorite either. Most keys are ideal size and easy to use but the arrows are annoyingly small and the FN sometimes works and sometimes just kind of glitches??
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 7, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I did a lot of research before choosing this keyboard, and man am I glad I got it! The split is great, very comfortable. The arch is minimal, but it does the job. I also really like this scissor-switch technology, no more backspacing to fix a key that didn't register the first time! The built-in wrist rest is also really nice. I type a lot for work, and at a rate of 55 WPM. The keyboard gives just the right amount of feedback, and the keys are not mushy at all.It's also a very good looking keyboard, and is very responsive. I have heard some people mention (not just on this keyboard) that they have some lag/delay with their typing. I would bet the farm that they have plugged the receiver into a USB hub. If you're going to do that, then get yourself a USB extension cable, because the hub will cause interference with ANY wireless dongle you plug into it. Just a foot or so of distance from the hub will alleviate that. I found that out with my prior Logitech keyboard, after lots of searching around for what the cause could be.The ONLY thing I would improve is fairly minor: It does not have dedicated keys for Page Up/Down, Home, or End. You need to hold down the function key and use the corresponding arrow key for those functions. Not even remotely a deal breaker, this keyboard is fantastic in every other aspect.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on November 22, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good keyboard, holds a charge a long time
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My son really likes this keyboard. After over a year the battery was not holding its charge like it used to - prior to the issues, it had lasted very long, like 9 months initially!  Then it started depleting very quickly.  The 2 year warranty was one of the reasons I purchased this keyboard so I was happy there were no issues when I wrote to support and they were friendly and responsive.  I will say the layout is a bit different. When I use his computer I sometimes hit the wrong keys as it is a different feel and spacing than what I am used to but he adapted quickly to it.  I am just using a basic cheap keyboard that is not ergonomic so it makes sense that the ergonomic layout would feel different to me.  Overall, I recommend it.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 8, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Arrived Battery DOA - But then something unexpected happened.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This was a one star review because the unit arrived with a batter that would not hold charge for more than a minute.  I am not changing the stars, because if you are like me, you read the one star reviews cause so many companies pay for fake 4 and 5 star reviews.When I first posted this review I also initiated a return and just planned to move on to another brand.  I was surprised when I got a personal email from the Arctek Service Team offering to send me a replacement free of charge. With nothing to lose I figured why not?The new unit arrived and I put a full charge on it and put it to work.  I chose this keyboard because it is the closest in layout to the original Microsoft ergo split keyboard, no longer in production, that I have used for years and truly enjoy.  I am pleased to report that the battery is working fine and the keyboard performs flawlessly.  No skipped strokes or stuck keys, no glitches with the proprietary wireless interface to the laptop (when I am using it on the desk with a large screen).My hat is off to the Arctek service team and management.  A company that cares enough about its reputation and customers to go to so much effort to take care of a customer with such a small dollar item sale is a company you can expect to rely on.  From now on when I want electronic gear on Amazon, I am going to use the word Arctek in my search.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on April 9, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It's quite good. The split has some keys that aren't where I'm used to, but I learned how to use it with some practice. The battery life lasts quite a while too. I've only charged it once and had it a few months, and it has an auto-shutoff after some time so it drains even less battery.I don't know how the longevity will be. The pad at the bottom is nice and helps with ergonomics, but I'm not sure how it'll last, especially because it doesn't seem to be detachable, so you can't clean or replace it. It's made of the fake leather material you see a lot in these kinds of products, so I assume eventually it'll peel and such, especially since your hands/arms will be wresting on it and transferring your skin's oils. I've already noticed some dust and dirt getting in the cracks between the keyboard and wrist rest.Other than that, I noticed one error that keeps popping up with it. When I type very quickly, sometimes the R key will double press. So when I try and write a word like "from" or "trying", it will type "frrom" or "trrying" which is quite annoying, because with my usual typing speed I will then have to go back and correct it. It seems to trigger depending on the previous key pressed (usually T or F) and also the typing speed.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Adequate But Not As Good As The Microsoft Ergonomic 4000
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I imagine many people will be asking the questions I asked before buying this keyboard. The first question is, is the Arteck as good as the Microsoft Ergonomic 4000? In a word, no. The second and third questions are, is it an adequate replacement for the 4000? Will it prevent my RSI? To which I would answer yes and probably.The reason it isn't as good as the 4000 (in my opinion) is in the first instance, the size. It is a good 30% or so smaller than the 4000 which has some benefits, like it is better to take travelling with you and will fit into a small to medium bag. However, the smaller size means that your hands aren't quite as relaxed and spread out on the keyboard. Although, it has to be said that I have rather large hands and so this might be a personal thing and anyone who found the 4000 too big in that respect, may disagree with me.The small size is an issue for me not just because of hand position but because there is less room for individual keys. So for example, the number pad on the 4000 is a separate entity and as far as I can remember does not have any important functions doubled up on the numbers. However this keyboard does not have so much room, so the 'Home' and 'End' buttons, are doubled up as the '7' and '1' keys respectively. This is less than ideal because instead of dedicated buttons that are easy to locate whilst touch-typing, the numberpad is not so instinctive to use, is not raised and is sloped away from the main keys. This means that I often have to glance down at the keyboard to use those keys (I use them a lot!) which in itself negates the advantage of touch-typing in the first place.Still on the subject of keys, their position and ease-of-use, the backspace key is also annoying. On the 4000 it is raised and positioned in such a way that you always hit the exact key you're aiming for. However, on the Arteck, the backspace key is flush with the surrounding keys and I find myself hitting the num lock key way too often for it to be a coincidence.The arrow keys (again, keys I use a lot) are not great either, they are flush with the 'ctrl' key and the 'zero' on the numberpad, therefore I am miss pressing a lot when I go to use them. As a side note the arrow keys double up as 'Home', 'End', 'Page up', and 'Page down', however these are functions so you need to hold down function whilst using them. I can't imagine any touch-typist using the keys in this way, it is cumbersome and time consuming.Now we come to the non-key part of the design. The Microsoft Ergonomic 4000 is comfortable and prevents RSI for two main reasons, one the soft pad to rest your palms on as you type. The second (more important) reason is the fact you can angle the 4000 up at the palms, so that the keyboard has a pronounced downward slope, this has the effect of putting the wrists into a more neutral and natural position. I can testify to the effectiveness of the 4000 in getting rid of RSI because it worked for me instantly, my intense wrist pain was alleviated the moment I used the 4000.The Arteck does the same thing but as in the key design, it doesn't do it as well. The 4000 has a separate piece which you attach to the underside of the keyboard, giving it around a 50mm rise height from the desk. This is cumbersome because you have two pieces instead of one; however, it is extremely effective at stopping any kind of repetitive strain.The Arteck achieves the lift by putting two small feet at the back, underside of the keyboard which raises it around 20 mm, so you can hardly notice it and my hands are nowhere near as comfy as when I use the 4000.  There are feet at the front as well and this is lucky because one of my back feet snapped off and I simply replaced it with one of the front ones, seeing as I won't ever use those.So in conclusion, what the Arteck has over the 4000 is it is bluetooth. This matters to me because I have destroyed about five different Microsoft keyboards by spilling stuff onto them, which would have been avoided in all the cases if I had simply moved my keyboard while eating my dinner, but because it was cable, I (stupidly) couldn't be bothered. Unfortunately the 4000 has rocketed in price and so hence me buying an Arteck.I suppose some people would see the smaller size as another thing the Arteck has over the Microsoft keyboard, but as mentioned above, I think it is to the Arteck's detriment as there isn't enough room on the keyboard.The 4000 has nicer feeling, better placed keys, it has more dedicated one-function-only keys that are easy to locate without looking at them. Even the small nobbles on the 'F' and 'J' keys are better on the 4000 than the Arteck.The 4000 is infinitely more comfortable (Just typing this review has got my wrist twinging a bit) than the Arteck but unfortunately it is about three and a half times the price.So if you're wondering if the Arteck is a like-for-like swap with the 4000, wonder no more, because it's not. It is adequate though and so I will carry on using it until I can afford to get a 4000 with bluetooth. The Arteck will always be my travel keyboard because lugging around the 4000 on holiday wasn't fun, but when it comes to typing at my desk, size matters and bigger is better!Hope that helps!
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United Kingdom on January 13, 2025

aPlusContent.rawText:
Product description
Industry Leading Ergonomic Design 
Stainless steel material gives heavy duty feeling and the low-profile keys offer quiet and comfortable typing. It allows you to gain quick access to common functions, such as volume level, playback control, copy paste text, and more. It also provides arrow keys, number pad with slim and compact design. 
Switch Between 3 Devices with A Single Clicking 
This keyboard is able to connect to 3 devices at the same time. After you pair the keyboard with 3 devices by long pressing the blue key at the first time, you can simply switch the keyboard to type on any of the device with a single key clicking. 
The keyboard is bluetooth, it doesn't come with a USB dongle. Your device should has built-in bluetooth. 
Cross Platform Compatible 
Fully functional to all four major operating system: IOS / Android / MacOS / Windows, and features system-specific function keys for each operating systems. Any Bluetooth supported devices such as laptop, computer, tablet, smartphone can easily be paired and gained quick access to common functions, such as volume level, playback control, copy paste text, and more. 
Comfortable, quiet typing 
The whisper-quiet, low-profile keys bring a whole new level of comfort to your fingertips. What's more, keep all your most-used functions and media controls closer than ever Windows-dedicated hot keys. Keyboard with scissors kick construction can be used more than 3 million times continuously. 
Rechargeable Battery 
Built-in industry-high rechargeable Li-polymer battery provides 6-month use on a single charge. (based on 2 hours non-stop use per day) 
2 Years Customer Care 
If you have problem to use the keyboard, you can reconnect the keyboard and the keyboard has 3 channels to change. If you still have the issue, you can contact the support team printed at the back of the keyboard as the product has 2 years customer care.

The whisper-quiet, low-profile keys bring a whole new level of comfort to your fingertips. What's more, keep all your most-used functions and media controls closer than ever Windows-dedicated hot keys. Keyboard with scissors kick construction can be used more than 3 million times continuously. 
Rechargeable Battery
