productPageReviews.reviewDescription: 4-21-22First my apologies to Artek for the delay in updating my review. I promised myself and them I would do so.After I wrote my initial review below, Arteck immediately contacted me through Amazon and offered to send me a replacement keyboard free. They sent me a code for one on Amazon and it arrived a day later. It was fully charged, which surprised me as not all of these do arrive this way. This keyboard worked amazing. No issues what so ever. It connected to all 3 of devices (my windows 10 PC, laptop and android phone) without a hitch. I've been using it non-stop since April 1st and been able to switch between all 3 devices seemlessly. There is a bit of a delay in the connection, but honestly, the 2 second delay occasionally that occurs is nothing. I've learned to adjust my habits a bit and wait and I'm good to go. I'm pretty sure most Bluetooth muliconnect keyboards suffer from this glitch... but either way I'm happy with this one.The customer service of this company alone has been outstanding and they have done everything they could to make sure I was happy. I would not only purchase this keyboard again, especially with the warranty it has, but I would purchase any product that Arteck sells and give it a chance.Initial impressions out of the box is that it's a nice looking and feeling keyboard. It doesn't feel cheap. They give you a micro USB cable to charge the keyboard with. It doesn't illuminate other than the LEDs above the buttons for multidevice.It's fairly easy to connect your devices to. Which is good, because you'll be reconnecting them often in an attempt to troubleshoot this device. I owned this product for less than a week. 3 days is all I had of a honeymoon period before it started giving me trouble. After that, it would randomly start going to sleep on me and refused to reconnect to my devices properly when it woke up. I checked all of my device settings (I'm in IT support for a living so yes I know what I'm doing). In an effort to be thorough, I even reinstalled my Bluetooth drivers on my 2 devices etc. It was a fruitless effort. This keyboard just didn't want to work properly. I even thought that it could be an issue with the distance of my pcs. Considering that both pcs were less than 5 feet from the keyboard already, I moved both of them so I was typing almost on top of them. Still problems with connecting and switching.So for the value and looks, please do be deceived. Have this company pull their stock and fix their product. Go with something a bit more established and with reviews much more positive. Returning this one and spending quite a bit more instead like I probably should have for a full sized keyboard, but I want one that works. Going for a Logitech with stellar reviews and no connection issues when it comes to PCs.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: If you want a BT full-size keyboard, this is IT!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Ok, I am super particular about keyboards! But this keyboard (Arteck HB192) delivers in all the ways I need it to. I did with this keyboard what I do with every new keyboard I get, I immediately go Google typing test and I do a typing test for a minute, usually a couple of times. I was concerned that I would get all those repetitive keystrokes I continuously read about in the reviews, but I never did - not once! I do type in the formal way, both hands - home keys, qwerty, etc. I type about 60wpm on an ergonomic mechanical keyboard (which is my preferred keyboard). On this one, I get about 4 wpm. For this particular application, used occasionally in my living room on a new mini PC, I wanted a full-size keyboard. I use Ctrl and Alt PrtScn a lot, in addition to the arrows, PgUp, PgDn, Home, End, and Delete. I am an IT professional and this is the 3rd keyboard I have gone through for this particular use case and I returned the other two for various reasons. This one has a nice keystroke travel and tactile feel - again, I never over typed not once. Furthermore, I think the build (even though I've only had it for a day) quality is impressive. It's light, yet feels strong and well made. The ability to pair 3 devices is just the coolest thing ever! I am typing on it right now while paired to my Samsung S26 phone and it's just awesome. On the primary PC which I bought it for, it does really well too. The distance - about 8/9ft - from the mini PC is not an issue. I did try two  2.4Ghz traditional wireless keyboard, and I found that they both struggled a bit with the distance and interference (there's a lot of stuff that operates in the 2.4Ghz range). With this one, I get none of that. I also like that there are indicator lights for caps lock and funtion lock - for those that this matters to, there is no indicator light for NumLk. But, being that this literally ticks every single other box for me, I'm ok with that part. I simply cannot say enough good things about this keyboard. And wow, for the price, I may just get another one just to have it around - it's a really, really great keyboard! If I could change one thing, that would be PLEASE ARTECK, get rid of the USB micro charging cable - this is such a nuisance. Make it USB A or preferably, USB C - this is what virtually everyone else is using. Oh, and one more thing. There is a power switch that allows you to turn it off and on - AND this power button LED doubles as a battery meter/indicator. If you hold and press it, you will get a series of blinks. Four blinks, the battery is fully charged/100%, 3 blinks, 75%, 2 blinks 50% etc. This is really a neat feature too. Ok, I'll stop blabbing. It's a really nice keyboard - if you're looking for a full-size Bluetooth keyboard that's not whisper quiet (it does make some sound - which I like), and is just a great keyboard all around, buy it, you will not regret it. I did pay for this on my own too, this is not a paid (or free product) review. I have it on a Windows 11 Pro, Samsung Galaxy S26, and a Lenovo Legion Tablet (Android 16). I love this thing, and I'm just totally giddy about it! :)

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Screen reader users will be annoyed
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My old Arteck 2.4ghz keyboard finally bit the dust, so I needed a new one. I saw this Bluetooth version and thought it would be great since I can pair it to my phone and iPad as well, or even my TV. Unfortunately there is a design flaw with the firmware that makes this keyboard quite annoying for screen reader users.When switching devices, the caps lock key is pressed twice upon connecting to whichever device you switched to. Normally this isn't much of an issue. The caps lock state is just toggled from one state back to the other. Add a screen reader into the mix though, and it creates quite the problem!Screen readers often use the caps lock key as a modifier. This means holding the caps lock and pressing other keys do screen reader specific functions like checking the window title, reading the current line, performing OCR on image based content and much more. Since this is the case, pressing caps lock twice quickly is what toggles the caps lock. This means that the caps lock state is changed every time I switch devices to one with an active screen reader that uses the caps lock as a modifier.I really love everything else about this keyboard. It includes the full 104 keys, typing is a breeze and the feel is really nice on a desk or even on your lap. This firmware issue is really bothersome though, so I may end up giving it to someone else that won't need to worry about this odd flaw.All in all it's a good keyboard, but screen reader users may want to look elsewhere!

This is the third keyboard I've purchased from Arteck. Not because it's a poor product. The exact opposite. I've purchased two of the smaller bluetooth keyboards to use with tablets and phones, and they've been excellent. Long time between battery charges, ability to connect to multiple devices, good key feel, good response. Overall, quality products for a really decent price.So I wanted a full size keyboard to go with my desktop, and purchased this one. It was packaged nicely and came in excellent condition. It already had a charge on the lithium battery, so I used that to do my initial BT pairing with my Dell Windows 10 Pro desktop. I've been using it for over a week now... using it at least three to four hours per day, and when I just checked it's still over 75% battery remaining.There's a little key at the top right next to the bluetooth pairing keys, and if you press it, it will flash the blue power light once for every 25% of battery remaining. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: The Ultimate 75% Mechanical Gaming Keyboard — With a Few QuirksThe Ultimate 75% Mechanical Gaming Keyboard — With a Few Quirks
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The ROG Azoth Extreme is undeniably expensive, but it’s also one of the most unique and well-built mechanical gaming keyboards I’ve ever used. If you’re already invested in the ROG ecosystem, want everything to match visually, or just appreciate high-end mechanical keyboards with an exquisite design, this one checks nearly every box. The layered aluminum and carbon-fiber construction is both visually striking and extremely solid. You can actually see the stacked layers along the side of the board, which gives it a refined, almost industrial look that feels more like a piece of art than a typical gaming keyboard.The unboxing experience alone sets the tone. Everything is neatly presented in double-layered packaging with a removable drawer underneath, and the keyboard itself comes wrapped in a branded cloth cover. It immediately feels like a premium product. Setup was flawless but did require a Armoury Crate device driver update which installed smoothly and automatically.As someone who spends hours at my computer every day and has owned many mechanical keyboards, this board offers nearly everything I look for. You get a compact 75% layout, fully customizable key assignments and macros "on-the-fly," tri-mode connectivity (RF, Bluetooth, and wired), customizable RGB, a color OLED touchscreen, a multifunction control knob, Speed Tap for gaming, a gasket-mounted design with multiple dampening layers, carbon-fiber plate, and excellent battery life. The pre-lubed ROG NX Snow linear switches feel smooth and consistent, with a controlled sound profile that isn’t overly loud, making this keyboard perfectly usable for both gaming and productivity.The included wrist rest deserves special mention. It’s heavy, well-built, and extremely comfortable, with a rubberized surface that matches the keyboard’s front profile nicely. It doesn’t slide around and feels like it belongs with the board rather than being an afterthought. On the back of the keyboard, there’s a magnetic metal nameplate that cleanly finishes the design while hiding storage for the RF dongle and the physical gasket-adjustment switch.That said, the gasket adjustment is my biggest disappointment. While it’s a great idea in theory, the difference between the two settings is extremely subtle. Neither position is labeled, and while one setting sounds slightly more “thocky” and the other a bit firmer, the change is minimal. After doing some research, it appears this is a common complaint rather than a defect.My other criticisms are fairly minor but worth mentioning at this price point. Customization relies heavily on ASUS Armoury Crate, which can be finicky, and while the Gear web app works for basic adjustments, Armoury Crate is still required for full control. The included braided cable feels surprisingly basic for such an expensive keyboard, and switch lube isn’t included despite this being marketed as a customizable, enthusiast-grade board. The magnetic metal feet work well overall, but they can slide off if you move the keyboard aggressively across a desk.Typing on this keyboard is genuinely enjoyable. The key spacing, textured PBT keycaps, and smooth switches make long typing sessions comfortable and fast. While it’s clearly marketed as a high-end gaming keyboard, I find it just as enjoyable for everyday productivity. The lack of a numpad doesn’t bother me, as everything else I need is here.If you can find the ROG Azoth Extreme below full retail pricing, I would recommend it without hesitation. At full price, it’s more of a luxury purchase that you really have to want. Remove price from the equation, though, and this is one of the best gaming keyboards I’ve ever used.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Wish I would have found this board first!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Build quality is amazing!  I took it apart to put switch pads on the pcb, but to my surprise it already had a dedicated pcb pad for the all switches and stabs!  I actually like the carbon plate (I tend to use PC), doesn't seem too stiff at all.  The Soft/Hard typing switch is interesting.  I don't see much of a difference yet, but maybe depends on the switches.  I did swap mine out with something else.  The small LCD has actually been very useful.  I love the fact that they left the top plate bare with no lcd cover or anything!  I plan on painting it now :)Yes $500 is a lot, BUT, I did buy the Glorious gmmk pro 3 for the same price and this board blows that away.  It doesn't have hall effect switches.  But for me, all the he switches I've tried were awful.  They had too much wobble, didn't always actuate, and sounded bad.  So I personally don't mind this being a non he board.  Armoury crate did act up on first use.  It kept wanting to update the same firmware over and over.  But after the last AC update, that stopped.  My only real complaint is the rgb could be a lot brighter.I really like this keyboard and love the fact that I didn't have to do any crazy mods or addons.  Everything it came with (pads, plate etc) are perfect right out of the box.  Well, minus the stabs.  They're ok but not great.  The battery life is fantastic!  My gmmk pro 3 lasted barely 2 days.  This board has gone a week and not dropped below 75%.  I'm happy with it and for me worth it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Premium build and typing feel, but not $200 better than contendersPremium build and typing feel, but not $200 better than contenders
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I picked up the ROG Azoth Extreme 75 ($500) and compared it side-by-side with the Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro 75% ($299). At this price point, you’re not paying for giant leaps in performance. Like most luxury items, the gains are real but incremental.Usage & Build:The ROG Azoth Extreme is heavier and sturdier, with tighter vertical key travel and almost no wobble. The keys feel more firmly seated in the sockets, giving a solid, precise typing experience. Key presses also have a bit more resistance compared to the Razer, which I personally enjoy since it feels more deliberate and controlled.Quick-Flip Switch & Cover Plate Gimmick:The keyboard also comes with a quick-flip toggle underneath, meant to change keystroke feel on the fly. I tested it multiple times, and if there’s a difference it’s so minor you could call it nonexistent. Honestly, it feels like another gimmick—same as the detachable magnetic feet.Then there’s the “premium” metallic cover card. You might ask: oh wow, what’s it for? Well, it’s a shiny badge that snaps over the toggle switch, so the switch feels a little cozier under the keyboard… while you’re not looking at it. That’s it. Probably got someone at ROG a promotion, but for the buyer it does absolutely nothing.Copilot Key Annoyance:One of the most frustrating design choices is that ASUS replaced the left CTRL key with a Windows Copilot key. And no, you can’t just change it in Windows. You’re forced to install ASUS’s massive, bloated Armoury Crate software just to remap it back to CTRL. They do throw in a replacement CTRL keycap in the box, but you’ll still have to manually swap the key out after fighting with the software. For a $500 keyboard, this is a ridiculous miss.Pros:• Excellent build quality, heavy and solid• Tight and precise key movement, no wobble• Typing feels fast, accurate, and premium• Slightly better feel than competitors (about 10–15% improvement)Cons:• $200 more than contenders for only minor improvements• Wrist rest has no magnets (cheaper boards include this)• Quick-flip switch does almost nothing• Metallic cover card is pointless fluff• Copilot key forces you into Armoury Crate bloatwareTips:If you’re deciding between this and other high-end boards, think about budget first. Cheaper options deliver about 85–90% of the same experience at a much lower cost.Gaming “Advantage” DUH!:Now, I will say this , after switching to the Azoth Extreme, I was suddenly unstoppable in Battlefield 6. My character was running faster than jeeps, 1v1 fights were instant wins, and the 0.00007-second faster press speed gave me cosmic precision that felt even better than the aimbot cheats I used earlier.…No, it’s not. Don’t fall for that corporate nonsense. Just pick a keyboard that feels good ergonomically. This one is very well built and feels great to type on, but it’s not going to turn you into a gaming god if you suck at it.Verdict:This is absolutely a 5-star keyboard in terms of build and typing feel, but I’m rating it 4 stars because of the weak value, poor design choices, and gimmicky extras. Honestly, it would be a strong contender if it was only $50–70 more than the competition. At $500, it’s simply not $200 better than contenders. If you want the best no matter what, you’ll love it. If you’re practical, stick with a more reasonably priced competitor and save yourself the headache (and the bloatware).

features: 96% Layout and Dual-Style Knob Design: The YUNZII B98 PRO wireless keyboard merges office efficiency with gaming versatility. It compact 96% layout packs 100-key plus a dedicated numeric pad. Customize your creamy keyboard with two unique knobs – a playful 3D cat knob or a round metal knob – easily swapped to match your style. The knob provides quick multimedia volume control by default and supports advanced customization via QMK/VIA for personalized shortcuts

QMK/VIA Custom Keyboard with RGB Backlight: B98 PRO full size keyboard with number pad, powered by open-source QMK/VIA firmware, offers deep customization for gamers and creators. Users can remap keys, record macros, and design intricate RGB lighting with 16.8 million colors (South-Facing LED). Advanced features like phrase typing and multiple layers enable the creation of complex shortcuts. Instantly save and switch between custom profiles to perfectly adapt your setup for game or work task

Tri-Mode Connectivity and Extended Battery Life: The YUNZII B98 PRO wireless gaming keyboard offers seamless tri-mode connectivity (Bluetooth 5.0, 2.4GHz, USB-C) for effortless switching across up to 5 devices and multiple systems (Windows, Mac, Android, etc.). A built-in large 8000mAh battery provides exceptionally long life, ideal for uninterrupted work and extended gaming sessions. Stay productive and immersed without worrying about frequent charging

Gasket Mount with Five Layers Filling Structure: B98 PRO mechanical keyboard features a gasket mount and five-layer filling structure that creates a uniquely creamy and premium typing feel. Its innovative design, with internal noise-dampening and a multi-layer cushioning system, absorbs harsh vibrations and eliminates hollow echoes. Combined with pre-lubed switches, tuned stabilizers, and double-shot PBT keycaps, every keystroke delivers a smooth, solid, and consistent sound profile

Hot-Swappable and Pre-Lubed Switches: Customize your flawless typing feel without soldering. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I had to replace an keyboard I only bought a year ago from Red Dragon, which I did love, but this YUNZI keyboard blows it out of the water.  The keys themselves have this nice, matte texture that feels really nice under your fingertips.  I have the "candy" variant and the noise is noticeable but still soft and muted.  It's tinny or sharp but has a nice pillowy sound.Connecting via bluetooth was very easy and I haven't had any issues with lag or the connection dropping.The only downside I've seen so far is that I'm not a biggest fan of the lighting effects, and I think my old keyboard had better options.  A lot of the effects are static and you're not able to change the color on most of them (since they're rainbow).  The cat details are something I didn't notice before purchase.  While they're cute I do feel they cheapen the product a little bit and the LED cat face under the "PgDn" key feels a little unnecessary.  However, they're subtle design elements so you can ignore them if you want, they just feel a little gimmicky.Overall, I'm very happy with my purchase! I hope this lasts a lot longer than my last keyboard!

aPlusContent.rawText:
Product description
60% Percent Gasket Mount Wired Gaming Keyboard - Black 
R65 mechanical gaming keyboard keyboard adopts a gasket structure with multiple layers of sound insulation material inside, which can effectively reduce noise and provide you with a comfortable, soft typing feel and pleasing acoustic feedback. Equipped with pre-lubed cream switches, bring you creamy, thocky sounding and excellent smooth keystroke feeling. 
This 60% percent mechanical gaming keyboard has many features such as hot swappable, dynamic RGB, volume knob, indicator lights, MDA profile PBT keycaps and QMK/VIA programable. You can enjoy the unlimited fun this gaming keyboard brings to you. 
Hot Swappable Cream Switch & MDA Profile PBT Keycaps 
Indicator Light: Equipped with three indicator lights, including Caps Lock, Win Lock, Mac OS. The status of this RGB gaming keyboard is at a glance.
3Pin/5Pin Hot Swappable: High quality PCB board compatible with 3pin/5pin switches. Compatible with 95% of keyboard switches on the market. You can have a high degree of customization
MDA Profile: Compared with ordinary keycaps, MDA Profile keycaps bring better tactile experience and better visual appearance, ergonomic design.
Custom Pre-lubed Cream Switch: This hot swappable gaming keyboard is equipped with RK's customized pre-lubricated linear cream switch, combined with gasket structure, which has creamy, thocky sounding and excellent smooth keystroke feeling.
PBT Keycap: PBT keycaps are made of double-shot technology, with a matte surface, non-fading, durability and longer service life.
Highly Customizable Programmable Gaming Keyboard 
R65 mechanical gaming keyboard supports QMK/VIA programming, you can highly customize your keyboard through VIA software, including Macro editing, RGB customization, key redefine, knob redefine, etc. 
QMK / VIA is an open source software for keyboards. You can deeply customize the keyboard functions through programming, or simply edit it through driver software such as VIA. 
VIA Website Address: usevia.app
RKR65 Layout for VIA: bit.ly/RK_QMK
Tips: Please load the layout file into VIA software first.

Enter the Layout address above and download the "RK R65 Layout for Via 508 Version" file in the folder of RK R65 Wired Version.
Enter the VIA website and connect the keyboard.
In "SETTING", turn on "Show Design Tab"

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So far so good! The sound is perfect, the lights work well, and you can customize it in so many ways! productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I want to start with how much I like the cream switches on this thing. I haven't had a ton of keyboards but this is by far the smoothest and best feeling typing experiences I have had on a keyboard. The sound dampening on this is great. Offers a (*relatively, it is still a mechanical kb and therefore not silent) quiet experience while typing. The keyboard body is surprisingly well built with nice materials and no, or none that I have noticed, flex in the board. I am not all that heavy handed while typing so that may lend to a different experience for you if you happen to type that way. I personally have always been a sucker for smaller keyboards but a 60% just misses the mark for me because it lacks the arrow keys. This being a 65% and having those plus a dedicated DEL key takes the cake for me.As great as this keyboard is, I do have a few problems with it. First, the lack of a manufacturer made software is a little disappointing. They do have some functionality with VIA but this specific keyboard is not officially supported by the makers of VIA according to the VIA website. VIA itself is a little unwieldy but does get the job done for some things. Regardless, I would like to see an officially supported software for this keyboard for those that want it (or for official support by VIA would be ok as well.) Second, the volume knob is a little mushy compared to the rest of the keyboard. It doesn't feel bad but it can definitely be better too. (This isn't as much of an issue for me considering the cost of the keyboard and the quality overall but might be a deal breaker for others). My final thing that I am not the biggest fan of is no shine through on the key caps. (Yes I am aware I can get another set of keycaps with them but I wish there was option that allowed me to pick shine through keys vs no shine through.) Having any amount of shine so that I can see what key I am pressing (sometimes I forget where a key is and I have to look to remember where it is. I am not the best typist so cut me some slack on that one) in darker conditions would be nice even if it meant that it was an option I had to choose rather than having to go and get a whole new set of keycaps.I have not tested any sort of wireless use. I use mine wired at a desktop so if you are looking for info on the battery life or wireless performance, I would keep looking.All in all, I really like this keyboard. I am pleasantly surprised with it and have already recommended it to some friends of mine. All my issues with it can easily be ignored since they are either features I don't use enough to care about or are not bad enough to care majorly about. I hope you will give this keyboard a go.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Customization support lacking, but like the keyboard overall
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Love the keyboard.  It feels nice and sounds nice.  The keys have smooth motion, but I wouldn't really call them "clicky."  They are much nicer than the nearly decade-old keyboard that I was previously using.  Even though the keyboard is small, it has good weight so that I don't need to worry about it moving around much.  This is a USB keyboard, so the only way it will disconnect is if the cable is unplugged.  It also came with four replacement key switches in case you start having sticky keys.The bad thing I will say about this keyboard that it's customization support is pretty bad.  You are supposed to be able to download a json file and plug it into the VIA software to customize your keybinds.  However, none of the json files on their website seemed to work properly.  The issue seemed to stem from the wired keyboard having a different Product ID from what was listed in the json.  It also appeared to have an issue with column numbers in the file.  I ended up editing my own version of the json file just to get it working properly... which many people will not be able to figure out.I can't post links for working json files, but if you do a web search for the keyboard type along with the correct Vendor ID and Product ID, you should be able to find a json file that works.  To find these IDs, open Edge and type " edge://usb-internals "  The devices tab should list all of your current USB devices.  Find the Product Name "RK-R65" or something similar.  That line should contain the Vendor/Product IDs.  Mine were Vendor ID 0x342D, and Product ID 0xE508.  However, there is no guarantee that these will be the same for you.  It seems there are multiple versions of this keyboard, so you have to make sure that the one you are grabbing matches your specific keyboard.All of that said, if you are just looking for a keyboard that will work out of the box, this will fit that bill.  It's just the customization portion of the keyboard that is somewhat problematic.  It sucks that you have to resort to using non-official json files in order to get the customization working properly.If you are somewhat tech savy, here is some more information about specifically what was wrong with the official json files.  The first problem was a mismatch of the Vendor/Product IDs.  The second issue was a mismatch of the line for "matrix": {"rows": 5, "cols": 15}.  Even though the keyboard physically has 15 columns, the firmware on some of the keyboards requires 16 columns.  Changing "cols:" from 15 to 16 allows the labels on the keys to line up properly.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is very well adjusted for those who have small hands and is great for typing very fast. The sound is perfect.I prefer using this over the Aula F99 keyboards because the back of the keyboard has a softer thud compared to the clicky keyboards.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: IF this is the size keyboard you need/use, this feels and works great!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I like RK's keyboards, at the price point I can keep one in the office and I'm not worried about an expensive custom keyboard being unattended 14 hours a day when I'm not there.This is very compact, and may not be what you need if you use function keys, the 10 key, or other extra keys.  It does, however, have a volume knob which I find essential for use with zoom meetings and occasional CBTs to quickly adjust the volume (or mute) without reaching up or some strange function key wigglery.This keyboard, to the average user, feels premium.  I have actual premium keyboards, and this is very comfortable for me.  The switches are responsive, again to the average keyboard user (YMMV if you're a switch snob like I am), and the keycaps have a pleasant texture.  The MDA keycap profile is spot on, and they are double-shot.  They are not shine through, but the backlighting (I keep it mono-chromatic, RGB is not my thing) is effective to accent the keys if you're not a touch typist.The cream switches are very nice, again at this price point, and I didn't feel compelled to change the switches (and I didn't).  I like the sound, but that's preference, and if you're into keyboard sounds I think these are a real cut above the average keyboard.All in all, I think this is an excellent keyboard at the price point, and better than the other 60% models I've tried around this price.  5/5!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Ok, so after spending a couple weeks with this board I can tell you-A couple of things I wasn't really aware of-1) Just how much pressure I'm used to applying at rest on keys2) How much I relied on outside esc and ctrl keys for orientationThese keys are very sensitive compared to the old BW I've used for years. I've been accidentally entering a lot of keystrokes at rest. They are very quiet and soft stroking compared to the green switches in the older Black Widow I've retired. So if you want clicks, feedback or resistance look elsewhere. Believe it or not my main hesitation for getting this board was the outside left row of programmable keys. I was afraid that it would be in the way and get confused with my escape and control keys, which yes has been very challenging to get used to, but it's no fault of the board itself knowing what I was getting. I pulled up all those caps on that row and replaced with wider pudding caps for brighter distinction. Programed those keys to mirror their neighbors, esc ,Ctrl etc so that when an erroneous keystroke is made it should at least still be the function I was looking for, albeit orientation may be off from wasd. So anyway I'm having to look down a lot more at the keyboard and retraining my mind to orient off the *F key

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Durable and well built. Survived a liquid disaster.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have the green switch version.Durable and Chroma lighting is excellent. Put O rings in the keys to dampen slightly. Key feeling and clicks are a matter of personal preference.Spilled coffee on this one twice. I thought the keyboard was toast after the last disaster spill. Keys weren't functioning and the leds were out. I took it apart and rinsed it out the affected areas heavily with alcohol. Blew the liquid out with compressed air/compressor. Works fine now.After taking it apart I could see how good the quality was. Keyboard backplate is actually solid metal.2 screws under the top two rubber foot pads. Careful, the pads tear easily.18+- screws under the keys. Remove the keys to find them all.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Had it for a bit over a week now and it's been great. I originally had the Razer blackwidow V1 with the green clicks switches and it was great the thing finally crapped out on me a few weeks ago. The thing lasted me forever, was super durable and felt very responsive. My biggest complaint was it was hard to clean. So I decided to go with the newest version and try the Yellow switches. I didn't like the softer yellow switches at first but have come to like them and this keyboard solved the cleaning issue. My biggest problem was actually the Macro keys on the left hand side. With my old keyboard I used the edge of they keyboard to orient my hand without looking when gaming, this makes it hard to do that because my fingers end up on the macro keys. I've started to retrain myself to position properly but it wasn't easy. Other than that this keyboard is fantastic.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Before I got this keyboard, I was using the 2016 edition razer blackwidow ultimate. That keyboard still works perfectly, and the only problem I had with it was that the keyboard was LOUD as heck.Enter the blackwidow v4 x with yellow switches. At first i was extremely happy with the look, feel, and materials of the keyboard, it felt very premium, and the keys were MUCH quieter.I bought it in December of 2023. By March 2024 I noticed an issue with the "P" key being unresponsive. Meaning when you press the key, there was a chance of it not registering the keypress. So if you press the key 10 times, it may only display about 5 or 6 times. Not that bad for gaming since the "P" key is hardly used. However when typing it could get very annoying. I attached a video showing me trying to press the button 3 times, followed by a space, then the button 3 times, then a space etc. You can clearly see it does not register the keypress quite often.Eventually I decided that since I paid $100+ I was going to get a working product. My RMA process started on April 20, 2024, and after many days of back and forth emails with razer trying to convince them it was a hardware, not software, issue they gave me a shipping label to send out on April 26, 2024. I received the replacement about 3 weeks later on May 17, 2024.Today on May 18, 2024 I noticed the same unresponsive key issue with the "2" key above the "W" key. This IS a big deal for gaming since it is used very often.I dont want to go through the RMA process again, and im pretty sure I cant get a refund from amazon after 4 months so this keyboard will likely just be tossed in the garbage where it belongs. A lot of time and money wasted on a sub-par product.Been using Razer keyboards and mice since about 2012 but its probably time to try a different brand to try since their quality seems to have gone down. Shame.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on May 18, 2024

In prior experience with Razer, the price is a bit up there, but I would wager its worth it.  Received on September 28th, 2025; will check back after a while to update review if needed.

breadCrumbs: Video Games > PC > Accessories > Gaming Keyboards
features: 【Tri-mode Wireless Membrane Keyboard, Multi Device Connection】: AULA S99pro v2 Gaming keyboard lights up the wireless cute keyboard and provides 3 connection modes, including Bluetooth 5.0, 2.4GHz wireless, and USB wired modes, allowing you to flexibly switch to adapt to different scenarios. It can connect up to multiple devices simultaneously and can be easily switched using the FN+key combination. Unrestricted keyboard connection improves multitasking efficiency.

【Multi Functional Application Creamy Silent Keyboards】: Fn+S enter WIN system: Fn+F1 wakes up the media player function, Fn+F2 volume-, Fn+F3 increases the volume+, Fn+F4 one click mute, Fn+F5 stops playing, Fn+F6 switches to the previous song, Fn+F7 plays/pauses, Fn+F8 switches to the next song, Fn+F9 emails, Fn+F10 returns to the main page, Fn+F11 locks the computer, Fn+F12 opens My Computer.Fn+A enter MAC system:Fn+F1: screen brightness -, Fn+F2: screen brightness+, Fn+F3: hide desktop icon, Fn+F4: search, Fn+F5: wake Siri, Fn+F6: screenshot, Fn+F7: previous track, Fn+F8: play/pause, Fn+F9: next track, Fn+F10: mute, Fn+F11: volume -, Fn+F12: volume+.

【16.8 Million Cool RGB Backlit Keyboard】: This Customization LED keyboard features 16.8 million RGB light colors, with 15 pre-set lighting effects to add a great atmosphere to the game. Lighting brightness and speed can be adjusted by the knob or the FN+ key combination. With Macro software, you can create unique lighting setups to make your rgb keyboard more interesting and create a personalized work or gaming environment.Note：Fn+←：Turn on or off lighting effects.

【97%Compact Layout, Ergonomic keyboard】: The 99-key keyboard that allows for quick switching between office and gaming use, with comprehensive functionality. Thoughtful two-stage tripod design, adjustable height in three levels, conforms to ergonomic typing posture, providing a comfortable tapping experience and built-in USB receiver storage compartment.

【4000mAh Large Battery, Long Endurance】:This Computer keyboards has a professional digital display screen with Fn+1: Bluetooth 1, Fn+2: Bluetooth 2, Fn+3:2.4 GHz modes. The corresponding indicator lights will remind you of the current mode, and there is also an intuitive battery level display.The built-in 4000mAh battery delivers extended battery life for uninterrupted work and gaming.

【Cool LED TFT Digital Keyboard with Screen & number pad】Stay in the know at a glance. The built-in LED display puts essential keyboard info right in front of you—no more guessing or digging through settings. Check battery status so you never get caught off guard mid-task. See which connection mode you're in (2.4G, Bluetooth, or wired) for seamless switching between devices. The screen also displays real-time keyboard status, lighting effect updates, and Num Lock status, so you always know exactly what's happening at a glance. It's smart, simple, and keeps you focused on your work, not your keyboard.

【Silent Membrane Wireless keyboard】：Work without the noise. The S99 Pro V2 features a whisper-quiet silent membrane design that absorbs keystroke sounds, so you can type all day in a shared office or open workspace without disturbing anyone. No loud clicks, no distractions—just smooth, responsive keys with a soft, cushioned feel that keeps your fingers comfortable during long typing sessions. The clean White/Green/Red colorway adds a polished look to any desk. Professional, quiet, and effortless to use.

Note:We fully understand the importance of product quality. During the injection molding process, all ABS products are treated with food-grade or industrial-grade release agents to ensure they demold completely. As a result, the surface of new products may feel slightly oily. We recommend wiping the surface with a soft cloth and a small amount of isopropyl alcohol before use or a specialized plastic cleaner before use.

1 Products Hightlights 2 Function&Material Detail 3 Tri-Modes Connection 
Quiet & Creamy Membrane Structure Computer keyboard 
Wireless membrane gaming keyboard, near-silent with creamy sound and solid tactile feedback. Ideal for open offices, late-night gaming, and focused work. 
Quiet yet tactile membrane keyboard with ergonomic design, reducing wrist strain. Dual-mode connectivity (BT/2.4GHz) for seamless device switching. Vibrant RGB lighting, 4000mAh battery for extended use. Compatible with Windows & macOS – perfect for office and gaming. 
Two Angle Kickstand 
The adjustable Ergonomic Keyboard Stand has 2 adjustable height level and can make users adjust the keyboard tilt according to their own requirements. 
Tri Modes Side Function Keys 
Support BT 3.0/5.0,2.4GHZ wireless and USB-C wired connection.Users can quickly switch between connection modes using the mode switch on the side. 
Compatible with Mac & Win 
This Bluetooth keyboard is compatible with Mac,Windows,laptops,tablets,and desktops,and can adapt to any workflow. 
4000mAh 
The large battery capacity increases the battery life in wireless mode.Please note that don't use a fast charging cable to charge this keyboard. 
What kind of wireless keyboard, and is it good for gaming? 
This is a membrane keyboard with a mechanical-style design. It provides a mechanical keyboard like appearance and a creamy feel, and supports wired and 2.4GHz wireless modes,making it perfect for quiet typing and casual gaming. 
Can I charge while using it? 
For sure,We strongly support using USB cables during use, as the keyboard's response speed is the fastest and most convenient in wired mode 
Can I turn off the lights and adjust brightness or color? 
Yes, you can turn off or on the lighting effects by short pressing the fn+backspace key, and switch between lighting effects by pressing fn+| \ key 
Is it hot-swappable? Can I change the switches? 
We're sorry, because this is a membrane keyboard, so the switches cannot be replaced and hot-swappable 
Does it have programmable keys? 
The F99Pro V2 keyboard is not equipped with dedicated software, so custom key functions, macro settings, and personalized backlight customization are not supported.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Worth 60 bucks easy, on sale it's an absolute bargain.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I ordered one of these after my place of employment got tired of keyboards failing constantly. After several months of outright abusive use by my co-workers, they still performed flawlessly with a lovely sense of tactile feedback, soda spills aside. One failed only after half a thermos of coffee was spilled into it, but that's to be expected from anything not waterproof rated.After ordering one for myself to use at home, I LOVE typing on it. It's my first true mechanical keyboard, and it's pleasant to just tap away, typing whatever I feel like. Each key feels like it's got two levels of depression (almost like me): First a clear 'catch' when the key activates and types, and then another more firm one when you reach the bottom of the key well. I've yet to have it double-type anything even when my clumsy fingers wanted to, although it hasn't saved me from butterfingering my keystrokes in games.As far as gaming goes, it's not PERFECT. It does make an audible noise when typing, so when you are frantically spamming the strafe or jump keys, it's going to sound like clicking the mouse over and over, but it's really no worse than your average mouse. If you're wearing headphones and blasting your speakers, you won't notice it. If you're in a silent small room, you can't avoid hearing it. Find your medium.Its clearly more meant for office work, but I find it good for gaming, and it's sturdy and heavy enough it doesn't move around at all or feel like it'll die if I drop my phone on it.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This was my first mechanical keyboard, but not the first one I've typed on.After using it for several weeks I have come to the conclusion that it is worth the $45 or $50 they charge. The keys feel nice, and the switches have a noticeable "bump" in each key press. It isn't too loud, which was a necessity for me as I game and type late at night, and clicky key switches get very annoying after a short time. The plate that the switches are mounted to is made of aluminum, so the board feels very solid and has almost no flex. I bought a slightly different version of this keyboard for my mother a few years ago, and hers is still working perfectly fine. The SE version that I have, has better key switches (Longhua Browns) than hers does (Logitech Romer G) as far as feel goes, and uses the standard cherry mx style, so most keycaps will fit this keyboard if you wish to change the look of your keyboard.I did do two mods, (tape mod, lubricated stabilizers) and that significantly improved the sound, it's less clacky and has a nice pop sound to it now. Highly recommend doing that if you buy this keyboard. I will say, this keyboard is NOT hot swappable, so changing the switches would require a soldering iron and patience. I plan to install hot swap sockets from mill-max so I can try different switches in this keyboard down the line. On a side note, you do have to take all of the keys off and remove several small screws in the aluminum plate to take it apart, so a switch puller is handy to have around. The plastic base cannot be filled with foam unless you choose to dremel out the support beams. I don't recommend doing this unless you know what you are doing as it may cause the keyboard to become less sturdy.All in all, it's excellent for the price and will work for gaming and casual typing and usage.

Overall it works as advertised and seems to be of solid construction and is worth the money just wish the backlight was dimmable.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I am using this keyboard right now to type this review. I got one of these for work, and I like it so much I bought another one for home. The brown switches have tactile feedback, but no audible click. The feel and sound of these keys while typing is very satisfying. This keyboard is a bit noisy, but I haven't heard any complaints about that so far. I much prefer this mechanical keyboard to my old membrane keyboards. I am still getting used to it, so I make a few typos, but the frequency of them is diminishing. Build quality is excellent, the chassis is aluminum. There is no pointless, annoying RGB backlighting. Only the keys light up, which makes it easy to use in the dark. I would recommend this keyboard. It's more expensive than membrane keyboards, but I think it's worth the extra money.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: I liked it so much I used it to write this review!
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I wanted to wait a couple months before writing this review, give myself time to decide my opinion.Well, I would say it is excellent, one can usually rely on Logitech to provide a good product and this is a prime example.The noise level is not the loudest I have heard from mechanical keyboards. Besides, if you want the responsiveness of a mechanical keyboard, you have to expect and accept a certain level of click-clack.I use it mostly to play games and secondly to write stories, as such it works well. While I do not play professionally, or online, nor care to, during my usage I have not noticed any lag or ghosting.In particular, I like the while lighting, it is not strong, but not weak either, allowing me to see the keys in any lighting situation. Which I appreciate, as the popular RGB keyboards are a bit too "loud" for me.It is also very tight and small for a mechanical, and fits comfortably on a small desk.I highly recommend this keyboard!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great Feel, Fun Design, and Packed With Features
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Comic keycaps look great in person. They're bright, crisp, and a fun break from the usual black‑and‑grey setup I was rocking previous. The switches feel smooth and consistent, with a satisfying sound that isn’t overly loud like I was worried about. Weird to say, but the sounds is almost nostalgic, unfortunately, I can't place from when. Typing feels smooth, there  is resistance so it feels like you're properly pushing a key, but it's not so much that  it ruins the flow if you are typing quite a bit, for instance this review. The frame/case/board together has a solid weight to it that keeps it from sliding around the desk. It does help that there are rubber feet on each of the leg types. While the case is plastic and feels a bit cheap to the touch, when you hold it/lift it, it really  does feel premium and solid.The three‑mode connectivity works exactly as expected. Switching between Bluetooth, 2.4GHz, and wired is quick, and the connection stays stable. Something to note is that the bluetooth and 2.4GHz modes will go into a 'sleep' mode after a certain amount of inactivity. You'll press a few keys, this will take the keyboard up (backlight illuminates), then your computer will recognize/respond as expected. I am currently using all three of the connection types, to replace needing a second keyboard. I have 2.4GHz connected to my Surface Pro 7+, direct connect to my personal machine, and bluetooth to my work laptop. It's nice to reduce the clutter of my remote set up.One the hardest things for me has been getting used to the 75% layout. It takes a good amount of time for the adjustment if you’re used to full‑size/10-key boards. A few niceties have been the directional keys being intact and the PgUp/PgDn buttons sitting above them. The volume knob is placed well and has a clean click for mute and volume control.The small LCD screen is more useful than I expected. It shows battery, connection mode, and system info at a glance, and you can upload a GIF or image if you want to personalize it. The software is straightforward enough for adjusting RGB, macros, and the screen settings and I didn't get any pop up from defender when I was using it.Hot‑swappable switches are a nice bonus. You can drop in 3‑pin or 5‑pin options without soldering, which makes this a good starter board for anyone curious about customizing later. RGB lighting is bright with plenty of effects, and the gradient‑injected keycaps let the colors show through nicely without feeling cheap.Battery life has been solid so far, especially on Bluetooth. After a week of 8-10 hour daily usage, I'm sitting at about 65% - this includes switching to the other machines and having it plugged-in for short bursts when I need to tinker on my personal machine. The default state for the keyboard is Bluetooth for me.I think my only gripe has been that there is no matching mouse for the keyboard.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this keyboard and mouse combo after my old wired setup finally gave up the ghost — rest in spaghetti, never forgetti. Setting it up was shockingly easy: plug in the USB receiver, turn on the devices, and boom — my fingers were back in business within 30 seconds. No driver downloads, no angry tech support calls, no sacrifices to the computer gods.The keyboard has a satisfying, clicky-but-not-obnoxious typing feel. My coworkers on video calls have not yet complained, which I consider a raving success. The full-sized layout means I actually have a number pad again, and I've rediscovered my long-lost ability to type numbers without slowly hunting them down across the top row like some kind of keyboard archaeologist.The mouse is comfortable in the hand and the adjustable DPI is a genuinely useful feature — low for precise work, high for when you want your cursor to teleport across three monitors like it's late for a meeting. Battery life has been solid so far; I've forgotten to turn it off multiple times and it's still going strong.A few minor gripes: the mouse scroll wheel is a tad stiff, and the keyboard could use a bit more wrist support for long sessions.Bottom line: it does exactly what a keyboard and mouse should do, and it does it without drama. Solid buy for home, office, or anyone tired of being tethered to their desk like a golden retriever on a leash.

description: TRIPLE THREAT POWERED BY QUICKSET — Apex Pro is the only line of keyboards in the world featuring Rapid Trigger, Rapid Tap, and Protection Mode (Patent Pending), automatically activated for your game in seconds with GG QuickSet auto-presets that load pro-level configs instantly. Rapid Trigger enables faster actions by resetting keys the moment you release them for ultra-responsive inputs, while Rapid Tap prioritizes your latest key press without requiring release, allowing faster strafing, peeking, and dodging. Protection Mode is a Patent Pending feature exclusive to SteelSeries which reduces accidental keypresses on surrounding keys—no more accidental ults—so you can stay precise under pressure. The OmniPoint 3 analog magnetic Hall Effect switches deliver 40 adjustable actuation levels from 0.1 mm to 4.0 mm with a 45g bottom-out force, offering unmatched customization for both fast-paced gaming and deliberate typing, with up to 20x faster actuation and 11x faster response times. A built-in OLED Smart Display lets you adjust settings, view info, and control media (Play/Pause/Skip) without leaving your game, with all configurations saved onboard. Built for performance and durability, Apex Pro features Double Shot PBT keycaps that resist fading, per-key lubrication for smoother and quieter keystrokes, a premium aluminum top plate for long-lasting strength, and triple-layer sound dampening foam to reduce noise and vibration. Complete your setup with per-key RGB illumination and Prism Sync support to customize and synchronize lighting across devices.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Unreal feel and performance — my new go-to gaming keyboardUnreal feel and performance — my new go-to gaming keyboard
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I recently upgraded to this keyboard and I honestly don’t see how anyone could give it anything less than 5 stars. My previous keyboard was a fully mechanical unit with Cherry MX Brown switches, so I had a good benchmark—and this one absolutely stands out.The keystrokes are super fast and precise—if you’ve ever watched keyboard ASMR videos and thought “I want that,” this is it.Gaming performance is fantastic. Every input feels responsive, smooth, and satisfying. Uses USB-C  for modern, reliable connection.One of the killer features is the adjustable actuation pressure: I can dial in exactly how far I need to press a key  (0.1mm to 4.0 mm) range, and that significantly reduces accidental key-presses.The lighting quality is excellent. The customizable RGB effects are rich and make it easy to match the keyboard to any build or desk setup.The form factor and build feel premium: the tenkeyless layout keeps things compact (my desktop is less cluttered) and the materials feel incredibly solid.I’m completely sold on this keyboard! It is the perfect fir for those who heavily type for long hours or a gamer looking to maximize their setup.Overall rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)In my experience, this keyboard delivers an exceptional blend of feel, responsiveness, customization, and build quality. If you’ve been looking for a keyboard that not only works great but feels great to use every day—this is one of the best I’ve tried.

features: Tri-mode Connection Keyboard: AULA F75 Pro wireless mechanical keyboards work with Bluetooth 5.0, 2.4GHz wireless and USB wired connection, can connect up to five devices at the same time, and easily switch by shortcut keys or side button. F75 Pro computer keyboard is suitable for PC, laptops, tablets, mobile phones, PS, XBOX etc, to meet all the needs of users. In addition, the rechargeable keyboard is equipped with a 4000mAh large-capacity battery, which has long-lasting battery life

Hot-swap Custom Keyboard: This custom mechanical keyboard with hot-swappable base supports 3-pin or 5-pin switches replacement. Even keyboard beginners can easily DIY there own keyboards without soldering issue. F75 Pro gaming keyboards equipped with pre-lubricated stabilizers and LEOBOG reaper switches, bring smooth typing feeling and pleasant creamy mechanical sound, provide fast response for exciting game

Advanced Structure and PCB Single Key Slotting: This thocky heavy mechanical keyboard features a advanced structure, extended integrated silicone pad, and PCB single key slotting, better optimizes resilience and stability, making the hand feel softer and more elastic. Five layers of filling silencer fills the gap between the PCB, the positioning plate and the shaft,effectively counteracting the cavity noise sound of the shaft hitting the positioning plate, and providing a solid feel

16.8 Million RGB Backlit: F75 Pro light up led keyboard features 16.8 million RGB lighting color. With 16 pre-set lighting effects to add a great atmosphere to the game. And supports 10 cool music rhythm lighting effects with driver. Lighting brightness and speed can be adjusted by the knob or the FN + key combination. You can select the single color effect as wish. And you can turn off the backlight if you do not need it

Professional Gaming Keyboard: No matter the outlook, the construction, or the function, F75 Pro mechanical keyboard is definitely a professional gaming keyboard. This 81-key 75% layout compact keyboard can save more desktop space while retaining the necessary arrow keys for gaming. Additionally, with the multi-function knob, you can easily control the backlight and Media. Keys macro programmable, you can customize the function of single key or key combination function through F75 driver to increase the probability of winning the game and improve the work efficiency. N key rollover, and supports WIN key lock to prevent accidental touches in intense games

Multi-function Control Knob: This AULA 75% wireless gaming keyboard is equipped with functional knob to switch gaming mode or office mode. In gaming mode, you can rotate the knob to adjust the brightness of the lights, and click the knob to switch the lighting effects easily; in office mode, rotate the knob to adjust the volume, and click the knob to play or pause. Long press the knob for about 5 seconds to switch modes

Side-Prined PBT Keycaps: Side-prined keycap keyboard are currently a new trend worldwide. These side-engraved PBT keycaps take double injection molding and heat sublimation process, which are more durable without fading, sweat-proof, and softer to the touch, allow the keyboard's light to shine through fonts. Compared with traditional keyboard, this side-prined keyboard can bring you a very different keyboard using experience. For the color of the keycaps, we choose gradient black color to make the whole keyboard looks cool and stylish

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this during prime day so I paid less than 70 bucks for it and it is probably worth over $100. I am very satisfied with this purchase.I originally bought it for my work computer but I was torn because it didn't come with the numbers pad And I use the numbers pad heavily for my job, but I was so attracted to the keyboard I ended up purchasing it anyway with a spare generic numbers pad which was a great investment.Then I realized it had multiple inputs. It is Bluetooth, It is wired, and it has a wireless dongle and so I said to myself, "hey I can plug this in both my work PC and my personal PC!" So I use the cord for my personal PC and the dongle for my work PC and all I have to do is flip the switch on the back of the keyboard to toggle between modes. It cleared up the clutter on my desk because I no longer have two keyboards for both my PCs.I'm a writer so I'm very attracted to the creamy sound and I added a video of one solid minute of me writing. I'm not pressing random buttons I'm actually typing in a word document lol.The appearance is very sleek I am very fond of the front facing letters and I don't have to worry about them getting worn out the more I use it.So far the quality and performance is great I will say with the dongle there's like a very very slight delay in terms of copying and pasting which is why I put the dongle into my work PC because I am also a gamer and I can't have the delay. So far I've played several games of OverWatch and have not had an issue with either the dongle or the wired connection in my personal PC because I originally did it with the dongle. So if you prefer to have the dongle in your gaming PC, you won't have any issues with delay.It's about as heavy as a regular cherry keyboard. me personally I like the weight to it. I keep my gaming mouse weighted as well but that's just me.I like the versatile knob on the right hand corner of the keyboard. It changes the modes of the lights on the keys and if you press and hold it it will change to volume So that was super convenient.I read another review that said the driver's contained malware so I was a little wary to download them however with all of the modes that the lights have, I don't believe I'll need to download anything for this keyboard.So far it's a solid five stars!!! productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The keyboard feels solid and sounds much better than I expected for the price. The keys are smooth, the compact 75% layout saves desk space, and it still keeps the function row and arrow keys. The wireless connection was easy to set up, and switching between devices has been convenient.The RGB lighting looks good without being too bright, and the battery has lasted well with the lights turned down. The software could be a little easier to use, but I did not need it for basic settings. Overall, it is a comfortable and good-looking keyboard for gaming, work, and everyday use.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great for both work and gamingGreat for both work and gaming
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this keyboard after spending some time looking for a wireless mechanical keyboard that I could use for both work and gaming, and I’m really happy with my purchase.What I like most is the feel of the keys when typing and the sound. It has that characteristic mechanical keyboard sound that is very satisfying without becoming annoying when I’m working for several hours. I also think the 75% size is perfect: it takes up much less space on my desk without sacrificing the keys I actually use.I also really like the way it looks. It feels stylish, solid, and much more polished than I expected. The wireless connection has worked very well, and being able to switch between devices is really convenient.I mainly use it for work and do a lot of typing, so it was important to me that it be comfortable as well as nice-looking, and so far it has completely met my expectations.When I bought it, I didn’t realize that the letters were printed on the front of the keycaps rather than on top. It only took me a few hours to get used to it, though, and now I actually like it because I think the lettering may wear off more slowly.The only thing I didn’t like is that it doesn’t have a dedicated “Home” key. It has an “End” key, but not “Home.” That said, the software makes it incredibly easy to remap keys and customize their functions, so it works perfectly for me anyway.I also like that you can choose from several colorful lighting effects, although I usually keep the lights turned off because I find them a little distracting while working. The keyboard is somewhat heavy, so I would consider it more of a desk keyboard than something you would want to carry around, which is completely fine for my use.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: 10/10 would buy another one, perfect gift
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The AULA F75 Pro isn’t just a keyboard — it’s a life upgrade. From the moment I unboxed it, I knew this thing was built different. The build quality feels premium in a way that makes everything else on my desk feel insecure. The weight, the finish, the layout — chef’s kiss.But the sound? Oh man… pure mechanical ASMR. Every keystroke is a buttery, creamy “thock” that makes typing feel less like a task and more like a treat. It’s so smooth and satisfying I found myself typing things I didn’t even need to type — emails, notes, grocery lists, lorem ipsum paragraphs — just to hear it sing.Key layout & switch orientation: One thing I absolutely love is how the keys are south-facing, sitting slightly inward instead of pointing outward toward you. It gives the whole board a cleaner, sleeker look and makes the RGB shine through in a softer, more premium way.Wireless performance: flawless. Zero lag, zero hiccups, zero drama. It connects instantly and stays rock-solid whether I’m gaming, working, or just vibing on YouTube comments.Battery life: absurdly good. I swear this thing runs on wizard energy because I keep checking the percentage and it keeps refusing to go down.RGB: The lighting is vibrant without being over-the-top, and the multi-function knob makes switching effects, brightness, and colors stupidly satisfying. One smooth twist and you can go from a calm ambient glow to full-on gamer neon. It’s intuitive, responsive, and makes controlling the RGB feel extra premium without the need of a software which is a plus.Overall? This keyboard is elite. Legendary. A masterpiece of clicky, thocky engineering. If you want something that feels incredible, sounds incredible, and looks incredible, the AULA F75 Pro is the one. I absolutely, genuinely loved this product.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on December 9, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'm impressed. Coming from a 4 year old Corsair mechanical keyboard with cherry mx switches, I had high hopes that this keyboard would get the job done. It lacks dedicated media keys, but you still have media keys by using the function key.The battery is excellent to start; I hope it lasts just as long as my Corsair did. The weight is a little beefy despite it being mostly plastic and thicc. The size is perfect if you intend to use it on your lap or TV tray. There are many different LED modes as well, which is nice, as well as the fact that you can set these modes without having to install some sort of app to control them.While I primarily use the 2.4 connection, I do like the fact that it supports 3 bt devices. The response rate is very good and on par with the Corsair. You will have to get used to the arrow key layout with end, pg up, pg dn, and delete being in one single vertical row.Probably the most intriguing thing that made me want to even look at it was the front etched keys, which were perfect for my use case. I usually rest the keyboard on a shelf slightly higher than my shoulder when I sit so the keyboard is closer to my eye level than my hands. These keys make it easier to quickly see and press some custom commands I have instead of having to pick up the keyboard, sit it on my lap or tray, and then use my commands.The key presses are also very muted from the cherry mx switches, which is a plus and slightly more satisfying.Overall, I'm Impressed.(update as of 3-15-26)Nearly a year later, the battery's lifespan has decreased to about 50% of its original capacity.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on May 6, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’m honestly really impressed with the AULA F75 Pro Wireless Mechanical Keyboard. Right out of the box, it feels like a premium product. The build quality is solid and has a nice weight to it, so it stays firmly in place and doesn’t slide around during use.One of my favorite things about this keyboard is the sound. The clicking is super satisfying without being overly loud—it just has that perfect mechanical feel that makes typing enjoyable.The RGB lighting is another standout feature. At first, I didn’t realize there was software available, but once I found the link at the bottom of the product page and installed it, the level of customization blew me away. You can really dial in the exact colors and effects you want.Overall, this keyboard exceeded my expectations. Great feel, great sound, and excellent customization options. Definitely a solid buy.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: So, awesome I’m jealous!So, awesome I’m jealous!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this keyboard for my husband and switched the keycaps to fit his aesthetic as well as so he can read a bit better. (He’s new to the computer club used to be console and he’s got bad eyesight from the military.) so in the picture the keycaps are changed but not the switches! The original keycaps it comes with is a grey with the letters, symbols, and words on the side.Even though I swapped them out I want to state they are absolutely excellent quality, super soft matte feel, and low profile. I kept the keycaps for future use instead of tossing them or offering them up to my family.Which is what I usually do with manufactured keycaps. So, that’s how good they are! That and they honestly are an absolutely gorgeous color in person despite just being greytones.Now onto more of the benefits this keyboards the forth of fifth I’ve customized (I just customize as a hobby for friends and family)This one though is the first of this brand and oh my gosh do I regret not buying this brand sooner! Mainly for myself because of all the bonuses with this keyboard. Haha.Firstly, the keyboard came in awesome packaging and when I realized it can be used wirelessly too! Absolutely fantastic! I didn’t check for that before purchasing so it was a super awesome surprise!And the quality too my husband has absolutely loved getting to use his new keyboard and he got so giddy with the RGB too.I feel like building wise too this is a great keyboard for beginners. If you want a nice keyboard that has easy hot-swappable capabilities this is definitely where to start!And the volume button is such a bonus too. It makes accessibility count with this keyboard. That along with how compact it is too it takes such little space. To put into retrospect his desk is only I think 38 inches width and he still has plenty of room on each side of his desk for his snacks and drinks because of how little space the keyboard is.Literally no issues have come from the keyboard, it even with his wonky usb ports (a custom built computer composed of old/used parts.) it works well and doesn’t have any connectivity issues.So, to put all the perks together:-compact and comfortable-easy to swap keycaps around and switches—switches it came with are the perfect click for those who don’t like it to be an overbearing sound.—perfect for beginners of customizing keyboards.-Volume nob to control volume with easy access rather than fighting around your desk to get to the speaker control.-has wired, Bluetooth, and dongle capabilities which cleans up wire management.— Battery life is great so charging doesn’t happen as often and it lasts even longer with rgb turned off.- I almost forgot: also, has amazing presets of rgb colors that are fun and is perfect for zoning out to when you are having writers or artist block.Now, for the jealousy caption. I need to save up to get me one too! Because, this keyboard is everythingggg and I am definitely in need of an upgrade from my wired keyboard as well as all the perks of this keyboard.Definitely, looking forward to customizing one for myself down the line! This company is for sure my go too for keyboards. I highly recommend!For now I’ll just enjoy seeing the smile on my husband’s face every time he looks at his keyboard while we game together! The best Christmas purchase I’ve ever made!

description: The CORSAIR K55 RGB PRO Gaming Keyboard lights up your desktop with vibrant five-zone dynamic RGB backlighting and powers up your gameplay with six easy to set up dedicated macro keys. Six Dedicated Macro Keys: Activate functions, shortcuts, or keypresses in just one stroke with six dedicated macro keys, easily set up through CORSAIR iCUE software, or use instant streaming commands through Elgato Stream Deck software.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Super satisfying milky/creamy switches and cute aesthetic! Very customizable too!Super satisfying milky/creamy switches and cute aesthetic! Very customizable too!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've purchased three different Yunzii keyboards and they are all super nice quality with a lovely sound! We have the IF99, the B75, and I purchased the B68 for my daughters gamer friend for her birthday. Both girls and myself love these keyboards! The cocoa cream switches are such a satisfying switch to type on! They are definitely that creamy "thock" kind of sound (video in review) and they have a nice smooth tactile touch to them. The Yunzii software needed to customize the lighting is easy to use and install though it lacks some of the more in depth customization options that my Logitech G-Hub and Razer Synapse software has. But for a simple color scheme change, its sufficient. You can connect with either your computer's built in bluetooth, wireless with the included receiver, and via USB-C cable. The keyboard comes standard with the ESC, Spacebar, and directional keys in the purple tone. But you can swap these out to the included pink keys. They also include a removable tool for ease of use. This keyboard is also hot-swappable meaning you can remove the actual switches and install a different switch if you want a different tactile feel or sound. The knob in the top right corner can be macroed to whatever function you desire but makes a great volume knob! Other keys can also be macroed. The LED backlight isn't super bright which I am disappointed in. Wish it could go just a bit brighter. I'd eventually like to get their pudding keycaps so I can see the backlight a little better. The backlight turns off after a period of inactivity to save battery power. It's a nice size and while I miss having the ten-key on the side, this takes up much less space on my desktop and makes it easier to type on my lap. Overall this is phenomenal keyboard for the price and I  will start recommending these to all of my gamer buddies!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this during a sale and I fell in love as soon as I saw it and tried it out. I’ve been waiting for a while to purchase my first keyboard, and I’m glad to have found this. I wish they had more colorways so I can recommend it to everyone.I got the pink, purple, and white one and it’s very pretty. It comes with instructions, and a keyboard cover. Also, if you’re forgetful, the digital guide is available online haha. There are so many useful keyboard shortcuts, and you can easily switch from mac to windows keyboard layout. The rgb light on the keyboard is customizable. I like that it’s easily connectable and easily switches from one device to another with a press of a couple buttons. It has good weight to it, the sound is very nice for the price. I would say that it’s a mixture of creamy/clacky (more creamier compared to the milky switches), and the spacebar is creamy/thunky. It is loud, so I wouldn’t recommend it in at a work office setting. But, if you’re looking for a satisfying sound for your home-use, I recommend this. I got the cocoa cream v2 keys and the video in the product description is spot on!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: This is literally the keyboard of my dreams. Very creamy, no latency, super cute, and durable. 10/10
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I cannot express how much I LOVE this keyboard. It is literally perfect. Creamy sounding switches (coco cream v.2), a decent weight, so it won’t be moving around on the desk. It also comes with some extra keys if you want to switch them out for designs instead of the letters. I love that the right side of the keyboard has a heart design on the keys. It’s the perfect size, not too big or bulky, but also not cheap and small. This keyboard feels like I spent hundreds on it. It also comes with a clear plastic cover, to keep your keyboard dust free. The RGB works great, the volume knob is very satisfying to use. It is very durable, doesn’t feel cheap or like it’ll break. The legs have 3 height options, making it a great option for comfort. Overall, I would recommend this keyboard to anyone looking for a cutesy, creamy, durable and very effective keyboard, without breaking the bank. I also wanna mention, I game pretty heavily, and have had 0 latency problems with it. It can be used both cordless and corded, just based on your preference. I literally love my keyboard so much.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this keyboard after a short of an out-of-the-box soundtest for it came across my feed..... I don't exactly know all the terms for the sounds of keyboards, but this thing SOUNDS way more expensive than I bought it for (on sale for $69 huehuehue.) The video called it 'thocky'.... which I guess it could be, though it doesn't have as deep of a sound with stock switches (Cocao Cream V2) as it did with the AKKO Rosewood switches I quickly tested on it. It sounds creamy or bubbly to me. I've been looking for a keyboard with a 'deeper' sound and this was very pleasantly surprising straight out of the box with a fairly deep, buttery 'clack'. I was very surprised that this was RGB with several really neat presets including the one where the lights only light up where you type and fade slowly, so you get the really cool waterfall-light effect when you run your finger down the keys. It is also fairly heavy, at least heavier than I was expecting buying (what I consider?) an inexpensive keyboard.
