productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent Wireless Mechanical Gaming Keyboard With Great Battery Life—Just Two AnnoyancesExcellent Wireless Mechanical Gaming Keyboard With Great Battery Life—Just Two Annoyances
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: For context, I previously owned the wired Redragon K580 PRO with Brown switches, and I currently use the Blue-switch version at work. I have always liked these keyboards. They include dedicated media keys, a volume roller, built-in RGB lighting, and programmable macros that can be saved directly to the keyboard without keeping software installed.Because of that, buying the wireless version to reduce the number of cables on my desk was an easy decision. I do not regret it. These keyboards offer a lot of features for their price.My biggest complaint is that the volume roller does not work while the keyboard is asleep. I have to press the “-”  button on the number pad to wake the keyboard before I can adjust the volume. This is annoying because I frequently change the volume while watching YouTube. I have gotten used to the workaround, but I still consider it a significant design flaw as every other key works in sleep.I immediately replaced the included Red switches with Kailh White Pro switches. These have an actuation force similar to Brown switches but also provide a softer click similar to Blue switches. For me, they offer the best of both worlds.So I cannot fairly review the included Red switches. However, Redragon’s Brown and Blue switches have both been excellent for the price, so I have no reason to think the Red switches would be poor quality.The keyboard does not require software for normal use, but I recommend installing the software at least once. After saving your settings to the keyboard, you do not need to leave the software installed or running. The software allows you to customize the RGB lighting and change the sleep timer. The timer can be set from 1 to 10 minutes and is set to 3 minutes by default. The keyboard enters a deeper standby mode after about 30 minutes.Waking the keyboard is extremely fast. Even after leaving it unused for an entire day, I can sit down and immediately start typing without losing the first few keystrokes.The sleep timer has a major effect on battery life due to RGB lighting, I changed mine to 1 minute.Another downside is the low-battery warning. When the battery reaches approximately 30%, the RGB lighting turns off and the lock indicator lights flash whenever the keyboard wakes up. I wish the software allowed users to change this warning level. I would set it to 10%, because most people will probably charge the keyboard soon after the warning begins anyway.The keyboard includes a high-quality six-foot braided USB-C-to-USB-A cable. Using a powered USB hub, it takes approximately two hours to charge fully from 0% while the keyboard is not being used.When connected by USB, it functions almost exactly like the wired Redragon K580 PRO.The Bluetooth works great, and it has 3 profiles, I use 2 of them, one for my Laptop and one for my tablet and I have never had an issue connecting.Battery LifeThere was very little detailed battery information available when I purchased this keyboard, so I tested it under several different settings. These results are approximate and will vary depending on usage.The two settings that have the largest effect on battery life are:1. RGB brightness, which has four brightness levels plus an off setting.2. The sleep timer, which is set to 3 minutes by default.My RGB setup uses two solid colors without any animated effects.During my first test, I used maximum RGB brightness and the default 3-minute sleep timer. My usage was fairly light: adjusting the volume, entering website addresses, writing YouTube comments, asking AI questions, and doing other basic typing.Under those conditions, the keyboard lasted approximately two weeks before reaching 30% battery. I charged it once the low-battery warning began.For my second test, I changed the sleep timer to 1 minute and lowered the RGB lighting to its minimum brightness. With approximately the same type of light usage, the keyboard lasted a full 30 days and still had 70% battery remaining. When I started playing a game the battery life dropped pretty fast. It was about 30 hours from 70% to a dead charge which is about the same as a wireless controller.Gaming battery life is naturally much shorter because the keyboard stays awake almost constantly.I then tested with RGB completely disabled and the timer to 1 minute and to no surprise the battery life is long. This test had moderately high usage of playing the same video game for another 30 hours and typing some documents for my job and after a full 30 days I am at 70%. If you do not care about RGB the battery life is very high.Final ThoughtsThis is not a basic Logitech keyboard that can run for two years on a pair of AA batteries. It is a full-size wireless mechanical keyboard with RGB lighting, media controls, macros, and replaceable switches.The volume roller issue and the aggressive 30% battery warning are frustrating, but neither one is a deal-breaker for me.If you want RGB and you set the sleep timer set to 1 minute and the RGB brightness kept low, the battery life is very good. If you don't care about RGB and just want a mechanical keyboard then you'll hardly plug this in.For the price, this keyboard offers an excellent combination of features, customization, and build quality.I would realistically rate this 4.5 out of 5 stars, but since Amazon does not allow half-star ratings, I rounded up to 5.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great for a MacGreat for a Mac
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: As a Desktop Mac user, it is hard to find a decent wired backlit mechanical keyboard at a good price. While all USB keyboards a compatible with a Mac, that is not the same thing as having a Mac keyboard layout. Being less expensive than many of the alternatives I found, I decided to give this one a try. I am very pleased with it. It has a pair of switches on the underside. One to switch between 2.4GHz, Bluetooth and off. And another, that is for Mac or Windows configuration. Switched it to Mac and left wireless turned off. Plugged it into my KVM and the was greeted by the macOS keyboard setup wizard. Afterwards, it worked like any normal Mac specific keyboard. Having the Command key next to the space bar for shortcuts like Copy&Paste was a must. No problem there. The extra media keys work great as well. However, they only light up when pressed. As a non-gamer, I did not think I would have much use for the Macro keys. But, I was wrong and set the first one up to do screen captures of the current window. I am very used to the brown switches on my old keyboard. This one has hot swap-able Red Linear switches. It will take a little while to get accustomed to their feel. But, they are comfortable, work great and are quieter. Out of the box, the RGB backlights were setup to perform a Las Vegas Christmas light show. While neat, not something I actually would want to have on a regular basis. Thankfully, it has different lighting modes and color schemes. I set mine to an unchanging near white and I'm happy. It is also possible to assigned each key one of 7 colors. I was able to do all of the things I mentioned above without ever setting up wireless or installing any software. Overall, it seems to be a great keyboard. Did I mention it even has the old school Num Lock, Caps Lock and Scroll Lock LEDs. Plus, it can live as a strictly USB keyboard.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Keyboard itself is great, but wireless performance is awful
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: At the price point, actually a pretty decent keyboard. Switches are a little wobbly, so I do recommend installing some Akko switches (a brand compatible with the 5 pin layout Redragon uses) in the hotswap sockets if key feel is important to you. It's made of plastic, but compensates by having what feels like a solid aluminum plate beneath the keys, which gives the keyboard a satisfying heft and prevents any serious deck flexing when attempting to bend the keyboard.  Battery life is fine, a bit shorter than my other wireless keyboards. I get around 3 days on a charge of all-day work and play, so I may take the keyboard apart and install my own aftermarket battery for a longer cycle, if I can sort out the issue below.My only gripe with this keyboard is its wireless performance. To say it's terrible would be an understatement. It's atrocious. I have my dongle within three feet of the keyboard, and I consistently have to reposition and tweak the angle of my keyboard in order to get consistent reception, otherwise inputs are lost or repeated until the keyboard reconnects. 50% of the time, it works perfectly, but that other 50% makes it virtually unusable. I've wired the keyboard now, and am experiencing no issues. I live in the middle of nowhere. I don't have a 2.4 ghz router (All of my devices are on ethernet or use wifi 7, and I've disabled the 2.4 and 5 ghz bands on my router). There is absolutely nothing that could reasonably be interfering with the connectivity outside of the keyboard itself, so I can't bring myself to give this any higher than 3 stars. If Redragon can't manage to put a functional wireless transmitter or receiver in the box, this keyboard might as well be advertised as wired.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Buena calidad a precio asequible. COMPLETÍSIMO.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Llevo ya varios meses usándolo y va siendo hora de plasmar mis impresiones.En cuanto a la fabricación y acabados, sobresalientes. Buenos materiales, teclas que da gusto pulsar (con su característico sonido), y robustez en el montaje.La conexión inalámbrica no tiene lag, la pulsación se corresponde de manera inmediata con el resultado en pantalla, probado a nivel usuario y en juegos online, tipo LOL (prefiero jugar con mando y soy poco asiduo a este estilo de juegos) no hay ningún retraso, o si lo hay es mínimo, entre pulsar las teclas de dirección o de acción y la respuesta en pantalla.El software propio para controlar la iluminación juega con todas las posibilidades: desde el tipo de iluminación, los colores, o la intensidad de la misma, hasta controlar el tiempo de apagado, algo que yo considero fundamental, ya que la gran mayoría de teclados gaming traen un tiempo de apagado por defecto que, normalmente, no suele ser de más de 1 o 2 minutos, y más si es en teclados inalámbricos, para ahorrar batería. Aquí se lo configuras tú.Punto negativo? La batería. Si no apagas el interruptor del teclado, se consume relativamente rápido. Yo le doy un uso intensivo y aguanta un par de días SIN apagar el interruptor, que no está mal, pero ahí sí flojea comparado con otros inalámbricos gaming que he tenido.La carga es aceptable, no se demora demasiado, aunque no he controlado el tiempo que tarda.Y para consultar cuánto le queda de batería, basta con pulsar dos teclas, y se iluminarán del 1 al 0 para indicarnos a cuánto está. Eso sí, una vez que baja del 7, cae en picado.El resto: teclas programables, control de volumen con un rodillo, gomas antideslizantes y elevadores, son todos puntos positivos.Dicho esto, por el precio que tiene, sabiendo que teclados similares pueden costar entre los 100 y los 200 euros, lo recomiendo totalmente.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a really good keyboard for a mechanical keyboard. Don't let the price fool you. Yes, it's a cheap price but in no way is it a cheap quality product. It's low cost for as described below.  I purchased the RED switch version and the BROWN switch version because I could not make up mind (at first).  I've already tried a Blue switch.BLUE Switch = Clicky tactile feel. Loud like an old typewriter. Nice still, if you like that. I thought I would stick with Blue until...RED Switch = Very smooth linear feel no clicky. It is more thump, thump.  Sounds solid.  (this became my favorite)BROWN Switch = Is like an in-between a Blue and Red where it has some clicky but with a more linear smooth thump like the RED.  Very good and thought this was going to be my default but ended up preferring the RED mostly.All of the above are all great options it is just a matter of personal preference.  There are no wrong choices.The keyboard base : is very well built with some heft to it.  Feels like a 1970's Japanese old quality plastic on the base that they used to make old computers with.  It is a 60% keyboard size Ten-keyless which is about as small as you can get.The keys : are very nice and very well spaced.  The letters are clear and the feel is very good. The keycaps are removable with a provided tool.  The switches are NOT hot-swappable.Lighting :  is only ONE color - a cyan blue.  It is sharp and bright and the color looks very good.  Each key is lit up by the lighting with no shadowing.  You can adjust the brightness (I keep mine on high) and you change the light effect/pattern if you want from a few key combinations.  I keep mine on the default.The Cable : it is USB-C on one end and USB-A on the other end that plugs into your PC.  The cable length is very good but I still used a USB-A extension cable because my computer is further away from my desk.A few reasons for the low price is: It is not a high end name-brand, the switches are not hot-swappable, it is a wired keyboard but most mechanical keyboards are anyway, the lighting is one color, no software, etc.  If all you want is a very good mechanical keyboard minus some options or you just want to find out what you like and don't like.  This keyboard is great.  I really don't care about hot-swapping my switches (yet) but someday I will get there.  For now this works for me.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A serious bang for your buck!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My old G915 gaming keyboard finally ran its course. So I was in need of a replacement. I do love mechanical switches, but not excessively loud ones. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I recently purchased the DIERYA T68SE Wired 60% Mechanical Gaming Keyboard in white, and I must say, it has exceeded my expectations. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I upgraded my home gaming setup with this keyboard after considerable research, and it’s been a joy to use for both gaming and typing.Strengths:Premium typing experience: The pre-lubed cream linear switches and gasket mount deliver a “thocky” feel and satisfyingly smooth keystrokes. Typing and gaming are both quiet and comfortable, with five layers of foam dampening any hollow sounds.Customization: The included software lets me remap keys, create macros, and adjust more than 20 dynamic RGB lighting modes quickly. I loved being able to easily tweak the look and functionality.Build quality: PBT double-shot keycaps with an MDA profile feel sturdy and resist wear; they’re grippy and comfortable for long sessions. The detachable aluminum volume knob is a treat for instant control.Layout: The 98-key layout keeps the numpad and arrow keys but eliminates wasted space—a space-saving solution perfect for both gaming and work.Universal compatibility: Works perfectly with Windows and Mac out of the box, and includes both a 2-in-1 keycap/switch puller and extra switches for future customization.Bottom Line:This is an exceptional value for anyone who wants a customizable, quiet, and responsive keyboard for gaming, work, and creative projects. The smooth switches, full-featured software, and premium build make it a standout in its price range. Highly recommended for enthusiasts and everyday users alike.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Where sound, price, and comfort meet.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Absolutely worth the money, and even got it on sale! As I was looking for a replacement for my Logitech G512 that had finally started to show its age, after nearly 5 years of daily wear and tear from both games and general typing, I stumbled upon this board after seeing the shop it was inside of.I've been using it now for close to a week, and it has sealed the deal for my desire to build a keyboard once I have the means to do such. Each keycap having a small variance in its elevation by just a few millimeters may not sound like much, but it allows for a much smoother flow in typing and touch feel as you move through the keys. Additionally the sound the keyboard makes with the lubed switches below each key, effectively a quiet thunk-click is just beautiful. Its also much quieter than the G512 was, and is less noticed by people when I am speaking with them over the phone for work. So major win there!Solid 5/5 stars, if you need a keyboard for a good price and solid function - fully recommend.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great keyboard, nice switches, poor LEDs
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I love hall-effect switches and the wired version of this keyboard is amazing. It's snappy, responsive, smooth, and relatively quiet. This keyboard overall is fantastic and the shortcuts are nice, the the price is affordable and probably the lowest price hall effect keyboard you can get with decent build quality. The one downfall, though, are the LED's. If you don't care about RGB and plan to leave it off, then there are no downsides, but a common problem are that the LED's will malfunction. Mine starting blinking wildly and randomly changing colors a few months into ownership and after a while, they all went dark except for the first five F-keys (F1 - F5) and ESC. So now, whenever I change my LED settings, only those first few keys light up and the rest are all dark. My only gripe about this is that the keys themselves on mine are black and so it's tough to see which key I'm pressing at a glance without the LED lit up behind it. Some of the keys are green and easy to read, but the dark keys are obscured. It's an annoying glitch that seems to be widespread and unaddressed. I tried cleaning it, I tried disassembling it to see if any connections were bad, but everything looks fine, it's all clean, it all looks good so I'm forced to conclude it's a hardware or software defect. If you can get past this, it's honestly a great keyboard and I have fallen in love with hall-effect switches. Overall, if they can just fix this LED thing, it would be the perfect keyboard at a fantastic price.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great wireless mechanical keyboard with good customization
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was looking for a wireless mechanical keyboard to replace typing on a laptop keyboard since it feels more natural.  I do like the keyboard layout where the keys are more compact with the handy knob on the upper right corner for quick access to increase and decrease the computer volume.  The keyboard is compatible with Windows and Mac and has some handy switches on the left side of the keyboard to easily toggle between wired, bluetooth and wireless 2.4 GHz USB receiver configuration usage.  One thing the product description doesn't mention is that this wireless mechanical keyboard is also compatible with Chromebooks which is great to bring for traveling.The keyboard keys are a bit quieter than I expected from a more traditional mechanical keyboard even though I prefer the keys to be a bit louder but that is a compromise that I am willing to accept.  The keys do feel comfortable with good build quality and the battery life on the keyboard is amazing.  I used the keyboard for 3 days and only lost 1% battery life.The keyboard does have customized software that you can install that allows you to toggle between different keyboard light effects and has a sleep timer setting that is configurable that sets your keyboard to go to sleep after a certain period to save battery life.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great-to-excellent for an entry-level mechanical keyboard!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This Keyboard is honestly so great for the price.  The 3 different connection modes are much appreciated.  I personally use BT for most of my needs (which is very responsive), but the option to wire in or to use 2.4 gHz for a (slightly) faster response is great!  I'm also glad I was able to find a full keyboard that fit my needs as the num-pad is something I didn't want to give up.I enjoy the design, and the different options are great if you aren't into the anime style.  The keyboard is suitably heavy, which makes sense as it is mechanical.  It also makes good use of the real estate on the board, which means the keyboard is surprisingly more compact than you'd think for a full size keyboard.  Definitely fits well on my dest!It's relatively early days for me using it, but I haven't had any reliability issues and it feels sturdy!I could take or leave the RGB lighting, especially for this particular design, as the keyboard is already stylized.  That being said, the lights aren't too bright so there's no distraction, but they're still noticable.This is a great keyboard for anyone looking to get into the mechanical keyboard space without going crazy on the budget.  Personally, when I switched I was skeptical, but the change from membrane to mechanical is palpable and I'll never go back now.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Quiet, Pretty, Easy to Use. My Hands and Eyes Love This Keyboard!Quiet, Pretty, Easy to Use. My Hands and Eyes Love This Keyboard!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have tried a lot of keyboards, from high end to budget, trying to find the right one. I am not a gamer. I primarily write papers for school, so I need something comfortable, quiet, and easy to type on. The HyperX Alloy Core RGB is the first keyboard that immediately felt right. It is quiet, comfortable, and very easy to type on. The RGB looks amazing, and the controls are simple and located in the top left corner.This keyboard is plug and play. No software is needed for any of the lighting controls. The brightness button is the top left key and cycles through off, low, and high. The middle button switches through the built in lighting modes. These include solid color, fade, zones, rolling rainbow, quick flash, fast color cycle, and more. The third button is Game Mode. FN and F12 lock the keyboard itself.The keyboard has a good height and feels stable. The keys seemed slippery at first, but they feel normal now. I did a quick typing test and reached 52 WPM with 100 percent accuracy after only a few minutes of using it. The keyboard has feet on the bottom so you can tilt it slightly. The dedicated media keys and volume buttons on the top right are convenient. The braided USB cord feels durable.The color is exactly as pictured. The keyboard is quiet, comfortable, and has a great typing feel. I have only had it a short time and I am already considering buying a backup.This is a great keyboard for anyone who wants quiet keys, easy controls, strong RGB, and a comfortable typing experience.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Looks Perfect! Could not be any happier!Looks Perfect! Could not be any happier!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I had to take a break from my job to write this because I am just so impressed. I am NOT being compensated by anyone for writing this.Short Version: It's well built, heavy, and the keystrokes are very smooth. The keys are quiet, not silent, and are lit up very nicely. It has greatly exceeded my expectations, and I will be actively recommending this to my family and friends.Long Version: So I've only used this keyboard for about an hour and, unless it suffers some type of catastrophic failure, this will be the only brand of keyboard I buy ever again. Immediately after picking this package up off of my doorstep I could tell this was a heavy, well-built unit, unlike my previous keyboard.Tangent! My last keyboard was purchased from another online retailer that maybe more specializes in computers and Black November sales. I was used to the standard stock keyboards I could get for $5-10, and that was fine. I decided to make the plunge into gaming keyboards, but quickly realized lots of them do not get good reviews or look any different than a cheap keyboard with lights behind it.  I didn't want some cheaply made unit, so I tried to spend a tiny bit more for a nice one. However the one I paid for was very lightweight, cheaply made, and wobbly. I am in the process of returning it. I'm also currently arguing that this was defective as well. Hopefully I can avoid the restocking fee, but even if I can't I am so happy I made the choice to come to the more trustworthy Amazon to find a better unit.Ok, got that off my chest. This unit is so sturdy, so smooth, so bright, so...I am so relieved I have found a good keyboard. There are different lighting modes that make the keyboard fun to use, but most of all, it seems very functionally sound. I paid $40 for this, and if I knew how much better it would be than my previous keyboards, I would've paid more.Now there could certainly be better keyboards on the market. They better be at the prices some companies charge. For the price though, this was an excellent deal. You will not be disappointed in this purchase, especially if you have previously dealt with the cheaply made light up keyboards.Is this a perfect unit? Maybe actually, but a couple things are intially making me rate this a mere 99/100. At first glance I wasn't sure why the keys had their "shift alternatives" right next to the regular output. The semicolon/colon key and the apostrophe/quote key look a little confusing at first glance. Not a big issue, but it does seem weird. The other thing I noticed was that the keys are higher up than my previous, flatter keyboard, perhaps due to the heft of the unit. I don't think this is a major problem, but the wrist pad I'm expecting to arrive tomorrow may end up being a great complement to this keyboard.If any of my thoughts change, I will update this review. For now though, HyperX is going to be the first place I go to when I need new PC components.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First thing you'll notice is this thing is heavy, it will not move around your desk!It reminds me of the long gone 1980's IBM PC keyboards from back in the day that were heavy as bricks. The keys are pretty much perfect height as I returned Red Dragon and Corsair membrane keyboards because the keys were just a bit too low for a man's larger hand/fingers. Pretty quiet keypresses, not silent, but way less than the clickty-clack of mechanical key keyboards. Now I don't get complaints from another room when I'm typing at night. Speaking of night time, the key illumination only has OFF-MEDIUM-FULL lED brightness levels. Medium brightness happens to be perfect for me (I was a bit concerned about only having two brightness levels), so your mileage may vary there. You can turn the key illumination off with a single dedicated button that controls the illumination level, but the letters are not white like a non-illuminated keyboard which makes them hard to make out without illumination. You will probably find you'll just leave illumination on all the time, it's really gorgeous anyway with illumination. I can type at full speed with this keyboard, no issues with hitting other keys because the tops of the keys are decent size. I really can't find anything I don't like about this keyboard.FWIW- my use case is I'm an IT guy, so all typing, no gaming on this keyboard.TLDR: Goldilocks membrane keyboard... give it a try, you can always return it if you don't like it.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Before I start, I am coming from a history of generally awful keyboards. Free ones from work or with pre built PCs. This keyboard feels so much more expensive than it is. I got it for $36 and bought a 2nd one within 24 hours of using it.The good: vibrant colors for the RGB. Rock solid build quality. Feels like it's solid metal (it's not). No key cap wiggle. Every keystroke is sturdy and deliberate. Keyboard is fairly tall and perfectly lined up with my rosewill(from newegg) wrist rest. Rightly woven braided cable that won't shred easily. Keys have a slight rubber texture and it makes my autism so happy.The bad: this keyboard is MASSIVE. check the specifications before purchasing. It's taller than my old keyboard, wider and has more depth. It's also quite heavy for a keyboard. The lights are needed to see the keys, black on black was an awful idea. The lighting control options are solid red, various rainbows and some breathing colors. It sucks they push you to download the software.Over all I'm in love still with his keyboard and buying a 2nd one while it's still on sale. This keyboard plus the hyper x cloud core headphones I've used for years has made me really like this brand.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Keyboard is above it's paygrade.Keyboard is above it's paygrade.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Purchased On May 11th 2021:YES, I know my keyboard is dusty.. IT's over a Year Old and it's been at my desk the whole time. ( I do clean it every now and then).. But this isn't about that.  I wanted to let you all know I got this keyboard for 39.99 and it was well worth it.  The Keys are very responsive and even now as I use it, I'm enjoying the feedback and sturdiness of the keyboard.  As others have said it's Heavy and won't move around easily on your desk. I would recommend a wrist "rest" for the keyboard though as it is, "slightly" high and you'll be way more comfortable typing on it with your wrists up.Hyperx's wrist rest is perfect for this keyboard: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07GP7JXQYNow onto the bad.  As of 1/5/2023 - My "Windows" key broke.  I've plugged in other keyboards and they work fine. (it's not a software issue) I've then taken the keyboard and plugged it into my work laptop and again, the Windows key is broken.  The reason I say this to you in this review, is I've used this keyboard over 9 hours a day for the last year and half and it's held up pretty well.  For this price, it's a no brainer.You'll enjoy the colors and the ability to change the brightness to your liking.  If you're shopping around and reading comments on this keyboard, just stop.. save yourself some time and get this one. You won't be disappointed (unless you hate slightly noisy keyboards) or are just VERY picky with your keyboards. If you are the latter... then you're probably not shopping for a $39 keyboard..UPDATE: 1/19/23 turns out, there is a "Gaming Mode" on the top left the G with the square.  It turns off the Windows key from working. This must of been bumped and now works fine.  So I continue my praise on the review and mark this as 5 stars from 4.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got the HyperX Alloy Core RGB Keyboard, and I am genuinely impressed with the combination of affordability, functionality, and vibrant RGB lighting that this keyboard brings to the table. Designed with gamers and casual users in mind, the Alloy Core RGB stands out as an excellent choice for those seeking a feature-packed keyboard without breaking the bank.The first thing that caught my attention was the keyboard's striking RGB backlighting. The customizable lighting effects add a touch of personality to my setup, allowing me to match the keyboard's illumination with my mood or gaming environment. The vibrant colors and dynamic lighting patterns, easily controlled through dedicated keys, make the Alloy Core RGB an aesthetic delight.Typing on the HyperX Alloy Core RGB is a satisfying experience. The membrane key switches offer a responsive and tactile feel without the audible click of mechanical switches. The quiet keystrokes are ideal for shared spaces or late-night gaming sessions where noise might be a concern. The full-sized layout with a numeric keypad ensures versatility for both gaming and productivity tasks.The dedicated media controls are a practical addition, allowing me to adjust volume, playback, and lighting settings on the fly without interrupting my gaming or work. The inclusion of quick access buttons for lighting customization and a Game Mode that disables the Windows key during gameplay further enhances the keyboard's user-friendly design.Durability is a notable feature of the HyperX Alloy Core RGB. The sturdy build, reinforced plastic frame, and spill-resistant design add a layer of reliability, ensuring the keyboard can withstand the rigors of daily use. The matte finish on the keycaps contributes to a comfortable feel and prevents fingerprints, maintaining a clean and professional look.Setting up the HyperX Alloy Core RGB is a breeze. The plug-and-play functionality ensures a straightforward installation, and the detachable USB cable provides flexibility for cable management. The keyboard is compatible with both Windows and macOS systems, making it versatile for a variety of users.While the Alloy Core RGB lacks the mechanical switches found in higher-end keyboards, it compensates with a budget-friendly price point and a quieter typing experience. The compromise in switch type might be a trade-off for some enthusiasts, but for those seeking an affordable and visually appealing gaming keyboard, the Alloy Core RGB delivers outstanding value.

Product description
MULTIFUNCTIONAL KNOB: CONTROL MEDIA VOLUME AND LIGHTING EFFECTS 
How to switch the mode of the knob? 
Long press the knob until the knob LED light OFF: enter the multimedia mode. 
Long press the knob until the knob LED light ON: enter the lighting control mode. 
Lighting Effect Control 
When the LED light of knob is on, the knob is in the light effect control mode: 
1.Click the button to switch the light effect mode and store up to 19 lighting effects. 
2.Rotate the knob to adjust the brightness. 
3.You can customize 3 lighting effects according to your preference through M1/M2/M3 keys. (Refer to the manual） 
Media Volume Control 
When the LED light of knob is off, the knob is in the multimedia mode: 
1.Click the button to mute the function. 
2.Rotate the knob to adjust the volume. 
FULL-SIZE GAMING/OFFICE MECHANICAL KEYBOARD 
Convenient Shortcut Keys

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Ok, for information purposes.  I am a female fast typer but I have long nails so typing on flat keyboards is just not a thing for me.  This works beautifully. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: WOW! I am impressed! This AULA mechanical keyboard is the real deal. Solid build, nice weight to it, and the retro typewriter look is just awesome. The clicky clickity sound from the keys, OH YEAH, IT'S LOUD! Like the old school manual typewriters I grew up with, but with less resistance, no teacher yelling at me, and way smoother feel.The media control knob is a cool . Super easy to cycle through all the RGB lighting options, and they look great, especially at night. I haven’t used the wrist rest — mostly because my hands are on the bigger side — but it’s a nice extra to have in the box.Another big win? Easy to clean. The round keycaps give enough space to wipe between keys without trouble.If you're into that vintage-meets-gaming vibe, this keyboard’s definitely worth it!NO JOKE! This is awesome!Mahalo nui loa AULA!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: For the price, this is an amazing keyboard. Please note, the description does not make clear that THE COLOR IS NOT CHANGEABLE, each key is a predetermined color. It took me a year almost to actually figure out it wasn't a firmware issue or me just not knowing the key commands. Maybe I just don't know enough about keyboards to have figured that out. But in my opinion that should be highlighted in the description. However, the style is unique and pleasant to see. I game and use it for normal operational stuff and it's easy and comfortable to use. I've had it for over a year now I think and there is no noticable wear so far with daily use. The issue I had is a minor one, but again for the price it is a great keyboard. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased up the Logitech Wave Keys MK670 Combo and it's been a great upgrade for my everyday use at work. The ergonomic wave-shaped keyboard feels fantastic right away, my wrists and hands stay much more relaxed during long typing sessions. The keys have a nice, soft touch and they're quiet enough that I don't disturb anyone around me (no annoying click-clack). The included mouse is the perfect size for my medium hands, fits naturally without feeling cramped or too bulky, and it glides smoothly. Setup was effortless with Bluetooth and Logi Bolt options, and it works flawlessly across my Windows devices. Overall, this combo delivers excellent comfort and quiet performance at a solid price. Highly recommend if you're looking for an ergonomic wireless setup that just feels good to use every day.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Might be my new favorite keyboard!Might be my new favorite keyboard!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was looking to get a split ergonomic keyboard but wasn’t sure it was the right fit for me or my current setup. This felt like a nice baby step towards one of those so I went with this one. And I’m so glad I did. The keys are so quiet compared to some of my other Logitech keyboards I’ve had in the past. The palm rests are so soft and comfortable. I normally find my wrists aching pretty quickly when using a keyboard without one. It’s pretty small but I’m a petite person so this is the perfect size for my hands. I connected it to my tablet with Bluetooth and it works perfect. Setup was pretty easy as well. I’m not a huge fan of the shape of the mouse that comes with it but I’m slowly getting used to it. The mouse clicks are so soft and quiet that they are virtually silent. Sometimes it feels like I’m not even clicking anything while using it. But it works great and connects to my computer with ease when using the usb.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Wonderful Ergonomic Keyboard - No more Wrist Pain!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: TLDR; a great keyboard that's super comfortable for typing and eliminated my wrist pain. Recommend this!I work as an accountant and do a LOT of typing and 10 key in my day-to-day so comfort is paramount (especially on closing periods and loooong days).My wrists and arms started killing me lately and I had done everything else; a more ergonomic chair, adjustable desk, monitors adjusted properly--you know, the WHOLE kitchen sink.  So, by process of elimination, I came to realize HEY bonehead--how about you try a better keyboard? So, I did and I'm freaking glad I have. NO MORE WRIST PAIN!Here's the deets:PROS:-Ergo shape helps hand placement, and the pad is comfy-Keys are quiet and have good feel-Full number pad just like a calculator-Batteries last longCONS:-Weird mashed together function keys add extra steps to thing-Mouse could be a little more ergonomic and is paired with keyboard (not a huge issue)-I wouldn’t say its necessarily for gaming (if you are into that) its more functional for typingThe “Wave”The wave shape may make it look like a strip of bacon or UFO (depending on the angle you look at it) but it just works. It makes your hands wrap around the keys and the pad supports your wrists at the exact correct angle.Key feel and noiseI learned to use a keyboard on a type writer and so , have always loved loud clickety clackity keyboards and buttons with a big travel. I was unsure how I would feel about this one, it’s actually pretty quiet and the keys have a short and easy travel. Despite my love of loud keyboards this one changed my mind.Hot keys and “functions”Okay this one grinds my gears a little because I think Logitech messed this one up. They prioritized their custom functions (volume, emojis, presentation view play/pause) over the actual function keys F1-F12, and Page up/Down. They kind of mashed them all into one.For most this will be no issue, but for myself in my work I do use an old system sometimes that uses the F keys, and it gets annoying having to hold the “fn” button while pressing the F key or risk accidentally changing my volume.Been spending all my time in 10-key paradise.As I said earlier, I do whole lot of 10-key and entries in my work, I HAD to have a good number pad. Well folks – this is a big win they integrated a full number pad with enter, = + and - , if you know how to run a tape calculator you are going to have no issue with this lovely number pad – its GREAT!Battery LifeI haven’t had it that long yet, but I can say I am running the original 2-duracell AAAs it came with and have had exactly zero problems with it thus far.MouseOf course, I cannot forget to mention the mouse. It is very comfortable as well, with zero clicking sound and a neat scroll wheel with nice weight. Out of the box functionality is great and it is a great companion to this keyboard. Note: The keyboard and mouse are a pair and connect through one USB receiver so if you change your mouse that may be an issue.Do I recommend it?Hell yeah! If you have been debating whether to grab a wave to surf the web or just to have a better typing experience, I’d say do it. Plus, this is amazon – super easy to return if you don’t like it.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on March 24, 2024

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've been a die-hard Logi user for many decades and for the first time I've been left to find a different keyboard manufacturer.I've used the K350 wave keyboard for many, many years and love it. Like others, I too was dumfounded with the K350 was discontinued and purchased a small stockpile. Sadly, that's all gone and I've been frustrated looking for a replacement.The MK670 wave is really a terrible keyboard if you use F1-F12 keys daily. As a software engineer, I spend my day at the keyboard. I use the function keys every day. Having to look to find them really sucks! Add to the fact that they are all in a line (something not done for more years than I can count), the printing on the keys is like glossy decals and reflects light. This means you can't tell the difference between F8 & F9 for example.They put the added media type keys as functions (Fn) on the F keys. You can lock the Fn but that's really an unusable situation.There is a replacement out there...trust me. I can't mention it here or my review wont be published. But I don't recommend this keyboard unless you never use the function or Fn/media keys. If all you need is the keys, it's not bad.Goodbye Logi...sad day.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on January 23, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a great keyboard, and the wireless mouse is a bonus too.  I’ve owned several iterations of this keyboard for about 15 years, and I’m on my fourth one (not for quality, but because I’ve moved jobs or wanted a more recent model).  It is easy to set up using Bluetooth and sets up within seconds.  The Bluetooth range is also great I can move the keyboard or mouse around my office and it still types no matter where I move.  The keys are easy to type with ergonomically and when they type they’re soft yet firm, if that makes sense.  They’re not loud.  Really happy with this keyboard!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on March 15, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Its ok, but a downgrade from K350 combo
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: replacing the Logitech K350 the MK670 is a downgrade.The wave keyboard retains a slight bump but the wave is far closer to a standard keyboard than the pronounced MK670 wave.  Key function is tactilely a pleasure to use.Ergonomics took a backseat.  It appears all the functionality is supported but requires a search to find; no more just feeling for the volume controls, zooming, page up/down.  The previous large easy to find controls have been mushed into a 'compact' keyboard.  Unfortunately.The combo mouse will never be used.  What was included in the previous combo, the M510 with customizable side buttons (which is a must have for me) is not included.  Another downgrade. The 510 is still working perfectly, unlike the keyboard which has suffered from too many spills and crumbs.So its not horrible but is definitely a downgrade from the previous combo.  Will keep as bought 'used-like new' at a very good price, and both the keyboard and mouse are in perfect condition (thanks amazon!) and usable, albeit without usability of previous version.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on January 9, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've had a number of Logitech ergonomic keyboards at home and work.  Likewise for their mice. The feel and feedback of both just seems perfect.  This combo set is no exception.  The promise of being able to switch between two devices with one keyboard/mouse...is not executed as flawlessly.  There are three selector buttons on the keyboard to activate a pairing.  It works perfectly for the keyboard, not so the mouse.  The best combination I've found is to pair the combo to the first device with the bolt receiver and the second device via bluetooth.  Then the keyboard function keys will switch the keyboard, however the mouse.  Long holding the pairing button on the mouse is required for the bolt receiver to re-activate the mouse when switching back.  Worse on the bluetooth device is that the mouse pairing must be deleted and re-added - each time.  It's workable but a bit tedious.  Still a five star review because of the ergonomics of the combo and the lack of any lag when bluetooth is finally connected.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: It's a great keyboard. Quiet, and comfortable to use. The mouse is also pretty quiet and nice to work with.The keyboard can pair to 3 devices and it can switch between seamlessly, HOWEVER, the mouse cannot. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Its a great keyboard so far. Especially for the price. The keys have a soft feel to typing rather than a "click" and are relatively quiet.I like the dedicated computer lock button. I won't make much use of it at home, but in an office environment it would be nice to have it for locking my system as I step away. Though I'm not sure why it has a dedicated refresh button when F5 already does that for any web browser I've ever encountered. The volume and music control buttons at the top are very nice. Usually keyboards just use the F-keys and function for that. This keyboard moved them to their own buttons and has different shortcuts for function + f-keys.The phone/tablet holder part is relatively useless if you have a case on your device. It's not a feature I personally look for in a keyboard, so I'm not letting it effect my score. It will likely end up being a pen holder for me.If you like that satisfying "clicking" of mechanical keyboards, you won't like this. But if you want a keyboard that won't keep your partner(s) awake when you're gaming or typing away at night, this is a great keyboard for you.The brightness of the light under the keys is a good balance of visible without being disruptive. White, green, yellow, pin, and cyan all have great brightness. Red and blue are less bright but have good intensity of color. The print on the keys are easily visible thanks to the large print. I personally just got it because I like the look of these keys, but if you have vision impairment, these should be good for you.Its just plug and play so there's no setup other than plugging it into a USB port.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Exactly What I Needed in a Low Profile KeyboardExactly What I Needed in a Low Profile Keyboard
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The SABLUTE K31PRO is exactly what I was looking for. It is low profile, quiet, and wired, which is all I really wanted in a budget keyboard. The letters are large, but that does not bother me at all. It was plug and play and worked instantly with no setup.The lighting options are great. You can choose a solid color, turn the lights off, or set it to fade through colors in a sequence. I do wish it had more of a breathing effect, but for the price, the lighting is still impressive. The wrist rest is comfortable and the overall typing feel is soft and quiet. For a budget keyboard, this checks all the boxes for me.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Recommended highly but NOTE: if there seems to be trouble lighting up watch the posted video
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I tried everything to get the backlight to work but only one little light was in green.  I need a backlit keyboard so I started a return. After filling it out I found a video the mfr posted to help with the backlight. I watched it and realized the help materials were confusing or inaccurate. I've never had a problem with a backlit keyboards out of the box (they tend to stop working by 2 years though).  The problem is the crazy. No mention that some tiny, little hard pieve on the keyboard needs to be switched ON or the buttons referred to in the materials don't work.  How can the be left off the diagram and written materials? At first this thing wouldn't move and I didn't know it existed til the video; I didn't want to break it since I didn't expect it to work. But then I was able to snap it to one side and the keyboard lit up!!  I'm keeping the keyboard. It's actually nice though a bit uneven in brightness.  The keyboard is otherwise, so far, perfect. The keys are big and they feel really good to type on.  No clicking or being tall/padded. There also was a sale on this keyboard so a great price. I'm calmed down now and really like this keyboard.  A lit keyboard makes typing 1000% easier.

description: With the Logitech Media Combo MK200, the things you do most are just one touch away. You can play music, change the volume or go to the Web—instantly. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Mouse is, once again, a disappointmentMouse is, once again, a disappointment
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I had a wired mouse and keyboard from CyberPower that shipped with the custom PC I ordered, but the mouse's squeaky clicks and the keyboard's awful over-sensitivity drove me to eventually seek out replacements.First off... I dunno about those "features" to rate. Ergonomic? Not so much. Volume control? Uh... simple up, down, and mute. What's there to rate? And.... "sheerness"? W..what?This is advertised as a "media" kb/m combo. Which the keyboard fits the description. It has the requisite media buttons (play/pause, skip/reverse, volume up/down/mute, etc) and some browsing controls. Shockingly enough, the mouse has NO features for media or web browsing. I was expecting at least the back and forward keys, maybe the tilt/scroll as well, but that's a negative on those. This is the most basic mouse I have ever used, and frankly, it annoys me that there's only two buttons and a scroll wheel. Not to mention that even though the box claims it's a "full-size" mouse, it's way too lightweight and small. I think that's the worst part for me, having mid-to-large hands. Though on the plus side, it's a very smooth mouse which is nice since my displays are 144 Hz. And as I was typing this out, I realized that this keyboard and mouse combo, are in fact, almost the same exact models shipped in the Logitech Wireless Combo (920-008971), minus the wireless part. So I should have expected the same for the mouse, I suppose. Then again, for the price I paid for these, I'm not disappointed, since hey, I have an extra mouse now. But It does mean having to find a mouse to suit my needs (or go back to using my semi-new, but otherwise reliable, wireless Logi M510 that mysteriously stopped working one day). But I will not go back to using that wireless Logitech keyboard, no matter how much I liked its layout and media controls. The intermittent stuttering and unresponsiveness just isn't worth it. I asked for help with that. Their response? "Use an extension cable." I had the dongle two inches from the keyboard, and still the problem persisted. But that's another story. Just be wary of their wireless keyboards!

K400 Plus 
Laid-back control of your PC connected TV 
Navigate your TV-connected computer more easily from the comfort of your couch. With Logitech’s all-in-one TV keyboard/touchpad, simply type, click and scroll to watch videos, browse the web and check Facebook on your PC-connected TV. 
Integrated wireless keyboard with touchpad

Previous page

Media-friendly TV keyboard

Plug-and-play simplicity

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've tried numerous "media Center" style keyboards.... Some with backlight, some without, some with specific freq receiver and some bluetooth. The thing about all those I've tried, the keyboards are tiny rubber keys and a small touchpad.Now to be fair the main reason I've tried so many different ones is because they all fail the same way... the legend comes off the rubber keys, the touchpad becomes so glossy smooth that it simply stops working, the rechargeable batteries die and are not easily replaceable,  and in time, they seem to lose connectivity.So what do I like about this Logitech.1. I've always had great success with Logitech products (Keyboards, Mice, Cameras) so yeah, this was a big part of trying this one to start with2. This Logitech has a touchpad that's in the region of 2-1/2 times the size of the previous controllers I've tried. I like that. Instead of scrolling fingers numerous times across, this reduces the wear are tear3. It uses "AA" batteries easily replaceable and not rechargeable that once they die, have to go on charge and you end up with a power lead dangling while you continue to use.4. It has much larger standard fill sized keys which are also very responsive and tactile. The other remotes I've used with small rubber keys..... you can never type something in without a key missing or kitting the key next to it.5.The layout is specific designed for Home Theater's/Media Centers. I use this on my Server running Emby and I've had zero problems with any keys. I have one keyboard I have that will not let you terminate an app or browser because you cannot hit Alt/F4.. You can with this one. It has very large separate Volume up/down/mute keys just above the touchpad. Nice touch.... Pause/Run for Emby and VLC also uses the space bar and this is a full size key on this Logitech.6. One odd feature which I'm also really liking!!!!... It has a separate Yellow Key above the keyboard on the left hand side... It's a Left Mouse Button!!!! Now to be honest, I use the left key all the time and the Touchpad has a very large left and right Mouse Button just below it but that additional yellow one sure is nice to haveWhat could they have done to make it just one tiny bit better... and I'm being picky (but for the price... I cannot complain)... I do wish it had the option to backlight the keys. My Thinkpad Laptop has a keyboard light capability which lights all the keys in between each other. Meaning the keys are not themselves backlit. It's not a show stopper but Most of the keyboards I've bought and tried for Home Theaters/Media Centers have a keyboard that lights up because in the dark it's hard to find the keys. HOWEVER... the main keys I do use are easy located by touch and their size so I've not had any issue so far.The other minor issue is size...this is a 14" x 5-1/2" sized keyboard which is definitely larger than the keyboards I've used before  for my media center but is still small enough and lightweight as to be acceptable.Overall The pros of this keyboard for me, totally outweigh the couple of con issues. Only had it a few days but I'd definitely recommend it.I'll update the review in a couple of months of hammering the keyboard and let you know how it has handled itself, battery life etc.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have  owned this kind of Logitech Keyboard before. It is of a good thin and portable design. It is lightweight for what it is. I find that I can use certain adapters  and attach the receiver of the Logitech keyboard to a cell phone and then use the mousepad  to use on the screen of a cell phone and type notes or use the cell phone like I would use a computer or tablet.One thing that is a bit of a peeve about the Logitech keyboard is that it is a bit too long and  if it were somehow designed to be an inch less wide it would fit in a small backpack better.I have found that this item does last a certain amount of time though. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Logitech once again delivers a fantastic product!Logitech once again delivers a fantastic product!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So I’ve had my Xbox Series X since it launched November 2020, and have been considering purchasing a wireless keyboard to solely use with it. Here recently more and more developers are including native keyboard and mouse support in their games, so the benefit of having a keyboard to use is growing. Since I did not plan to actually “play” the games with the keyboard, but instead use it for “QOL” enhancements, I didn’t want to spend a substantial amount of money on a wireless keyboard. After doing some research on gaming forums, and multiple Reddit /Subreddits, I continually kept seeing a specific Brand/Model of keyboard a lot of posters were suggesting. The keyboard being suggested was the “Logitech K400 Plus”, so I decided to pull the trigger and give it a shot…. I’m glad I did.The Keyboard arrived my house and I instantly noticed how insanely light weight it was. It’s weight was what shocked me initially, but the bigger shock was how well built and durable it felt, especially considering it’s budget friendly price point. So I removed the included USB-A dongle, and inserted it into my 4-port USB 3.0 hub plugged into my Xbox Series X. I flipped the keyboard switch to “ON” and it instantly connected to my Series X and was flawlessly responsive, and had no sign of lag whatsoever. What I didn’t pay much attention to when I researched and decided to purchase the “K400 Plus” was the functionality it possesses pertaining to “Multimedia”. Logitech designed this keyboard to be the perfect “couch” companion for use with smart tv’s, especially tv’s with native web browser applications. So this keyboard became that much better of an addition to my Series X. All of the playback multimedia buttons work perfectly with my Series X, and since Microsoft manufactures the Xbox systems and this keyboard is geared towards “Windows” based computing, the two handshake together in perfect harmony.Another neat features of this keyboard is the “Left Click (Mouse)” button that is situated in the very top right corner of the keyboard. When I first looked at the Left Click button location I was somewhat confused as to why it would be beneficial in that location. It didn’t take long for me to realize it’s genius though, and I can confirm that it is brilliantly placed in the perfect location. I launched the “Microsoft Edge” browser on my Series X, and instantly realized how perfect it was while scrolling the webpages with my right hand on the touchpad, and being able to use the button to click everything I needed to seamlessly. All in all I love this wireless keyboard, and IMO it’s the hands down best budget wireless keyboard on the market. I’ve attached some photos (they didn’t turn out that great due to room darkness) that will hopefully give you an idea of its size.- PROS:• It’s size is perfect for sitting in your lap, and honestly it’s so light you will forget it is even there.• Logitech designed this keyboard for media consumption, so it excels in it’s functionality with media.• Even though it’s price is very budget friendly, you will be surprised by just how well built it feels.• Button clicks feel very tactile and solid, and IMO have the perfect “Spacing” for ease of use.• It’s manufactured by Logitech, and Logitech has world class customer service if something doesn’t function correctly after your keyboard purchase.• All in all a rock solid wireless keyboard that is rich in features without breaking the bank.- CONS:• In all reality I honestly can’t list anything that I feel is a con, but I will list some things that potentially could of placed multiple cherries on top.• This keyboard used AA batteries (2) for it power source, and I imagine some people would of preferred a  rechargeable Li-Po battery, but quite frankly I could care less. I personally like being able to simply change batteries when it dies and instantly go back to using it, versus being unable to use it while it has to charge, but to each his own.• If this keyboard had backlit keys it would be pretty awesome, but I wouldn’t expect it to considering it’s price point. Nonetheless it would enhance it’s appeal that much more.• It would be nice to have bluetooth functionality but at this price point it would be shocking if Logitech had designed it with bluetooth support. In my individual case, the Xbox Series X can only use keyboards via USB-A connection (Wired or Wireless w/ Dongle), so bluetooth wouldn’t benefit my application at all but having the ability to use it with other devices would never hurt.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Functional and Reliable Addition to My Entertainment System
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This review is for the Logitech K400 Wireless Touch TV Keyboard.----------------------------------------------------------------Update, July 20, 2023This wireless keyboard still functions like new, but there is one additional quirk discovered since the original review below. Quite often when using the volume controls on the keyboard to raise or lower volume, those two buttons will instead turn off sound entirely. It's a mild nuisance, and only requires pressing the adjacent volume on/off button. Still love this keyboard and use it nearly every day!----------------------------------------------------------------October 12, 2021Wireless keyboards have been around for many years with many brands now available. As far as function, they're all pretty much the same. I've used a few of them over the years and have been happy with this particular device so far.This Logitech K400 Wireless Touch TV Keyboard performs just as you'd expect, with a full-sized standard keyboard layout and a built-in touchpad on the far right. It's perfect for controlling my old laptop that is now connected to my TV. The farthest away I've used it is about 15 feet from the laptop and it has worked flawlessly at that distance. The keys have a nice feel when depressed, providing adequate soft feedback when fully depressed, without clicking. The touchpad is adequate but does have some quirks as described below.The transmitter operates in the 2.4 GHz band, so theoretically could interfere with your wireless network and other wireless devices, although I've used this keyboard extensively and haven't noticed any issues.The Function keys are claimed to be customizable to create shortcuts. I don't have a use for that capability, so haven't tried it and can't comment on how it's implemented. I've only used this wireless keyboard on Windows 10 computers, but the specs say it works on 'Windows 7, 8, 10 or later, Android 5.0 or later, Chrome OS'.The Volume buttons immediately above the touchpad come in very handy. Be aware though, they control system volume and not the volume of individual applications. To control the volume of a single application, use the on-screen controls for that application.The keyboard is a good weight to operate while holding in my hands and seems plenty sturdy for daily use, but not for unnecessary roughhousing - as you might expect.  It operates on 2 AA batteries which last a long, long time, taking several months of daily use to deplete. (And that's without turning the power switch off.)USABILITY NOTES:=================SIGNAL STRENGTH -The signal seems to be very strong, but the keyboard must have a line-of-sight, unobstructed view of the receiver. For instance, when using the keyboard in my lap the signal doesn't reach the receiver if my legs are crossed or my knees elevated so the front of the keyboard can't quite 'see' the receiver. Similarly, I've found that if the keyboard front is facing 90 degrees away from the receiver, the signal is not received.  Not big issues, but they may be important to some people.TOUCHPAD QUIRKS -1. As stated above, the touchpad does have some quirks. On two occasions the touchpad all of a sudden started to ONLY control screen magnification - increasing and decreasing as I dragged one finger across the surface. I've never determined the cause but in one instance, only removing the battery remedied the strange behavior.2. The touchpad seems to be particularly sensitive to moisture or oil from the skin on my fingers. Meaning, it sometimes simply stops working properly until I thoroughly wipe my fingers with a dry cloth. This is a common issue when using touchpads, but this one is more sensitive than any others I have used, or currently use.MYSTERIOUS YELLOW BUTTON -1. The yellow button at the upper left of the keyboard is poorly documented and I've seen many posts asking what the heck it does. After more research than expected I found it simply functions as a left mouse button, and I've found it most useful when holding the keyboard in my hands. That way, fingers on the right hand work the touchpad and the left thumb presses the yellow button to select things. After about 5 minutes of practice it seems natural.2. Some Windows OS menus and windows won't respond to the yellow button. There doesn't seem to be any predictable pattern as to which items will or will-not respond to the yellow button - but when that happens, the left button under the touchpad must be used.FOUR WAYS TO SCROLL A WINDOW -There are four ways to scroll a window; Pick the one that seems most natural to you.1. Press and hold the Function [FN] button while dragging a finger up/down on the touchpad.2. Position the arrow pointer over the scroll bar slider; Press the Yellow Button; Drag your finger up/down on the touchpad.3. Click the mouse pointer on an inactive part of the screen, then use the Up and Down buttons in the lower right part of the keyboard.3. As with most touchpads, drag two fingers horizontally or vertically.I use this keyboard daily and have been very happy with it. It has a few quirks, but nothing close to a deal breaker. If you need a wireless keyboard, give this one a try.Highly recommended!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Perfect for use with my Samsung Smart TV
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have two 6 Series (MU6290) 40" Samsung 4K Smart TVs that I purchased at Costco, one in my office and the other in my master bedroom.  For about $19 I purchased a wireless keyboard and mouse combo on Amazon to use with the TV in my office.  They use a single unifying USB reciever and work great, just plug and play.  The only thing I found I didn't like was having two devices to keep track of and having to switch between them to point and input data.  I saw this keyboard as an Amazon Deal of the Day two days ago and just received it, in fact I'm writing this review with it while sitting on the bed and using my bedroom TV.  It turns out to have been a very good purchase because it works great!  I merely plugged the unifying USB receiver into the first USB input on the back of the TV, turned the keyboard on and started using it, true plug and play.  And boy do I love using the touchpad to cursor around instead of having to switch between the keyboard and mouse like I do in my office.  In fact, even though the keyboard and mouse work fine on the TV in the office,  I may end up buying another K400+ to use in the office, it's "that nice" not having to use two devices.  I know the K400+ is advertised as a device for using with a computer connected to a TV but I read other reviews where it was being used directly with a smart TV without a computer and, even though it works great with my Samsung, I can't speak to whether it works with all smart TVs, though I expect it should work with any of the later Samsung Smart TVs which use Samsung's Tizen OS.  I don't know if it works with the other two major Smart TV operating systems, WebOS & Android.  It's light, seems well made, has a QWERTY keboard with nice key response and feel and is spaced fine for touch typing.  It's great for basic input and I'm finding out more about how it functions with my TV.  For instance, I found out holding down the CTRL key while cursoring moves the cursor one word at a time, holding down the SHIFT key while cursoring highlights one letter at a time, holding down the SHIFT + CTRL keys while cursoring highlights one word at a time, etc.  These are familiar, however I've discovered by playing around that other keys and key combinations do things but the result may not necessarily be what I expected, but I'm the type who likes to play and learn and will thus get even more use from this keyboard as I learn.  For example, just discovered esc key is equivalent to the "back"  function when used in your browser.  I can mention the media keys, previous chapter, next chapter, pause/play, volume up & down don't work with my TV.  I'm sure they do if the keyboard is connected to a computer that's connected to a TV, as advertised.  However this keyboard is perfect for anyone who only simply wants to point and input, especially if you only want to use one device!  Overall I'm "extremely pleased" with the K400+ and am so glad I decided to give it a try.  Of course the only thing I can't comment on is it's longevity but I hope it lasts a good long time because I love this thing!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great for budget entertaiment peripheral, outstanding operating system compatability
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Logitech K400 Plus is a great addition to your multimedia TV setup when you set up a PC or Android TV. Rather than using the remote with Gyroscope to type out each letter to a show or movie that you are trying to find, This wireless keyboard makes it easier for you to type the words out at ease without fatiguing you arms when swinging them back and forth to each virtual QWERTY pad on screen. It also has a built-in track pad that is conveniently placed on the right side so you can not only use typing, but also cursor your way to specific buttons and search bar. It is packed with so many features that I find it useful in any way. I mainly use it for my Android Box, so the digital volume button and the back button has been used plenty of times for me and I didn't have to cursor my way down to the task bar to change the settings from there.The connectivity is pretty simple as you turn on the keyboard, plug in the USB dongle in the box, turn on your TV, and it should recognize immediately without any use of driver install. The size of this keyboard is around a 65% layout with an added track pad to the side. It is on the thinner side, so don't expect that the keyboard is made with quality as it does display creeking noises when pressed down. Speaking of pressed down, the key strokes are not mechanical and have a short travel. It feel very mushy when pressed, not the best keyboard per say, but it does get the job done. Battery life, is surprisingly very good as it lasted quite a long time for me, but your mileage may vary as I turn the keyboard off after every use to conserve battery. I like how the USB is conveniently place in the back cover inside where you access the battery compartment.Now, the reason, why I gave this keyboard a 3 star, is because of the way the keyboard felt. Although its features is a standout, it ruined it for me with the mushy keys. I'm also comparing this to the Logitech K600 that I also owned and that keyboard, although a tad more expensive, felt way better then the K400. Too bad, I don't understand why Logitech still kept this keyboard the K400 and discontinued the K600. There is no way you can find psychically in stores or in any online sellers. The K600 keys are mushy, however, a different kind of mushy. This mushy is muted and very composed, while the K400 felt so out of place. The built quality, although both made of some find of plastic, the heft from the K600 felt like it is quality. The design on the K600 also felt like it was well thought out compared to the K400.Overall, as a budget wireless keyboard that is practically compatible with almost all platforms without any drivers needed is a huge plus for me. Anyone who are looking for a keyboard and wonder if it is compatible with their system, I can safely recommend this keyboard as long as they are only using it for a short while and not long sessions. I find that using this keyboard on long sessions can feel fatiguing and wanting to have that extra key travel that "normal" keyboards do.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Logitech K400 Plus Wireless Touch TV Keyboard Review
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Logitech K400 Plus Wireless Touch TV Keyboard ReviewThe Logitech K400 Plus Wireless Touch TV Keyboard works flawlessly with the Nvidia Shield Pro. Setup is incredibly simple—just plug the USB receiver into the Shield Pro, and you’re ready to go. No complicated installations or software are required, making it a plug-and-play solution for any home theater or media center setup.One of the most impressive aspects of this keyboard is its responsiveness. There is no delay in either typing or mouse movement, even when navigating menus, typing in search fields, or browsing the web. The touchpad is smooth and precise, ensuring that you can control the cursor just as easily as you would on a desktop or laptop. This level of performance is crucial for a seamless user experience, and the K400 Plus delivers it without a hitch.Another standout feature is the battery life. Logitech claims up to 18 months of battery life, and based on my experience, it’s spot on. I’ve been using it regularly for several months without needing to replace the batteries, which is impressive for a wireless device.Overall, the Logitech K400 Plus Wireless Touch TV Keyboard is a highly reliable and efficient accessory for the Nvidia Shield Pro. It offers a simple setup, fast and precise performance, and excellent battery life. If you're looking for a no-fuss, responsive keyboard and touchpad combo for your home theater or streaming setup, this one comes highly recommended.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Excellent product. Lightweight and small, without compromising too much on key size.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Just had it delivered a few hours ago. Tried it with my mobile (had to get a small OTG adaptor to get started). I also own the K480, and got this one because it has a touchpad. Comparing the two, both have unique features that I would not call positive or negative, because how one views a feature, or the lack thereof, depends on one's requirements. The plus-point of the K480 is that it connects through bluetooth, leaving the port free to charge the mobile (if you want to use it with your mobile/tab) or connect a pendrive to it. The keys are larger and better spaced out (important if typing comfort is a major priority). The K400 plus, on the other hand, requires the OTG adaptor, plus, the unifying receiver used to connect the keyboard to devices like the mobile, tab, or the LCD TV. The plus point of this feature is that connection is immediate. The minus point is that one must be careful not to lose the 'unifying receiver'. Also, if you forget the OTG connector, there is no way you can connect the keyboard to anything. The 'K400 Plus' is also lighter and slightly tinier: But comfortable enough for normal to large sized fingers to type without any obstacles. Unlike the K480, this piece has the touch pad. One main advantage of going for these keyboards ( be it the K480 and K400) is the amount of money saved...in my case, I saved 28K approx., the amount I would have to invest for getting a new laptop. And just didn't have the money to invest in one. Now, with this, I can complete most college assigments. And a couple of years later when my phone conks off, I can simply get a new smartphone for about 8-10K. If one calculates the interest accumulated, one has way more in one's hand than one thinks.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Good keyboard but a bit overpriced.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Very useful keyboard for a media centre PC. Very handy having both the keyboard and trackpad in one unit rather than trying to find a surface to use a mouse on. Keyboard is good to type on. The unit as a whole feels solid but the plastic it is made out of seem quite cheap - which the product definitely was not! So the prices Logitech charge are a bit high but its the only media centre keyboard on the market so you just have to deal with it.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: The dongle is on the flap of the box.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Very important detail. You would expect the dongle to be in the battery compartment, but it is actually on a flap on the box. Seller was very polite and helpful when I enquired about it. On an unrelated note, this keyboard works with the Logitech Options software, but Logitech Options, the program to configure the keyboard does not seem to work with Window 11. Just something to be aware of. The keyboard and trackpad will still work, only there won't be a way to reverse two finger scrolling direction. That is a Logitech issue.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Durable. My god it is durable.Durable. My god it is durable.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: A decent and DURABLE keyboard. Has somewhat frequent double press issues, but otherwise very good.I bought this initially as a bad replacement for my KeyCron keyboard. a 10x downgrade in price, but found it very responsive when typing - satisfying. Haven't felt like I needed to rush repairing my old keyboard since this one functions mostly fine, and looks cute!Nearly a year after purchase, tragedy happened. My last keyboard had started smoking after the inevitability of a spilled drink, and like clock work, this keyboard suffered the same fate. An uncoordinated motion sent a torrent of liquid against the keyboard. Not water, that would be too covenant. This torrent was sugary, sticky, and 10-15% abv. title wave sent crashing directly between the keys and into the circuitry of this durable device. Despite my panic and frantic attempts to pad up liquid, this keyboard kept it's familiar and comforting pink hue, not wavering in the slightest - acting as a proxy of a beaconed confidence towards it's creators.While I had been short circuiting, this modest device had survived a mechanical equivalent to hurricane Katrina. Not one LED flickered, not one key had it's functionality damaged. It had survived what no keyboard ever should - mechanical nor membrane.-- Real talk --This keyboard is pretty decent. I bought it because my NAS couldn't understand my expensive keyboard, and it ended up being my main keyboard for over a year. My job requires a lot of typing, and I've noticed it occasionally double presses keys with a delay of ~100ms, causing an accidental letter or space to be inserted where it wasn't intended. Having used/purchased at least 20 keyboards in my days, no temporary keyboard has performed better than this one. It's affordable, and you can't expect perfection AT THIS PRICE RANGE, but for gaming and for daily use or work, it's durability and functionality are exceptional compared to others in the same range. 8.6/10, don't daily drive unless you need to, but if you need to, you can count on it to last.
