productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great for those with long nails.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this keyboard for a couple of reasons.  I type at night, and when I wake up early, I'll do schoolwork.  It's backlit and I can see the keys in the dark.  There are a few settings to have the keys act or light up differently.  And, because I have medium-long nails - the keys are large enough, and there is enough space between them, to accommodate my medium-length gel nails.  I got raised keycaps to stick on the keys of this keyboard but they are not necessary for the length of my nails.  Its appearance is as depicted, not too big, not too small.  The keyboard connected easily to my laptop and is just as easy to set on top when not in use.  It unplugs from the USB outlet easily, making removability a cinch when I decide enough is enough (not often) and pack everything up and put it away.  It's very responsive, typing exactly as I type or game.  None of the keys have stopped working or gotten stuck, even with my long nails.  I love the sound of the keys clicking, again not too loud nor too soft.  It gives me a 90s vibe while typing, and I can hear if I've hit the keys.  Overall, I'm very glad I decided to buy this keyboard.  It's perfect for my needs.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Nice, blue switch. led mechanical keyboard that doesn't break the bank.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If you're looking for a slim, low profile, led mechanical keyboard with blue switches, then you will be happy with this. The keyboad is exactly as described in the listing. The keyboard housing is made of plastic which makes the keyboard lightweight. The keys have a nice tactile feel with a nice "clicky" sound. The build quality is good, but doesn't compare to the solid feel of my Motospeed or Red Dragon keyboards. Included with the keyboard is a little plastic keycap puller.The led's are nice and bright and can be turned off. The CON is that each key is a set color, so if you're looking for a keyboard whose keys can change to various colors, you might want to skp this one. I personally did not care for any of the available 9 light modes. The 9 modes were definitely not exciting in my opinion and with keys being a preset color, I found some of the modes quite distracting. You can increase, decrease the brightness or turn off the leds. If you're looking for a keyboard where each key can display a multitude of different colors, this is keyboard is not for you.As for the the sole purpose of using this as a mechanical keyboard, then you won't be disappointed. I purchased this for use at work because I love the tactile feedback of mechanical keyboards. I didn't not test the liquid resistance of the kayboard but there are cutouts on the bottom for liquid drainage. No key ghosting was detected during its use. Again, if LED keyboards is what you fancy, I don't think you will be pleased with this because the keys are a preset color and can't be changed. As for the function of being a mechnical keyboard, this works well for the price point.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Bought this keyboard for my office, as a replacement for a wireless, membrane based keyboard that was starting to show its age.The value of this keyboard is excellent.  Based on the feel, it seems to be a true mechanical keyboard with switches, and not a simulated one using a membrane contact with a clicky mechanism.  The feel is great and the pressure is just right to prevent most accidental touches to adjacent keys from inserting extra letters.  Nice and clicky, maybe not the best for noise if you're in an office with other people, but the feel is great and if you work in a private office like I do the noise won't matter much.  I had thought the RGB colors would be distracting, especially for an office, but actually they are fairly subdued and actually seem to help with positioning (I am a fast hunt-and-peck 3 finger typist, so this actually matters a lot to me).I have a much more expensive Razer mechanical gaming keyboard at home, and the main difference I see between them, other than cosmetic differences, is that the Razer keys seem like they have a hair trigger and require very little motion to produce keystrokes, while this keyboard is a bit stiffer and requires the keys to be depressed a little harder in order to produce a keystroke.  So if you are relying on a hair trigger response for gaming, this maybe is not the best choice, although for a casual gamer like me it's more than adequate.  But for actually getting work done, the hair-trigger of the Razer keyboard makes it really hard not to make typos, and this keyboard is a lot better in that regard.One minor nitpick is that the font used to label the keys is a little odd, and the "6" really, really looks like a "G", which can be a little off-putting at first.  But that's just a minor quibble.Final verdict:  Definitely worth buying, unless you're an absolutely elite hardcore gamer.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Mechanical Gaming Keyboard – Over a Year of Flawless Performance!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: After using this mechanical gaming keyboard for well over a year now, I can confidently say it's one of the best purchases I've ever made — not a single issue has come up the entire time. It's seen heavy daily use for both gaming and typing, and it's held up beautifully, including one memorable incident where I accidentally spilled soda right onto it; I was able to quickly disassemble it, clean it thoroughly with water and some rubbing alcohol, and it came back working like nothing ever happened, which speaks volumes about its build quality and durability. The RGB lighting is absolutely vibrant and stunning, with multiple settings and effects that let me customize the look to match my setup, whether I'm going for a subtle glow or a full-blown rainbow light show. The mechanical blue switches are honestly the sweet spot — they offer that satisfying, tactile clicky feel that's so satisfying for typing, while still being incredibly responsive and snappy for gaming, and thanks to the full anti-ghosting on the 104 keys, every single keypress registers perfectly even during the most intense, fast-paced gaming moments. With its rugged build, gorgeous RGB, fantastic switches, and full-sized layout, this keyboard has completely exceeded my expectations — I couldn't recommend it more to anyone looking for a reliable, high-performing mechanical keyboard!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Feels like the legendary Model M, sporting it strong points and its quirks.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If you missed the old,clicky Model M from IBM, this keyboard emulates it pretty well.  One must consider though, that it may emulate it too well.  If you have fat fingers, you will find yourself making the same typos that you mad in high school when you learned to type on one.  However, this is no deal breaker in my opinion.  The speed at which I can type has vastly improved with the solid tactile feedback that tells you without a doubt that you press was registered.Setup couldn't be easier, just plug it into any USB port and away you go.  Recognizes immediately as a 104 key with perks.  Having the media controls and other immediate functions right there is nice too.As far as the design goes, it is very rugged and ready for the millions of keystrokes you will put on it as a writer.  You will find a kind of typing joy you haven't experienced in quite a long time.  No soft-touch or sickle keyboard will match the feel from what you get here.The only thing I find really off is the shallow height of the back stands. I think that they should be redesigned to be a bit taller.  I cut a little piece of flat trim to set them on and that made the angle perfect.All-in-all, this keyboard is a joy to type on.  I don't use it for gaming, because I see this as a waste of a premium feeling keyboard, wearing out the ASWD area and ruining it.  I haven't had such a good keyboard in years and I'm not destroying that way.The one caveat I would warn you about is that if you use it on a KVM switch that is USB powered, this keyboard draws quite a bit of power to run the back light.  be aware that you may get video background issues.  Mine works just fine if I turn the backlight down low.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: High Quality, Gorgeous LED Backlighting, Perfect PriceHigh Quality, Gorgeous LED Backlighting, Perfect Price
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: This mechanical keyboard is amazing for gamers looking to pick up a high-quality blue-switch mechanical keyboard. When I consider and review this product, I keep the following factors in mind:Functionality and Use - 5/5The overall functionality of this keyboard is perfect, leaving me with minimal complains as a high-frequency and intensity user. As a proficient typist, I frequently type over 120 WPM and use combinations of hotkeys to complete tasks efficiently. This keyboard has supported this level of use during work/office settings, and feels highly responsive and crisp during high-intensity gaming moments, due to the blue key-switches creating a noticeable "click" with each keypress. If you have roommates or family, you may want to consider the clicking sounds of this keyboard while typing. The fact that they will likely hear your typing due to the pure "clicky-ness" of the key switches may present itself as an issue to some. Personally, this is not a factor that applies to my circumstances.Build Quality and Durability - 5/5After 1 Month of intensive use, I have not noticed any issues so far in terms of key-press responsiveness, structural integrity, or wiring/USB issues. The keys hold in place well and the LED's have stayed consistently bright.Product Design - 5/5The design of this keyboard is minimal, but effective. Exactly what I was looking for when shopping for a keyboard within this general price range. The all-black style allows the LED backlights to really *pop*, even in bright light/daylight. The inclusion of a "Fn" key allows for the same hotkeys and macros most would be used to with other keyboards, such as volume control and media playback, amongst other things.QoL Features - 4.5/5This keyboard comes with 9 different LED-backlighting effects, such as lighting per keypress, "breathing" effects, WASD + Arrow Key backlighting, and more to complement a variety of use-cases. It would be nice to have the option to customize the LED backlighting colours themselves, as the backlighting options are pre-set; however, the crisp glow and colour choice are visually appealing and I am happy with the options provided.Value for Money - 5/5Overall, I am highly satisfied with the purchase of this Keyboard and would recommend it to any gamer, office-worker, or avid tech geek like myself. For such a low price-point, you are getting a physical product that is equal in quality to that of a name brand like Razer or Corsair, without paying for the related bloatware and branding. Anybody looking to pick up their first mechanical keyboard, you cannot go wrong with this!

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Good quality, affordable mechanical keyboard. Surprised by its quality given its price range.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Very satisfied with this purchase. Head and shoulders above my membrane Logitech K120 Wired Business Keyboard, and without breaking the bank too! To be honest, I feel lucky to have gotten this keyboard at such a low price. At this price point, I could not find a single mechanical keyboard that met all of my requirements but this one. In fact, even some of the more expensive mechanical keyboards didn't meet all of my requirements. For starters, the keyboard uses the UK layout with the pound sign and hash symbol key in the right place—very important for me. Second, this is a full-size keyboard with a numeric keypad at the right. This was important for me as I wanted a keyboard that did all of the same things as my previous keyboard, the only difference being that it is mechanical—a requirement that this RisoPhy mechanical keyboard fulfils precisely. (I should note, too, that most of the mechanical keyboards at this price range and even some more expensive ones, being shorter in width, lacked a numeric keypad.) Then there is the feel of the keyboard. The product description says that it uses "BLUE switches", seemingly modelling its switches on the classic tactile and clicky Cherry MX Blue switches. (It is unlikely that the keyboard uses actual Cherry MX Blue switches, given the price range, but rather its own knock-off versions of the switches.) While this may not be what some gamers are looking for (looking for something smoother and offering the same resistance all the way down without a slight bump as you press each key), this is perfect for me, as I was looking for a keyboard that produced nice responsive, tactile feedback, mirroring a classic typewriter effect. Some people may be put off by this, thinking that it makes the keyboard too noisy, and while, yes, there is a clicking noise with each key press, it honestly isn't that loud (though because there is still an audible clicking noise, I can understand criticisms saying that this keyboard is inappropriate for an office environment, for example, where such a constant clicking noise can cause distractions.) The keyboard is nice to type on, which is my primary use for it rather than gaming.A feature I don't care as much for is the rainbow backlighting. From my tests, the "9 different backlights" settings mentioned in the product description work exactly as expected. Also working as intended (at least from my tests on Windows 11) are the "12 multimedia combinations", effectively function keys that perform operations, such as, open a calculator and open Windows search.The major downside to this keyboard that I can think of is that the keyboard switches are not hot-swappable (though at this price point, this isn't a disappointment but just something to be expected.)In all, if you are looking for a keyboard that meets some of the same requirements as I was, at this price, I am unaware of a better keyboard on this website than this one.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Comme dit dans un autre commentaire, il est parfait quand c'est ce qu'on veut. J'écris énormément et j'ai une frappe très rapide.Quand on frappe vite, le top c'est un clavier mécanique de ce type, et c'est très rare d'en trouver à moins de 100€![FRAPPE]J'ai une préférence pour ceux avec un retour son (comme sont les claviers à switch/commutateur bleu) et bon un anti-ghosting: on peut frapper vite, avec exactitude et si besoin corriger dans l'immédiat. Que ce soit pour du gaming ou de la frappe écrite très rapide, c'est un excellent clavier.Par contre, clairement, je ne vois pas des personnes qui tapent occasionnellement supporter ce clavier, qui est bruyant... comme un clavier à commutateur bleu! Quand je suis au téléphone, j'essaie parfois de taper un truc discrètement: je me fais griller systématiquement et on me dit de ne pas fracasser mon clavier... les gens sont habitués à des claviers silencieux.[SOLIDITÉ]Le clavier est vraiment excellent: je l'utilise depuis 1 an, de manière intensive. La touche espace est un peu usée (lustrée mais on voit toujours la barre horizontale) mais toutes les touches sont encore parfaitement lisibles, ce qui est exceptionnel pour de l'ABS et mon utilisation intensive! Des heures de frappe par jour, au moins un nettoyage par semaine (pas délicat, avec un produit, et des brosses pour enlever les masses de poils de chats... et les miettes ^^ ).[ERGONOMIE]La surélévation est un peu trop marquée pour moi: elle créé une casse du poignet qui fatigue, mais le retour tactile est énorme.Comme dit, le rétroéclairage est à un dosage parfait: ni trop peu (aide au repère rapide en cas de besoin), ni trop (fatigue des yeux).Les pattes arrières qui ont tendance à se replier, mais je suis une grosse brute et ça me gêne moins que sur de nombreux claviers.[CONCLUSION] Clavier adapté à une personne qui cherche du matériel solide, efficace, de bonne qualité à petit prix et surtout un clavier mécanique avec un retour son marqué. Pour moi on n'est pas loin du clavier parfait!

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Great laptop keyboard replacement with a caviet when booting
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I have three laptops that all suffer from the dreaded disease: Beerus Spillus. So, I checked into replacement keyboards and found that this option was about a third the price of buying a specific replacement keyboard for even one laptop. The keyboard appears tiny, but it's actually the same size as a laptop keyboard. I'm probably going to miss not having a numeric keypad. You'll need to get a wrist rest for it, if you use it a lot. Pairing is just standard Bluetooth stuff that only takes a few seconds.The big issue is if you dual boot your computer, since you don't actually have a working keyboard until the operating system boots. Assuming you're using as Linux/Windows combination and Grub to select which operating system to boot, you need to configure it to start Linux by default. In Linux, create a shell script file with the following command "sudo grub-reboot X && reboot"  where X is whatever menu item your Windows option is on your grub boot menu (usually 2 or 3).  I just added an icon to the Linux desktop that I double click to run the script. Note that you have to pair the keyboard separately for Windows and Linux, so those three nifty toggle buttons get filled up fast. I need 8 toggle buttons for my three laptops :-(If you're trying to do anything with the bios, such as a boot password, you can't do it, since you don't have an active keyboard. In that case, consider a wireless keyboard since the dongle should be active on power-up.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A quality keyboard that fits me perfectly.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have been a power computer user since the mid-80's.  I put a lot of wear and tear on my peripherals.  My fingers polish the keys smooth over time from typing.  Just any keyboard will not do.Recently my Razer Huntsman Elite keyboard starting to show signs of dying.  My 'e' key intermittently repeating or not typing at all.  It was time to get a new keyboard, but I wasn't willing to spend over $200.  Even though my Huntsman has lasted me about 7 years, I still can't justify spending that kind of money.  And so I set about looking for a fairly inexpensive quality keyboard.I had been hearing good things about Keychron, so I looked on Amazon and saw this retro style keyboard, which is exactly what I like in a keyboard.  I remember back in the day, I had an old metal keyboard that looked similar to this.  It had the old style AT connector.  That keyboard died when I spilled soda pop on it.  I've always wanted to get another one.  The days of metal keyboards are long since gone, but thanks to Keychron we can still get that old styling.The first thing I noticed about the keyboard was the quality in the packaging, and the care taken to give extra keys and a key puller.  The next thing I noticed is the quality of the keyboard itself.  The keys do not click, but when you type the natural noise of the keys being pressed is soothing and provides the feedback you need when typing.  The keys do not feel sluggish, unlike my cheap Logitech wireless keyboard/mouse combo I was using as a go-between.  The weight of the keyboard is what you would expect for a quality keyboard.  The material (plastic) feels durable and not cheap.  The indicator lights are blue LED, which I find appealing.  This is not an RGB keyboard.  I don't want lit keys.  I specifically sought out the non-RGB version.I am happy with my purchase.  I can see myself loving this keyboard for many years.  Big thanks to Keychron for making quality keyboards that computer users want.  Thank you for this retro keyboard that suits me perfectly.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased this keyboard for office work and because I wanted something with a classic look and feel. The first person to comment on it was a coworker who said "that keyboard looks like it came straight out of the 90's" and that is exactly the kind of feedback I was expecting. The design of the keyboard is solid, sturdy, and is heavier than your average thick, hardcover book which prevents any unwanted wandering/movement while typing. My typing experience is exactly as I expected: tactile, light, and loud enough for others to know that you are at work when writing emails or taking notes. I describe the typing sound like a classic *klop* per key that is pressed and released. The keys release immediately and do not stick. The space bar has a pronounced tone that sounds lower and heavier. The keys look and feel tall, are easy to remove for interchanging. I would recommend this for casual typing. Overall this tool is well engineered and I am very satisfied with the value for my money~!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Nice keyboard! I wanted to really like this. I love the color and the layout. It's amazing that it includes "ALT" and "windows" keys for windows layouts, and "Option" and "Command" keys for Mac layouts. There's also a switch that enables you to switch between Mac and Windows layout (which have the alt/windows keys swapped with command/option.) The brown key switches are really nice too. I am a huge fan of the cherry MX red switches but they're extremely noisy for a corporate environment. The brown switches are not quite as precise, but it's a nice balance to keep your office mates happy. There's enough feedback to type well. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Once Forgotten - Now Loved!Once Forgotten - Now Loved!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: After buying this keyboard, testing it for a day, and immediately crawling back to my Magic Keyboard, I let it sit untouched for six months. Recently I decided to give it another chance—and now I can’t believe I held out for so long. The brown switches I opted for are pretty awesome (no experience with mechanical keyboards, but they seem to be close to preference for me). They’ve got this smooth, cushioned tactility that makes every press feel deliberate yet effortless. Once I adjusted my seat and desk height, the typing position finally clicked, and I’ve been hooked since. The dedicated keys, retro design, and seamless Mac integration make me want to reach for it every time I pass my desk. While part of me still wants to experiment with other switch types—maybe something a hair stiffer or softer—that’s just the tinkerer in me. For the price, this is a ridiculously good entry point into the world of mechanical keyboards, I've been converted:(

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: In the last year or so I’ve gotten into PC gaming from console gaming and looked everywhere for affordable and quality additions for my setup and found my way to the Redragon company. I was originally using a full sized mechanical keyboard and wanted a smaller 60% hotswappable one that wouldn’t break the bank and this was a great option. My previous keyboard was heavy, had loud sharp sounding switches, and had a problem with response time when gaming and this one solves most of those problems. It has great response time, nicer soft sounding switches that can be modded or replaced, and is very light weight and small and can easily fit in my relatively small hands.  The only things I will say about it is that it takes a particular type of switch connection that isn’t found in the more popular switches, the power chord is kind of short, and the feet on the back of the keyboard don’t do much and I find using my arm rest under it works better but I can’t beat the price and overall quality. It comes with replacement red linear switches, keycap and switch pullers, and a downloadable software to customize the rbg lighting of the keyboard. Of course as with any kind of electronic purchase do your own research and watch videos about it but I definitely recommend.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent tactile feeedback with this lighted keyboard... Less typos? Maybe.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Who would benefit from this lighted keyboard?1- People with vision problem, as the bold, larger size is truly easy on the eyes.2- People who need a lighted keyboard so it will not disturb other family members,3- People who would like programmed function keys already in place,4-Or Insert your own/different reasons here, there are many more.The wired USB connectivity is good; no worries about bluetooth problems.The lighting brightness is adjustable: 3 levels and off/on.Be aware: this only has a single back light color choice: white.I've been using it for less than a week. It is obvious the manufacturer cares about making a quality product.Keyboard response can be a subjective opinion, so take that into consideration, read a lot of the reviews.I definitely like the "feel". It gives good tactile feedback: you know it when you hit a key.So I think my typos have decreased: there were SO many!It is a bargain at this price, but again I can't comment on how long it will last.Now, I did Not actually pour water on this keyboard to test it for this review... I just knocked a tumbler of water on it by mistake! I quickly wiped off the water and the keyboard is still working fine, thanks to the membrane feature.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I do a lot of work at night in a relatively dimly lit home office and although I am a reasonably experienced keyboarder (formally known as a typist), I still need to search for the seldom used keys and symbols.  I was looking on Amazon for a keyboard with more legible nomenclature when I ran across this one that not only had larger nomenclature but was also backlit.  I had used wireless keyboards for years, but having a wired unit is not a problem with a stationary desk computer.  I fell in love with this keyboard out of the box.  It is full sized and has a nice feel, is relatively quiet and has almost every feature I have ever seen on any keyboard.  The frosting on the cake, however, is the adjustable backlighting which makes it totally functional in a completely dark room.  A great feature of the backlighted keys is that the nomenclature is molded into each key and will never wear off as with screen printed keys.I now have 2 of these keyboards because as soon as my wife saw it, she had to have one as well.  I think that backlighted keyboards are sort of like heated seats and steering wheels in cars in that they seem like a gimmick at first, but once you use them you will never get a new car without them.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Love the lighting and Big font, but other things should be a bit better at this price point.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: TDLR: Bought this for 3 reasons. Backlighting, large font on keys, and hardwired. Overall, I feel it's a decent product, but it has plenty of places where it should be better for the price range it's in.PRO:Backlighting is good. Highest setting does not glare, but still bright enough for daytime use. Lowest setting is perfect for dark room. Large Font makes it easy to read for anyone who struggles with vision. also just looks comfy to me.everything is mapped out well. Function and brightness keys are on right side so they don't conflict with the more often used left alt and ctrl. never thought about that until I had it on this keyboard. Good forethought. Also lights for numpad/Caps/Scroll lock are all very visible and easy to see when on.Simple and easy to use. Hardwired is a plus for me: I get really tired of wifi or bluetooth keyboards that even being wireless still take up a USB slot (when all motherboards over the past 5-7 years have integral bluetooth), and even with that still lose connection regularly. I prefer cords for my keyboard and mouse.CON:Light button doesn't adjust light level: you have to press Function + PageUp/PageDwn. This combo can also turn off the light, so why the extra key? weird and needlessly duplicative.  And the adjustment combo is listed nowhere on the keyboard like you would see other function options on other keyboards, so how is someone to figure that out?Keys are reasonably soft, but they have 90* edges and flat sides instead of sloped sides. Most keyboards slope the sides of the keys a bit so transitioning from one key to the next is a bit smoother. This ends up making the keys feel harder to press then other keyboards since your fingers catch on them if you drag a bit.Case has a reasonable weight to it, rear stands are solid, but the case feels a bit cheap at the edges. This may just be a personal choice, but the case design feels a bit like an afterthought. I've had cheaper keyboards that felt higher quality. This one has noticeable edges along the sides where the plastic pieces fit together. All around it gives off a "cheap keyboard" feel when it doesn't have to.Keys are louder than a softkey keyboard, but quieter than a full mechanical one. spacebar is noticeable louder than the other keys, enough that I'm noticing it after only 10m of typing and it's a bit irritating. This adds to the "cheap" feel. Feels cheaper than it's price point should reflect IMO.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I just ordered a second one.  I bought the first December 2023.  I have enjoyed it until it started to cause issues.  For the past number of months, when I log on  to my computer, I could not enter text, or send an email until perhaps a half hour or more passed, then it seemed to work OK.  I thought  it was a problem with my computer, especially when I could not get into the BIOS, and checked into that for a long time.  Finally, I set up another computer and set it in the same location and connected the keyboard.  The same problems occurred. I checked every cable to see if there was a problem. Finally, I switched keyboards and found the problem all along has been the keyboard.So, there appears to be a problem that can develop over time.  The interesting thing was that after a period of time elapsed, everything worked fine.  Anyway, I ordered a second one, hoping for a few good years, and if similar things occurred, I will be aware.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am on a long housesitting stay, and I didn't bring a keyboard and mouse. Turns out that to really work on my laptop I need them. So I got these. They're fine. Neither the mouse nor the keyboard is quiet, so if you're in a place where others might be bothered, this isn't the set for you. There's a lot of travel on the keys, much more than on the Apple keyboard I'm accustomed to, but I can type almost as fast. If you want to use this with a Mac like I am, you have to hit Fn-W to put the keyboard in the right mode, and you WILL need a USB-A to USB-C converter or hub. The USB-A dongle in the base of the mouse is what connects the keyboard AND the mouse to the computer. I wish they just had regular Bluetooth instead, but you can't complain at this price. These won't be everyday tools for me, but I will keep them for travel.

It connected quickly without any confusion, and I was able to start using it right away.I use this for work every day, and so far it’s been reliable. No connectivity issues, no lag, and everything responds the way it should.The only downside is that it doesn’t come with batteries. Most sets I’ve bought before at least included the initial ones, so that was a little inconvenient.Other than that, it works well, looks good, and does exactly what I needed it to do.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Update: This mouse is wild. It jumps wherever it wants, not where I want it to go. I hate this mouse. I changed the settings to go slower. Did not help. I put in new batteries again. Did not help.  I bought a freaking mouse pad. Did help. It made me lose points on my computer game because it floated all over the screen and when I managed to pin it down, it would not click to select. I can handle disappointment, but mess with my game points and I get cranky.Super cute, if you are into that (I am). The keyboard is very comfortable. But the Mouse...it fits my hand fine, pretty light weight though, I prefer a hardier build in a mouse. The only truly issue is that the mouse does not have a on/off switch. I use the switch daily to save on battery. The keyboard, on the other hand, does have a power switch. The product description states that the keyboard and mouse will go into auto sleep, that is a good thing. They keyboard has several features that I have not tried because 1) I just got it yesterday and 2) I mostly care about the typing.

features: 65% QMK Aluminum Keyboard with Enhanced Typing Sound: Following the EPOMAKER Galaxy70, Galaxy80 and Galaxy100, we are proud to present the innovative new member of the Galaxy Aluminum Keyboard series, with smaller size and greater functions. Introducing Galaxy65, the 65% compact layout wireless keyboard with ball-catch Gasket-Mount and QMK support. Featuring a gasket-mounted structure, high-quality lubed linear switches, and 5 soft cushioning layers, a market-tested formula for satisfying creamy typing sound, the Galaxy65 Keyboard aims at maximum comfort and customization with wide compatibility across PC, Linux computer, Mac Laptop, Android mobiles, and mainstream gaming controllers

Ball-Catch Gasket-Mount Keyboard: Unleash your creativity and embrace the limitless possibilities of personalization, with the ball-catch mechanism that streamlines the customization process. For a perfect fusion of typing stability, typing comfort, creamy sound and portability, the Galaxy65 Mechanical keyboard weighs 1.12kg with an anodized aluminum body and FR4 plate. With ball-catch instead of screws, tweaking switch sockets or experimenting with internal dampening materials become an absolute breeze, as disassembling and reassembling keyboard is as simple as a push and click, empowering you to fine-tune your typing experience with unparalleled ease

QMK/VIA Custom Keyboard: Level up your game with the Galaxy65 QMK Keyboard – the ultimate custom keyboard with unbeatable control. With QMK firmware and VIA software, Galaxy65 keyboard offers limitless customization, where complex commands can be executed with a single keystroke thanks to recorded macros and layouts can be personalized with remapping for maximum efficiency and accessibility. From key’s function to typing feel, fine-tune every aspect of this QMK keyboard with hot-swappable PCB that support both plate-mount and screw-in stabilizers. Elevate your setup, enhance your gameplay, and unleash your full potential with our Galaxy65

200-Hour Long-Lasting Wireless Performance: Upgraded in circuit design and battery quality, the Galaxy65 keyboard presents reliable and long-lasting wireless performance, offering an impressive 200 hours of use with backlight off on a single charge with a 4000mAh rechargeable battery. Packed with three modes of connection and an easily accessible mode switch besides the USB port, the Galaxy65 keyboard offers reliable 2.4Ghz wireless, low-latency cable mode and the versatile BT connectivity. Indulge yourself in continuous gaming sessions with no hassle of cable nor interruptions from charging, and relish in the enduring and stable performance made possible by Galaxy65 keyboard

South-Facing RGB Backlight: Upgrade your desk setup to the style of professional and high-tech, with the Backlit Galaxy65 RGB keyboard. With south-facing LED underneath, every key of Galaxy65 keyboard shines bright and vivid from the typist’s angle. The per-key illumination comes with customizable RGB options, for gamers to personalize brightness, colors and light effects for an immersive session. The thick PBT keycaps are not shine-through, with dye-subbed colors and legends that stay clear and vivid after long-term usage, and compatible with other MX keycaps for customization

Compact 65% Layout 

Following the EPOMAKER Galaxy70, Galaxy80, and Galaxy100, EPOMAKER is proud to launch the innovative new member of the Galaxy Wireless Aluminum Mechanical Keyboard series, Galaxy65. It has a Ball-Catch quick release and sound-dampened gasket-mount structure. Pull the knob and unclick the keyboard shell with a simple push. Long-Lasting Wireless Performance 
Wireless 2.4Ghz, BT & Cable Wired 

Packed with three modes of connection and an easily accessible mode switch besides the USB port, the Galaxy65 keyboard offers reliable 2.4Ghz wireless, low-latency cable mode and the versatile BT connectivity. 
Pair to New Device: 1).Toggle to BT/2.4G Mode. 2).Pressing FN+Q/W/E/R until Q/W/E/R key's flash quicken from slow to rapid. 3).Set Bluetooth on PC or Plug 2.4Ghz Dongle to PC.
Connect to Paired Devices: 1).Toggle to BT/2.4G Mode. 2).Clcik on FN+Q/W/E/R once.
Web Driver for WIN, Mac & Linux 
Customize with VIA Software 

Level up your game with the Galaxy65 VIA Keyboard – the ultimate custom keyboard with unbeatable control. 
Enjoy limitless customization with the VIA web driver, where complex commands can be delivered with a single keystroke thanks to recorded macros, and layouts can be personalized with remapping for maximum efficiency and accessibility. 
Tips: Load JSON to VIA web-based software to start settings. Check the manual inside product package for detailed guide on using VIA.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Galaxy series boards are by far some of Epomaker best, but with it still being Epomaker there are corners cut and some oversights.What is good about this board is that it is full aluminum, has a non flex cut Aluminum plate (says FR4 but I don’t believe this whatsoever), A knob, great RGB, VIA compatibility, and is relatively light and is a ball catch design that good for mod nuts who want to put in their own foam or add tapes.Another great thing about this board is that it’s comfortable and hot swap compatible with decently designed sockets which I suspect are Kailh. In my experience, this board works best with low to mid pitch switches, clicky switches, and silent switches. The ones it comes with are okay but not great. Not sure who makes the but I think it is either Outemu, Leobog, but I really can’t say. I ended up putting Epomaker (Haimu) Silent Sea Salts as this is my office board.The downsides are that since its a ball catch, it almost requires all of its foam to sound good, and it does sound pretty good but if you’re a fan of clacky switches like myself, maybe don’t get this as they will sound foamy winsome people do enjoy as it’s a very mellow ASMR.Another downer is the knob feeling out of place on a ball catch, as you need to remove the cap before you can open up the case. I actually damaged the knob to the point the pole won’t stay flush on the module which is soldered into the board and I do not recommend de-soldering it.And if you planned to Run this foamless, I highly advise against that since the foam is actually keeping the PCB and plate in place which is kinda odd since it uses dumbbell gaskets which are easily what makes this board comfortable beyond belief.I recommend this board when it’s on sale here on Amazon, but you can get it for under $50 on AliExpress. This board is for the average gamer honestly, nothing wrong with it, if you want something sturdy with mod potential.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Classic Epomaker - Amazing Keyboard, Horrible Quality Control
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This keyboard is all around great (physically), 5 stars on that. Metal case, super nice feeling KTT switches, non flex cut PCB (My personal preference), and a really nice gasket mounting style. I'm usually one for different types of builds, but the sort of marbly sound these KTT switches make in the aluminum case is so amazing. Sadly, old Epomaker has never been known for their quality control (just look at their Reddit). I'm only taking off one star because this is Amazon and you can use their great return/replacement policy, but AVOID buying it direct from Epomaker. Mmm, I'm actually typing this review on my Galaxy65 and it still sounds so good... Yummers... Anyways, back to the point. Not just this board, but a lot of other Epomaker boards have had issues with dead PCBs out of the box or broken keys. Mine didn't, thankfully, but it had a weird quirk. It defaulted to Via layer 2 instead of 0, which meant the num keys were mapped to the F keys. This is a super easy fix, though. Just go into via and copy over the layout of layer 0 to layer 2. Okay, with that detail I feel like I'm not being harsh enough with the 4 star rating... But wow, the actual keyboard itself is just a joy to use. Epomaker, PLEASE get your QC team in check because your new keyboards are actually so good and I wish I could recommend them without any caveats.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Ok for 50 ish dollar, but there is a reason for being this cheap...
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: This keyboard sounds very nice and has great build quality for its price. The ball catch system made it feel more premium. The stabs were good, but it would be better to reapply lubes yourself.This keyboard being VIA and QMK compatible is a big plus, but you will need to download the json file on their website.However, I couldn't connect this keyboard via bluetooth(it would not show up in the bluetooth setting) and the 2.4GHz dongle stopped working randomly. It eventually connected back, but it could be frustrating if that happened in the middle of some important task.It would also have a significant input lag (i.e you will see the letter you typed appear on the screen as if it was loading a lagging youtube video, idk how to elaborate on this one. Its not ground breaking though.)Also, it would sometime input random keys when I wasn't even touching the keyboard. This problem comes and goes just like the connection problem above. (I think these problems could be because my pcb is somewhat faulty)Lastly, I personally didn't like the power saving mode and the deep sleep mode. I would prefer charge the keyboard more often than reconnecting with the issues above. This keyboard has 4000 mAh battery, which I feel is way more than enough for a wireless keyboard.If you have low budget this keyboard would be great, but there is reason this keyboard is so cheap for what it offers.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Sehr schöne und hochwertige Tastatur mit einem Problem...
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Erstmal, Epomaker macht meiner Meinung nach echt hammer Tastaturen zu fairen Preisen, im Bereich Custom Tastaturen, nur leider sind alle Tastaturen, die etwas hochwertiger sind, oft immer mit US-Layout. Was eine Verwendung im deutschen Raum etwas schwerer macht. Da fehlende Ä, Ö und Ü Tasten, was schon ärgerlich ist. Beim zocken fällt das allerdings nicht auf, wofür die Tastatur von mir hauptsächlich genutzt wird. Im Thema zocken ist sie perfekt für mich, schöner Klang, angenehmer Auslöse-Weg und gute Haptik auf den Tasten. Dazu ist die Tastatur Gasket-Mounted, was tippen und schreiben sehr angenehm macht. Zudem ist der Aluminium-Rahmen ein Hingucker und sorgt für ordentliches Gewicht. Die LED-Beleuchtung ist auch toll, bei mir aber immer aus. Allem in Allem eine sehr schöne und hochwertige Tastatur, das US-Layout ist nur leider ein wenig unpraktisch hierzulande. Wem das nicht stört, macht gar nichts falsch!
Very good board for the price tbh

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A well built but poorly thought out product.A well built but poorly thought out product.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I like the feel of the keyboard, that’s what attracted me to it. I wanted the key feel of the old IBM Selectric typewriter and this comes somewhat close. It’s interesting that it has the tactile feel of the old manual Royals I learned to type on 60 years ago. However, the little raised bar at the bottoms of the F And J keys used to identify the home position for my hands is useless because the chrome plastic decorative rings that encircle the keys is raised and block it. Another issue is that for some reason these plastic rings split down one side making them lose and through the course of typing cause them to pop off the key. (See photos) The manufacturer is aware of this engineering defect and chose to address it by enclosing a bag with about a dozen replacement rings and replacement key switches. I’ve not had a key switch fail yet. I type probably 6 to 10 hours a day so I use the keyboard more than the average consumer. But I’ve had 5 of these rings split within a month’s use. At this rate I’ll be out of replacements within another month or so. When you under engineer a part, offering more under engineered parts is not a solution. I use the keyboard in my lap while I’m sitting in a recliner. I know that’s not ideal, but it works best for me. Given that it sits in my lap the fact that it’s quite heavy for a keyboard is taxing on muy legs. I’d guess it weighs in excess of 2 pounds which I find odd since every external part is plastic. It must have a cast iron frame internally. I don’t know as I haven’t disassembled it. The last issue I want to address is the fact that the key labels are only visible when the keys are illuminated in certain colors. Yellow works best. Blue doesn’t, (See video). Given my needs and the shortcomings I probably wouldn’t buy it again. I might if I used it at a table and only used it occasionally but as an amateur writer I sometimes write 30 to 60 pages a day. I hope this sheds some light on the product so you can determine if it’s for you. I want to stress that the overall quality of the product’s function is excellent in my opinion and expect it to last a long time, but I’m going to have to try something like actually putting a small amount of  glue on the rings to cement them to the keys. There’s no reason to ever remove them anyway. The manufacturer probably should have done this as a part of the manufacturing process considering the premium price charged for it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I've Had It A Month- How It Holds upI've Had It A Month- How It Holds up
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got the Royal Kludge R-75 about a month ago and honestly, I'm blown away by what you get for the price.I’m really into the look of this thing. The pink and white-ish colors are great, and it doesn't take up my whole desk because it's a compact size profile,  but it still has the arrow keys and the function row, which I actually use. The first thing I noticed was the weight. It feels solid, not flimsy at all. And the metal volume knob is just a really nice touch. It feels solid when you turn it, not cheap.The Sound is the Reason I'm most glad I bought It. I’ve been on the hunt for a keyboard that gives you that deep, soft "thock" without any annoying echo, and this is it. It sounds so rich and creamy right out of the box. Whatever they put inside this thing totally kills any hollow sound. Every keypress sounds substantial and satisfying. I spend a lot of time typing, and the sound alone makes it worth it.I love the feeling of the keycaps. They have this nice, soft texture to them, and they feel thick and durable, like they’ll last forever. They're also shaped in a way that just feels comfortable and natural for my hands.The stock switches are super smooth. They glide really easily. I came from clicky switches and then tried membrane, but these linear cream switches are the happy medium. It's an effortless press that just feels super precise, when I'm gaming or just writing an email.If you're looking for a keyboard that feels and sounds custom-made, but you just want to buy it, plug it in, and go, the RK R-75 is probably it!  The quality you get for the money is kind of unreal. I highly recommend it.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Dateline: A Desktop, Under the Harsh Light of a Monitor. In the world of mechanical keyboards, you are on a holy quest. A search for the perfect combination of feel, sound, and function. The RK ROYAL KLUDGE R75 is a machine that gets you agonizingly close to the promised land. It is a dense, substantial slab of pure typing pleasure, a tool that feels like it was carved from a single, solid block of intent.The 75% layout is a masterstroke of efficiency, keeping all the essential keys while trimming the fat, leaving just enough room for that beautiful, beautiful volume knob—a tactile, analog dial in a world gone mad with touchscreen nonsense. The keycaps are a revelation. Thick, textured PBT with a clean, dignified font, a welcome rebellion against the spiky, illegible "gamer" typeface that plagues so many other boards. This is a keyboard for a grown-up.But the real magic happens when you type. This is a gasket-mounted board. The entire plate that holds the switches is cushioned, suspended, isolated from the main chassis. The result is a sound and feel that is nothing short of a religious experience. There is no harsh, metallic clatter. There is only a deep, creamy, and profoundly satisfying thonk. Each keystroke is a tiny, rhythmic sermon. It is the sound of work being done, of thoughts being hammered into existence. It is glorious.And it is here, at the peak of this sensory delight, that the bitterness creeps in. The digital ghost that haunts this otherwise magnificent machine. I speak, of course, of the firmware.This particular R75, an early soldier from a previous hardware revision, is a ghost ship. It has no soul. It lacks the crucial QMK/VIA support that would allow a true power user to remap its keys, to mold it into a perfect, customized extension of their own will. To have a machine this physically perfect, this satisfying to the ear and hand, but to be locked out of its brain… it is a special kind of torment. It’s like being handed the keys to a vintage muscle car, only to find the hood has been welded shut.There is no wireless, no Bluetooth, a simple, honest wired connection that I can respect. But the lack of deep, customizable firmware is a wound that cannot be ignored. It is the one, single, glaring flaw in an otherwise masterpiece of affordable engineering.So here it sits. A four-star champion in a five-star body. It is a joy to type on, a solid, thonky, and beautiful piece of hardware. But the knowledge of what it could be, of the potential locked away behind an outdated bit of silicon, is a constant, nagging reminder of its tragic, near-perfect status. It is a keyboard that has perfected the body, but is still waiting for its soul.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a nice wireless keyboard and mouse set! I just wish I had thoroughly read about the product before purchasing. To me, the biggest downside is the lack of effects. My old keyboard (RIP) had so many light settings/colors and functions. This keyboard does not- 3 brightness settings is all you get. The keys clicks softly and feels good (if you’re into that kind of thing. I do not like that some of the keys don’t respond all the time. It may be user error and I need to get used to it. The mouse clicks are great! I like how it feels and it’s small. I think I may have needed the matte black as my lamp creates a glare of the keys and makes it hard to read. But a non issue for me.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Ok.  Well, it's definitely a keyboard and mouse combo.  It arrived on time.  It was super easy to set up.  Lights are neat (I'm a nerd... it's ok. lol)  The mouse bottom has a LOT of friction.  On my desk top, the amount of drag is crazy.  Ended up actually having to put scotch tape on the bottom so it would slide as it's supposed to.  If you do lots of "dragging and dropping" I strongly suggest against this set.  Mouse constantly drops prematurely.  Really annoying.  It is quiet tho!  It just quietly drops everything your trying to drag!  Buttons on the keyboard are sticky specifically the left shift and space bar.  I've had to back space twice writing this review because it didn't registera (leaving that one in there so make it 3 times) anyways, it didn't register a space bar strike.  Going to keep theset (again) for aw crap moments, but definitely getting something else.  This might be a factory whoops, but I kinda feel like it's just meh.  Hope this helps someone, I'm out!**EDIT**  Company sent me a replacement.  When I get a chance I will set it up and see if it's better, worse or the same, and then edit this again.  5 stars for company feedback!**EDIT** (Again)  Finally got a chance to use the replacement. Used the C to USB to hook it up to my tablet, seems to be much better!  No set up required, just took off and worked nicely.  Left shift button is a bit sticky but I can live with that!  Might loosen up with use.  Mouse seems smoother as well, upgrading to 5 stars, even with the sticky button simply because of the customer service and my first set must have been a exception, not the rule.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 26, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Connectivity and Longevity are not strong points
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've had this for about 9 months now. At first, it worked very well, although it needed charging every couple of weeks. First, the black on the keys started to wear off, which isn't a huge deal as I know which key is where. Then it would "fall asleep" during regular use. With a few minutes, the keys would stop responding. This was addressed by charging weekly. Then keys would stop responding during game play. At this point, I'll be walking forward in a game and suddenly stop, because the keyboard's connection has failed while in use. Used to be that turning of the keyboard and back on would fix this, but at this point, I have to remove and replug the connector into my computer's USB port. The same happens on all USB ports, and if I use the USB-C adaptor. The backlighting is fine for me, although the brightness between lowest and highest isn't a huge spectrum.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 13, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Stopped Working After 4 Mo.  (Replaced AND Refunded!!)
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was truly pleased with this mouse/keyboard combo. The lighting options were quite fun, and it worked just as it was supposed to, until it didn't. After four months of use, the mouse just stopped working. I have reached out to the company about it, and will update this review if they respond. I gave them 2 stars because the colorful lights made me happy every time I saw them, and I appreciated that.UPDATE: After I reached out to the company, they quickly got back to me, and after a few failed troubleshooting exchanges, they offered to send me a new mouse, free of charge. The representative, Mary Hurley, seemed genuinely sympathetic and committed to resolving the issue, so much so that I would have liked to bump them back up to 5 stars. Alas, the product did fail, so they get 4.NEW UPDATE: The replacement mouse arrived and works fine, AND the manufacturer reached out to me and offered a full refund. Full disclosure, although it did stop working and that was kind of a pain - I would still buy it again, or any other product this company makes. I felt quite seen and heard by them, and that's the type of company I want to support.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It's a different kind of Keyboard that's for sure. They added a bunch of added features that you would think would be great. I'm not a gamer, so I'm using the keyboard as my daily typer at work. It works ok for the most part once your muscle memory gets used to the new key layout.My biggest complaint, is it's a 98% keyboard. Big sticker on the side of it that said so. I had to figure out what a 98% keyboard is, and then I figured it out. It's missing buttons or keys. They added a bunch of FUNCTION buttons, where if you function and / it does the PRTSCREEN or a function and - and you get the PAUSE. Well, no where on this keyboard, with all the functions and everything else is there an "END" that key is just left off completely.Most of you might not ever use the END key, but in excel or other programs the END key brings you the end of the line. Seems simple enough, but when your Fx variable is 1000 characters long that "END" key is useful. I don't know why they wouldn't give it a function key or something.I like the LED's, it helps me see my keys during those early morning sessions. The volume dial works great, but some of the other shortcut keys don't do anything at all. The Explorer button, email button, and calculator button do nothing.All in all it's a nice, quiet keyboard. I'll have to figure out a key mapping shortcut for my "END" key.

If your computer is experiencing incompatibility issues, and solutions. 
Connection Problems
Check that the keyboard is properly plugged into the USB port on your computer. Try replacing the USB port with a different one, including other USB ports on the motherboard, USB docking station, etc. to rule out whether it is a faulty interface or the keyboard itself. 
Driver problems
The system is newer (e.g. Win10, etc.) and the keyboard driver does not support the system, you may need to update the driver. Sometimes the keyboard driver related registry files in the system registry are missing or corrupted, which may lead to incompatibility. You can try to perform registry operations, such as re-registering the keyboard driver 
Operating System Problems
The keyboard is not compatible with the operating system. For example, some newer keyboards may not support older versions of the operating system (e.g. Win7, etc.) and require systems such as Win8 or Win10. In this case, a system reinstallation may be required. 
System setup issues. For example, there may be conflicting or incorrect settings for the keyboard driver in the system's device manager. You can try to update or reset the keyboard driver in the device manager. 
Hardware failure
The keyboard itself is faulty. For example, the keyboard plug is damaged, the internal circuitry of the keyboard is faulty and so on. In this case, it is recommended to contact after-sales service for a new keyboard. 
The USB interface of the computer motherboard is faulty. It may be that the interface is damaged, poor contact, etc. You can try to use other interface devices to test whether the motherboard USB interface is normal. 
The problem of incompatibility of Windows keyboard on Mac 
The problem of incompatibility of Windows keyboard on Mac is mainly caused by the difference of key layout and function keys, you can use System Preferences to adjust the key layout: 
Open Launchpad interface and enter “System Preferences”. 
Select the “Keyboard” setting. 
In the lower right corner of the “Keyboard” page, click “Modify Keys”. 
Modify the position of Control, Option, Command, etc. as needed.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: The Office Upgrade I Didn’t Know I Needed
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this keyboard for work, and somehow a keyboard has become one of my favorite purchases. I didn’t expect to have strong feelings about a keyboard, yet here we are.The clickity-clack is incredibly satisfying without being obnoxious, the keys are smooth and responsive, and the lighting is gorgeous. It looks amazing lit up, but it’s honestly just as pretty with the lights off. The wired connection is another huge plus for me because I never have to worry about charging batteries or having it die at the worst possible moment.As a bonus, it makes me feel at least 37% more productive and significantly more important every time I type an email. Is that scientifically proven? No. Do I believe it anyway? Absolutely.If you’re looking to upgrade your office setup and want something that looks great, feels great, and turns everyday typing into a tiny source of joy, this keyboard is a 10/10 from me.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Best money I've spent in a long time
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: UPDATE 1/14/2026As of 1/13/ I have now had this keyboard for 1,000 days. I've officially racked up 1,260,071 tracked words. (I'm sure there's a good chance that there's at least half that number in un-trackable words (like these) that I've used this keyboard for too. The most-used keys are smooth, but have no worn out any more than they were when I mentioned the wear on the below update. All the lights still work. The keystrokes are just as smooth and flawless as the first time I used this keyboard. It works easier than my laptop keys. The strokes are longer and take almost zero pressure to move them.I've written at LEAST three novellas and four full novels on this keyboard. And I think the day it dies will be the day that I cry. Hopefully, this keyboard will still be available, so I can purchase it as a replacement if I ever need to!UPDATE 2/1/2025As of 1/31 I have now been able to track 1,003,148 words on this keyboard. I'm sure that I've reached a MUCH higher number with all the non-traceable typing that has been done since last February! I am still thrilled with this keyboard! The lights still work and switch between styles if/when I want it to. The keys that I apparently use the most have a slight shine on them from where my fingers have worn them down a bit, but there's basically zero wear damage as of yet. The only thing that I can actively notice is a slight wear on the silver ring around the E key (maybe an 1/8th inch long if that). The keystrokes are still flawless.A fantastic author companion!UPDATE 2/21/2024:As of 2/20 this year I have now written 502,870 tracked words with this keyboard. I say tracked because I have typed many emails/facebook messages/discord messages ect. that I haven't tracked over the last 297 days that I have owned this keyboard. In those 297 days, I've cranked out 11 manuscripts finished manuscripts on this keyboard. (with many still in progress). It still works as well as the day that I first used it. There have been some days that I have written out almost 13,000 words in 24 hours, and have had NO issues with the performance or how my hands feel after it (my brain on the other hand...pure mush). The lights still work like it did when it was brand new. I'm honestly shocked that the letters have not worn out yet. I HAVE started to create a shine on the keys that I use the most. 10/10 would reccomend this keyboard still. BEST money I've spent in my writing career so far. Get this keyboard, you won't regret it.I've had this keyboard for 42 days now. I'm a novelist that regularly writes over 50,000 words a month (sometimes more than 10,000 in a day). As of yesterday (day 41) I have written over 1004,000 words on it. Just on manuscripts alone. There's no telling how high the actual word count is total because I don't track emails or facebook posts or reviews (like this one!!) just the manuscript words.I bought this because I had started to get "laptop hands" because I was writing so much and the squished together keys were straining my tendons.This keyboard has been my saving grace. I love the lights, the key action is smooth and makes my little writer's heart happy. The clacking noises sound just like an old typewriter, and I've found that it actually keeps the juices flowing for my imagination, since I write mostly in the Prohibition Era. The lights are entertaining and are just as bright on day 42 as they were on day 1.I also have long (natural) nails, so laptop keyboards always made my fingers hit weird as I was typing. This keyboard doesn't have that problem. The key stroke is so light it takes barely any pressure to make a key move. I'm pretty sure that my typing speed has increased because of this keyboard.Worth. Every. Cent.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: To be clear, I'm not big on what qualifies as a top of the line gaming keyboard. To my knowledge, all the top of the line gaming keyboards are going to cost over $100 dollars for a keyboard alone. They usually have a wrist-rest and interchangeable keys. I'm coming from a keyboard that had for years been falling apart and a mouse that was for a turn of the century Mac so literally buying anything would be a step up, lol.To start, the keyboard feels good. There's still some clicking and clacking to be had, but compared to my previous keyboard (An outdated logitech trash fire that was missing screws with a number of numeric keys no longer operational) The keyboard also has a good weight to it and doesn't slide all over the desk. Without the arm rest below the keyboard, it's actually great for me and the limited desk space I have.Something I didn't expect was the RGB settings. It has a lot. 6-7 colors with various modes, like breathings, rainbow-cycling - All which can have the speed of which they display changed by holding ESC+FN keys.The mouse was more simple. Standard Right/Left Click, Scroll Wheel, 2 right side thumb clicks with a DPI button below the scroll wheel to cycle thru colors or DPI Key+ Side Key on the mouse adjust single color modes that only seem to do breathing color (Fading in and out) I was able to match my keyboard and mouse to a pretty Cyan/Purple Neon to match the RGB lights in my tower and they look really cool together.Both Keyboard and Mouse use their dedicated USB cords which for the most part are decent lengths and not totally intrusive (I have minimal desk space for all my music/art crap, mind you) One cable has a somewhat fat USB connector for some reason, making a tight fit for any other USB next to it which seems a bit pointless.All and all it still gets an all star review from me. I tested gaming with Doom Eternal and the key inputs fell into place, with the mouse feeling like a good fit with the extra side keys being used for up close Melee.If you're like me and your keyboard mouse set up was a dumpster fire, this is a great upgrade. I don't usually write reviews but I'm happy with my purchase. Someday maybe I'll step up tot he world of customizable gaming keyboards but I'm in no rush with this set up. :)

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: will be returning soon, don't recommend
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: TLDR: cute for WFH office job. don't get if you're planning on gaming and messaging the bois on discord or in twitch chat at any point. seriously, sticky keys without spilling anything and without spamming shift is a huge no-no.pros: RGB (currently set to static but don't see an option to have the colours shift in any way), small keyboard, good clackety soundthing to mention: it's a very light keyboard (nothing wrong with it, i'm just used to ones i use at home having some heft to help deal better with my typing and gaming), only the QWERTY section is coloured, the F# keys are all just white, and the box this thing came in has a picture of a square key keyboard and not the typrewriter style it is?cons: you will need a wrist rest for this keyboard (even with the legs out it's still almost flat to the desk), no buttons or switches to change the RGB lighting so if you want it to pulse or wave then you might be SOL (this also might be user error), they only send you two extra switches to switch out but after that you're SOLthis is the reason i'm returning: sticky keys. FRESH OUT THE BOX, and mind you the box was undamaged, the keys were sticking together. a key would get stuck pressed down JUST ENOUGH it wouldn't register when i hit it (so it would've been lght and not light, for example). the worst happened while i was playing a game with friends: the W key got stuck so the keyboard was only registering i was pressing W and not anything else. try to strafe? NOPE. try to type literally anything else? NOPE. the only thing that fixed it was unplugging and plugging it back in, but it's still having a hard time with some of the other keys. i've tried various resets but to no avail. so i'll be returning this and getting the RGB typewriter keyboard i had so long ago instead.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: The keyboard is entirely made of plastic.I pressed Esc three or four times, and the next day the key stopped responding.I fully disassembled the keyboard to replace the switches and the frame—its structure is just cheap plastic.No way to add insulation.The PCB is also cheap, with solder joints barely holding the components together.The switches are low quality; they need to be lubricated or they'll wear out prematurely.The entire keyboard feels cheap and isn’t worth the price.Its real value is $20 USD, max.I don’t understand why this keyboard has so many stars—it doesn’t deserve them.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I don't normally give reviews, but this product was honestly worth my time in the case it may help someone else...I am currently starting my new career as a legal transcriptionist and typing thousand of pages a month on my laptop keyboard was not not ergonomic and slowing me down.  I researched all of Logitech's keyboard options\ and decided on this one.  It was important to me that function keys could be used as primaries (without having to press the function key) as I use them hundreds of times a day in my transcript creation and this keyboard has the feature of setting functions keys as primary shortcuts or primary function keys.  It's super easy to toggle back and forth between features with just two key presses.  I put a sticky note on the back of the keyboard with the shortcut, so I won't forget it in the future. Also, my USB dongle was floating around in the box, instead of placed inside the secure compartment in the back of the keyboard.  I only got lucky and saw it on the floor one day, otherwise it would have been lost so beware when you unbox.  On to my review...The Pros: soft, rounded corner keys that feel like pressing clouds and relatively quiet.  Is it the quietest keyboard on the market? Probably not.  But it's not clunky-sounding and doesn't wake my family when I'm working well into the midnight hours.  Connectivity was super easy and had no hang ups.  Connects via USB or Bluetooth, which is great because with all my transcription gear, I have no USB space left on my current computer.  I've had no issues with lag or it keeping up with key presses and I type fast!  There is an LED indicator light on the CAPS LOCK key. All of the shortcut keys are extremely useful, especially the screenshot, as well as the media keys at the top, and there is a dedicated lock key if you work in an office setting where you need to lock your computer if you step away.  Even though this keyboard isn't advertised as portable in size, it isn't so large or heavy that it wouldn't fit in a larger size bag to carry with you somewhere or from room to room.  I keep mine in a basket beneath my desk when not in use and I love that feature.  It's also got a built-in plastic wrist rest that I cannot live without, although some may find that a con as you can not use your own padded or softer version.  There are two incline levels, as well as flat, and all three options use premium rubber feet so you've got good traction and shouldn't scar or scratch any surface you place it on.Cons: This keyboard is not backlit. I am worried the white color will likely stain over time and lose it's aesthetics. USB dongle was not packed inside the secure battery storage compartment.  No instruction manual - an illustration of the shortcuts and their meanings would have been super useful as well as the primary function key feature switch shortcut.  Had it not been for other reviews, I would not have known about this feature and I had look it up on my own from the Logitech website.  I cannot get the media controls to control my media when I'm using mini-player mode (ExpressScribe). I'm hoping with some research this may be remedied.Would be better if: It was backlit.  Include some instructions-short, sweet and simple would do the trick.  Maybe have a manual switch for the primary function key feature.  For me personally,  the keys could have a little more spacing between them, but this of course would sacrifice space and portability.What I can't speak on... I haven't typed for hours on this yet, so I can't speak to it's durability or battery life.  I also have not tried using this with more than one device, so I cannot speak to that either.For my career needs, I can't see finding a better keyboard in this price range and I will likely order a second one in the near future to have as a backup.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Small, quiet, & light weight, but could be good or bad depending on the person....
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: CON's:> Wrist support not as large, or as soft, as the K350 Wave wrist support> I almost threw out the USB receiver because it was not in the battery compartment where there's a holder for it.  Instead it was in a cutout in the cardboard inside the box....> Doesn't have the tactile feel of my K350> Included batteries are at 65% despite having the paper separator in place upon delivery.> Does not work with the older Logitech "Unifying" keyboard receiver.PRO's> Quiet keyboard - which is also why it doesn't have that tactile feel of the K350> Lots of user programmable keys.> Doesn't take up as much space as the wave keyboard - but mostly because of the smaller wrist pad....Only thing I actually docked the keyboard for is the wrist pad.  It is only marginally softer than the rest of the plastic in the keyboard.  Plus, in natural typing position, the heel of my palms are right on the edge of the keyboard/wrist pad which is only about 2 inches wide.  My hands are only slightly larger than average, so I imagine that a LOT of people are going to have this problem as well.  The K350 wrist pad is perfect, but I decided to change keyboards due to my old mouse dying, and the new "Logi Bolt" system from the new mouse is not compatible with the old Logitech Unifying Hardware receiver used with the K350 keyboard.  I prefer to only have 1 controller in use, saving my USB ports for various other hardware, so I got this keyboard.I may end up sending this back and getting the new version of the Logitech Wave keyboard instead, it looks like it has a better wrist pad with it even if it's a larger keyboard overall.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Terrible keystroke feel and bad ergonomicsTerrible keystroke feel and bad ergonomics
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have been using this keyboard for about 4 months now and I absolutely hate it.  The keyboard Bluetooth connection works well and easily connects to my Dell Pro14 PC14255 but this is the only positive that I have experienced with this product.I grew up leaning to type from a young age and have worked in an office environment for over a decade.  I have always been proficient at typing.  I type on many different devices and am used to adapting to different keyboard sizes and feels.  The feel and ergonomics of this keyboard are awful.  I have been using this keyboard for months and I am still struggling to get used to it.  The keys are more shallow than a traditional keyboard but yet somehow you have to press them harder to get them to register…I frequently have to press a key more than once to get it to register the stroke.  This makes for frequent typing errors and has impacted my productivity.  The keyboard has an overall cheap and unrefined feel, especially in the feedback of the keys through the fingers.  The key stokes somehow feel both nebulous  (too soft) and yet clunky and difficult to press at the same time…I don’t how they managed to combine two awful, yet opposite traits.  I use both small, laptop keyboards, iPad keyboards(touch screen), and full size keyboards and even though this is nearly a full size keyboard, I find it more difficult to use than smaller, cheaper keyboards.  If you’re used to a traditional, desktop, office style keyboard, I would highly recommend you avoid this product.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: This wireless Logitech keyboard replaced an earlier somewhat similar wired/battery powered Logitech keyboard that developed an issue in the battery compartment. This led to a constantly flashing red light on the keyboard. Nothing I tried would resolve the problem, so along with experiencing a few keys having become less responsive and precise over the years, I decided to replace it with this one. I am not at all disappointed I did.This keyboard is lighter than my earlier Logitech model but it is in no way flimsy or "cheap" feeling. Once connected to my desktop computer through the Bluetooth connection, a fast and simple process, the keyboard functioned flawlessly. The keys fall readily to hand and were I a better typist, it would no doubt be even more pleasurable to use. As it is, with my tried and true hunt and peck method, it works as well as can be expected.This is a quality accessory from a trusted maker of superior computer accessories. I am very pleased with my purchase.
The only minus is it has single device pairing only. It needs to pair and re-pair if we want to use it for another device. But the rest is good.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Simple et efficace ! Magnifique clavier!Simple et efficace ! Magnifique clavier!
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Ce clavier Logitech sans fil a remplacé un précédent clavier Logitech filaire/alimenté par batterie quelque peu similaire qui a développé un problème dans le compartiment de la batterie. Cela a donné lieu à un voyant rouge clignotant constamment sur le clavier. Rien de ce que j'ai essayé ne résoudrait le problème, alors en plus de constater que quelques clés sont devenues moins réactives et précises au fil des ans, j'ai décidé de les remplacer par celle-ci. Je ne suis pas du tout déçu de l'avoir fait.Ce clavier est plus léger que mon ancien modèle Logitech, mais il n'est en aucun cas fragilisée ou « bon marché ». Une fois connecté à mon ordinateur de bureau par le biais de la connexion Bluetooth, un processus simple et rapide, le clavier fonctionnait parfaitement. Les touches tombent facilement à portée de main et si je devais mieux dactylographier, ce serait sans doute encore plus agréable à utiliser. En l'état actuel des choses, avec ma méthode de chasse et de peck éprouvée, cela fonctionne aussi bien que prévu.Il s'agit d'un accessoire de qualité provenant d'un fabricant de confiance d'accessoires informatiques de qualité supérieure. Je suis très satisfait de mon achat!
