Optimized switches effectively reduce cavity echo, delivering a smooth and consistent keystroke every time.

98 Keys Compact Layout Computer Keyboard: Full-Size Functionality in 30% Less Desk Space.The K99 green keyboard packs a full set of arrow keys, a dedicated numpad, and essential function keys into a space-saving 98-key layout — all while taking up 30% less desktop space than traditional full-size keyboards. Perfect for small desks, cramped dorm rooms, or anyone who wants a clean, clutter-free workspace.K99 ergonomic green keyboard features a foldable 2-stage kickstand with silicone non-slip mat,so there are 3 stage height levels in total,allows you to choose the tilt angle that best suits you for a better keying posture.

2000Mah Membrane Keyboard: Days of Mixed Use on a Single Charge.Built-in 2000mAh rechargeable battery keeps you productive and entertained for extendedperiods. With RGB backlighting turned off, enjoy days of uninterrupted work, study, and gaming before reaching for the USB-C charging cable. Full recharge takes approximately 7-8 hours. (All keyboard need to use the original charging cable which included in the package,please don't use other cables or charging it by the chargers!Only charging through the computer's own charging port can better protect the lifespan of the keyboard!)

Triple-Mode Connectivity: Seamlessly Switch Between BT 5.0, 2.4GHz & USB-C.K99 wireless keyboard works with Bluetooth 5.0,2.4GHz wireless and USB-C wired connection,giving you the freedom to switch between up to 5 devices (PC,Mac,iPad,phone,laptop) with a single FN key combo.Whether you're gaming on your desktop,typing on your tablet,or answering emails on your phone, one keyboard does it all.K99 Green Keyboard compatible with Win and Mac system etc,you need point ''FN''+''S'' for windows system,or point ''FN''+''A'' for mac system to paire system then you can use keyboard.Please refer to the image and description for specific instructions on how to switch the keyboard connection method.

Silent Keyboard Creamy Color: With silicone structure, this K99 membrane keyboard can offers more quiet typing experience than mechanical keyboard,perfect for study in shared dorm or professional work in open-concept office.quiet-Silicone dampening structure absorbs keystroke noise, delivering a quiet typing experience that won't disturb roommates.No matter the outlook,the construction or the function,K99 is definitely a best quite keyboard for working and amateur games gaming.But different nail length can produce a little different typing sounds,long nails typing will cause a little creamy feeling and short nails typing will be more quiet feeling.

Product description
K99 Membrane Keyboard Wireless Computer Gaming Keyboards Creamy Cute Tri-Mode 
98-Key Green Keyboard Multifunctional RGB Backlit 2000mAh Rechargeable Keyboards 
Three Mode Connection, More Convenience, Switching Mode Method 
Leobog x Aula K99 pc gaming keyboards rgb backlit wireless bluetooth keyboard provides 3 connection methods,including BT5.0, 2.4GHz wireless mode and Type-c wired mode. It can be connected to up to five devices at the same time and no limits connection to meet the needs of working, gaming and study. 
Wireless Creamy Keyboard with Number Pad Bluetooth / Wired Fit for Mult-Systems 
This bluetooth wired creamy keyboard with number pad have many connection methods.Custom rgb backlight shines brightly with dozens of pre-set dynamic effects, adjustable in color and style via shortcut. Comes with a Type-c keyboard charging cable, fast transmission speed, and durability. 
Compact Backlit Keyboard for Office/Amateur Games– A Great Holiday Gift Idea 
1.Full-size functionality in 30% less desk space 
2.Silicone-dampened keys for peaceful work & play 
3.Ergonomic design,the two-step kickstand allows user can have 3 heights in total to adjust keyboards' height to the desired angle 
4.Weight:1048g(2.31lb) 
Quiet or Creamy Tap & Smooth Typing Experience 
How to deal with the connection problem 
Note: To protect this green keyboard and extend its battery life, please use only the provided charging cable. Do not use other phone charging cables. If you have any questions, please let us know first.Suitable using for shared dorm/open office/home office/gaming/study/christmas gift. 
Rechargebale, Multi-Mode, Ergonomic Keyboard 
Charging time:7~8 hours 
Connection:Type-C Wired & 2.4G Wireless & BT 5.0 
Rated current:<200mAH 
Rechargebale battary 2000mAH 
Note: Different nail lengths will produce different typing sounds on this green keyboard. Long nails will create a slightly creamy sound, while short ones will be quieter). 
Is the LEOBOG K99 compatible with Mac? 
Yes! This K99 supports both Windows and macOS systems via its tri-mode connection(Bluetooth 5.0, 2.4GHz, and USB-C wired). Simply use the FN+key combo to switch between Win and Mac key layouts. No additional software or driver installation needed. 
Is this keyboard quiet? 
Yes, the K99 features a silicone dampening structure that significantly reduces typing noise —it's noticeably quieter than typical mechanical keyboards. Ideal for shared dorms, open-plan offices, and late-night use without disturbing others. 
How long does the battery last? 
The built-in 2000mAh rechargeable battery provides extended usage.With backlit off,you can use it for days.Full charge takes approximately 7-8 hours via the included USB-C cable.Please use the provided charging cable for optimal battery health. 
Is this a mechanical keyboard? 
No!The K99 uses a premium membrane switch system designed at more lower price and much quieter operation.It offers the satisfying silent tactile experience than a mechanical keyboard also fit for amateur gamers.think of it as the best of both worlds.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: STOP SCROLLING. The Search for the Perfect Pink Keyboard is OVER. 🎀✨
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Let’s get one thing straight: I have never been more wrong in my life. 💁🏼‍♀️✨hair flipI am obsessed with pink, but as a girlie with long nails, I was trapped in a toxic relationship with flat, Mac-style keyboards. My nails were sliding everywhere, it was a mess. I’ve been eyeing this keyboard for about three weeks, terrified that the higher keys would be even more of a struggle. Instead? I’m typing faster than I ever have. It’s not just a keyboard; it’s an experience.THE QUALITY & PRICE POINT:Can we talk about the price point?! Because I’m still trying to process it. We are seeing a level of quality here that you usually have to pay triple for. The build is solid, the weight is perfect, and it feels like a premium piece of tech, not a budget find. The value is actually insane. 💸📈THE SOUND (THE 'THOCK'):If you’re looking for that satisfying, creamy typing noise, this is it. It’s not loud or clackety; it has this perfect, muted, expensive 'thock' sound. It’s quiet enough for a professional setting but satisfying enough to keep me in my happy space all day. 🎧☁️THE AESTHETIC:The pink design is stunning, and the lights are the perfect mood-setter. I was typing away today feeling like an absolute boss that I am.VERDICT: 10/10. If you have long nails and a pink obsession, stop waiting. You cannot beat this quality, this sound, or this price. Amazon, this is the one. 🎀🔥

features: PRO with Screen, Upgrade on Display: Featuring a sophisticated smart screen, the TH108 PRO gaming keyboard puts vital information and personalised flair right at your fingertips. With this powerful display, instantly verify the time, monitor keyboard power, or toggle RGB backlight with the volume knob doubles as screen control (FN+Knob to switch), without losing focus. Easily upload your own GIFs or pictures with the Chrome-based software on Mac or Windows computers; to flaunt the team you battle for or show off a perfectly timed meme that puts a smile on your face. With the custom screen, express your unique style that moves beyond static backlight.

100% Sized, 100% Spectacular Performance: Level up your setup with the TH108 PRO full-sized gaming keyboard, engineered for intense gaming sessions and demanding office tasks. Built to last, this full-sized keyboard features 104 double-shot PBT keycaps with unfading colors that withstand the test of time, and a thick body in ABS plastic that weighs over 1.1kg for un-moving stable typing. The premium build quality goes beyond the exterior, with the massive 10,000mAh battery and the lab-tested gaming chips, the TH108 PRO gaming keyboard promises 2ms super low latency in cable mode and 1k polling in convenient 2.4Ghz wireless mode, for swift and stable execution of complex in-game maneuvers.

Long-Lasting Wireless Keyboard: Power passes the competition and ditches the charging cable with the outstanding 10000mAh battery of the TH108 PRO keyboard. Unlocking the realm of unfettered movement and sustained performance with this tri-mode wireless keyboard, without frustrating cable drag hindering swift mouse movements, for seamless transition between up to 5 paired devices under cable, 2.4Ghz and BT modes. PC, Mac laptop, or Android tablet, whichever devices you game on, the 200-hour wire-free battery life makes inconvenient mid-game recharge a worry in the past.

Hot-Swappable Custom Keyboard: Personalise functions, sounds and feel of each keystroke as you please, with the powerful set-up of the TH108 PRO custom keyboard. Experiment the various acoustic feedback and feel of mainstream 5-pin mechanical switches with this hot-swappable keyboard; and bask in the thocky melody of Creamy Jade or the tranquil silence of Sea Salt Silent switches of ours, both factory-lubed for out-of-box perfection. Try out the intuitive web-based driver to remap, record macros, toggle backlight and sensitivity of TH108 RRO keyboard across Mac and WIN devices, for the ultimate PC peripheral that matches your gaming style and workflow.

Acoustic Bliss with 5-Layer Padded Gasket-Mount: Crafted with a 5-layer enhancement set and a complex internal design, the TH108 PRO Gasket keyboard promises blissful switch ASMR with a soft, flexible feel. The market-tested sound-improvement formula of sandwich foam, IXPE switch pad, Sound-Enhancement PET, EPDM switch socket foam, and bottom silicone gifted TH108 the satisfying creamy sound by riding resonance and delivering exceptional comfort by cushioning shocks after each bottom-out. Treat your ears and fingers to an unparalleled level of tactile and auditory joy, as TH108 PRO accompanies your gaming victories and professional endeavors.

RGB Backlight Keyboard with Modern Style: Dive into a symphony of light and step up your gaming ambience with the TH108 PRO backlight keyboard, featuring adjustable RGB illumination. Seamlessly locate macro bindings or dedicated keys in dimly lit gaming dens, with a dynamic effect that lights up as movement goes, minimising mis clicks with intuitive visual signs; personalise your battle station to reflect your individual style and mood, with the color, effect, brightness and speed adjustable backlight of TH108 PRO keyboard, creating a visually stunning centerpiece that complements your high-performance rig.

Sound-Dampened & Precision-Lubricated Acoustics 
Pre-Lubed Linear Switch 

Experience the TH108 PRO’s soft, flexible typing and creamy-quiet acoustics, engineered through its integrated gasket structure. Enjoy a flawlessly smooth feel thanks to pre-lubed plate stabilizers and precision-tuned linear switches. 
Creamy Jade Switch: 5-pin Mechanical Linear Switch.
Trigger Force: 45±5gf (50±5gf)
Trigger & Total Travel: 2.0±0.4mm (3.6±0.4mm)
The video showcases the product in use.The video guides you through product setup.The video compares multiple products.The video shows the product being unpacked.
TH108 PRO Teclado inalámbrico para juegos
Tri-Mode Connectivity 
Long-Lasting Wireless Performance 

Packed with three modes of connection and an easily accessible mode switch besides the USB port, the TH108 PRO keyboard offers reliable 2.4GHz wireless, low-latency cable mode, and versatile Bluetooth connectivity. 
Pair to New Device: 1) Toggle to BT/2.4G Mode. 2) Pressing FN+Q/W/E/R until Q/W/E/R keys flash quickly from slow to rapid. 3) Set Bluetooth on PC or Plug 2.4Ghz Dongle to PC
Connect to Paired Devices: 1) Toggle to BT/2.4G Mode. 2) Press on FN+Q/W/E/R once
Dynamic RGB & Single Color 
Immersive Gaming Atmosphere 

The TH108 PRO mechanical keyboard's RGB backlighting transforms the keys into a mesmerizing river of light, where colors cascade and dance seamlessly across the surface. Choose from dynamic effects like breathing, cycling, and chasing to infuse your typing experience with vibrant energy and motion. 
FN+Insert: Change Light Effect; Fn + Delete: Change Light Colors; FN+↑↓←→:Adjust Brightness/Speed
FN+Home: Change Side Light Bar Effect; FN+End: Change Logo Effect Colors

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Feature Rich Prebuilt with Good Sound and Typing FeelFeature Rich Prebuilt with Good Sound and Typing Feel
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Epomaker TH108 Pro is a feature-packed full-size mechanical keyboard that offers a 108-key layout, tri-mode connectivity (wired, Bluetooth, and 2.4 GHz), hot-swap PCB, gasket mounting, a volume knob, and a small LCD display all for just $90–$100.Build quality feels solid for the price. The plastic case doesn’t feel cheap, the board has a solid sense of weight and heft for a prebuilt, there’s minimal flex while typing, and fit and finish are clean with no obvious defects. The aluminum volume knob adds a more premium touch, though its side-facing position isn’t ideal for quick adjustments, at least for me, and the tiny smart LCD feels more like a novelty than a useful tool.My unit came with Creamy Jade switches, which are smooth and comfortable for both typing and gaming. They have a unique, marbly sonic character, and the board doesn't sound hollow at all. The stabilizers are plate-mounted and well-lubed out of the box, and the included Cherry-profile PBT keycaps feel nice to type on, with only slightly fuzzy legends typical of boards at this price.Typing feel is firm but a bit softer and less fatiguing than some other budget boards I’ve used. Connectivity has been rock solid in wired use, though I haven’t spent much time with wireless modes. LED backlighting is bright and consistent across the board.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Title: Great Full-Size Keyboard with Excellent Switches, Minor Connection Issue
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've been wanting to switch back to a full-size keyboard for a while, and this one has been a great choice overall. I missed having a numpad, and it's nice having all the extra keys again without sacrificing the feel of a good mechanical keyboard.The switches sound and feel really good right out of the box. They have a satisfying, thocky sound and are smooth to type on, whether I'm gaming or just using it for work. The build quality also feels solid, and the keyboard has a nice premium feel to it.One feature I really like is that the customization software is browser-based. I didn't have to download any extra software just to remap keys or change settings, which made the setup process much easier. The built-in screen is also a fun addition, and being able to upload your own GIFs gives the keyboard a little extra personality.My only real complaint is a connectivity issue I run into whenever I boot up my PC while using it in USB mode. The keyboard is usually unresponsive until I flip the connection switch to another mode and then back to USB. After that it works perfectly, but it's something I have to do almost every time I turn my computer on. I'm hoping this is something that can be fixed with a firmware update.Other than that issue, I've really enjoyed using this keyboard. If you're looking for a full-size mechanical keyboard with great sounding switches, useful customization, and a fun display, this is a solid option.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: One of the nicest keebs in our collectionOne of the nicest keebs in our collection
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I picked this up for my husband and it’s basically taken over his desk. He’s been using it for a few months now, not just for gaming but also for work, so it’s had a proper run. First thing he kept mentioning was how it feels to type on. The keys are really responsive and smooth, with just enough give from the gasket mount to provide the perfect balance of flex and cushioning that it doesn’t feel stiff even after a long stretch.The sound is a big part of it too. Those pre-lubed creamy jade switches have that deeper, thocky tone we are both drawn to, and it actually does sound delightful and rounded in person, not just in videos. We did swap the keycaps out for a HyperX set, purely for aesthetic preferences, and it changed the sound slightly but in a good way. He hasn’t felt the need to touch the switches at all, which says a lot since he usually tinkers with everything.The custom side is pretty straightforward. Being hot-swappable makes it easy if you do want to change things later, and the little screen is more fun than I expected. You can upload whatever you want through the web tool to download to your keyboard in a few clicks. The knob on the side is also surprisingly useful for scrolling through settings and adjusting things quickly with a couple of clicks and rotations.The RGB lighting has been great and a lot of fun to play with. Once you start adjusting it, you realise how much control you’ve got. You can tweak the brightness, colours, and the way the lighting moves or reacts, so it’s easy to get something that suits your setup instead of just leaving it on a default rainbow wave. He’s messed around with a few different effects depending on mood, from something subtle for work to more animated patterns when he’s gaming.It’s got a nice weight to it too, which I like. Its solid build means it stays put and feels robust without being bulky. Battery life with the 10,000mAh battery has been impressive too. He only plugs it in occasionally to top it up and it just keeps going in the background without becoming a thing you have to think about.If I had to nitpick, the web software is decent but not the most polished interface I’ve used, and it took a little poking around at first to figure out where everything was, but it was useable.I’ve ended up using it a few times myself and now I’m seriously considering getting one. Bit dangerous, honestly.

features: 【Wave Ergonomic Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo】The wireless keyboard features a wave key and wrist rest design that naturally fits your fingers and relieves wrist strain. The adjustable stand allows you to set the keyboard to the most comfortable height, making it ideal for long-term use. Note: The USB receiver is located on the back of the mouse.

【Wireless Optical Mouse】The wireless mouse is designed with comfort in mind, featuring a contoured shape that fits snugly in the palm and complements the natural curve of your right hand. All controls are easily within reach. This mouse is equipped with forward and back functions, allowing you to navigate the web faster and more efficiently than ever before.

【Plug-and-Play 2.4G Wireless Connection】One 2.4 GHz USB receiver can connect both the keyboard and mouse, or they can be used separately. Plug and play—no software download is required. The 2.4 GHz wireless connection offers a strong and reliable signal up to 33 feet (10 meters), without delays.

【Automatic Power Saving Function】The ULSOU wireless keyboard and mouse combo features an automatic power-saving function. After 30 seconds of inactivity on the keyboard and 15 minutes of inactivity on the mouse, both devices enter sleep mode to conserve battery life. This greatly extends battery life, and any button press will activate the devices again. The keyboard requires 1 AA battery, and the mouse requires 1 AA battery. (batteries not included).

【Wide Compatibility and Dual System Layout】This wireless keyboard and mouse combo is compatible with Windows XP/Vista/7/8/10/11, Mac, and other operating systems. It’s suitable for desktops, Chromebooks, PCs, laptops, and more. You can switch between Windows and macOS by pressing FN+Q or FN+W.

【After-sales Service】We promise that all customers who purchase ULSOU wireless keyboards and mice will receive worry-free after-sales warranty service. Even if the return period on Amazon has passed, simply contact us, and we will provide a satisfactory solution as soon as possible.

features: 【75% Space‑saving Layout】The KN85 series is a compact 85‑key keyboard (13.68" × 5.51" × 1.77") that keeps all the essentials (F1–F12, arrows, shortcuts) without the number pad. It frees up 25% of desk space for better mouse movement. Designed for small desks, laptop setups, gamers and minimalists. For frequent number‑pad input, choose our full‑size KN104 with a complete dedicated numpad, or opt for our new KN98 model — compact 99‑key that retains the numpad while saving desktop real‑estate

【Tri-mode Connectivity with All-Day Battery】Connect via USB‑C, 2.4GHz wireless, or Bluetooth 5.0 (3 channels supported), with ultra‑low latency (USB 2ms, 2.4G 5ms, BT 11ms). Switch seamlessly between Windows and Mac to work across your PC, laptop, tablet, smartphone, or gaming console. Perfect for programmer, student, creator, or hybrid worker. The built‑in 4000mAh rechargeable battery ensures stable wireless performance. Continue typing while charging via wired mode when power runs low

【RGB Backlighting & Programmable】Choose from 20 preset dynamic lighting effects with adjustable color and brightness, easily controlled via software or shortcut keys. The RGB backlight glows around the PBT keycaps and edges to create the glowing effect. With the KN85 driver (Windows only, wired/2.4G mode), all keys support programming- remap keys and edit macros to boost work efficiency and gaming competitiveness

【Hot-Swappable for Easy Customization】Pre-lubed Bsun linear switches (45-50gf actuation) deliver buttery-smooth typing and gaming performance. Compatible with 3/5 pin switches, easily swap tactile or clicky switches without any soldering. From beginner to heavy typist and writer, you can fine-tune your feel or explore new switch styles effortlessly

【Gasket-mounted with Creamy Sound】Born to redefine your typing experience, every Kisnt mechanical keyboard is enhanced with base dampener, silicone pad, 5 layers of sound-dampening foam, producing a deeper, more satisfying marbly "thock" that keyboard enthusiasts love, just indulge in pure typing bliss with less distraction. If you're looking to upgrade from traditional clacky keyboards to a creamy one with every keystroke feel consistent, the KN85 is the top budget choice

【2-year Warranty& Support】We treat people the way we'd want to be treated. You will enjoy 24/7 specialist support and 30-day free returns in Kisnt. We stand by our products. Whether it's damaged packaging, a quality defect, or a used item, contact us via Amazon. We're here to make it right

【Important Before You Buy】1. Charge: Fully charge before first use. A full charge ≈7–8h (may vary). Use a 5V 1A charger or a computer USB port. Fast chargers may damage the keyboard. 2. Choose static over animated effects – animated RGB drains more battery. Press Fn+↓to dim/off, power off completely during long breaks. 3. Bluetooth Pairing: Toggle to [BT], hold FN+W (or E/R) for 3–5s until key flashes rapidly, then pair with [KN85 BT-1/2/3]. Bluetooth requires Windows 8 or later & Bluetooth 4.0–5.3. 4. Sound& Height: Not silent but creamier, less clacky than traditional mechs. Front height 0.79". Wrist rest recommended

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Best board for the price, BY FAR !!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Great board especially at this price point. This really raises the bar for entry level products and makes it much more accessible. This thing will impress most seasoned enthusiast. I could see this thing attaining a similar status to the Aula F75.You get really good acoustics, great switches (lubed BSUN Purples), gasket mounting AND hotswap.I've been typing on it for a few days and the sound tests you see online are very accurate, board sounds very creamy and poppy, which makes for a very satisfying typing experience.The RGB on this board is really bright and has some cool preset animations.Definitely NOT office friendly, I took this thing to the office one day and had to swap it for a normal keyboard because it is quite loud. I enjoy the sound but I don't think my coworkers did. lolUnfortunately I did notice that the space bar seems to make a really loud thunk which doesn't match the sound of the rest of the board, but you can fix this pretty easily with a rubber O-Ring or some foam inside the space bar.And sadly I did not get any spare keycaps with my order, as I've seen other buyers receive in their reviews :(Overall though, really good board and significantly raises the bar for entry level products. This thing will outperform boards that cost twice the price. I am very happy with my purchase and will be buying one for my gf too
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 25, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'm shocked at the quality of this keyboard for the price. The main case is plastic but a is very good quality plastic. Obviously, it's not going to be aluminum at this price. The quality of the keycaps is also excellent. They are the more premium PBT plastic rather than the cheaper ABS plastic and they feel great. It even has more features than my other higher end mechanical keyboard as this one not only has wired USB (obviously), but also 2.4 Ghz dongle (which secures nicely in a little cutout of the bottom of the keyboard and held in magnetically), and a whooping 3 Bluetooth channels so you can pair this keyboard with many different devices at the same time.I love the layout as well. It's a little smaller than a TKL layout keyboard, but without any compromises. Typically, I don't like 75% or less because you lose too many useful keys or they have them in a weird place, but this keyboard's layout is perfectly done. You still have all of your Home, End, PgUp, PgDn, Insert, Delete, and Print Screen and Pause/Break keys. The only key missing is the Scroll Lock key which is never used anyway so this is perfect.It has nice RGB that lights up under and around the keys. Also comes with some extra switches and even a decent keycap and switch puller tool.  Even comes a thin, cheap, plastic dust cover which I appreciate.My only complaint whatsoever about this keyboard is that I'm not too crazy about the switches, but that's really a personal preference thing. They're certainly not terrible and I can definitely see other people with different preferences liking these, as actually a lot of other reviewers did really like the switches. But I'll probably be swapping them out, which is another great thing about this keyboard is that they are hot swappable.For those wondering about the sound - the stock keyboard is clacky rather than thocky.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on January 24, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Chances are, you've found this keyboard after reading a number of Reddit threads or watching a review or 2 on Youtube, and I can confirm they're all very correct to recommend this keyboard.It's kind of obvious that it's not trying to be high-end, as evidenced by the all plastic build, basic and other creature-comforts that are left out, like volume knobs and little near-useless LED screens, but it is still a solid, well built keyboard with a decent-enough feature set.But, it's a keyboard, so if we're being real, its the tactile feel of typing on this thing along with it's really nice, satisfying "creamy" sound (at least that's what I've heard it called, though I still don't quite get why) that makes you want mechanical keyboard like this and this one does the thing real well while also looking pretty dang nice at the same time (I got the gray gradient version with side-printed keycaps. The battery life using the included USB 2.4G wireless dongle is exceptionally good and it also has RGB backlighting with 20 preprogrammed lighting modes, if you're into that thing, but I've got it set to a static color and it looks good enough for me.All of that at this price point makes this a really, really, really good option and one that I can absolutely recommend.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: The best value for a budget keyboard, hands down.The best value for a budget keyboard, hands down.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This keyboard has been an absolute dream, and the price cannot be beat. It uses bsun switches (I'm honestly not sure which, I've done some digging but can't find them), of which I got the linear version. These switches are nice, there is no noticeable scratch, a crisp bottom out, and the stabilizers are actually silent with no rattle or ticking. There is a variety of foam included, but they leave a bit of room in the case which keeps the board from sounding muted. There are NO SCREWS, so modding this thing is a breeze (might need a small flathead tho) and you have a lot of options straight out of the box. It also comes with a hotswap board, so you can lube the switches (already lubed, but do what you want) or change them out entirely. There are also FLIPPY FEET (2 STAGE!!) so you can adjust your typing angle. I have heard people complain about the software that comes with the board, but it turns out it is fully compatible with the Signal RGB app. Now I can assign any pattern I want, even outside of the presets! The lighting is very prominent since the LEDs are south-facing. 3 of the lights do not work in the software, but they are on the edge of the board with the modifier keys so they are not noticeable.My ONLY gripe is that the keycaps are not very durable. I have been using mine for a few months now and the tops of the WASD keys are starting to become shiny and smoother. These are likely not PBT, but they are a very thick ABS so the sound stays deeper and fuller. However, a PBT set from a name brand manufacturer costs more than this entire keyboard, so this is an incredibly minor complaint.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Comfortable, creamy sound, easy set up.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Set up was a breeze, simply plug in. It charges in a few hours.This keyboard is really nice. I like the “creamy” sound other viewers have described. A VERY light touch is all you need to type. I won’t say it’s sensitive, it just requires a light touch of each key. That is something I need to get used to.I have a laptop set up on a riser, and needed a keyboard that will fit in the small space beneath it. This was my choice after reviewing MANY keyboards. I also wanted a laptop with raised keys, a mechanical keyboard. I like the “old school” feel of it.Weight: it’s heavy. I won’t be traveling with it, so that doesn’t matter to me. But I love the heaviness of it. Feels secure in its spot.Ergonomics: there are two levels if you want to change the angle. Three is you count not using the little feet at the back. I also have a padded hand/wrist rest for extra comfort (NOT INCLUDED) but the keyboard itself is comfortable to use.Color: I would have preferred black to match my desk accessories and laptop, or blue my favorite color. I went for the least expensive option as the color doesn’t change the effectiveness of the device.Lights: it’s advertised as a gaming keyboard. I’m not a gamer, nor will I ever be. You CAN turn off the lights. Simply read the paperwork that comes in the package to know how.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I kept seeing this keyboard everywhere — the one that kept getting away. I wasn’t sure about the build quality at first. Months ago, I saw a great review from Hipoyotec, but still didn’t pull the trigger. Eventually my keyboard addiction got the best of me, and I’m glad it did.This thing is thocky, creamy, sturdy, and feels like real quality when you’re using it. I love it. 100% worth the price. The layout on the right side is perfect, it works great with Linux, and it just looks slick.I do wish they included a bit more in the box — maybe extra caps or switches — but that’s just the spoiled keyboard addict in me talking. I’ve lost count of how many keyboards I own at this point. I’ll try anything: cheap, midrange, “premium.” I rarely spend over $150, and honestly, I usually stay under $90. I love finding hidden gems like this one.Half the fun of this hobby is taking something mediocre and making it great. A while back I bought a $7 keyboard off Amazon, swapped the switches, lubed it, threw on new caps, and took it traveling — it ended up becoming one of my favorites. Aluminum boards are gorgeous, sure, but they can be overrated. Leobog makes some fantastic ones too. I’ve got boxes of switches and caps I haven’t even opened yet. I’ve stopped counting. Probably over fifty by now. And don’t even get me started on HE switches — that’s another rabbit hole entirely.Anyway, back on track: this Kisnt keyboard is easily in my top ten, maybe even top five. Every Wednesday I rotate keyboards — swap, tune, re-evaluate — but this one doesn’t need a thing. It sounds and feels perfect right out of the box.Thanks, Kisnt. You nailed it.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on October 9, 2025

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Buen sonido y calidad por el precio, pero software y patas mejorables
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: El teclado superó mis expectativas en lo esencial: sonido “thock” muy placentero, pulsaciones firmes y tres modos de conexión que funcionan sin problema. La construcción se siente sólida; el plástico es grueso y limpio al tacto, de mejor calidad que en otros modelos de su rango.Puntos a favor:Excelente sensación y respuesta lineal.Sonido grave-cremoso desde fábrica, sin necesidad de mods.Muy buen valor por el precio: se acerca a prestaciones “custom” de gamas más altas.Puntos a mejorar:El software de administración fue inútil en dos PC. La página es confusa, y aunque el teclado fue reconocido, no ofrecía opciones reales de configuración.La parte trasera utiliza un plástico más sencillo, y las gomas antideslizantes están pegadas con cinta doble faz que comenzó a despegarse desde el primer día. Me preocupa que se pierdan o necesiten ser reemplazadas pronto.No incluye numpad: ideal para gaming y escritura, pero puede ser limitante para quienes usan mucho la entrada numérica.Conclusión:Una excelente puerta de entrada al mundo “custom” por su sonido, tacto y conectividad, siempre que no dependas del software ni necesites un teclado completo.Nota aparte (no influye en la calificación del producto): el rastreo tardó cuatro días en actualizarse; el paquete llegó sin daños, pero el proceso logístico, la comunicación y el profesionalismo por parte del vendedor pueden mejorar.
Excellent Product

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: BEST KEYBOARD I HAVE EVER USED. WORTH EVERY PENNY.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Honestly, I am absolutely blown away with the quality of this kisnt KN85, it's hands down the best keyboard I have ever owned. First of all, the sound quality of the key click is insane, this thing is so thocky with the bsun switches, PBT double shot key caps, gasket mounts and multiple layers of dampening foam/silicone, genuinely such a pleasure to type with. It is even hot-swappable if you want to change or upgrade your switches. The battery life is amazing, first use never charged out of the box lasted over a full week of heavy daily use.I find it very hard to find any fault with this keyboard whatsoever. One note is that the LED's are south-facing, so shine-through backlit keycaps won't work, I like double-shot caps for the thock, so this doesn't bother me one bit. But seriously, I have never been so happy to be typing at my desk. It has changed my whole experience. I watch reviews of £200-£500 keyboards, and I still think this is better.All I will say is get it fast, as prices are constantly rising due to demand.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: looks and feels amazing, setup was easy and battery is lasting along time which is great.  but the sound of the keyboard is so creamy, it really does sound like a premium keyboard. I also love the beige color scheme its very clean yet retro and the letters are bolded and of course its not a lousy 60% so you can enjoy all the key functions without having to press FN all the time

Awesome keyboard that punches above its weight. Stock switches are louder than I'd like, but hey it's a custom keyboard, so just swap them out easily for anything you like. For the price it's great keyboard. ONLY major issue is I like separate numpad controllers (I put these on the right of my mouse so it's quicker) but Kisnt only make these seperate numpads for the two other colour schemes that exist. The beige and green scheme is missing.

features: Smart LCD Screen & Multi-function Knob: Stylish AULA S98 Pro wireless mechanical keyboard with smart LCD screen and multi-function knob will lead the new trend. The screen homepage displays various information such as date, time, battery level, system, connection mode and status indicator. By rotating or pressing the multi-function knob, you can adjust the system, connection mode, volume, RGB light mode, language and screen image/GIF(Note: You need to download the software under windows system and keep in wired mode to set the screen image/GIF, calibrate the date and time)

Tri-mode Mechanical Keyboard & Multi-Device Connection: The AULA S98 Pro mechanical gaming keyboard supports BT5.0, 2.4GHz wireless and USB-C wired connectivity to provide reliable and lag-free performance. It can save up to five devices and can be easily switched using the knob. The S98PRO wireless gaming keyboard is compatible with Windows, Mac, IOS and Android operating systems, which is suitable for PCs, laptops, tablets, smartphones, PS, XBOX and other devices to meet the needs of all users

Hot-swappable Custom Keyboard: The S98 Pro mechanical keyboard wireless comes with a hot-swappable base that is compatible with 3-pin or 5-pin switches. Without the soldering process, users can easily replace switches and keycaps to customize their keying experience (keycap/switch puller is included in the package). Equipped with pre-lubricated stabilizers and switches, the creamy keyboard bring smooth typing feeling and pleasant creamy mechanical sound, providing fast response for exciting games(NOTE: Turn off the power to the keyboard when replacing the switch.)

Mechanical Keyboard with Advanced Structure: The S98 Pro thocky heavy computer keyboard features an advanced construction, extended integrated silicone pads, and PCB single key slotting to optimize elasticity and stability for a softer, more resilient typing experience. Five layers of sound deadening material fills the gap between the PCB, the positioning plate and the shaft, effectively counteracting the cavity noise sound of the shaft hitting the positioning plate, provide a stable and comfortable typing sound and solid feel

RGB Backlight & Programmable Software: The rgb keyboard comes with 19 rgb lighting effects, over 16.8 million rgb colors and front side light, adding a stronger gaming atmosphere. Download the S98 Pro driver via bit.ly/m/AULA, the mechanical gaming keyboard is fully programmable, with key mapping, macro definitions, sleep time, on-screen Gif images, and RGB lighting effects(including the cool music rhythm backlight) to suit any work and gaming. (Note:The driver is officially released by AULA and will not cause any adverse effects on your computer, which only supports windows system in wired mode.)

PBT Keycaps & Large Capacity Battery: These side-engraved PBT keycaps take double injection molding and heat sublimation process, which are more durable without fading, sweat-proof, and softer to the touch. With the south-facing LEDs, the pc keyboard backlight clearly illuminates each key through the font, allowing you to operate accurately in the dark. Built-in 5000mAh high-capacity battery, the creamy keyboard with number pad is suitable for long-time work or high-intensity gaming, keeping you away from the anxiety of running out of battery

How to download the software? Is it compatible with Mac? 
1.Download the software via bit.ly/m/AULA 
2.This S98Pro mechanical keyboard is compatible with Windows, Mac, IOS and Android systems, but the software only supports Windows system and wired mode. 
How to calibrate the date/time on the screen? 
1.Download and install the S98pro driver in wired mode with windows system. 
2.Find the "TFT screen" and click to "Time Syns" button on the driver. 
Note: The LCD screen has a transparent protective film that can be peeled off before use. 
How to use custom GIF images? 
Upload an image or gif in wired mode via the S98pro software on your Windows computer. 
How to adjust the backlit or turn off the light? And how to quickly solve keyboard unresponsive or other unknown issues？ 
1.You can do adjust the backlit with the knob or the driver. 
2.Reset the S98pro wireless mechanical keyboard by holding down FN+ESC for a few seconds until the keyboard light flashes 
Is there anything to note when charging the S98 PRO keyboard? 
1. Please use only the USB interface of the computer to charge the keyboard; 
2. Do not use the mobile phone fast charging charger/over-voltage/over-current power adapter to charge the keyboard.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My musts were simple: has to have a wired connection, has to be "backlit" in some way, and has to be sturdy enough to last through another 2 years of college.Well... I LOVE this keyboard. Totally worth the price. I'm building a pink PC setup for both college + gaming and fell down a rabbit hole of mechanical keyboards and all the customization. The sound is great, not too loud but not too soft, has a great creamy feel and is smooth all around. The keycaps are thick and large and pleasant to type on. Keyboard itself has sturdy weight, doesn't bend or flex. The customization is great - i love that you can have static colors (including static rgb) or different movements, and the light bar on the front is customizable via the keyboard too (just read the manual for how to change that). The knob just makes EVERYTHING easier, and even though I custom mapped some of the F keys for volume control, I much prefer using the knob!No lag whatsoever... In fact, it feels quicker than my Dell Inspiron laptop keyboard somehow. Right now it's connected to my laptop until I hook it up to my monitor, but there were 0 issues in setup. I didn't pick it specifically because of the ability to add gifs on the screen, but omg I didn't know how much i'd love it until now haha!! It adds another layer of personalization that makes it really feel like yours. Oh, and the feet on the bottom have both "short" and "tall" options, which I enjoy. Also came with 2 extra switches and a cap+switch puller. Basically, I see this keyboard lasting for a long time with care and maintenance. I'm very happy with the prospect of being able to replace just one component if it breaks instead of the whole product. f you're on the fence, do it! You won't regret it!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on March 12, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The AULA S98 Pro is a rare beast in the mechanical keyboard world; it’s a factory-built board that sounds and feels like a $300 custom commission. The defining feature here is the gasket-mount architecture paired with a five-layer sound-dampening system. This combination produces a deep, "creamy" acoustic profile that completely eliminates the hollow ping common in other boards. Whether you’re grinding through a late-night study session or hitting a marathon gaming block, the pre-lubed linear switches provide a buttery-smooth travel that’s light on the fingers but heavy on the satisfaction.---Technical Breakdown---Build Quality & Sound:Integrated silicone pads and PCB single-key slotting optimize the flex and stability of every keystroke.The 5000mAh battery is a absolute powerhouse, lasting weeks on a single charge even with the RGB and screen active.PBT keycaps feature side-printed legends, which look incredibly sleek and prevent the characters from ever wearing off.Innovation & Control:The 1.2-inch TFT LCD screen is the star of the show—you can upload custom GIFs or use it to monitor battery life and connection modes in real-time.A dedicated precision metal knob allows for instant, tactile control over volume and lighting without needing to alt-tab out of your work.Tri-mode connectivity (Bluetooth 5.0, 2.4GHz, and USB-C) ensures you can toggle between your PC, laptop, and tablet with a single switch.Aesthetic & Color Options:The S98 Pro isn't just a performance tool; it’s a centerpiece. AULA has released several distinct colorways to match any build vibe:Gradient Black (Side-Printed): The ultimate stealth look. The keys transition from dark to light grey with legends on the front of the caps for a clean, minimalist top-down view.Side-Printed Pink: Perfect for a "sakura" or "kawaii" setup, usually paired with the ultra-smooth Flower linear switches.White & Blue: A crisp, nautical aesthetic that looks incredibly sharp with the RGB set to a cool ice-blue or white.Purple & Blue (Violet): A vibrant, synth-wave inspired palette that pops under desk mats and accent lighting.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This keyboard is much higher quality than I expected. It feels nice and heavy, and not cheap at all. The keys sound really nice if that's important to you. I thought I would hate this since I have to look to type but it hasn't been a hindrance at all, especially with the LED lights on. The gradient of pink is really pretty, better than the photo.There are a lot of LED background options. The little screen and knob are nice, although I'm not sure that the knob serves much purpose other than controlling volume. Also, the knob has a little give which may not be good for longevity. The little screen can display time/date, select a custom setting, or you can download the driver and upload a cute gif.I was able to plug and play instantly by inserting the wireless USB connector, however, to get the time and date correct I had to plug the keyboard in with the cord. I don't ever use items wirelessly so I will probably leave mine like that. So, I am not sure if the battery life is good or not.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Sound is perfection! LCD screen customization is so fun!!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got the pink keyboard this afternoon and I gotta say, so far, it is a dream!! It sounds so creamy, the keys feel so fluid and have a great response time. So far all I've done is type on it, I have yet to game with it but I will be surprised if it has any issues.I have so far gotten the bluetoth to connect, as well as the cable, it may be me or perhaps something else but I cannot get my computer to register the USB, which is why I give 4 stars. So it could be user error. But with bluetooth I can still enjoy the wireless benefits. I will say you will need to download the drivers from the official AULA website: I just googled AULA S98 pro drivers and used some discernment to find the right one. Having the drivers will allow you to customize the small screen and you can simply save gifs to your pc and upload them through the app. I did enjoy how the keyboard came with a small plastic cover to go over it (its a simple thin covering, but it's better than nothing) I also like how sturdy this thing feels, it's got weight and it feels strong. I have yet to judge the battery, but it seems ok for now. So I will say for a (roughly) $80 keyboard it's pretty great! I'm looking forward to playing around with this baby and enjoying the clickity-clack of the keys.

Overall, it delivers excellent performance, comfort, and durability at a great price. Whether you're gaming, typing, or doing schoolwork, the TMKB 60% Mechanical Gaming Keyboard is a fantastic choice that offers outstanding value.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I am going to teach you how to keep it silent
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Alright here’s the deal. I used this keyboard and mouse combo for like six years before it finally gave up the ghost because my cat ran in front of me and I tripped and stepped on it. it didn’t even break tbh, it just broke one of the tiny springs in the space bar so the space bar couldn’t be made silent anymore.Two of those years it was crammed in a closet. When I dug it out it worked perfectly. The point is, in general, this thing is durable.I’ll get the bad out of the way first. These dongle based keyboards suck at wireless interference and they always have. Honestly I have no idea if this is a logitech mk295 thing or a dongle in general thing but it always freezes up whenever, for example, someone else’s airpods (not yours, someone else’s, don’t ask me why it’s witchcraft) are being used while you’re typing. You can mostly solve this with a $5 USB extension cord that brings the dongle close to the mouse and keyboard. I’d knock a star off for that but six years for $30 is such an insane value even considering that one issue that I can’t.Here’s what’s going to happen. you are going to buy this keyboard. If you type several hours a day, it will stop being zero decibel quiet in 6 weeks. In 2 years, it will clatter a little. You will be angry about this, as if it’s an insurmountable problem. It’s not.Basically, this keyboard is comprised of silicone “switches” that house the keys, and then keys that perfectly fit over them. but that’s not why it’s silent. You cannot make a piece of plastic that slides over another piece of plastic forever without either making noise or breaking the laws of physics. The reason it’s silent is because they grease the keys.This is important.It’s also good news. If the keys themselves had shoddy plastic printing, they would squeak and rattle no matter what. But they’re great! All you need to maintain it is one incredibly specific product, and you have to get the expensive version of it:It’s called Krytox 205g0.This is how they get them to be silent. It costs like $30 for a very small tube. Luckily, you don’t need a lot, but trust me, you are going to be tempted to get the $10 knockoff “keyboard lubricant” instead. “what’s the difference, right?”no. It is not the same thing. Krytox 205g0, exactly. This will make your keys silent again, and nothing else will. If you buy the $10 stuff, you will be mad. If you buy this $30something keyboard and a $30 grease tube, you will have silent keys forever.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Is the best backIs the best back
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: When I test a product and review it I don’t usually use superlative words and I will only rate something five stars if it truly deserves it, and not every product does. This one does. I’ll try to explain briefly. I am a prolific writer and I have actually worn more keyboards out than some small stores sell in a year. Not that I am rough on them, they just don’t last long, and this brand has been my nemesis for as many years as I can remember. While I think they often make the best of class, sometimes, they also sometimes make things I believe are calculated to not last long. But that aside, my other goal this round in addition to durability is I need my keyboard and mouse to be silent, not quiet but silent. Almost none are and currently it’s even trendy to own keyboards with varying degrees of clicky sounds. Not me.IS THIS SILENTMy gold standard for keyboards in Logitech’s own K740, which practically every source has called the best keyboard ever made. Unfortunately due to an incredible lack of understanding, they discontinued it with no suitable replacement. Their current high-end offerings are wrong in every way but they don’t think that way which means I have zero interest in them. I like the K740 so much that I bought a second one as soon as I heard they were discontinuing them and I still have it sealed away unopened. Read back a couple of lines and you know what happened to my beloved keyboard, it reached that predicable end of life when the enter key broke and then the letter vee stopped working properly. Both can be fixed with time and patience, which I don’t have so I started shopping and it came down to this model that they call silent and the model K650 which is also claimed to be silent and in fact I couldn’t see way it was going for twice as much, and this one even included a basic but decent mouse, which I thought I would just keep in the box. I had low expectations but I ordered this anyway. From the moment my fingers touched the keys it was love, it is actually very slightly quieter than the K740 (which makes it almost impossible to hear) and the keys are as high quality, solid and non-rattling, perfectly shaped, ideal key travel, in short it’s like this is the long awaited replacement for the best keyboard on the planet. So keep it a secret between you and me, this is its twin brother with a couple of exceptions, which I’ll list below.IS ANYTHING PERFECTI am going to be nitpicking to try to come up with any flaws and there aren’t really any.  They are just things to know about, for example this model isn’t illuminated. I used to like that feature but now I’m not sure I miss it. The other has to do with the shift lock light which is in an inconvenient location and hard to see with the glossy clear cover over it. I miss having the on-screen reminder.  As far as the mouse, it’s actually better than I though and I put my MX series away for now. If I would improve anything I would say it’s a little small for my hand and a trifle light so when I touch it I’m always wanting to lift it up. Oh and one more thing. Why did they feel it was necessary to print the annoying ad message printed on the space bar with the words silent touch? It’s distracting and completely destroys the professional restrained look of the rest of the unit. Someone is just not thinking at Logi.YES NO MAYBEWhen I couldn’t find what I wanted I thought I would look for a K740, of course they’ve been long gone for years. There are a lot of people offering them used at as much as $500 bucks and I even saw one for a thousand. No thanks, I know it’s hard to believe but this one is just as good. End of story.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good value and function for my needsGood value and function for my needs
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: One of very last Logitech wireless keyboards that you can find in full-standard layout. Otherwise (with the new branding) “Logi” almost exclusively went to multi-device “flow” keyboards. What’s wrong with that? ; it tries to please every platform and you end up both with confusing labels on accustomed keys (like Start – Alt – Ctrl etc) and you have missing/sacrified keys (like print screen, scroll lock, pause/break) or usual functions are hidden under some combination keys – totally in different places. I’m a Windows PC user and has absolutely no multi/flow need with my keyboard.I’m coming from wonderful K800 wireless illuminated keyboard. It served me for about 10 years – quite respected life. But of course, Logitech killed its manufacturing – while there is still a loyal demand for it. I get the urge for coming up with multi-platform niche devices. But I don’t get why you have to kill your best seller and not offer both of them. Alas, corporations like hurting themselves sometimes, for absolute no reason.Illuminated wireless function was my first priority on new keyboard search. That brought me to new MX Keys S series and I was about to hit order button (although quite steep price). Then after reading many reviews my attention came to those non-standard/missing key issues (for Windows users) and some connection issues as well. So I had to drop that model and focused on unknown Chinese illuminated KBs (which there are quite a few). But reviews revealed; high failure rate, connection/battery issues etc.Then I dropped illumination function and focused on standard PC layout with “quiet” feature. This MK295 came up. Extremely reasonable priced KB, very good tactile feel (to my taste) and almost completely quiet typing. It even has those 8 media control/quick function keys on top that I always use. Its full standard PC layout – yet quite compact size. No palm-rest (which I didn’t need anyway) to keep it compact. Yet bundled mouse (M220) has very small toy-like size and rattling top plate. So I’ll never be using that mouse, as I already have two quiet Logitech mice (M330 and M350 “pebble”) and a trackball+mouse M570; all on “unifying” platform.Now we come to connection subject (USB dongle and its utility software), which is quite a mess in Logitech realm. All previous logitech KB and mice simply worked on one single USB dongle type; Unifying. But today all new logitech products are shifting to Bolt USB dongle (which is a modified version of bluetooth). And in between; there is 2.4 GHz USB dongle (which this MK209 uses). None of these 3 dongles work with products from other camp. This is the hardware side.Then we have utility software side; that small SW you load to pair & manage your devices. There is old unifying SW, current Options+ SW and in between Options SW. Options+ SW sees (and only sees) all 3 dongle types. It lists all my my existing paired mice and K800 KB under unifying dongle. But I can only manage the mice and NOT my K800 keyboard! Yet, it doesn’t even show my new K295 keyboard at all! When I do “add” under 2.4 GHz dongle; it says that the SW is not compatible with this new K295 KB. But keyboard itself works at all times – since its factory paired. I found logitech support pages for both Options+ and Options SW – which lists all “compatibe” products. And this K295 keyboard is not even listed under any software! I still uninstalled Options+ and installed Options SW; such a nightmare, as it constantly push you to “login to Logi Web Connect” (otherwise basically it doesn’t let you do anything). But it also does NOT see this new K295 KB! So yes; Logitech is essentially selling this K295 keyboard that NONE of its 3 connection software works with! Isn’t that wonderful? The bottom line is; its factory paired to that 2.4 GHz USB dongle and if your dongle dies; so does your keyboard! Good job Logi!Bottom line; I decided to keep this MK295 combo (and only use K295 keyboard). That means I’ll be having two USB dongles on my PC; old unifying dongle for rest of my existing mice and 2.4 GHz dongle only for MK295. So far I’m OK with that, as I couldn’t find any other keyboard (which satisfies my full PC layout and silent typing demand, as I had to drop illumination feature). Price is quite low on this “transitionary” combo, that I’ll probably buy one more as backup.Why backup? The standard answer is; as with all cheap keyboards, this is a membrane type keyboard (as opposed to individual mechanical switches). That design is inherently prone to early oxidation. But this KB even has an extra “feature” (whether intentional or not, I’m not sure). Check out my pics (against lighted background) to see “air-holes” between front or back. No, they are not intended for cooling down this high-performance keyboard (sarcasm intended). They might speed up that oxidation process, after all. Otherwise why do you put holes both on top and bottom?There is an earlier version of this KB (K270) which has unifying dongle, spill-proof feature and is even cheaper than this. So it should probably last longer than this K295. But it doesn’t have quiet typing feature.Unfortunately, there is no other trusted OEM (amongst HP, Lenovo etc) when it comes to wireless keyboards with full standard layout. Logitech is the only brand that mastered enough key mechanics, tactile feel, reliable wireless connection etc. I wish Apple made PC keyboards for even better quality and functionality! Till then; find your Logitech that is best suited for your current needs.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Truly Silent Performance – The Perfect Choice for a Shared Office Space
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: When you spend a lot of time typing reports or managing digital infrastructure, the constant "clack" of a standard keyboard can become a major distraction, both for you and anyone else in the room. I picked up the Logitech MK295 combo to use with my primary workstation, and the "SilentTouch" technology is significantly more effective than I anticipated.Quiet Without Sacrificing Tactile FeelThe headline feature here is the noise—or lack thereof. It reduces typing and clicking sounds by a huge margin compared to a traditional membrane setup. What’s impressive is that the keys don't feel "mushy." There is still a satisfying tactile response and enough travel to maintain your typing speed, but the acoustic output is muffled to a dull thud. This is a game-changer if you’re frequently on calls or working in a quiet office environment.Reliable Wireless ConnectivitySetup was as simple as plugging in the tiny USB receiver. I haven’t experienced any lag or dropped connections, even with multiple other wireless devices and a server rack nearby. The range is solid, allowing me to move the keyboard around my desk without any stuttering.Functional Design and Battery LifeFull-Size Layout: Having the dedicated numpad is essential for data entry and technical work. The addition of the shortcut keys at the top for volume and media control is a nice convenience for a daily driver.The Mouse: The included mouse is compact and shares the same silent-click technology. It tracks accurately on various surfaces, including my standard desk mat, without needing a dedicated mousepad.Spill Resistance: The keyboard is designed to handle minor spills, which provides some extra peace of mind when there’s a coffee on the desk during a long shift.Final ThoughtsLogitech is known for their battery efficiency, and this set is no different—I expect to get months, if not years, out of a single set of batteries. If you want a clean, wireless, and nearly silent input setup that just works out of the box, the MK295 is a fantastic value. It’s a professional-looking kit that prioritizes comfort and a quiet workspace.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Quiet Typing Doesn't Last Long, But is a Decent Keyboard
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this keyboard for work and school use. I was looking for one that was (1) still full sized, as I really can't type on the compact or mini sized keyboards that are popular nowadays; (2) quiet, as I'm regularly on calls and need something that isn't going to distract people with loud typing; and (3) affordable. After having the keyboard for about 8 months now and found the keyboard itself is decent, I'd recommend to those who need an affordable full-sized keyboard that isn't too loud but still gets the job done.I personally have different opinions about the keyboard and mouse -(1) I haven't seen other reviews mention this, but the mouse and keyboard do not work well together. Not sure why as I have the USB receiver plugged directly into my laptop, but I can really only use one or the other - never together at the same time. I ultimately opted to stick with the keyboard, since it seemed to perform to near perfection without the mouse present.(2) I ended up getting new mouse because the the one that came with the keyboard was incredibly glitchy and wouldn't track properly, despite putting in new batteries, turning it on/off, etc. Even though I have small hands, the mouse was actually uncomfortably small. The clicks were strangely and noticeably louder than the keyboard (enough for someone on a phone call to notice and make a comment about it). I actually had to get another mouse (Logi Pebble) for this specific reason.(2) The keyboard itself is quiet at first, as it has a bit of a spongey (?) feeling to dull the noise when typing. Since it's used for long periods of time for ~6/7 days of the week, the spongey feeling has since gone away almost completely and the quietness noticeably subsided around 3.5-4 months of use. While I personally would like it to be quieter (since a few people can hear me typing while I'm on the phone), it's not a deal-breaker for me as it's still a bit quieter than other laptops I've used and have grown accustomed to the feedback. There are some who are bothered by the noise, but I suspect it's due to the keys being more mechanical than low-profile.(3) Despite being used very often for long periods of time, they keyboard itself is still going strong. There are some minor things (like my "T" and my "R" keys are slowly fading, the occasional hiccups in typing where a key won't register properly) that happen with the keyboard, but overall still functions great and reliably (without the mouse that it came with).(3) The keyboard is very light, surprisingly so since it looked a bit heftier in the images. For those who travel for work and want a full-sized external keyboard to work on (instead of their laptops), this might be a good option.Overall, I think 4/5 stars is fair enough. While I'm pretty bummed that the quietness of the keyboard didn't last as long as I'd hoped; the affordability, full-sized, and strong continued performance of the keyboard is a huge plus.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great keyboard with a great look & feelGreat keyboard with a great look & feel
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This keyboard is great. I got this for someone else in my home after they tried my K380 (Which is basically the same keyboard minus the aluminum holder at the top and no numpad on the right). They're super happy with it and loves how the keys feel and operate. This isn't a mechanical keyboard but still super nice. One of the best things about the keyboard is the ability to pair it with 3 different devices. To change between devices you just have to push the corresponding button that matches the device you want to use. The keyboard is Bluetooth and also comes with 2.4Ghz Logitech unifying usb receiver. It's powered by two AAA Batteries. To remove the battery cover you slide the door towards the center of the keyboard and not to the edge like you would imagine. The keyboard does have a power switch on the right narrow edge that you can manually power down with but typically you won't need it as they keyboard does go to sleep after not being used. If the keyboard goes to sleep you will want to press the button that corresponds to the numbered item you want to use, you will need to wait a moment until the button stops blinking. To pair the device to something using bluetooth simply press and hold the numbered button until it blinks rapidly then open your bluetooth settings and locate the keyboard in the list of devices. This keyboard is labeled for both a Windows computer and a Mac. I personally use the keyboard with a Mac.Pros:Great keyboardVery well madeComes with Duracell batteriesComes with a unifying receiver for devices that may not have bluetooth or if you don't want to use it that wayKeys feel good when typing and are a good size for small or large handsCan be used with a total of 4 devicesEasily switchable between multiple devices with the push of a buttonSwitch to manually power off, this would be good if you need to take it with you and need to toss it into a bagCons:If you must have a device with its own built in rechargeable battery this one may not be the keyboard for you.No way to remove the aluminum stand if you don't plan to use itHas a bit of extra weight from other keyboards but that's likely due to the aluminum

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: No more "not Logitech" keyboards for me
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've got four different keyboards that have crapped out on me in the last year, several of them quite pricey. I decided to get this oldie-but-goodie keyboard from Logitech because it looked like it might hold my iPad in its case, and I was hoping it would be stable. I sit in a recliner with a lapdesk over the arms to work, and the real estate is limited for stands, keyboard, mouse, remote, coffee cup, etc. Not to mention the fact that things slide off and crash to the floor.This keyboard stays absolutely solidly put on my lapdesk; no sliding around. It's like it's been glued to the board. I have it coupled with another oldie-but-goodie M185 Logitech mouse, and they work well together. The round keys are kind of funky, but I like the touch and the slight rubbery feedback when typing. The switchable keys are clearly marked in white at the top left of the function key row, and the keyboard has the full complement of keys (Mac keys are marked in grey along with the white Windows labeling). Best of all, my Samsung A15 phone in its wallet case sits solidly to the right of my iPad on the back slanted "slot" shelf, with the overhang only covering the logitech logo and not impeding the numeric keypad keys at all. I've got a large monitor on my desk coupled with a Mac Mini that I use for consuming videos from YouTube or TV programs that I can see over the top of my iPad/phone setup, and it's easy to switch the keyboard between all three. So I'm in heaven. Perfect keyboard for me, and I hope they never stop making it.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Some things to really like about this keyboard are:1. The round keys.  I have a high end mechanical keyboard at home and while I really like these mechanical switches, the keys on top are square.  I am finding with the rounded keys on the K780 the whole inadvertently bumping neighboring keys is basically a thing of the past and I have the confidence to type faster than ever before.  Even after a day of using the keyboard it is become very obvious that the rounded indented key design is just a lot better than the square intended keys as I am just no longer clipping the high corner ridges of the neighboring keys and the rounded indent is just naturally easier to properly center your fingers on from any position.  I suppose the one wish here is with the mechanical keys I don't need to bottom out the keys, so I save my fingers from repetitive stress issues.  However these keys need to be pressed all the way down, however the resistance on them is well balanced and at least new I am having no problems with triggering keypress events with relatively light, rapid presses.  One of the things I really like about mechanical keyboards is they always trigger half way down even after millions of key presses and so I am not killing things in my hands.  I suppose only time will tell with this keyboard though as it is not the same tech.2. The ability to switch between devices.  This is just awesome.  For so long it has been a challenge to switch between compute devices while this is just you press a button, it pairs up and just works.  So many of us have more than one device we want to use a keyboard with and often on and in the same room at the same time, but most of us don't have piles and pile of devices to switch between, so this is a good combination of capability.  For example my wife and I have our phones paired to this keyboard and we can and have just handed the keyboard over, pressed one button and then start typing away.  No hassle and no question which phone it is actively talking to.The one complaint I have is the phone / tablet mount does not have an adjustable width.  If I take the case off of my phone it will fit in there, but not with the case on.  I have the case on the phone for a reason and it is a pain to take off, so I really prefer to leave it on.  For some laying down situations, I can prop the phone against my leg and type away.  For other situations I will need a kickstand or something or I am just SOL.  Without the keyboard you are using your hands to both hold the phone and type on the screen and even with a large phone my fat fingers hit a lot of neighboring keys.  However if you are trying to type on this keyboard, well you only have two hands so what is supposed to hold the phone in place while you type?
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on October 8, 2018

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I really like this keyboard. It has some heft to it so it stays in place on my desk. The keys feel good. It's pretty quiet. The size is perfect for me. It easily switches between my desktop pc and macbook with the bluetooth connection. It can handle up to three devices and it's as easy as pressing a button to switch.  It connects right away when I fire up the computer in the morning. And it has a numeric pad which is needed if you type numbers frequently. Some negatives: First the battery cover was difficult to remove and I ended up breaking it. Some gaffers tape fixed that up and it's on the bottom so it's not visible at all. The other thing is there is no numlock key light and no visual indication of the numlock key status. Fortunately once you toggle the numlock on it stays that way, but if you accidentally hit that key, you can't tell it's off until you try to use it. And the power light turns off a few seconds after  you turn it on, so you can't tell by looking if the keyboard is on or off.  The battery life is supposed to be very good so it's understandable why it is built that way. Time will tell.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Já tive vários teclados sem fio, mas este é o primeiro em que busquei eliminar todos os demais (tenho 3 computadores). Poder usar o mesmo teclado para todos os meus computadores facilitou incrivelmente meu trabalho e organizou a minha área de trabalho.A instalação e configuração é facílima e muito rápida e intuitiva.É robusto e pesado. Sólido. Transmite segurança no uso e adere à superfície da mesa.O chaveamento entre computadores é instantâneo e sem complicações (tenho dois PCs e um Mac).Como comprei o importado, ele não vem com os carácteres especiais da língua portuguesa (ç, por exemplo), mas isso é facilmente resolvido uma vez que você se habitue com o mapa do teclado.Bom espaçamento entre teclas, blue tooth rápido e estável.Excelente compra. Se soubesse que era tão bom, teria comprado antes.

I have tried the MX keys mini in the past; however, having this one before, I immediately noticed the difference. The K780 is my most comfortable and favourite keyboard. I love the fact that it is a silent keyboard, so working from home and receiving/responding to calls while taking notes have been a charm. MX keys; however, has these keycaps and switches where the edges move and make more noise than the K780. And the typing experience, in general, is not as pleasant. Having said that, I love how compact the MX keys mini is and it is a much better-looking keyboard than K780 in my opinion.I wish they released a mini version of the K780 or used the exact same switches and keycaps for the MX keys mini. 2 years of battery life is really great, and I personally prefer the AA or AAA batteries than the USB C rechargeable ones, as they have a limited cycle for charge and eventually the charge will not last as long. However, the charge for MX keys is supposed to last for 6 months, so recharging through USB C once every six months should be that bad.The K780 receives 10/10 in my book. But in the future, I would really love it if they made it look a little better. I do not make use of the top portion of the keyboard to connect to iPads or phones, but I do acknowledge the appeal.  This keyboard perfectly matches with my M720 mouse.

I really like this keyboard. The Bluetooth is easy to manage and easy to switch between devices. I tried using it on my phone, which worked, but that is not really what I primarily use it for. I don't really use the little USB plug, Bluetooth totally meets the need.Anyways, uses AA batteries, which are easy to come by; lasts a really long time on those batteries.The keys feel nice - they are fairly quiet which I like. I thought the circle-shaped keys would be weird to type on but I didn't notice a difference at all.It's quite light and easy to transport.Overall, solid. Not especially ergonomic because it's just a flat slab of tech, but it's comfy enough.

aPlusContent.title: Product description
aPlusContent.rawText:
Product description
Make Typing More Comfortable 
The split design helps to position wrists and forearms in a natural, relaxed position. The keyboard has comfortable wrist rest so you can place your wrist on the cushioned palm to rest and enjoy the typing. The keyboard has built-in 4 foldable legs so you can adjust to your favorite typing angle. 
Let there be Light 
Elegant LED backlight with 2 adjustable brightness level, 7 different colors(deep blue, soft blue, bright green, soft green, red, purple, cyan) making typing that much more enjoyable and awesome to look at. 
Easy Setup and Use 
Just simply insert the 1.8M (6 feet) USB wire into your computer like desktop or laptop, then the keyboard can be used instantly. No need driver. The cable length is 1.8meters or 6 feet. It allows you to gain quick access to common functions, such as volume level, playback control, brightness, and more. It also provides number pad with slim and compact design. The keyboard doesn't have separate arrow and Home End keys. Please press the Fn + Home /end keys to get the function if the key can not work. 
Comfortable, quiet typing 
The whisper-quiet, low-profile keys bring a whole new level of comfort to your fingertips. What's more, keep all your most-used functions and media controls closer than ever Windows-dedicated hot keys. The construction of this scissors-kick keys can be used more than 3 million times continuously. 
2 Years Customer Care 
If you have problem using the keyboard, you can contact the support team printed at the back of the keyboard as the product has 2 years customer care.
