productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Precisely What I Was Looking For
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've used this keyboard daily for 3 months now, and it has been a great experience so far.It's my first time purchasing an Arteck keyboard, so I wasn't sure what to expect, but I had heard their brand is reputable for making solid, reliable devices, and thus far I would agree with that.I was looking for a very specific set of features in a keyboard, and this was literally the only one that checked all of the boxes on Amazon at the time of purchasing.Features I was looking for that it had:Ergonomic split key style with a padded wrist rest.Scissor-style key press mechanism (feels like a laptop keyboard when typing)Backlit keys with multiple color choices, including whiteA full sized number pad on the right sideWired, rather than wireless (although in hindsight, either would have been fine.)There are a few things about the keyboard that are relatively minor, not anything that makes it a bad experience, but that if I could have everything perfect in a single keyboard, I would prefer they were slightly different.The half-sized Up/Down arrow buttons, while functional, I would prefer full size ones like the right and left arrows. They feel a bit cramped to use.The delete key being about 3/4 sized is not that strange, but its position above and right-aligned to the backspace key is just awkward for me. I'm used to it being underneath, or off to the right side. Very often I will blind-press either the "FN Lock" (Function Lock) key to the left of it by mistake, thinking it is the Delete key, either that or the Calculator key (which works great in Linux by the way) to the right of it. 3 months in and I'm still not used to its size or placement unfortunately.Similarly, I'd rather the top row of keys on the number pad were positioned elsewhere, (or mainly just the color change button for the backlight not being above the - key) but I do understand that there are limitations to the amount of space they can work with, and appreciate that they managed to pack a bunch of extra feature keys.I'd prefer the print screen feature to have its own dedicated key, rather than being a toggle ON/OFF via the function lock. For example, to switch between the ability to take a screenshot, and the ability to refresh a webpage via the F5 key, you have to press the function lock key in between to toggle the functionality.Most of the functions controlled by FN Lock are used sparingly (volume controls, media playback controls, brightness settings, scroll lock and the insert key) but print screen is one of those that's pretty common for me, and would have been more helpful having its own key instead.Two more minor things related to the lights... if I had it all my way...By the way, at the time of writing, there was a discrepancy in the product description in regards to the backlighting colors so, for those who are wondering, the key colors on the HA315B model are: yellow, purple, cyan, white, red, green, and indigo (blue.)The first one is just a personal preference. I've surprised myself by gravitating to the yellow color lights.I wish the yellow color was more to the orange/red side, like a golden color. Instead it is closer to a yellow-green, which is fine, I would have just preferred something a bit more gold if I could pick. Not a big deal at all. I like that it has a lot of color choices!The other "issue" was just that the green lights in the center of the keyboard that tell you what buttons are ON/OFF for capslock, function lock, numlock, and so on, are SUPER bright. Way too unnecessarily bright. It looks great when you're using the green color on the backlight, since it matches well, but for everything else it's too intense and visually distracting, especially in a darker room.But, I got some old solid black electrical tape I had laying around, and cut little tiny squares of out it, and covered about 75-90% of the visible lights with that, drastically reducing their brightness to a more sane and tolerable level, while also being careful not to completely cover the lights, so I can still tell when they are on or off in general.It's a simple, low-tech fix, and again not a huge deal, but for future keyboard designs I would highly suggest putting a much dimmer and more subtle light in for those.All in all, it may sound like I have a lot of complaints, but honestly none of them are all that big of a deal.Almost every keyboard I've ever used has at least a few aspects that feel are a bit less than ideal compared to what I would prefer, and none of these things are detrimental enough to feel like a disservice to the experience.It's a very enjoyable keyboard to use and I'm quite pleased with it. The pros far outweigh the cons, in other words.I would definitely recommend this keyboard if you are looking for these very specific combination of features, like I was, and I'm pleased with my purchase for sure.If everything continues to go this well throughout the rest of the year, I'd safely be able to recommend Arteck, or at least this specific product, to anyone interested.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: To me, this is a Logitech Wave killer
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Just what I wanted: ergonomic with backlit keys. I love this keyboard.  I've used Logitech Wave and several Microsoft ergonomic  models over the years. But this beats them hands down. The keys feel great with a satisfying sound.  I like the split keyboard design which lets the wrists line up with your arms for comfort. The wrist pad is very comfortable. What makes this a standout though, are the backlit keys. I prefer the wired keyboards. The Logitech Wave is wireless - means battery. It will just fail suddenly when  the battery dies; always at the worst possible times. I like that it has angle adjusters at the top and bottom! I find it more comfortable for the keyboard to tilt down towards the screen. A minor inconvenience are the Page Up and Page Down keys; half size, too small, but not a show stopper. Another plus; the function key don't require a shift key to work as standard F1 - F12. On the Logitech Wave you can't just hit an F key with out the FN shift key. Great price too.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: High quality Windows keyboard that's a perfect fit for my needs
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Have only been using a few days but love this keyboard. Very quiet, responsive keys that provides a high-quality, tactile feel and an accurate rendering (no extra or missed characters). Specifically selected a wired keyboard that is easy to use, just works once plugged in w/o any configuration hassle, and isn't susceptible to unpredictable Bluetooth / wireless connectivity issues or delays.Very natural hand position, with flexible positioning by using front and/or rear stable kickstands under the keyboard to position to your liking. Fingers quickly adjusted to key size and spacing for predictable touch typing. Spacebars for each hand are broad enough that my thumb lands naturally on them without worrying about thumb position or a gap between keys. The result is a keyboard where I can type quickly, accurately, without hesitation.Visually maximizes readability if you're not a fluid touch typist, whether typing in well-lit or low-light conditions. You can easily adjust brightness, and nice set of available colors for preference/variety. This keyboard is built for Windows so if that's all you use like me there's no clutter showing Mac content on keys. Left-hand keys (Tab, Caps, Shift, Ctrl) are slightly larger making them easy to hit, and are labeled rather than icons if you haven't got those memorized. Fn toggle key is included on bottom left row (which surprising wasn't there on some other keyboards I considered) along with a Fn Lock key to the right of the F12 key for camping out in that mode.Bottom line is that there isn't a single thing I have found to complain about yet with this keyboard. Hoping you find this keyboard meets your needs as well as I do!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Nice keys, build quality feels solid, but keys too cramped and some key locations are really bad
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I like the feel of the keys on this keyboard. They're fairly firm, short-throw, somewhat chiclet-style keys. However, the placement of some of the keys makes it difficult to type, causes pain in my hands, causes me to make typing errors.The PgUp and PgDown keys closest to the spacebar are so tiny they look they'd suit a young child. The Home and End buttons on each side of those buttons are also placed in such a way that I have to really stress my hands to reach them, and I frequently make typos because of it. And the Backspace key is so high up and so far to the right that I often miss it, and hit other keys instead.Finally, the location of the Insert button in the numeric keypad areas means I am constantly turning NumLock on, off, on off. I have to constantly keep track of the NumLock state, an added stress.In short, while I like the feel of the keys, the key placement, and in some cases the key size make it both uncomfortable and stressful to type, and cause a lot more errors than with normal keyboards.This keyboard could get 4 or 5 stars if it were redesigned with these changes in mind. If you read the reviews, you'll see others have had a similar experience.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: High quality, comfortable and great design
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: If you are in the market for a well-rounded, budget-friendly ergonomic keyboard that offers a comfortable typing experience, the Arteck Ergonomic Wired Keyboard is a top contender. Here's why:1. Design and Build Quality (5/5)The Arteck keyboard boasts a sleek and modern design that stands out in its price range. The build quality is impressive, featuring a robust structure that doesn’t feel flimsy or cheap. Its ergonomic shape immediately catches the eye, with a slight curvature that ensures your wrists are at a comfortable angle while typing. I’ve found this to be especially helpful during long work sessions.2. Ergonomics and Comfort (5/5)The standout feature of this keyboard is its ergonomic design. It provides excellent wrist support with a gentle slope and a soft, cushioned wrist rest. This helps reduce strain on your hands and wrists, making it ideal for people who type for extended periods. The keys are also well-spaced and have a satisfying tactile feel, making typing a pleasure.The adjustable stand at the back allows you to raise the keyboard to your preferred angle, which further enhances the comfort and reduces the risk of repetitive strain injury. After using it for a week, I noticed less fatigue compared to my previous flat keyboard.3. Typing Experience (4.7/5)Typing on this keyboard is smooth and comfortable. The keys have a nice bounce to them, and the low travel distance means you don't have to press down too hard. This makes typing faster and more accurate. Additionally, the keys are quiet, so it's perfect for shared office spaces or if you prefer a quieter working environment.One minor downside is that it may take a bit of time to adjust to the layout if you're coming from a traditional keyboard. However, once you're used to it, the typing experience is significantly improved. The backlit keys, which are adjustable for brightness, are a nice touch, especially when working in low-light conditions.4. Backlighting (4.5/5)The Arteck keyboard comes with adjustable backlighting that enhances both the aesthetic appeal and the functionality, particularly in dimly lit environments. You can adjust the brightness to your liking, and the illumination is evenly distributed across the keys, ensuring each key is clearly visible.While the back light works well, it offers limited customization colors or fancy lighting modes, which might be a deal-breaker for those looking for something more dynamic. However, for most users who need functional lighting, this is more than enough.5. Connectivity and Setup (5/5)Being a wired keyboard, the Arteck is incredibly simple to set up. It’s plug-and-play—no need to install drivers or software. Just connect it to your PC or laptop, and you’re good to go. The cable is long enough to accommodate various setups, whether you’re using it for a desktop or laptop.6. Durability and Longevity (4.8/5)After weeks of heavy use, the Arteck keyboard shows no signs of wear. The keys feel just as responsive as they did on day one. The materials used in the build are durable, ensuring this keyboard can handle regular usage without losing its quality.7. Value for Money (5/5)At its price point, the Arteck Ergonomic Wired Keyboard offers incredible value for money. It packs features you’d expect from higher-end models—like adjustable backlighting and ergonomic support—into a much more affordable package. Whether you’re working from home, gaming, or just want a more comfortable typing experience, this keyboard is a great investment.Final Verdict:Pros:Excellent ergonomic design with wrist supportQuiet, responsive keysAdjustable backlightingDurable build qualityPlug-and-play setupCons:Limited backlight customizationMay require a short adjustment period for some usersIn conclusion, the Arteck Ergonomic Wired Keyboard is a great product for anyone looking for an affordable yet high-quality typing experience. Its ergonomic design, quiet keys, and backlighting make it ideal for both work and leisure. I highly recommend this to anyone in need of a reliable, comfortable keyboard for everyday use.Would definitely buy again!

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: After years of trying different keyboards this is it: Ergonomic, and illuminated and no blue tooth
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I have nothing against blue tooth, but I don't want any more of it around. It's a nuisance, drops connections, needs charging, etc, etc. In my hunt for a usb wired ergonomic keyboard I've tried (and have) most of them, since I'm an editor/writer, but even though I love the old Microsoft, and I really like my old mechanical ergonmics, I really wanted -- as my eyesight get's worse with age -- illuminated keys. I don't need it for wordsmithing, but for numbers and special characters, especially today with keyboards moving things around when they feel like it (i.e. there's a standard folks! Keep it!) I needed that light, especially at my desk. I don't like to flood my desk with light as I work on keyboard and monitor all day. Finally, after endless hunting, and many keyboards I found one both Ergonomic (and that means full sized keys!, not just wrist supports and angles) and USB with LED-lit keys. I didn't order for awhile, as it was pricey for what I thought was an unknown brand (I don't know it, myself, anyway), but finally, when I didn't find alternates I ordered.No regrets. It may be an unknown sleeper, but it's comfortable, quiet, easy to type on all day, USB plugin (yeah, no more charging!! Is there anything dumber than having to charge a keyboard and mouse? I'm already charging laptop, phone, ereader, tablet and a dozen other things. Why would I want to both with charging keyboards and mice?)Am I lazy? Maybe, but anyway Arteck built the lazy-man's keyboard, ergonimic with lights and no batteries. Amazing how the small things matter. (The leather-ish wrist wrest is nice, too).One small nit is the up/down/left/right arrows are small keys when everyting else is full size.

Very pleased with this keyboard.I've had tennis elbow (apparently now sometimes called "mouse elbow" in some circles) which has been very painful when working with a standard mouse and keyboard.  As my job requires pretty much full time use of both (I'm a programmer), I needed to find something that would reduce the pressure on my elbow/wrist/tendon.I did a bit of research and eventually found and bought this keyboard and a Protoarc upright mouse (which I've also reviewed positively).I was never sure about erganomic keyboards before, but with the pain that I was having, I needed to try something to reduce the pressure on my elbow.This has been pleasantly surprising.It's a well built keyboard with a surprisingly very nice feel to the keys, which are well spaced and have a decent amount of travel. It has a really comfortable (non removable) padded palm/wrist rest and has legs on both the front and the back of the keyboard so you can angle it away from you as well as tilting it toward you, or raise the keyboard slightly, as I do. This makes (for me, anyway) a very comfortable typing position.If you've not used one before, having a split keyboard might be a little different for you for a short while, but I've found that I've lost no accuracy or speed and can touch type as well as I could before.The keyboard has several built in macros on the function keys  for things like media: volume, skip forward/backward, search - accessible using the Fn key. This can be toggled using the function lock key to either have the Fn keys or macros in use full time with the Fn key performing the "opposite" function. There are also several other macro keys - lock session, calculator, plus a couple of keyboard specific keys for the backlight.The backlight is quite good- there are 7 colours (including white) with 3 brightness levels and although I never really used a backlit keyboard prior to this, during the darker months working from home, it does provide a nice even glow across the whole keyboard.Connectivity, really simple - it's plug and play, no drivers required, just plug in the USB and goIn all, I'd recommend this.

features: 1800 QMK Aluminum Keyboard with Enhanced Typing Sound: Drawing from the success of Galaxy80 and Galaxy70, the EPOMAKER Galaxy100 QMK keyboard joins the Galaxy Aluminum Keyboard series with new functionality and upgrades. Featuring a gasket-mounted structure, high-quality lubed linear switches, and 5 soft cushioning layers, the Galaxy100 keyboard provides a uniquely satisfying, creamy typing sound. The addition of Numpad and metal knob, essential for volume control and data entry tasks, offers more programmable keys for custom controls, significantly improving workflow efficiency and enhancing gaming experience

QMK/VIA Keyboard with Multi-Device Compatibility: To elevate your typing experience, the Galaxy100 keyboard is upgraded with QMK/VIA support. The VIA Software offers endless possibilities in remapping keys, editing automating repetitive macros, and customizing layers, making Galaxy100 perfect for those seeking maximum control and personalization. Compatible with WIN, Mac, and Android systems, the Galaxy100 works across multiple devices with ease, ideal for those seeking a versatile office keyboard that also moonlights as gaming controller

Long-Lasting Wireless Performance: Powered by the outstanding 8000mah battery, the Galaxy100 keyboard gives you convenience and productivity. Packed with three modes of connection, the Galaxy100 keyboard offers reliable 2.4Ghz wireless, low-latency cable mode, and versatile BT connectivity. Indulge yourself in continuous gaming sessions with no hassle of cable nor interruptions from charging, and relish in the enduring and stable performance made possible by Galaxy100 keyboard

Pre-Lubed Hot-Swappable Linear Switches: Lubed in factory, the Galaxy100 keyboard houses linear marble switches that sounds as gentle and enjoyable as mellow marbles. With the cushioned Gasket-Structure, the typing sound is dampened to a soft thud perfect for various use scenarios. The Galaxy100 Keyboard also comes with hot-swappable PCB and a 2-in-1 switch puller, for keyboard enthusiasts to test out different switches seamlessly and effortlessly. No more soldering iron, as a switch swap can be as simple as a pull-and-push

Aluminum Gasket Keyboard: Enjoy the sleek, modern look of Galaxy100’s aluminum alloy shell, which brings the keyboards to the next level in more than appearance. Its satisfying and weighty feel aids in typing stability, while the thick aluminum case promises quality and durability. The Gasket-Mount design of Galaxy100 keyboard gives a perfect mix of rigidity and flexibility, helping achieve the soft but stable typing feel loved by many. Full of sound-dampening materials such as Poron, IXPE, EMDP, and PET Sound Enhancement Pad, the shock of each keystroke is cushioned to dampen typing sound, highlight pure Thocky thud of the switch, and reduce hand fatigue for ultimate typing comfort

South-Facing RGB Backlight: Upgrade your desk setup to a professional, high-tech style, with the Backlit Galaxy100 keyboard. Each key on the keyboard is equipped with a south-facing LED, to be brighter from the typist’s angle. The per-key illumination comes with customizable RGB options, for gamers to personalize brightness, colors and light effects for an immersive session. The thick PBT keycaps are not shine-through, with dye-subbed colors and legends that stay clear and vivid after long-term usage

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A Tank of a Keyboard – Exceptional Build, Minor Software Issues
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is my first time buying a mechanical keyboard brand new, not secondhand off Amazon or eBay, and I couldn’t be happier with the choice. I’ve used a few different keyboards before—starting with a wired Logitech, then moving on to a Keychron K1 Slim Profile. That one was fine, but the ultra-thin, chiclet-style keys made it a little tougher to get used to for long typing sessions. There was no real curvature to the keys, so it didn’t do much for muscle memory.I’m not super into the custom keyboard world, and I don’t know a ton about switches or keycap quality, but this thing blows every keyboard I’ve used out of the water.The standout feature? The build quality.The entire body is made of metal—something you almost never see in this price range. Most keyboards around this price point are plastic, plain and simple. The metal frame was 90% of why I bought it, and it did not disappoint. It’s got a solid weight to it and feels incredibly durable. This is the kind of keyboard that stays on your desk for years. I wouldn’t travel with it—way too hefty for that—but as a permanent setup piece, it’s perfect.Typing experience? Smooth and satisfying.The keys sound great—soft, muted clicks with none of the harsh clatter you might associate with mechanical boards. The default keycaps are a neutral tone that goes nicely with my setup (I’m using a white monitor currently), and while they’re not see-through, they still look clean and well-made.A few small drawbacks worth mentioning:• The included software didn’t recognize the keyboard at all on my system. That means I couldn’t customize anything—not even rebind the volume knob (which I believe is supposed to be customizable). This might just be a firmware thing, but it was frustrating.• The LEDs underneath the keys are okay, but the keys themselves are solid (not translucent), so the lighting doesn’t shine through the legends like it does on other boards I’ve used. Not a dealbreaker, but something to be aware of if RGB is important to you.Overall:If you’re looking for a high-quality, metal-frame mechanical keyboard without jumping into the $200+ range, this is absolutely it. It’s easily the best-built keyboard I’ve owned, and despite the software issues, I love typing on it. Would buy again in a heartbeat.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This has everything I'm looking for in a keyboard. It's aluminum (this baby is HEAVY!), has a numpad with a big zero, connects wirelessly, and best of all, it sounds as good as it feels. I have never touched a keyboard like this before, and I tried a lot before landing on this one. The marble white switches feel plush when you press, as if there's a cushion below. Granted, I wasn't used to the light weight at first, but the benefits showed itself after several hours and there was no fatigue. While I wish this came in prettier colors, the knob is a nice enough bonus.Now, why I say be careful: I am currently using a replacement keyboard. I had to send the original one back because the USB connection would randomly disconnect. It's not a problem with the wire, because I did test this with other USB cables, and then again on a different computer, and the problem persisted. Perhaps I just got a faulty keyboard, but it's not really a big deal for me thanks to Amazon's 30-day refund policy.Overall, I would give this 5 stars. This is great for productivity and long typing sessions. It feels premium and way more lux for the price.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This keyboard is really well made!The 96% layout will take some getting used to, but the reduction in size is great if you have limited space but still want/ need a numpad.The switches themselves are linear, smooth, and on the lighter side of activation. That being said, typing on them is easy enough and feels really solid!The sound of this keyboard is a major reason a lot of people get it. And, having used it myself? Yeah, it sounds really really good. It's not silent, but it isn't clicky. The sound comes from both the bottom-out and top-out of the switch, so when typing with any energy, each switch will make TWO sounds. This creates a "rolling marbley raindrops" sound that is very satisfying. If you type softly and carefully, the sound is manageable. However, if you begin to type with fervor, it could be a little loud for certain environments.The keyboard is heavy. Like, really heavy. This is great if you don't want it to move, but this thing is way too heavy to just chuck in a bag and travel around.This keyboard has no adjusting feet. If you want/ need a different typing angle, you WILL need some method of tilting the keyboard.The USB connection is solid. It is not loose or wobbly. This has been a problem for me on other keyboards, so I am happy to report a strong connection.The mode switch (2.4Ghz, Wired, Bluetooth) has a strong snap but is a little "loose." For general use, I don't imagine it being an issue. But if you regularly engage the switch, it does not inspire the greatest confidence.The rotary dial is useful with prominent detents. However, because of the stiff detents and smooth surface, it can be challenging to rotate with a single finger. This is great if you're concerned about accidental engagement, but does require more deliberate manipulation.VIA, the "software" for modifying keybindings and lighting, can be a little finicky. It is largely browser-based (meaning you will need an internet connection). It does not appear to work on Firefox at all. I did manage to get it to work with Opera. They have a .exe version, but I could not get it to work. The software is quite bare-bones, but has a strong amount of third-party user support. I have no interest in rebinding anything, but the ability to adjust the lighting effects within the software is a big plus!The NumLock indicator is simply the LED beneath the NumLock switch itself. This is fine, but "When NumLock is on, the LED is on." I prefer having NumLock on, which means the switch is constantly lit up. Currently there is no option to swap this function or change the color. If you know anything about coding, this is a QMK keyboard (meaning you can flash your own custom firmware). That means this behavior is potentially adjustable, but there is no current method for easily changing this.Overall?This thing is really really well-made. For around $100 USD this might be one of the best keyboards available. It feels rock solid and sounds really nice!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: In love with the smooth clacks and how heavy/sturdy this keyboard is. I purchased one other mechanical keyboard recently. The instructions that came with it were minimal and not very clear. I ended up returning it due to software dysfunction. These instructions are very simple and you can just feel the quality of the keyboard right out from the packaging. It was very easy and quick to connect via Bluetooth with a simple step and there it was popped up on my new devices list. Though the keycaps are solid and the light doesn't shine through them, I think I actually prefer it this way, since I'll mostly be using this for work, I'll rarely have concerns about the lighting. But it does come with some cool features for RGB colors and effects. Not disappointed at all. I am usually on a tight budget when it comes to buying new tech, but I bought this one during the prime day deals and it wasn't that much of a difference compared to the current sale price, but it was worth every penny. The key caps it comes with are very clean and comfortable, though I did get some other key caps simply for personalization purposes. This keyboard is overall great and I will definitely be holding onto it as long as it continues with this great performance and operation.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Love the creaminess of this keyboard. It’s heavy but I’m not traveling with it so it’s fine. My issue is that I’ve been using this Epomaker Galaxy100 for two weeks and today it stopped typing completely on two separate times. It just froze.  One of the times it froze then proceeded to erase everything that I had typed, which thankfully I had just started typing. These were meeting notes not yet saved. My hands were off the keyboard and I looked at the backspace key and it was not stuck or anything. I am using the keyboard wired and I had to disconnect it twice while typing important meeting notes some of which got deleted by the keyboard without me touching the backspace key.  I haven’t had any issues with other keyboards I have used for years in this price range or lower so I’m not sure what’s going on there, especially less than a month into using it. I am not sure if it was not worth the price at this point and may have to return it. I like it otherwise but I need it to work for my work without disruption.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Tank keyboard, light switches, good RGB
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is definitely an early review.  I've had the keyboard for just under a week.  So far it's really nice.  The backlighting under the keys is pretty good and has interesting patterns, etc.  The keys are not transparent, all backlighting is behind the keys.I'm not a huge fan of the white marble switches.  They sound great, but I think I'm going to buy some different ones to try out that are tactile.  These ones feel very sensitive to any slight press.  Thankfully that's an easy thing to replace and I like the keyboard frame/weight.  This is not a criticism of the keyboard, just the switches I picked.  Maybe the other option would have been better but I'm not sure.  They are definitely "thocky" and sound really good.The keyboard is heavy (4lbs).  Which is great for my desk.  If you're looking for an easy keyboard to tote around with you, 4lbs is something to consider.Setting it up with the 2.4ghz dongle was very easy and I can use my work laptop along with my desktop (via USB C). It's easy to switch between devices without any hassle (switch on the back).  I have not yet tried the bluetooth connectivity.  The nice thing is that the USB C cable that comes with it has fabric braded on it and comes with a rubber "dongle holder" for the 2.4ghz dongle.The volume dial works great and I have had no issues with it at all.  Since this is QMC/VIA compatible I guess you can remap the keyboard and create macros for it.  I haven't tried any of that as I don't use macros or have a need to change the keyboard layout at the moment.My biggest complaint about it is that there is only one CTRL key and it's located on the left side of the keyboard.  The way I have my messaging apps set up, I have to press CTRL+Enter to send a message.  Normally I use right CTRL+Enter, but obviously can't as there is only one on the left side of the keyboard.  Muscle memory will fix that eventually.Typing on the keyboard as I've become used to the switches has improved.  I just have to keep my fingers off the keyboard.  My prior keyboard was a cheap dell one and I could slightly rest my fingers on the keys.  This one I have a tendency to press keys I don't want unless I keep my fingers completely off the keys.I don't know anything about how the battery life is since it's constantly connected to a PC and I haven't owned it long enough.Overall it's a tank and hopefully continues working well.  No regrets so far.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Love love this! I typically hate how aggressive mechanical keyboards sound but this one sounds and feels very smooth. Spending most of my day at work typing case notes motivated me to bite the bullet and purchase a keyboard and it was definitely worth it. I leave the light setting on during my 8 hour day and it’s held an amazing battery life. I charge it at the end of the work week just to make sure it’s ready for the next one, but it hasn’t died on me while I’ve been working. The first time I bought it (via open box), I ordered it in white but it accidentally shipped in black. I noticed the keyboard was not only different in color but also the feel of the keyboard itself. On the black keyboard, my fingers accidentally grazed keys while typing, the keys felt more “bubbled”, and stuck out more. When the correct keyboard in white came, it felt more “squared” and felt much easier to type quickly and more accurately. The Bluetooth/wireless connection wasn’t the best since I felt that I had to reconnect (forget the device and add) every time my computer locked but once I switched to the wireless USB setting, it was no longer a problem. The keyboard itself is sturdy and a bit heavy, but I liked that since it’s not going to move from my desk.  Again, I bought this more for my 9-5 job but my husband who is a PC gamer was quite impressed with my find :)

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The EPOMAKER Galaxy100 offers excellent value considering the premium aluminum build and overall feature set. The gasket mounted design combined with multiple sound dampening layers delivers a smooth, soft, and satisfying typing experience with a pleasant thocky sound. The included pre lubed linear switches feel consistent and comfortable right out of the box, making this keyboard especially enjoyable for long typing or office sessions. QMK and VIA support add a high level of customization, allowing deep key remapping and macro control across multiple devices. Wireless performance is strong thanks to the large battery and flexible tri mode connectivity options. The aluminum case gives the keyboard a solid, high quality feel that stays firmly planted on the desk. That said, gamers should note that there are better options around this price that include Hall effect switches and SOCD support, which may offer a competitive edge for gaming focused use.

It is not a standout enthusiast board, but it is a solid and affordable starting point for someone getting into mechanical keyboards.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Unique Color and Decent Features, but No VIA and the Meh Switches
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this because I collect mechanical keyboards, and I didn't have one in a brown color. The color is definitely unique and looks nice on the desk.The keyboard is decent overall, but the switches weren't my favorite. I generally prefer a heavier linear switch, and these felt a little too light for my taste. I also noticed more stem wobble than I'd like, which made the typing experience feel a little less solid. There is a pretty decent thock sound right out of the box, however.Bluetooth worked great right off the bat, but you can connect with a cord or dongle if you prefer.One thing to know is that it doesn't support VIA, and the key remapping software is Windows-only. I'm currently using a Mac, so I wasn't able to test the customization software. If cross-platform customization is important to you, that's something to keep in mind.There are config settings via the onboard screen and the knob, so that is handy to change the backlight color if you lose the shortcuts. The preset light options include white, but it comes across as pink because of the switches. Setting the time was also easy.Overall I like this keyboard, and it has some solid features. For me, the standout feature is the uncommon color, while the typing feel was just okay. I will replace the switches at some point, and I can see this going into the regular rotation.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 25, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great keyboard, very easy to customize
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Before receiving this keyboard, I was unfamiliar with the SOLAKAKA brand, so I didn't know what to expect. I was, however, pleasantly surprised to see that this device lives up to its price tag. I own a few other mechanical keyboards from different brands, and did a side-by-side comparison for the purposes of review.1) Material / Build Quality -Excellent; The keyboard has a nice weight and heft to it, making it feel high quality. The construction and fitment are on par with keyboards costing upwards of twice as much. I do somewhat wish that, for this price point, the pre-installed mechanical switches were a bit better. They would really benefit from having those translucent LED focusing pieces instead of just having an open channel in the switch.2) Appearance -The quality of this keyboard is very nice; with a consistent high-quality look and feel. There are no cosmetic flaws or issues to be found, either on the body itself or the keycaps.3) Connectivity -I appreciate the tri-mode connectivity feature, which is a must have for all my peripherals. The 2.4GHz dongle connects instantly and I've not experienced any lag, even when first booting up my computer, the keyboard is immediately responsive. The Bluetooth connection is also incredibly fast and easy to set up right out of the box. I run a Linux system with KDE Plasma (which is notoriously finicky when it comes to configuring Bluetooth connections) and this keyboard was the fastest/easiest to connect out of all the ones I own.4) Features -I love the convenience of the multi-function knob and display screen. Changing volume, RGB effects, and other settings is very quick and easy.  I also appreciate that the keyboard goes into "sleep" mode rather quickly, just turning off the RGB and display to conserve battery, but remaining immediately responsive to key presses. This makes a massive difference in conserving battery life.Overall, I'm extremely satisfied with my SOLAKAKA A75 PRO, and it's become my new daily driver. I'll definitely be keeping this brand in mind for my future peripheral/accessory purchases.

How can I get the software and the latest version of the firmware?

How to correct the time/volume on the screen? 
When you open the software in wired mode, the screen time or volume will automatically synchronize with the one on your computer. 
Why the keyboard becomes disconnected in the BT mode? 
When the battery level is low, the keyboard cannot support the BT function normally, Please re-update the BT function of the device and fully charge the keyboard. 
Can it work with a PS4, PS5 or Xbox? 
RK keyboards are compatible with some games of PS4, PS5 and Xbox on wired mode. Our keyboard can't connect with Xbox one, PS4 and PS5 through Bluetooth mode 
Why is the S98 mechanical keyboard still not working after connecting the cable? 
Please check the connection mode first. Make sure it's set to Wired Mode by using the connection switch on the top-left or selecting Wired Mode in the keyboard screen settings. Once switched, the keyboard should work normally.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent Keyboard With Minor Software IssuesExcellent Keyboard With Minor Software Issues
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is my first mechanical keyboard, and I finally understand what all the hype is about.The sound is incredibly satisfying. It has that nice mechanical sound without being overly loud or obnoxious, but it also isn't so quiet that you lose the satisfying typing experience. The typing feel is probably my favorite part—the keys feel incredibly smooth and satisfying, and so far everything has felt flawless.The build quality is also really impressive for the price. It has some nice weight to it and doesn't feel cheap or flimsy at all.The smart display is a fun addition. Is it necessary? Absolutely not. 😂 But it's definitely nice to have. You can use it for things like Bluetooth connection and volume settings, and you can also customize it with your own photo or GIF.The one area that could definitely be improved is the software. It's not particularly user-friendly, and finding the correct software to customize the keyboard took me longer than it should have. Once I actually found it, though, it wasn't too difficult to figure out with a little patience. The software itself also feels a little chunky and dated. That said, this has zero effect on the actual performance of the keyboard, so it's a very minor complaint.I've had absolutely no issues with wireless connectivity. I've used both Bluetooth and the included cable and haven't experienced any disconnections, lag, or other problems. One thing to note is that you'll need to use the included cable when connecting the keyboard to the software for customization.The battery life has also been surprisingly good so far. I haven't actually had to charge it yet, so I can't speak to the full battery life, but I work from home about 9 hours a day and also casually game in the evenings. After two days of that, the battery has only dropped about 5%.Overall, I have very little negative to say about this keyboard. The software could definitely use some improvement, and there could be better information provided about where to find and how to use it. But that's a very small complaint compared to everything else this keyboard does well.For my first mechanical keyboard, I'm extremely happy with it. Everything about it has exceeded my expectations. 5/5 and definitely recommend!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great design. Great functionality. 100% Recommend if it fits your general specifications.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: tl;dr: I am EXTREMELY happy with this keyboard. Build? Beautiful. Sound? Amazing. Functionality? PERFECT. Price? FANTASTIC. If this keyboard fits your specifications for your desk and you happen to work with two different computers at the same time, get it ASAP.More details:Previously I had a significantly smaller RK 68 which was great for me. It was perfect for what I wanted, a small profile and clacky keyboard. Unfortunately, I spilled soda all over it and it died so I had to get a new one. Fortunately, it was this keyboard.In my search for a new keyboard I had a couple things I was looking for:- A green color way to match my set up- A nice clack to it.- A numpad attached.Clearly it's not something very specific. But during my search I came across other features that I had no idea I wanted. But this one hit pretty much what I was looking for so I decided to give it a try and boy did it blow my expectations out of the water.== Design ==Pros:This keyboard looks sleek. Before, to build something like this I had considered paying my friend to build it from scratch but the colorway and the key placements are just so clean. With multifunctional keycaps, they've added the second function on the side of the keycap so you can easily see the primary and the secondary without it feeling too cluttered.The back lighting options really make it fun to customize. They give you default options you can run with and each of those options you can tweak to your liking in terms of color.The digital display seems more like a part of the design the way it links to the volume knob, rather than an after thought like some other keyboards. This provides another option for you to make the keyboard your own by letting you upload a gif to just loop by default.Cons:No complaints really, except the digital display occasionally pops off slightly, requiring you to press it back in but it hasn't become too much of an issue for me yet. Also, uploading the gif to the keyboard takes a good amount of time (something like 5 minutes) , so if they could fix that speed that would be amazing.Oh one more complaint is that it's too tall. I had to get a wrist mount just to feel comfortable typing on it.== Functionality ==Pros:MAN, this keyboard is PACKED with features I never thought I would need. Aside from the aforementioned backlight customization, something that has made my life so much better is hidden behind the digital display. It's base functionality of controlling the volume of your computer works like a charm but it's when you get into the submenus that you can really see where it shines.You see, I am someone who bounces between a macbook pro for work and a windows PC for play and so I'm constantly bouncing between the two. Before, I had a mac specific keyboard and a windows specific keyboard, both occupying space on my desk. This keyboard has eliminated that need in a sleek and elegant way by allowing me to hardwire into my desktop and bluetooth to my macbook. From there, I can easily use the digital display + volume knob to switch my connection between the two. Heck, if I needed to add another couple I could. It seems like I can have up to 5 different devices connected (3 bluetooth, 1 wired, 1 wireless dongle). So if for some reason I had another device, I could easily switch between the two.You might ask yourself, but what about the difference in layout between macs and windows machines? Oh my friend, you see... THEY THOUGHT OF EVERYTHING. Through the same digital display, you can swap the layouts between the two types. I was totally fine with that until I read the manual a bit more and found you could even use a hotkey JUST for that. Remember the secondary functions of the various keys? If you look on the side of the 'A' and 'S' keys, you can see that they read 'WIN' and 'MAC' respectively. So to switch formats, all you have to do is hit 'Fn' + 'A' or 'S' to switch between the two. This really pushed my like for this keyboard to love.Cons:The only thing I can really think of is a nitpick and is possibly even already a function, I'd just have to read through the manual a bit more. It would be nice to be able to use a shortcut to bounce between the different keyboard connections like you can switch formats.== Sound and Feel ==Pros:I am having a BLAST typing this review. Every keypress feels so satisfying as the switches engage and disengage making you really feel connected to the keyboard. The sound is more thocky than clacky which is extremely pleasing to my ears, especially after coming from a clackier keyboard.Cons:While this keyboard is probably 50 percent quieter than my last keyboard, it's still definitely louder than a membrane keyboard, so if you're looking for silent, this isn't what you want. But if you're looking at mechanical keyboards, then this most likely isn't you.== Price ==I feel like this keyboard is well worth the 89 dollar price tag for what you get. I feel like even a couple years ago, you'd have to pay 300 bucks to someone to custom make something like this with the design options. Sure, it's not as bespoke as the true customs, but I feel like it holds up just as well.Overall, I'd give this keyboard a 'have no fear, buy away' if your needs are similar to what I've mentioned above!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: All the mechanical keyboard I need
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First mechanical keyboard I’ve owned, can’t imagine I’d need anything different. Bought two of these, one for my workspace and one for my wife. We both needed accurate and responsive keys for frequent data and password entry, the lights and display are just bonus points. I change out my display for random gifs and RGB weekly using the web portal, easy enough once you get the hang of it, takes 5-10 minutes to upload a gif. Can confirm battery lasts about a week with moderate workday use. Keys are on the quieter end of clacky, not as obnoxious as some mechanical keyboards I’ve used in the past. Key travel registers about 75% from fully depressed which took me a tiny bit of time to adapt to. More often now, I’ll think I missed a letter because I didn’t press quite hard enough, but look back to find it registered after all. Comes with a few replacement switches, key puller, and usb-c cable which is nice. I’m sure there is better quality for more money out there but I’m not the demographic for it, this is all the keyboard I think I’ll ever need.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A must have for anyone looking for an amazing sounding keyboard!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: When I first got a gaming PC, I figured I didn't really need a super expensive keyboard and that a cheap one that sounded "clicky" and had lights was fine enough. I also didn't want to bother with charging a wireless keyboard. However, I started to hear from YouTube videos and TikToks about "creamy" and "thocky" keyboards. I immediately started to do research, because I was obsessed with the sound. This is one of those rare purchases that I cannot stop thinking about how happy it makes me. I have absolutely no qualms with it. Here's what I love:The sound is excellent. Videos that I watched were a good indicator, but as other reviews have said, they really do not do the keyboard justice for how it actually sounds. The letters themselves are very creamy, while the function buttons (spacebar, shift, enter, backspace, etc.) have a much deeper "thocky" sound to them. If you're on the fence, at least try it and return if it's not for you.The functionality is incredible. There are a ton of lighting options that you can play with. You can mess around with them in the software on your PC. But because this keyboard has a small LCD screen, you can also change them directly on the keyboard itself. I have mine set to light up the entire keyboard cyan from whichever key I press, expanding out.Speaking of the LCD screen, you're able to upload GIFS or images to the screen, which is a really cool feature.As far as connectivity, you have every imaginable option available to you. I have my gaming rig connected via the 2.4USB wireless adapter. You can also connect up to three devices via bluetooth. And of course you can opt to hardware in.I love the the keyboard has both a USB-A and USB-C port. I am a huge advocate for technology having USB-C as an option, as it is much more convenient, provide faster transfer times, and faster charging times.Speaking of charging, the battery life on this keyboard is excellent. I seem to get about a week's worth of charge with extreme use daily.I know that the keyboard is hot swappable, meaning you can swap out the switches, which ultimately determine the sound of the keyboard, but personally, I haven't messed with that, as I love the way it sounds now.Overall, this is an excellent keyboard. If you're in the market for a wireless keyboard that sounds great, this is the best option out there! I typically don't like spending a ton of money on stuff unless I am absolutely sure of its value, and let me put your mind at ease that this keyboard is worth so much more than what the price tag shows.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: To many firmware glitches - basically unusable for any serious work
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Today, I initially wrote a negative review of this keyboard due to issues with missed or repeated keystrokes, or keys continuing to fire until another key was pressed. However, after extensive investigation (because I really wanted to keep this keyboard for its mechanical build), I finally discovered that the issues were caused by an obscure, lingering USB driver from a device no longer connected to my PC. That driver was behind all the trouble. I hope this revised review is published before the original one, which is no longer valid.After 15+ years of using Cherry MX Blue switches on a single keyboard that eventually got damaged, I was in search of a replacement. This keyboard seemed like a good option - more compact than my full-size board and featuring “tactile” pale green switches. I hoped they would resemble MX Blues in feel, just without the audible click. Unfortunately, these switches aren’t really that much (or at all) tactile. I don’t understand the claim. There is a point somewhere along the key travel where pressure slightly decreases, but you’d need to press very slowly and have an extremely sensitive touch to notice it. In actual typing, it feels - at least to me - indistinguishable from a regular linear switch. That said, I’ve gotten used to them and didn’t have much trouble adapting after so many years with MX Blues. And the 'thocky' sound still sounds nice.The build quality is solid. The board is sturdy, heavy, and a definite improvement over my old keyboard. I’m not particularly interested in the display or LED lighting. I don’t see the point - especially since the keycaps aren’t translucent, so the lights don’t help in the dark. Omitting those toddler-toy-like features and lowering the price - or populating that space with more keys - would be more useful, in my opinion.I used the included keycap puller to swap the positions of the 'Home' and 'Del' keys, then made the change in the RK software. It took just a few seconds. These settings are retained even if you unplug the keyboard or uninstall the RK software entirely from your PC.All things considered, in terms of mechanical construction, this is a very good keyboard. I do wish the switches were more tactile, but that’s just a matter of personal preference. These switches are still decent, and I’ll probably swap them out in the future for some Kailh clicky switches.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Premessa.La tastiera mi è arrivata nuova ma palesemente usata.La confezione era sigillata da un secondo adesivo applicato sul precedente, la tastiera aveva delle ditate, il libretto come in foto, il cavo di alimentazione addirittura pizzicato, tutti i sacchettini rovinati.Insomma, se acquisto un prodotto nuovo quello dev'essere nuovo, altrimenti avrei preso un usato garantito spendendo meno.Posso capire un eventuale reso nei tempi di recesso ma almeno il cavetto andava sostituito.Andando alla tastieraTop di gamma della Royal Kludge.Non vengono dichiarati la tipologia di switch montati, arrivata con i tactile e sono comunque ottimi, non mi era capitato di provarli. Molto piacevoli e che fanno un minimo di resistenza per poi abbassarsi in modo deciso. Il suono è abbastanza piacevole, un po' asciutto ma non fastidioso probabilmente influenzato dalla struttura rigida della tastiera.La scrittura è agevolata dall'ampiezza ridotta della superfice dei tasti seppur non abbiano l'inclinatura ergonomica che offrono altre tastiere di pari fascia, ma il tono su tono su alcuni tasti li rende non di immediata individuazione.Manca la retroilluminazione. Assenza che trovo inspiegabile in tastiere che passano i 100€ di costo ma vedo che, escludendo i classici marchi da gaming, si trova poco.La tastiera ha due livelli di altezza con piedini gommati, ma è abbastanza alta. Personalmente la uso senza rialzo.Full RGB, totalmente modulabile tramite software ma con la possibilità gestire il tutto tramite lo schermo integrato.Buona luminosità e colori intensi.Possibilità di connessione via cavo, incluso nella confezione, via Bluetooth e con chiavetta. Quest'ultima con una sede magnetica laterale.Presenta anche due tasti fisici. Su un angolo troviamo la selezione di collegamento tra via cavo o chiavetta e poco più in là il tasto di accensione e spegnimento.Il comando del piccolo monitor è comodo e si legge bene, così come i led per il Blck Num e il Caps Lock presenti anche come led vicino al tasto Esc.Ben individuabili al tocco anche i segni su F, J e 5.Il piccolo monitor ha una funzione di menù per diverse impostazioni navigabili tramite una pratica rotelle.Livello batteria, data, tipologia di connessione, caps lock e block num, se è in modalità Win o IOS. Insomma, mostra ciò che serve ed è ben leggibile.È possibile anche caricare delle GIF limitate a 60 immagini. Un po pochine e va a togliere le altre info. Opzione carina ma resto dell'idea che, avendo a disposizione un piccolo monitor aggiuntivo, si dovrebbe poter sfruttare meglio.Per esempio con le temperature di esercizio dei componenti, la percentuale di utilizzo, ecc..Il software è completo. Offre di salvare 3 mappature differenti dei comandi e gestire in modo totale l'illuminazione. Non molto intuitivo, devo ammetterlo. C'è un menù di cui non ho chiaro l'utilizzo e non viene fornita alcuna informazione né nel manuale cartaceo ne per quello disponibile sul sito (Entrambi in inglese).Ottima tastiera, nel complesso quella con cui mi sto trovando meglio delle diverse che provate (e ne ho provate diverse nella fascia 50/150€).Peccato davvero per la mancanza della retroilluminazione oltre che, vedendo che è presente su altri prodotti, la mancanza di poterci abbinare il poggia polsi magnetico.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: The sound and typing experience is amazing.The sound and typing experience is amazing.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: This is my 2nd Royal Kludge keyboard and I am very impressed. I've had mechanical keyboards from Logitech, Keychron, Corsair, Drevo and Redragon and I like my RK ones more. This one in particular is just super satisfying to type on. I love the creamy sound from the keys, it's unlike anything else I've owned so far. The green and clay-red color scheme also looks awesome. Keycaps are soft touch but not shine-through which is a bit of a disappointment but not a deal breaker. The little screen and knob is easy to use and actually useful. It's nice to change settings in a menu vs using function keys, and being able to check the time when enjoying full screen entertainment is also handy to me. My audio setup is also able to use the knob as a volume control which is an added bonus. All three connectivity modes work well for me - Bluetooth is reliable, 2.4Ghz is fast and reliable, and wired mode is also fast and reliable. Range on BT/2.4Ghz is average, but since this isnt really an HTPC keyboard I don't think it matters much.My only complaint is the battery life. RK claims they have a gigantic battery in this keyboard but I only get 2-3 days of use between charges, and it takes a loooooong time to charge so it ends up being plugged in a little more than I'd like. If I keep the RGB lighting on the 2nd lowest setting, I can get another day or two of usage but I wish I didn't have to charge this keyboard once a week.I really like this keyboard overall and I'd definitely recommend it! It's a good keyboard for full price but RK has sales all the time so I'd wait for a 20-25% discount, where it becomes a killer deal in my opinion.Edit: 3 months in and still very fun to type on and 100% reliable. I just keep the backlighting off most of the time now to conserve battery and it lasts a while without the backlight on 2.4Ghz link (2-3 weeks light use). Only thing I don't like after a few months of use is having to press fn + PgDn for the End key.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Surprisingly Premium Feel with a Few Annoying QuirksSurprisingly Premium Feel with a Few Annoying Quirks
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've tried numerous keyboards in the past, but this one absolutely stands out above the competition. The build quality is surprisingly solid and does not feel cheap. The acoustics are also great; there is a decent amount of sound dampening padding within the keyboard, which makes it a great base even if you don't like the stock switches.The volume knob features distinct steps that add a nice tactile feel when adjusting the volume, making it feel premium for the price.That being said, I have a few gripes that I will knock off a star for, since I had not known this going into purchasing the product. There is a red indicator light on the FN key (to the right of the space bar) while in wired mode. I’m not sure if this is a charging indicator or something else, but it is quite distracting as it clashes with the custom color settings. I couldn't find any documentation explaining this, and even after downloading the software, I found I couldn't turn it off.Speaking of the software, it feels quite outdated. It cheapens the overall experience and reminds you that this is, in fact, an off-brand product.Overall, this is a solid 75% keyboard. The multimedia functionality is valuable for my professional work, but I just wish I had known about these specific quirks prior to purchasing. If you are on a budget and are looking for a solid inexpensive option for a mechanical, wireless keyboard, this is absolutely an option worth considering.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: My favorite keyboard I have ever had the pleasure of typing on!My favorite keyboard I have ever had the pleasure of typing on!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This keyboard is everything I had hoped for, and more! Where do I even start.I have had my laptop for going on 4 years and being an IT major in college, I have used my keyboard a lot. My keys are extremely worn down and many don't work right. I had seen a review on Youtube about this keyboard and wanted to get it for myself, but then my husband bought it for me instead.It sounds so nice, it is not super loud and obnoxious like many mechanical keyboards are, it is a sort of soothing sound, especially if you are typing a lot. It doesn't become hard to listen to after a while and does not flood your area with loud clacking. I thought that this keyboard was only wireless so I was fine with that, but then I unboxed a wire that came with it! having the option to be wired or wireless is wonderful, especially when I am travelling and have to take my school work on the go with me. I have had 0 issues with the wired option though I have not tried the wireless option, the USB for using is wirelessly is very easy to access. And quite cute too!! Very creative making it a little fish.The lighting and everything is perfect, it isn't too bright like some backlit keyboards, it is more subtle and easy on the eyes. And finding the website to adjust it manually is super simple, I current have mine set on a sort of gently star twinkle with a very light purple to match the keyboard. My typing speed has seen no hinderance since using this keyboard, my average WMP sits between 67 and 70 so I am still able to maintain such as the keys are slightly indented which allows me to set my fingers nicely and they feel very nice typing. There is no resistance and no miss clicking anything. It also feels very sturdy. it doesn't feel cheap like it is going to fall apart in a few months.It also came with some little goodies!! A very cute mousepad, extra keycaps, and a little bunch of stickers. I already swapped the spacebar keycap because I liked the extra a little more than the base one and the mousepad is so perfect it matches the keyboard very well. I am so happy with this keyboard and would gladly buy it again, it feels so well built, sounds so nice, looks so adorable, and really feels like my perfect keyboard!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve had my PC set-up for almost 6 years now, and I never once thought I would get anything pink and “girly”, mainly because it never fits the theme in my room. But I’ve always found the cute, pink theme absolutely adorable.So when I stumbled upon this keyboard, I told myself, “I HAVE to buy this. It’s too cute to pass up on, and plus, I’ve been needing a keyboard that is smaller than my current” (it’s ridiculous that standard gaming keyboards from huge gaming companies like Razor and Logitech are usually made for bigger man-hands).So, I bought it. It took awhile because of a mishap on Amazon’s side, but the keyboard finally arrived. I cannot stress enough HOW BEAUTIFULLY CRAFTED this keyboard is. All the little accessories and gadgetry is just 🧑‍🍳💋🤌 chef’s kiss. The fish dongle, the removable paw pads, and the silicone siding that looks like icing WITH THE LITTLE SPRINKLES are all fabulous. The SOUND OF THE KEYS 🤤😮‍💨 delectable. It’s sooooo creaaaaamy, I cannot get over how smooth the sound is (compared to my clicky keyboard, this is truly melodious). The mousepad and the extra little stickers are fun little goodies and I really appreciate the love put into designing this keyboard. Truly exceptional quality.There was a bit to figure out with the keyboard, like understanding the battery percentage (that’s on my end, not the company’s fault for my slowness lol). The manual does answer this query, BUT, I’m still not sure how the lights show the battery ratio. According to the instructions, I have to press Fn + Right Ctrl, and then the number caps 1-0 light up. But so far, all 10 numbers light up green, even though the last charging session did not yield a green cat face, which would have meant battery percentage is at 100%. Not a complaint, trust me. I’m just a bit confused 😭😭. BUT BUT BUT, OVERALL, the keyboard’s instruction manual is very straightforward, and this is coming from someone who is technologically inept at (most) times lol.Would I recommend? Absolutely, yes, buy this keyboard if you’ve been salivating over it and having the most vivid dreams about owning it. It’s worthwhile.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent, well-constructed, aesthetically pleasing keyboard that is an auditory delight to type on!Excellent, well-constructed, aesthetically pleasing keyboard that is an auditory delight to type on!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Once my old Logitech MX Mini keyboard started getting worn down, I decided that since I work from home, why not get an adorable, fun keyboard instead of one that was so utilitarian and bland? I settled on this keyboard after seeing the excellent reviews and while I'm no mechanical keyboard aficionado, I can say that this keyboard feels well-constructed in every way. The design is adorable, the printing of the keys and additional details (like flowers or sparkles) is crisp and colorful, the backlight is vibrant and enjoyable even high brightness environments, with the battery lasting a good amount of time - I tend to recharge weekly but the battery is often at ~40% at that point. It could easily last much longer if I didn't insist on having the brightness up on the backlight. And the sound, of course, is exquisite. I'm someone who almost always wears headphones while working, but I have found myself taking my headphones off just so that I can listen to the satisfying sound of typing on this keyboard - it makes me feel so productive!I use the keyboard exclusively via bluetooth and have no had any issues - it always connects flawlessly, including after my machine is asleep and the bluetooth needs to freshly reconnect. I will say that sometimes when I have my keyboard, mouse, and headphones connected to my computer, the audio I'm listening to can get a little choppy - but I'm not sure if that's really the fault of the keyboard or just a limitation of how many devices I can have connected simultaneously to my computer.I was also impressed by all of the things that came in the package - the mouse pad, the spare key caps, the key swapping tool, the stickers! Let me tell you, my MX Mini didn't come with any of those things and it was actually more expensive than this keyboard! I've since gotten a nice pastel yellow wrist wrest and a blue vertical mouse to go with the keyboard and mousepad and it makes me smile just to look at my set up now.I have been using this keyboard for about a month and I've already had to stop myself multiple times from getting a second one (with a numpad) just because I enjoy the look and experience of it so much. All in all, I can't recommend this keyboard enough.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I love this keyboard so much!!! Cake + Cat = Adorable
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Pros:- Beautiful keyboard!!! I love it so much. I am currently typing this review using the YUNZII C75 (Beige, Milk V2 Switch) - typing on it feels so good!- Adorable designs. Cake + Cat! What's not to love?- Super easy to use. It's ready to use right out of the box. They also give you some free gifts, including extra key caps (they're all super cute) for further customizing your keyboard.- I bought the Milk V2 Switch version because I wanted something that wouldn't tire my fingers after long hours of typing, and it does the job very well.- Good size for a desktop mechanical keyboard. It's slightly too heavy to be truly portable though, if you want to carry it around everywhere.- I haven't checked the bluetooth connectivity yet, but the 2.4gHz Wireless dongle (the part you plug into your computer) is super cute! It's a little fish hidden in one of the keyboard's cat paws.- Tons of LED settings for the backlight and sidelight.Cons:- Slightly expensive for a 75% mechanical keyboard. Yes, the YUNZII C75 is definitely worth every penny for my use case (because it's super cute!), but if you want good bang for your buck performance-wise (not just looks), you can get great deals for ~$50.- The key clicking sounds are satsifying and very "cakey", but it's a tad bit too loud.- No volume control knob... But there are tons of keyboard shortcuts (you can customize them too) for volume control and other functions.- The key caps are smooth to the touch (which makes typing super enjoyable), but it also means when you try to remove/replace key caps using the provided metal keycap pullers, it's very easy to scratch up the plastic sides of your beautiful key caps.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Absolutely adorable but not ergonomic. Sounds amazing even better with some customizations.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this keyboard after tons and tons of influencing. It's my first custom/switchable keyboard and the start of a new obsession.In short, out of the box it had that great thocky creamy sound which I was looking for and it is so absolutely cute. I adore this keyboard so much. It gives me so much joy to here the tapping sounds I get from it when typing out emails and messages at work. (WFH, so not bothering anyone in an office)I actually switched out the switches on it to the  Akko V3 Creamy Blue Pro ,which added a dampening sound effect to the keys. I think the rounded keys add to the creamy thock sound. On top of that I switched out a few keys, to theYUNZII Coffee Cat Dye Sub PBT Keycaps, which sound a bit different.On the original switch, the coffee cats sounds more like light summer rainOriginal keycaps with akko v3 switch sound like night time mid-sized rain drops falling on the roof in the winterOut of box set up sounds like Rain on a plastic umbrella.If I love this keyboard why the -1 star? It is REALLY NOT ERGONOMIC. And the amount of pain I am in at the end of a 8hr work day is too much.  I find my shoulders have to round in a lot more to keep my hands on the keys. Unfortunately I find myself seeking out a new ergonomic switch keyboard (just haven't found a great sounding one yet).I do not know why there is such a lack of ergonomic keyboards out there that are mechanical.Yunzii, if you are reading this, please please please (I'm begging you) can you make an Alice style keyboard of this or sounds like this?For reference I am female, 5'4/164cm. features: Full-Size Premium Wired Keyboard: The ROG Strix Scope II X is a 100% keyboard with a number pad and wired USB-C connectivity. The aluminum top plate and PBT doubleshot keycaps give it a weighty, durable presence while keeping each key resistant to wear

Hot Swappable, Pre-Lubed Mechanical Switches V2: Create your own custom aesthetics and typing experience with your choice of ROG NX Snow linear switches (for smooth, thocky keystrokes) or ROG NX Storm clicky switches (for crisp, tactile keystrokes)
ROG NX V2 Switches: These switches retain the dust-proof, wall-stem design of the original V1 switches while adding an LED lens for enhanced RGB illumination
Enhanced Acoustics: Integrated sound-dampening foam and switch-dampening pads effectively absorb pinging noises and echoes, resulting in improved keystroke acoustics

Optimized for Gaming, Streaming, and Daily Work: Pre-programmed hotkeys (F1-F5) for control over Xbox Game Bar and recording functions. A multi-function wheel allows for intuitive media and lighting adjustments. All keys are fully macro-programmable
Ergonomic Comfort: This keyboard features three angle adjustments while the detachable wrist rest positions your hands just right for long sessions
Included Accessories: Detachable wrist rest, 2-in-1 ROG keycap & switch puller, ROG-themed spacebar keycap, USB cable, and ROG sticker

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very nice quality, way above my expectations
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’m very happy with this so far it’s comfortable to use and the key presses are quiet and smooth presses all the way through without any unexpected resistance at the end. The disconnect of the wire at the keyboard itself is very useful for transport to move it off my desk when I need a workspace when I’m not gaming and still leave the wire to easily plug it in again instead of having to dive under my desk to plug in so a big plus there. Then the LEDS are very nice with a lot of colors with adjustable brightness and modes that don’t need a PC to change through the modes which is very good since I’m on Xbox
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on November 6, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Best Asus Keyboard For The Price
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I didn’t get a perfect keyboard. Space bar and left shift key was a bit sticky. I think the kit came with spare keys. It doesn’t bother me enough to need to replace the keys. Regardless with those issues, I definitely recommend this keyboard. I started with an Asus 65% brown keys, next was a Asus 65% blue keys for my Mac, then this snow red keys. It’s way quieter than the brown keys for sure. I got this keyboard for work just to make my dull computer tasks / paperwork more enjoyable. Was it worth the price? I’d say so. I like the weight, it makes it feel like a quality keyboard. Key controls make it easy to change the themes and I appreciate you can change the brightness settings. I did not expect scroll wheel to be useful, and I use it a lot when playing music to skip, pause, and mute songs. My favorite keyboard so far.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on December 29, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Pretty good, especially for the price.  Not really for gaming but that's fine for me.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I saw the reviews, and I was not sure what to think.  Well it arrived, it's fully mechanical.  The feedback feels good too, the switches are a bit less reactive, so for FPS games or stuff like that, it may not be the best option.  But the keys feel great for typing.  And they aren't "quite" as loud as some of the other switches.  They still have a good "thwack" though.  The lighting seems decent, and the black matches the rest of my stuff lol.A couple of things I don't necessarily like, first it seems a bit too light.  I guess that could be good or bad.  Also, the cord to connect it feels kinda cheap and flimsy.  Even like some of the lower end Razer product have a nice fabric wrap on the cord.  Idk, I guess for the price, it isn't too bad.So overall, yeah.  If you just need something pretty good and not too expensive, it's a good option.  If you want something better, just pay a little bit more for like cherry switches and a full metal one.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 3, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Just got keyboard today to use in place of my other recent purchase of the ASUS ROG Strix Scope II (also a decent keyboard), I got this mainly because 1. while the other recent purchase of other ROG keyboard mentioned here is a good one and has my much desired number pad, it isn't considered a 100% full size keyboard like the Scope II X here. it is a 96% size so still "full" just without the negative spaces which I do like to keep things seperated (and helps prevent some keys from being forced to double up and share a button with use of the FN key. My only two MINOR "gripes" about this keyboard here, (which lets be honest up front are more so personal prefrence), 1. Not wireless, not a huge deal breaker, but I knew that going in before I purchased it, and it was a sacrifise I was willing to make as while wireless is a desired function it wasn't a NEEDED or MUST HAVE function.... and 2. after opening the box I noticed the wrist rest isn't as padded as the Scope II above I mentioned. Small disappointment but not enough to return it. The other reason I got this keyboard was for the Linear keys (on top of the above mentioned 100% full size keyboard.) When I got the Scope II I had accidentially got the storm clicky version, the clicks don't bother me and I do like them, but I do also play videogames and is why I got a gaming based keyboard, it is why I still wanted to keep it as well as get THIS keyboard the Scope II X for the quieter keys. I highly reccomended BOTH keyboards
