features: Full-Sized Keyboard with Screen & Knob: Missing the full set of keys unavailable on cramped compact keyboards? Step up your setup with the EPOMAKER QK108 for ultimate usability. This full-sized keyboard features 104 keys, a familiar complete layout that requires no learning curve, a fully customizable volume knob, and a vibrant Smart Screen. Program the easy-to-reach knob to control anything—from toggle brightness to scrolling through your playlist, or take the screen to check the date, monitor keyboard status or load up a custom GIF. No more fumbling with complex shortcuts, with the QK108 keyboard, get the full-sized comfort you demand, with the cutting-edge customization you deserve.

RGB Keyboard with 8000mAh Battery: Gaming for days or crushing a week of work without worrying about finding an outlet, the QK108 Keyboard delivers unmatched longevity with a massive 8000mAh battery. Just finished a late-night session and want to stretch that remaining power? One press of the dedicated buttons switches off the backlight or screen, instantly maximising the already huge battery life to 229 hours. Offering dozens of pre-saved effects and full control over saturation, tone, speed, and direction, the bright, fully customizable RGB backlight of QK108 is your canvas, whether you need a subtle, singular colour for focused work or a vibrant RGB wave to match your stream.

Custom Keyboard with QMK/VIA Support: Fully compatible with QMK and VIA, the QK108 custom keyboard puts the power of personalization directly into your hands. Serious enthusiasts can dive into the QMK firmware for unmatched, ground-up function remapping using custom code, while the VIA software offers easy customization friendly to beginners. Easily record complex macros to execute a series of actions like a combo attack or data entry sequence, or use the powerful Mod-Tap function to have a single key perform two functions when tapped or held. Save up to 4 layouts with on-board layer switch keys, eliminating the need to open the software mid-game or work session.

Tri-Mode Wireless Keyboard for WIN/Mac: Enjoy lag-free 2.4GHz for intense gaming, seamless BT for productivity, and wired connectivity for QMK flash, with the QK108 wireless gaming keyboard. Compatible with your desktop, laptop, tablet, and phone, effortlessly switching from coding on your PC to replying to a message on your Mac laptop, with up to 5 devices paired and remembered simultaneously (2.4G/Cable/BT1/2/3). Plus, true cross-platform power is guaranteed with dedicated Mac modifier keycaps, the VIA software that works flawlessly on WIN, Mac, and Linux, and on-board memory that ensures personalized setup is ready for you no matter which devices you connect to next.

Hot-Swappable Keyboard with EPOMAKER Switches: Tired of being locked into one switch type or dealing with frustrating key chatter mid-game? Imagine instantly swapping your linear switches on the WASD cluster for ultra-fast response in an FPS, then quickly installing tactile switches on your utility keys for that crucial, unmistakable feedback—all thanks to the 5-pin hot-swap sockets and included 2-in-1 puller that make switch changes effortless. For users who prefer to experience right out of the box, the included EPOMAKER switches are lubed and tuned, offering smooth, stable, and consistent typing.

Dye-Sub PBT Keycap in Cherry Profile: Business-like in grey and white but decorated with mint-green, the originally designed keycap set on the EPOMAKER QK108 keyboard can blend into the office setting but still pops up as the center piece on any desk setup. These originally designed, comfortable Cherry profile PBT keycaps are crafted from high-strength PBT plastic, resisting the greasy, shiny wear-and-tear that plagues standard keycaps over time. The legends and signs are dye-subbed into the keycap’s body, ensuring your keyboard looks and feels like new through years of intense use and marathon sessions.

Creamy Keyboard with Sound-Dampening: Crafted with the complex 5-layer acoustic enhancement internal design, the QK108 Gasket keyboard promises blissful switch asmr with soft flexible feel. The market-tested sound-improvement formula of sandwich foam (latex), IXPE switch pad, Sound-Enhancement PET, bottom foam (sponge), and bottom silicone gives this creamy keyboard the satisfying thocky sound by riding resonance and delivering exceptional comfort by cushioning shocks after each bottom-out. Treat your ears and fingers to an unparalleled level of tactile and auditory joy, as QK108 accompanies your gaming victories and professional endeavors.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Insane RGB ! Great build for the price!Insane RGB ! Great build for the price!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Got this on sale and I’m thrilled with the board I got for the pricepoint ! I bought the pink Sakura style keycaps version and I must say it’s a bit lighter than I thought it would be weight wise. I tested out switching the switches and they are hard to remove with the provided switch puller but I do feel it’s higher quality than some of my Yunzi boards. The RGB is insaaaaane! I swapped the keycaps so I could get the full effect and 10/10 I’ll be entertained all day by this board. it’s gorgeous has a great typing feel and the silent switches are oddly satisfying to hit and make a soft thockthud noise. Very quiet though. One thing to be aware of, the dongle on the bottom of the board will fall out of the feet are extended. Keep track of that little guy!  Also the keycaps I added are by womier , plastic but silicone look. I think silicone keycaps would be cool on this board too.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: This this THE ONE for the office!This this THE ONE for the office!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I think I’ve finally found my perfect office keyboard!I picked up this model because I needed a full-size mechanical keyboard with a modern look, and after some research, this one seemed like the best fit for my office use.Since my workplace requires a relatively quiet environment, I chose my first silent switch option. Epomaker calls this switch the Sea Salt Silent, and I’d say the keyboard is nearly as quiet as a membrane board while still delivering the satisfying feel of a mechanical switch.The small display in the top-right corner is a nice touch as it shows the time along with useful indicators like Caps Lock and Num Lock status.Overall, this is a very solid choice for anyone looking for a full-size mechanical keyboard that produces little to no typing noise.

The sea salt switches are very quiet, which helps reduce the noise I make, but I still get a nice tactical feel. * My major qualm with this keyboard is the fact that it goes into sleep mode in five minutes. I use the wireless connection via usb that comes with it, and it will almost immediately go into sleep mode when I am not using it. The manual says it usually will wait 30 or so minutes. But it is less than five. And every time I go to type after a few minutes, it misses the first key, and I have to retype everything or go back and fix it. This is a real problem, especially in my line of work with data entry. It almost made me consider returning the product. I have found no way to fix this, but I am hoping someone has figured it out. I am not using the backlighting or the screen. Also, the numpad button being left on despite the backlight being turned off is sort of annoying because sometimes I don't want any light on at all. Also there are not a lot of options for backlight colors despite being able to change vibrancy. I am not sure if I need to download a software to customize this keyboard more. Overall, a good quality keyboard, but slightly annoying, unchangeable features for an expensive and supposedly customizable keyboard.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: US配列、104キーのフルサイズ、QMK/VIA対応のゲーミングキーボードです。長年JIS配列を使用していましたが、自身の小指の短さからホームポジションを維持した状態でのエンターキーの入力やカギ括弧周りの入力にストレスがあったため(これまではそれを当たり前のものとして受け入れていました)、一念発起してUS配列のキーボードにトライしてみました。ゲーミングキーボードと銘打たれていますが、キーキャップがシャインスルーではないため、ちょっと見の印象は一般ユースのフルサイズキーボードです。また、型番は108ですが、以前のモデルで4キーあった右上の部分がミニサイズのディスプレイ、ライティングのスイッチ、ボリュームノブに変更されているため、キー数は104キーです。この部分については好みが分かれるかと思いますが、個人的に一番大きいのはキースイッチをフル換装する場合に35個×3セットで足りる点です(交換用スイッチの確保を考えると結局4セット買うことになるかもですが)。キースイッチは静音タイプのSea Salt Silentを選択しました。以前の環境ではYUNZIIのCaramel Coffeeを使用しており、不満があればこちら(現在はV2)を購入して換装するつもりでしたが、結果として換装の必要性は感じませんでした。キースイッチの静音性について厳密に評価すると、耳を近付けた状態でキーを底まで押し込み、その状態から勢いよく戻した際に僅かにスプリング音が聞こえます。静音性にこだわり抜きたい方ならお気に入りのキースイッチに換装してもいいと思いますが、通常のタイピングにおいては遜色ないので、殆どの方はキースイッチの換装をする前に追加ルブを考えた方がよさそうです(※追加ルブをする気力のある方のみ)。キーキャップは昇華印刷PBTですので、ライティングに拘らない一般的な用途であれば不満はないと思いますが、キーキャップのライティングが必要であれば互換性のあるシャインスルーキーキャップや、同メーカーのシリコンキーキャップを購入して換装するといいでしょう(※他ルートで注文済み。届いたら換装してみる予定です)。更なる静音性を得ながらある程度のライティングによって暗所での視認性が向上するシリコンキーキャップは良いアップグレード先だと思いますが、ゲーミングキーボードを標榜するのであれば、最初からシャインスルーキーキャップが採用されていてもいいのかもしれません。RGBライティングについては、暗所での視認性をメリットとして感じてはいるものの、イルミネーションにはこれといった魅力を感じていないため、ただでさえ長いレビューを少しでも短くするため詳細は割愛します。マニュアルを見ながらFnキーを組み合わせた操作をすれば、目的のライティングにすることは難しくないかと思います。ミニサイズの画面はデフォルトの状態で日付・時刻を含めた各種インジケーターの機能を持っていますが、常時注視する必要性はおそらくないかと思います。ここについても詳細は割愛します。ボリュームノブは設定不要でメイン音量の調整に使えます。ボリュームはFnキー＋ファンクションキーでも操作可能になっていますが、あると便利なのは間違いないでしょう。さて、このモデルにおける本題はQMK/VIA対応にあり、US配置キーボードで日本語入力をするユーザーにとっての柔軟なカスタマイズ性にあります。私の場合はJIS配列の環境で変換キーと無変換キーにIMEのON/OFFを割り当てていたため、これをQMK/VIAのMod-Tapで再現することが本機を購入する最大の目的でした(現在使用中のIMEはGoogle日本語入力です)。結果として、VIAによるカスタマイズはネット上の情報と出力AIの助けを借りて難なく完了。左右Altキーのタップ(押してすぐに離す)でIMEのON/OFF、長押しでAltキーとして問題なく機能するようになり、日本語入力環境におけるUS配列キーボードへの移行のハードルの一つを簡単に越えることができました。また、無変換キーで行っていたひらがな・カタカナの切り替えはIMEの設定でTabキーに割り当て、Tabキーに割り当てられていた予測変換をShift+Spaceキーに割り当てることで代用することにしたため、後は異なる配置の記号入力、形状の違う物理キーへの適応を進めていくことで、US配列キーボードへの移行は遠くない内に完遂できるだろうと期待しています。自宅内のメインマシンにおける有線接続の環境としてはおまけとも言えるワイヤレス接続機能ですが、このモデルは技適の認証を受け、キーボードの裏側にしっかり技適マークも表示されているため、日本国内で合法的にBluetooth接続が使用可能です。マニュアルを見ながらスマートフォンとのペアリングを試みて問題なく完了し、メールを書く際にこちらのキーボードを使ってみましたが……これは思わず笑みがこぼれる位には快速・快適でした。今まではLogicoolのK480を使用していたのですが、やや特殊な形状・メンブレンキーのキーボードであったため、不自由するほどではなかったものの快適とまでは言い難い入力環境でした。これがこのキーボードによって爆速とも(相対的比較で)言える環境に変貌したのは、あまりにも劇的な変化だったと言えます。キーボードとしては全部入りでQMK/VIA対応、ゲーミングキーボードとしてもキーキャップがシャインスルーでないことさえ除けば他に何もいらないと言えるほど充実しており、Windowsマシンの環境を新たに作る際はこれを買っておけば不足はまずないと言えるでしょう(※日本語配列をご希望の場合はTH108 JISをどうぞ)。一つ前の環境(キーボード)を作った当時はJIS配列のフルキーでホットスワップ対応+PBTシャインスルーキーキャップというキーボードがそもそも市場に存在しなかったため、80％キーボードのベアボーンキット、好みの静音キースイッチ、PBTのキーキャップで1台作り上げ、これにテンキーボードを組み合わせることで実質フルキーの環境を作っていたのですが、コスト的にはそれらの半分以下(※セール価格の場合です)のこれ1台でほぼ全部が揃い、尚且つワイヤレス対応までついてきてしまった訳です。ですので、乗り換えのコストとしてはむしろ安いとすら思えるほどでした。一般的なフルキーボードをお使いの方がUS配列キーボードに日本語環境の変化・最適化を求める場合、これを買っておけばまず間違いなく、追加のコストも原則として不要です。今でこそ複数の選択肢がありますが、単純にキーボードとして良い出来の商品だと思います。おすすめします。

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Have been using mechanical keyboards for close to 15 years I think now and it's impressive how good value they have now become. And this one is a step above in value in terms of features and also high build quality.Love the inclusion of a knob which I've got setup for volume. The small screen I thought was slightly gimmicky but actually I have found a purpose for the time displayed on it.I still use my wired keyboard but use this on my racing sim rig for it's wireless capabilities. Have almost never used a wireless keyboard and this has absolutely zero delay as far as I can tell. As mentioned before, I now have the time whilst I'm racing thanks to the keyboard. Have been using the keyboard for weeks and battery is still going, although I must admit I don't actually type on it as much as a normal keyboard.Sound of the keyboard is brilliant and uses linear switches that are easy to press. Only small downside is that this has a US layout so the enter key isn't full size and both " and @ are switched. I haven't found this a problem though.All in all, great bit of kit.

inStockText: In Stock  Only 3 left in stock - order soon.
breadCrumbs: Electronics > Computers & Accessories > Computer Accessories & Peripherals > Keyboards, Mice & Accessories > Keyboards
features: Keychron K3, a compact 75% layout ultra-slim wireless mechanical keyboard built for peak productivity and a great tactile typing experience.

Be ready to multitask without missing a beat by connecting the K3 with up to 3 devices via the stable Broadcom Bluetooth 5.1 chipset and switch between your laptop, PC, tablet and phone seamlessly. *Keep the distance between the keyboard and the device within reasonable limits to minimize signal interference.

With a unique Mac layout, the K3 has all the necessary Mac multimedia keys while still being compatible with Windows. Extra keycaps for both Windows and Mac operating systems are included. *If it doesn't match your device exactly, you can try updating the keyboard's firmware.

With open-source QMK firmware, it offers endless possibilities for key remapping, macros, and shortcuts. Customize every key easily using the Keychron Launcher web app for a more personalized typing experience. With its built-in AI assistant (live in beta now), keyboard customization is no longer complicated — just ask in plain language, and AI handles the rest.

Together with the reinforced aluminum body (plastic bottom frame) make the K3 one of the thinnest and lightweight wireless mechanical keyboards on the market. The K3 also comes with a floating keycap design with a charming white backlight with modern keycap legends to sync with your mood.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've used a lot of keyboards going all the way back to the original IBM PC. Most modern keyboards feel mushy to me. This feels great.I bought both the brown and the blue switch variations. The blue had a great feel, but its relatively high-pitched click was annoying. The brown is closer to a Goldilocks switch, quiet and with good tactility, although just a tiny bit mushy. I chose the K3 for its low-profile design, as I had read that the standard Keychron keyboards are very thick and need wrist rests. The K3 at only 7/8" thick feels fine without one. Key travel is also quite good. Fresh out of the box, I don't seem to have lost any typing speed compared with the MacBook Pro keyboard which I've been using for the last few years.I haven't had any problems with the Bluetooth connection. I have it paired with three devices – an iMac, a MacBook Pro and an iPad Pro. Just a few seconds each to pair initially, then no trouble with any of them. Switching between devices takes just a couple of keystrokes. As a Mac user, I really like that the media function keys work out of the box and are labeled properly. Likewise the command and option keys. I have no real need for the backlighting and certainly not for all the fancy, flashy chasing light modes. It's a keyboard, not a theater marquee. But I do find it handy to have on at minimum brightness when I have to work in a darkened room.If there's one thing I wish Keychron offered, it's a low-profile numeric keypad to go with this. I didn't want a full-size keyboard like the K5 which would force me to reach pretty far for my trackpad. But a numeric keypad comes in handy when I have to type in more than few digits, and it would be nice to have one to put to the right of the trackpad.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 12, 2022

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I like it, but wanted to love it.  Be sure to disable "power saving" on your Bluetooth adapter!I like it, but wanted to love it.  Be sure to disable "power saving" on your Bluetooth adapter!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I needed a good quality wireless mechanical keyboard for using my PC on my living room TV.  I like this one a lot, but have a few gripes.The keys have a good feel to them (especially for a keyboard this size), and typing is comfortable.  The form factor is quite small, so it works great as a media center keyboard, etc.I don't love the placement of the Home, Page Up, Page Down, End keys.  I am getting used to them, but wish they were on the top.  Also, the location of the Print Screen button (the at the top one with the icon) is in an inconvenient location, and frequently gets pressed, activating my screen capture utility.  Also, I don't love that the Arrow keys are grouped together and not in separated like my Razer. This is a tradeoff for the compact size.Initially, I was having major problems with the keyboard frequently losing it's Bluetooth connection, and with keys pressing multiple times.  I disabled "Power Saving" on my Bluetooth adapter in Device Manager (see my screenshot) and this completely solved these problems.  Be sure to do this if you buy this keyboard to save yourself some headaches!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Update - 2/12/26I really want to love this keyboard.  It would be perfect if it actually worked.  The first one had issues with its battery life, then with the keys sticking.  I tried unpairing it from my PC, and repairing it.  Didn't help. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this to replace the Nuphy Air60 V2, which has been nothing but a PITA for me from jump street. Right away I realized the K3 was the better choice. For starters, it JUST WORKED right out of the box. I had it set up and connected to my Windows laptop via Bluetooth in approximately 5 seconds. No software headaches, no programs needed to download, no "firmware flashing," none of that nonsense. Just connected and ready to go right away.But even aside from that, the key-feel of this is much better. I never jived with the Air60 keys (even when the stupid thing worked) and was constantly mis-typing. The keys were slippery or something--hard to describe. Right out of the gate, the Keychron feels better under my fingers. Oh, and it's half the price of the Air60. Let's not forget that tiny detail.Very happy with this. I also have a Keychron K2 which I've used as my daily workhorse without trouble for years, and the brand will continue to get my business. Well done!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent reasonably priced slim mechanical TKL keyboard!Excellent reasonably priced slim mechanical TKL keyboard!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've been looking for a slim TKL mechanical keyboard for a long time. I've read about the Keychron products, but hesitated to pull the trigger because other brands had more reviews with similar ratings. I shouldn't have and hope my review will help others who are relying on the number of reviews to make an informed decision.This little beauty is the best slim TKL mechanical keyboard I've tried by a long shot! The form factor is perfect, quality is great (especially given the very reasonable price) and it feels and works great! I might end up buying one or two more, one for the office and the other just so I have a replacement for when this one wears out. I have not tried using it in wireless mode or using it with a Mac. The default key configuration is for Mac, but there are spare key caps to replace Mac specific keys with Win (which I promptly did :) ). It is small enough to leave plenty of space on your desk, yet heavy enough to not move about when you type. The keyboard comes with brown mechanical switches, which are smooth and quiet enough to not annoy people sitting around you.All keys are mapped correctly to their designated functions. I'm actually using it with a Chrome book, was super impressed that all the keys do what they said they would, even the screenshot button.All in all, I've very happy with my purchase - great product Keychron!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A great mechanical keyboard for gaming.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Pros,1. Got this on sale for 10% off so the price wasn't that bad.2. It's a full sized mechanical keyboard with ARGB lighting and easy to install software to control the lighting and assign program functions to the keyboard.3. Unlike most mechanical keyboards this one has a softer touch to it. It's not as tactile as other mechanical keyboards I've  used, but I think that could be good for people who actually do a lot of typing.4. The keys are interchangeable with custom keys.5. This can be ran either with the included 2.4Ghz adapter, Bluetooth or straight into a PC or laptop with USB type C connector.6. The keyboard is rechargeable and if the keyboard power gets low you can plug it into a USB port on a PC or laptop so you can continue using it while it charges.7. The lighting has a lot of different colors,  pattern and it gets decently bright for using at night or in a darker room.Cons,1. Being a softer touch IDK what the reliability is going to be like yet, but so far it seems to be built well.2. Since it's a rechargeable keyboard eventually the internal battery will be useless. I prefer keyboards that take external rechargeable batteries so I can recharge batteries instead and replace it when it can no longer be recharged.One of my Redragon keyboards I was used malfunctioned and I couldn't get it to work so I bought this one to replace it. Normally I don't have keyboards fail on me, but this was an electrical error that prevented the keyboard from working. If the same thing happen with this one I'll never buy another Redragon product. I'll give a product one chance. I could have tried to return the keyboard for a replacement, but since Redragon isn't a US company I didn't want to go through the trouble. Only time will tell.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Budget-friendly pro-level fullsize with a smooth, creamy sound.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I really, REALLY like this keyboard. The Mint Mambo switches are super reactive with a satisfying soft 'clocky' sound, instead of clacky or clicky. I like the shape of the keys, the MT3 profile is really unique, the subtle concave dip in the center of the keys makes for a really comfortable, smooth transition from key to key as I type.I like the software, though I wish it was multifunctional, as I have a few Redragon RGB devices, and having an app for each one is kinda silly- but it's not worth a demerit, in my opinion. Redragon is consistent with updating/upgrading their offerings.The board is made of a heavy, high-quality plastic that has a sturdy weight to it. The keys are PBT and are quite scratch-resistant. I appreciate the on-board options to change the brightness of the RGB or disable it altogether. Having three modes of connectivity is super convenient.Despite what some of these reviews say, this board does NOT come with extra keycaps, but it does include a handful of replacement switches. As well, the USB-C cord included is nice, but I wish it were a braided style instead of the standard silicone like the one that came with the Storm Pro.Pros: Nice feel to the switches, smooth transition from key to key, good sound dampening and a nice soft mechanical sound instead of the typical click/clack. Connects via USB-C, 2.4ghz dongle (included) or Bluetooth. Hot-swappable switches that can be made compatible with almost any 3 or 5-pin switches (untested).Cons: Battery is internal, lower quality cable than other Redragon 'pro' devices, no wrist rest.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a nice semi-quiet keyboard, I do like the full size as I do use the 10-key a lot when analyzing data. The keys are a nice, comfortable height; if you’re not use to a higher profile key it will take some getting used to. It also has the stands in the back to be able to angle to keyboard up to make it more comfortable to type on. The material feels like a soft plastic, so it’s smooth and nice to the touch. It also has more of a “thock” sound to it rather than a “clicky” which I prefer in an office setting.It was extremely easy to connect to my Mac system. My MacBook prompted exactly what to do and it recognized the keyboard immediately. I am also using the Bluetooth connection and it doesn’t seem to have any lag to it. The battery is also pretty good, I used it from 9AM-1PM and it went from 99% to 97% with the RGB on.The one downside that it may have is the RGBs is not really visible in bright settings. As you can see in the video they don’t seem very bright, however in a low light/dark setting they do shine through well.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Wonderful mechanical keyboard!! I spent WEEKS searching for a simple 100%, hot swappable wired keyboard that didn't cost an arm and a leg, and THIS keyboard is the only one I found that was ACTUALLY AFFORDABLE and very high-quality for the price!Though others have said that their keyboards came with keycaps in different colours, mine only came with the stock keycaps on the board, and some extra switches. The default colour is not my style, but it's not hard to find keycaps in your own preferred style and just swap them out, which is exactly what I did.This is my first ever truly mechanical keyboard after at least 15 years of membrane keyboards, so take my opinion with a grain of salt; the stock switches feel really nice!! They're honestly not much louder than my steelseries apex 3 membrane keyboard was, and they don't tire my fingers out when typing or gaming. They seem pretty well lubed right out of the gate, as even after i did my own lubing of a few keys, there really wasn't much difference in terms of feel or sound.Having 4 extra system shortcut keys above the numpad is really nice, though i don't use them as i already have a seperate 24-key macropad with volume control and calculator shortcut, but the 'sign-in lock screen' and the 'show desktop' keys would be pretty convenient if you need to quickly minimize windows for whatever reason, or step away from your computer for a bit at work or in the living room or whatever.I LOVE that the lock key lights are in the right space above the arrow keys, having the lock lights RIGHT THERE makes it so much easier to notice I've accidentally hit caps lock or disabled num lock, as my aforementioned steelseries keyboard's lock lights were blocked from view at a 'normal' typing angle, so i had no clue if numlock was on or off unless i looked straight down at the keyboard.LOVE that it's tri-mode connectivity too! I use it solely wired just because I already have a solely wireless keyboard for 'away from desk' control, but having the option of using it either via USB, Bluetooth, or 2.4GHz USB dongle receiver is really nice! Connect it to whatever device you want, however you want! Plus, it can work for both Windows and Mac with a literal slide of a switch, so that's even more convenient for people who switch between them in their day to day lives.The RGB is really nice with 16 different lighting patterns, 4 speed and brightness settings, as well as a full on-board per-key-colouring option which is quite fun to 'paint' different keys with.TL;DR - If you like full-sized keyboards, and want to give mechanical keyboards a try without needing to take out a small loan, GET THIS KEYBOARD ASAP

Working perfectly fine in any mode out of the box, but one can also download an app from their company website and configure it further. Typing is really nice, even while typing this review I want to type it a bit longer so that to click a bit more, really satisfying.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I first purchased this keyboard in April of 2020 after building my first custom PC. If there's one thing I hate, it's being wired in on a computer setup so that shifting around in your space is tedious. I do professional editing, and gaming is a major hobby of mine, so a comfy keyboard is critical for me as I'm on my computer more often than I'd like to admit (please, go touch grass if you identify with this statement).Personally, this keyboard is a lifer product. Being so thin, and low to the desk, it's extremely ergonomic. Your wrists stay naturally resting on your desk throughout your time using this keyboard, so fatigue isn't a problem. And I do notice when I go to a keyboard that's higher up, my wrists do get tired--so it's not my superhuman 30yr old wrists, it really is the keyboard.The keys themselves are spaced masterfully, and typing feels extremely natural. The extended size that includes a number pad makes a really big difference when doing calculations, or putting together spreadsheets. There's pretty much everything you could need on this keyboard. If you have small hands, I will say this may not be the best keyboard for you. It's by no means compact, but rather a perfect match for your average-sized hands. Typing feels really good to me. It's fluid, nothing gets in the way, and again--nothing is missing from this keyboard.I almost forgot to mention battery life because I literally never think about it. I use this keyboard on a regular basis. Do I forget to turn my keyboard and mouse off overnight? Often. The battery life however is insane. And when you do lose battery, pop it into wired hell-mode for a few hours while you keep using it, and then don't worry about it for another month, or three.There's only two downfalls I have found in this keyboard over the last near-4 years:1) the arrow keys are teeny--they are essentially useless if you find yourself playing an older game that doesn't use WASD for movement (a very niche situation, but it's a major learning curve to overcome)2) spilling your coffeeSpilling your coffee deserves it's own paragraph, so here we go. I'm prone to spilling. Sometimes I get up earlier than I want for a meeting. And sometimes this leads to spilling my coffee. Sometimes I'm just a clumsy girl having a clumsy day. And sometimes my cat is an idiot. This keyboard takes a spill like a blumbering idiot. As in - it doesn't. At least not at first. Spill a major drop on this guy that seeps into the keys, and he's down for the hour. Spill your whole entire cup all over your desk, and on TOP of your keyboard? Have a backup keyboard for the day. If your spill isn't directly onto your keyboard, you'll be fine. This keyboard's metal bottom is a champ, and so so easy to clean. But the second something drips onto the electronics between the keys, you'll be typing 5 letters instead of 1. Like so: "lm;kio"; rather than "l". Now. You CAN bounce back from this. Turn your keyboard off, put that baby upside-down, and let it rest. Turn it off, and take to it with the cool cycle of a hairdryer (don't take my advice on this method, I am not a professional keyboard scientist). Generally, wait it out. However, it takes time, and obviously liquid in any electronic is a risk. I've bounced back from many a spill with this keyboard. So if you have time, it's no big deal. If you have a backup keyboard that cost you $10 that you tolerate in desperate times, no big deal. But there may be a time where your cat knocks something over in the middle of the night, and your keyboard sits in liquid for ????hrs. And it may fry the top 2 rows on your keyboard, so you have to CTRL-C/CTRL-V the exclamation point for two weeks before you convince yourself to rebuy your keyboard. I can't tell you what your life is going to look like.What I can say is that this keyboard--for me--is worth all of it's two minor downfalls. I may or may not have just bought this keyboard for the second time because of the above spill incident. Who's to say. But I love this keyboard. It feels good to be able to use my exclamation point again! It feels good to type away on a newer version with sturdy, fresh keys. I'll miss the smooth divot my thumbs wore away from 3.5yrs of spacebar usage, but I'm excited to wear new spacebar smoothness into this new keyboard. Also. I love the addition of the calculator shortcut on the numpad. Extremely useful for a keyboard that has a numpad.This keyboard? This keyboard is an It-Girl™. Certified. By me. I hope you buy this keyboard. I hope you fall in love with this keyboard. I hope you have a nice, late-summer marriage with this keyboard at sunset. It's what this keyboard deserves. I know it has flaws. But don't we all?

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I build computers and the recent Microsoft requirements for older motherboards and cpus made it necessary to upgrade several network computers.  In doing so, wired keyboards were replaced with wireless ones.  The Arteck HW193 fit the bill beautifully. Since I have to move about to various computers, its light weight and size makes it the most efficient keyboard I have encountered.  Highly recommended and a great value for the money.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Amazing value keyboard that turns out to be my favorite.Amazing value keyboard that turns out to be my favorite.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So, what does $25 get you in terms of quality for a keyboard in 2026?  Turns out, pretty dang good!I have owned several keyboards over the years, and this is both the cheapest and the best I've had.The keys are hard plastic key caps, but the action is mashmellowy goodness.  Quiet keys that feel good when typing to your fingertips.  My only complaint is the space bar, it's the loudest key by far, but even then not too bad.The volume knob / light knob on the top right is perfect.  I don't need a full control center on my keyboard, but having quick access to turn up and down sound on the computer is the most practical and useful control to have within reach.The function keys on the F keys up top are a nice touch.The battery life is fantastic.  It easily lasts well over a month between charges.  It will last far less if the lights are on, but I keep them off to extend battery life, and I prefer them off anyways.Comes with a 2.4Ghz dongle, which I use on my desktop.  Also pairs using Bluetooth which let's me use it with my laptop or tablet.  All connected immediately with no bumps or hiccups.Something worth mentioning is that it will put itself to sleep to save battery, but you can hit a key and it won't miss a stroke.  Other keyboards I've used, you have to "wake" the board with a key, then type what you need.  But not on this, which is great!Overall I would be willing to wager $25 that this is the best money you can spend on a keyboard.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Great laptop keyboard replacement with a caviet when booting
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I have three laptops that all suffer from the dreaded disease: Beerus Spillus. So, I checked into replacement keyboards and found that this option was about a third the price of buying a specific replacement keyboard for even one laptop. The keyboard appears tiny, but it's actually the same size as a laptop keyboard. I'm probably going to miss not having a numeric keypad. You'll need to get a wrist rest for it, if you use it a lot. Pairing is just standard Bluetooth stuff that only takes a few seconds.The big issue is if you dual boot your computer, since you don't actually have a working keyboard until the operating system boots. Assuming you're using as Linux/Windows combination and Grub to select which operating system to boot, you need to configure it to start Linux by default. In Linux, create a shell script file with the following command "sudo grub-reboot X && reboot"  where X is whatever menu item your Windows option is on your grub boot menu (usually 2 or 3).  I just added an icon to the Linux desktop that I double click to run the script. Note that you have to pair the keyboard separately for Windows and Linux, so those three nifty toggle buttons get filled up fast. I need 8 toggle buttons for my three laptops :-(If you're trying to do anything with the bios, such as a boot password, you can't do it, since you don't have an active keyboard. In that case, consider a wireless keyboard since the dongle should be active on power-up.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Replaced my Razer Ornata because of "key feel"
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I don't usually write reviews (you can check my profile, I think), but I felt compelled on this keyboard.  This thing is bada$$.  I have had a Razer Ornata that's been my "daily driver".  I like the mechanical clicky sound and it's just felt solid. The keys are "light" to press, and the whole thing feels pretty dang good.  I realize that the feel of a keyboard is very subjective, so this might not be the same case with you.Only been using it for a week, but I feel like this will be my go-to keyboard for the foreseeable future. I do wish the manual told you how to switch through the lights, but you can google that pretty quickly (function key plus the \| key, the one right above the Enter key).  Otherwise, I love this thing.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: The thock is real!The thock is real!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This thing is awesome! The gasket and foam really make a huge impact on the thocky sound and feel. Sound is lovely, and so is the typing feel. productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: If you want a keyboard that just feels good without turning your desk into a NASA control panel, this one hits the mark.Typing on it is super satisfying. The keys have that nice, responsive feel where every press actually feels intentional, not like you’re poking a soggy sponge. Whether you’re gaming, typing essays, or rage-slamming keys after dying in Fallout, it keeps up without feeling cheap.Build-wise, it’s solid without pretending it’s some luxury centerpiece. It’s got a clean look, maybe some RGB if you’re into the “my desk glows like a UFO landing strip” aesthetic, but it’s not overdoing it.It’s also comfortable for longer sessions. No weird key spacing, no awkward height that makes your wrists feel like they’re doing yoga. You can sit there for hours and not feel like your hands are filing a complaint.Now, it’s not one of those ultra-premium custom keyboards people spend half their rent on. But honestly? That’s kinda the point. It gives you most of the good stuff without the “I built this myself and now I judge everyone” energy.Overall: smooth, reliable, and actually enjoyable to use. If you just want a keyboard that works great and feels nice every time you touch it, this is a solid pick.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Onky worked right for about 6 months
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this to see if it was easier to type with long nails, and it really was. I liked the backlit keys, not bc of the lights (I turned them off, everytime) but bc it meant the letters couldn’t wear off, which is an issue with my “normal” keyboards. I also enjoyed the clacking sounds. Every now and then a button would fly off, but ok think it was more of me hitting it at angle. They were easy to put back on.Unfortunately, after about 6 months it started having issues with the I button… sometimes it would work, sometimes not, sometimes it would iii in a row. The problem would come and go. Then the problem was T. Same scenario, same spotty performance. Then it was the E’s. Never more than 1 letter being an issue at a time. The other letters would just suddenly be fine and a new 1 would mess up.But what finally made me give up (at the 9 mos point now) is the spacebar just quit working. It started out with the normal issues, but then it all but stopped working— like I’d type 3 sentences, and there wouldn’t be a single space. I’d try to go back and add the spaces, and I’d press spacebar 15 times but nothing happened.I don’t need lights, but I did want the typewriter style keys. It’s a shame the keyboard can’t even make it 6 mos. I paid $30 for junk.

aPlusContent.title: Product description
aPlusContent.rawText:
Product description
Xisoguu is professional in providing Colorful Keyboard and Mouse Combo. We take advantage of our experienced quality control and supply chain to bring you “Quality products that exceed end-user expectations. 
1.2.4 GHz wireless technology delivers a reliable connection with up to a 10M range; 
2.Works with your PC, desktop computer, laptop or notebook. Compatible with Windows XP / Vista / 7 / 8 /10 operating systems; 
3.Auto sleep/wake smart keyboard and mouse and conserves the battery life without the hassle of changing batteries; 
4.Features 12 multimedia hotkeys for instant access to the Internet, email, play/pause, and volume so you can easily check out your favorite sites; 
5.Wireless keyboard is ergonomically designed with phone holder and anti-slide pads. 
Q：The keyboard or mouse response is delayed, how can I fix it? 
A: Low batteries may be the cause. Please replace them with fully charged batteries. Use the device within a 5-meter radius. If the issue persists, please contact the XISOGUU support team immediately. We can resolve your issue more quickly and efficiently, avoiding unnecessary inconvenience. 
Q：Is there only one USB receiver? Where can I find it? 
A：YES, the wireless keyboard and mouse share ONE USB receiver, it is stored on the back of the mouse next to the battery compartment. 
Q: Does it include a USB-C receiver? 
A: No, it does not include a USB-C receiver. 
Q:Does it come with batteries? 
A:Not included, the battery needs to be purchased by the buyer, the keyboard requires 2 AAA batteries, the mouse requires 1AAA or 1AA battery. 
Q: Do the keyboard and mouse have on/off switches? 
A: The keyboard and mouse both have on/off switches. The keyboard switch is on the side of the keyboard, and the mouse switch is on the bottom of the mouse. 
Q:Why doesn't the keyboard respond when the batteries are installed? 
A:1. Confirm that the batteries have power. 
2. When installing the batteries, please follow the positive and negative polarity instructions. 
Q: What to do if the keys are stuck or frozen while typing? 
A: There are no obvious obstructions between the keyboard/mouse and the computer. 
2.4 GHz wireless 
One 2.4 GHz USB receiver can connect both the keyboard and mouse, can also be used separately, plug & play, no need to download any software. 2.4 GHz wireless provides a powerful and reliable connection up to 33 feet(10m) without any delays.(Wireless USB receiver is at the bottom of the mouse). No Delay, No Dropout. 
Ergonomic Design 
The round key keyboard has a gentle slope that helps to ease the strain on your wrists and the muscles in your arm. Compact and wireless, this mouse is designed to be equally comfortable for both left and right hands thanks to the contoured shape that follows the natural curve of your hand. 
Where to Find USB Receiver 
The wireless receiver is at the bottom of the mouse.（The keyboard mouse shares a USB receiver.） 
PLEASE NOTE 2-in-1 USB Receiver: The keyboard and mouse ONLY require ONE USB receiver, and NO need to use two USB receivers. 
How to use the Keyboard and Mouse Set: 
Take out the USB receiver, insert it into the USB port of the PC or laptop, then plug 1 AAA battery into the keyboard, 1 AA battery into the mouse, wait a few seconds, you can start using it. 
Note: 
1. Batteries are not included. 
2. The receiver is on the bottom of the mouse. 
Package: 
1 * Wireless Keyboard 
1 * Wireless Mouse 
1 * USB Receiver (stored in mouse) 
1 * User Manual

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: ---Overview first impressionWhen I first opened the box, I was struck by how charming this combo looks. The retro typewriter aesthetic with round keycaps really gives it personality—it’s the kind of thing that catches your eye on a desk. The matching mouse finishes the look; it doesn’t feel like they just paired a generic mouse, which is often what happens in combos.Physically, the keyboard feels lightweight but reasonably solid for what it is. The mouse has some heft, not overly premium but enough that it doesn’t feel toy-ish. The packaging was adequate—protective foam, wrapped parts, everything in place, no damage.---Design & Build QualityKeyboardKeycaps: The round keycaps are the star of the show. They’re cute, fun, and evoke that vintage typewriter vibe without being gimmicky. The material feels like standard ABS plastic, which means they’re slightly soft-matte, a bit prone to shine over time but also less likely to crack if you press too hard. The legends are clear and readable.Layout and Size: It’s a compact USB wireless keyboard (full-size in width, but no numeric keypad if I remember correctly, or at least reduced/compact layout). The slope is gentle. It has rubber pads on the bottom so it doesn’t slide around too easily. There are no crazy multimedia gimmicks, but it’s sufficient for regular typing, casual use, office tasks.Weight & Feel: As mentioned, lightweight. For typing, the keys have a mild tactile feel—not mechanical, obviously—but comfortable. No big rattle. Some flex in the board under heavier pressing, but not enough to be distracting. For general writing, browsing, etc., it’s more than usable.MouseThe mouse is modest in size, contoured enough so it sits comfortably in hand. The clicks are quiet (“silent click”) as advertised, which is a plus in shared spaces. DPI adjustability (three levels: 800 / 1200 / 1600) works well; it’s responsive and I didn’t notice major lag or skipping when moving fast or across multiple surfaces (mouse pad vs wood vs cloth). The scroll wheel is smooth enough, though a bit light.---Wireless & ConnectivityUses a 2.4GHz USB receiver that handles both keyboard and mouse. That’s very convenient—just one dongle, less clutter. The receiver is stored in the bottom of the mouse.Range: advertised up to ~10 meters (≈33 feet). In practice, in my home setup, it works well from across the room (maybe ~4-5 meters) without noticeable delay. Walls add some interference as always, but no dropouts in normal office distances.Plug-and-play: No driver/install needed, recognized immediately by Windows machines. I tested on a Windows 10 laptop and a Windows 11 desktop; both worked right out of the box with full functionality. (I did not test on Mac or Linux, but some users report potential differences.)---Battery Life & Power ManagementKeyboard needs 2×AAA batteries, mouse uses 1×AA.Has auto-sleep mode: after about 10 minutes of inactivity, the combo sleeps to save battery. That does help; whereas before sleeping the keyboard and/or mouse can stay responsive when I pick them up.Power indicator LED: there’s a red light on both when turning on and when low battery (red flashes). Useful, though the low battery warning isn’t super early—sometimes I notice sluggishness before the light starts flashing.---Strengths & What Works WellAesthetic appeal: If you like vintage / typewriter look, this delivers. It’s fun and decorative as well as functional.Quiet use: Silent clicks on the mouse, quiet keyboard / no loud mechanical clacks, which makes it good for quiet spaces, shared rooms, evenings, etc.Convenience: Shared dongle, wireless, no driver setup. Good for plugging into laptops, using in living room, etc.Cost-effectiveness: Given what you get (keyboard + mouse combo, decent wireless range, sleep mode, etc.), seems reasonably priced. You’re getting more than a barebones combo, in my opinion.Good value for casual / light users: For typing emails, essays, browsing, web work, streaming, etc., it delivers well.---Weaknesses & What Could Be BetterNo numeric pad (if it’s the compact version)—for folks doing spreadsheets or heavy number input, that can be a downside. If your workflow depends on numpad, you’ll need to consider that.Key feel isn’t mechanical: This is obvious, but if you're used to a mechanical keyboard, the “give” / mushiness in keypress is noticeable. For touch-typists who like strong tactile feedback, this might feel a little soft or “flat.”Battery lifespan: Even with sleep mode, batteries will need replacement. For heavy use, or high brightness/LED-if any (though I think this model doesn’t have backlighting beyond the LED indicators), it can add up.Build rigidity: There’s some flex in long key rows when typing hard. If you tend to press firmly, the centre can flex a bit. Not enough to be a dealbreaker, but perceptible.Mouse scroll wheel: The wheel is smooth but light; in some cases, I felt it could use a sharper tactile feedback. For very precise scrolling (e.g. in long documents), it sometimes overshoots or feels a little sensitive.Limited OS compatibilities mentioned: The description says Windows XP / Vista / 7 / 8 / 10. It doesn’t explicitly mention macOS, Linux, or Chromebook. If you use non-Windows machines, you might run into quirks.---Real-World Use Cases & FitHere are some contexts in which I think this keyboard/mouse combo is especially good — and others where maybe it isn’t:Ideal for Less ideal forCasual typing (emails, social media, web browsing) Heavy gaming, fast reflex mouse work (e.g. FPS)Home-offices, shared spaces, dorm rooms Professional typists / writers who need mechanical feelAesthetic setups / decor, streaming setups with style elements Users needing numeric pad or very specific keyboard macrosUsers who dislike loud clicking / want quieter peripherals Users expecting high-end mechanical keyboard features or full desktop grade mouse precision---Performance Over TimeOver about 1–2 weeks of mixed use (web browsing, document writing, media control) I noticed:Battery performance is decent: I haven’t had to change batteries yet. The sleep mode seems to work reliably—keyboard enters a low-power state after inactivity.Connectivity remains stable. No random dropouts so far even with moving laptop around, distance about 5-7 meters, occasional obstacles.Key legends remain intact; after some use, no visible wear yet (but I’m not typing tens of thousands of characters a day).Mouse still good; clicks remain quiet, the DPI switch works, though the finish (paint/plastic) shows very minor scuffing after moving it on rougher surfaces.---Verdict & RecommendationIf I had to summarize: this is a very good keyboard & mouse combo for light to moderate use, especially if you care about aesthetics and low noise. It won’t replace a mechanical keyboard or a high-end gaming mouse, but that’s not its goal. For home use, office work, school, casual content creation, etc., it punches above its weight given its price.I’d recommend it to:Writers, students, anyone who types a lot but doesn’t need mechanical key travel.People who want a stylish desk set-up.Those who share rooms / want quiet peripherals.Casual gamers who don’t need ultra-fast mouse polling / mechanical switches.I’d hesitate to recommend it to:Gamers who want ultra-low latency or precise mouse control.Power users who need a numpad or custom keyboard macros.Users who prefer fully mechanical switches.---Suggestions for ImprovementIf I were giving feedback to the manufacturer, here’s what I’d suggest to improve future versions:1. Add a backlight or LED options (especially under keycaps): even a soft glow or customizable lighting could enhance aesthetics and usability in dim light.2. Improve key travel / feedback: maybe a slightly firmer switch or hybrid membrane/switch that feels more tactile.3. Include numpad or a detachable extension: many users need numeric input regularly.4. Better scroll wheel resistance / tactile feedback on the mouse – make it feel less “loose”.5. Mention compatibility more explicitly: include Mac, Linux, maybe mobile/tablet support.6. Provide rechargeable battery option or include rechargeable batteries
